title: Recife's AI Policy and City Strategy (Subnational: Recife)
description: Recife’s AI Initiative was created to address a clear challenge: public institutions were under growing pressure to deliver faster, more personalised, and more transparent services, while lacking structured guidance on how to use artificial intelligence responsibly. At the same time, the city recognised AI as an opportunity to improve decision-making, expand access to services, and strengthen innovation across government, academia, and the private sector. The initiative seeks to balance innovation with safeguards, ensuring that technology improves people’s lives without compromising rights or public trust. The core objectives are threefold. First, to establish clear governance rules for the ethical and transparent use of AI in public services, including risk assessment, data protection, and human oversight. Second, to build institutional capacity by providing practical tools, shared infrastructure, and training for civil servants. Third, to stimulate an ecosystem approach, encouraging collaboration among public institutions, universities, start-ups, and civil society so that AI solutions can address real social and economic needs. Implementation combines regulation and experimentation. The initiative is anchored in a municipal AI decree that defines principles and responsibilities, while also promoting pilot projects in areas such as digital public services, data-driven policy, and citizen support systems. It is supported by governance structures for data management, monitoring mechanisms for algorithmic risks, and partnerships with local and international organisations. Over time, these elements are being integrated into standard administrative processes, making AI governance part of routine public management rather than an isolated programme. Since its inception, the initiative has evolved from isolated digital transformation efforts into a structured policy framework for responsible AI adoption. Future steps include expanding cross-sector partnerships, refining risk evaluation methods, and scaling successful pilots into permanent services. The long-term vision is to position Recife as a reference for practical, citizen-centred AI in government, while creating a model that can be adapted by other cities facing similar challenges.

title: AI Principles in Media
description: In light of the accelerating use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in media, alongside growing challenges related to misleading, false, and fraudulent content, deepfakes, public opinion manipulation, algorithmic influence, and the difficulty of regulating content across cross-border digital platforms. This initiative establishes guiding principles for the use of AI across the media content lifecycle, including production, editing, publication, and redistribution on media and digital platforms, to ensure responsible and safe use, mitigate associated risks, preserve media integrity, and protect societal values and individual rights. The objectives of this initiative are: • Guide the use of AI technologies in the media sector based on responsible practices and risk management. • Enhance the reliability of media content and protect public trust. • Contribute to reducing the risks of misinformation, deepfakes, privacy violations, and infringements of intellectual property rights. • Clarify the responsibilities of media entities, platforms, and content creators. Additionally, this initiative is expected to be a reference guide that adopts the approach of balancing and enabling media innovation with the protection of society, grounded in transparency, responsibility, and proportionality to the level of impact. It ensures compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and controls and the regulatory requirements issued by SDAIA in the fields of data and AI. Results, outcomes and impacts: The planned initiative to develop AI principles in the media sector is expected to strengthen responsible AI use, enhance content integrity, and build trust in digital media. It will support alignment across media stakeholders by promoting transparency, accountability, and safeguards against misuse such as misinformation and manipulation. Impact will be measured through adoption of principles, integration into editorial and production processes, and improvements in compliance and risk management practices. In the future, the initiative is expected to enable more resilient media ecosystems, reduce harmful content risks, and support sustainable innovation in AI-driven media applications.

title: CanChat Use Cases and Accessibility
description: CanChat is an internal web application hosted on departmental infrastructure using a Canadian-provided model. It supports knowledge-grounded responses, official languages, accessibility requirements and responsible use aligned with policy and governance. HICC is launching two priority AI use cases to streamline departmental operations and improve service delivery. The first is a generative AI assistant for the Build Canada Homes programme designed to help Canadians and partners navigate new housing initiatives with ease. The second is an automated analysis model for the National Housing Council that summarises complex public consultations, ensuring that diverse perspectives are accurately reflected in policy development. Both tools prioritise universal accessibility to ensure that information and engagement remain inclusive for all Canadians. Results, outcomes and impacts The project is intended to provide secure and accurate GPT capabilities with the ability to adapt and train to HICC needs. It is expected to have decision-making capabilities, although this is not the primary use case. An Algorithmic Impact Assessment is forthcoming. title: AI for the Detection of Compliance Breaches in Public Procurement
description: Public procurement monitoring requires expert knowledge applied to a complex and increasing volume of legal and administrative documents. AI algorithms, including large language models (LLMs), could help to ensure broad coverage, as well as provide rapid and accurate analysis to detect compliance breaches, prevent corruption risks, diminish inefficiencies and reduce potential misuse of public funding. The initiative pursues the following objectives: Extract, read and process unstructured data from text documents submitted by government agencies and suppliers. Develop and implement an LLM model trained on public procurement regulations that allows the detection of compliance breaches. Enable processing, updating and data analysis of information on a daily basis for large volumes of files in short timeframes. This initiative is part of ChileCompra’s broader strategy to incorporate AI responsibly within the public procurement system. It includes complementary projects such as AI-based corruption detection tools, predictive price comparison instruments and models to promote supplier participation, especially among small and medium enterprises. Moving forward, the ethical governance framework will be applied throughout the entire lifecycle of the institution’s AI systems, incorporating continuous risk assessments, bias monitoring, model validation, impact tracking and public transparency reporting. The goal is to institutionalise these practices and gradually extend them to additional platforms within the public procurement ecosystem. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative started its implementation in January 2026. The first outcomes of the project include an overall design of the technological architecture, selection and prioritisation of red flags, as well as quality assurance indicators and strategies. The proposed metrics to assess implementation results are organised into six main dimensions: Ground Truth or minimum evaluation baseline; rates of automatically detected anomalies; rates of confirmed compliance breaches; rates of correction of detected anomalies; OCR processing quality metrics; and language model (LLM) performance metrics.

title: Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence and European Data Regulation
description: The Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence and European Data Regulation represents a crucial step in Slovakia's digital governance. It addresses the need for a robust institutional framework to enforce European regulations (EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, and Data Act, Regulation (EU) 2023/2854). Objectives : The primary objective is to create a trustworthy environment for AI deployment. The Act would establish the Office of Digital Integrity (Úrad digitálnej integrity) as a new central state administration body. This Office would serve as the market surveillance authority for AI, ensuring that high-risk AI systems meet safety and transparency requirements before entering the market. Implementation & Evolution : The initiative would centralise digital supervision. Besides AI, the new Office would also handle competencies related to the Digital Services Act (DSA) and co-ordinate with cyber security bodies. The Act would create a "Permanent Commission for Digital Integrity" to facilitate cross-sectoral co-operation with other regulators (e.g. National Bank of Slovakia, Trade Inspection). Future evolution focuses on building the Office's capacity (hiring experts, establishing testing facilities) and fostering an ecosystem where innovation complies with ethical standards. Evolution over time : Supervision is currently described as fragmented. The proposed Act would unify the oversight of digital technologies under one roof to prevent regulatory silos and ensure consistent application of EU law. Results, outcomes and impacts As the initiative is currently in the legislative process (proposed), the impacts are projected based on the Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA). Expected Outcomes: Institutional: Establishment of a fully functional Office of Digital Integrity by 2026. Legal: Harmonisation of Slovak law with EU standards, removing legal barriers for AI developers. Economic: Increased trust in digital products, fostering the data economy. Measurement: Success will be measured by the effective operationalisation of the Office, the number of supervised entities, and the efficient handling of complaints regarding AI systems.

title: Korea Digital Inclusion Act
description: The Digital Inclusion Act of Korea establishes a comprehensive legal framework to ensure that all people can benefit from digital and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies without discrimination or exclusion. As digital and AI-based systems have become central to public administration and service delivery, gaps in access, skills, and usability have created new forms of inequality, particularly affecting older persons, persons with disabilities, migrants, and individuals with limited digital experience. To address these challenges, the Act defines digital inclusion as a shared responsibility of government and society and sets out clear obligations for national and local authorities. It requires the development of multi-year national plans and annual implementation plans to systematically reduce digital barriers and strengthen digital capabilities across the population. This planning framework enables coordinated action across ministries, levels of government, and policy sectors. A key feature of the Act is the introduction of a Digital Inclusion Impact Assessment. Public authorities are required to assess whether new or significantly modified digital and AI-based services, products, or policies may create barriers for digitally vulnerable groups. When risks are identified, authorities are encouraged to take corrective actions at an early stage. This mechanism supports the prevention of exclusion before harms occur and aligns with international discussions on trustworthy and human-centred AI. The Act also strengthens accessibility requirements for digital and AI-enabled public services. It includes certification schemes and incentives to promote accessible digital products and services, as well as mandatory accessibility measures for self-service technologies such as kiosks. These provisions aim to ensure that digital transformation in government does not disadvantage people who rely on alternative formats, assistive technologies, or human support. Beyond public service delivery, the Act promotes the development and scaling of digital inclusion technologies. It supports research and development, standardization, professional training, and international cooperation related to inclusive digital and AI solutions. By linking social inclusion goals with innovation and industry development, the Act provides a sustainable foundation for inclusive digital transformation. Through its legal basis, implementation mechanisms, and preventive approach, the Digital Inclusion Act offers a replicable policy and governance model for governments seeking to advance inclusive and trustworthy AI adoption in the public sector.

title: Automatic AI-powered mail categorisation
description: KRPAN is an information system for document management designed to support the management of documentary records. It is deployed on the central information infrastructure of the Ministry of Digital Transformation as a central web-based information system for the public sector. It enables government employees to work with documentary material more quickly, flexibly and efficiently. It provides for the secure capture and management of original and scanned documentary material in digital form; supports the recording and management of general and administrative matters; and provides support for working with government materials, e-invoices and other financial documents. Due to the increased volume of documents and the need for faster, more flexible and more efficient processing and conclusion of administrative matters, the idea of using artificial intelligence emerged. AI would enable the automatic sorting of incoming mail, increasing efficiency, simplifying work processes and ensuring consistent access to information. The purpose of the solution is to establish a comprehensive system for the automatic sorting of incoming mail using AI. The service will be used within IS KRPAN and is expected to increase document-processing efficiency, reduce manual intervention, and improve the accuracy of the classification and processing of incoming mail. The selected contractor will establish and configure a generic solution for the automatic sorting of incoming mail on its own local infrastructure located within the Republic of Slovenia and integrate the solution into IS KRPAN. The contractor will provide all necessary hardware and software resources for the system’s operation. The implementation process will include configuration of the automatic mail-sorting and classification module, integration with IS KRPAN, system testing and deployment. It will also include: the automatic processing of documents received through MailSync integration in IS KRPAN; technical analysis of documents; the use of optical character recognition (OCR) and AI language models for document sorting and classification; and entry of the processing result, including the category of the administrative matter, into IS KRPAN. The solution will initially be deployed at the Ljubljana Administrative Unit and, if required, at up to ten additional organisations. Following successful deployment at the Ljubljana Administrative Unit, the contractor will ensure the uninterrupted operation and continuous availability of the solution.

title: Mentor.AI
description: MentorIA is a conversational virtual assistant developed by the Secretariat of Management and Innovation of the Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services (Seges/MGI), in partnership with Serpro. Integrated into the Compras.gov.br system, it uses generative artificial intelligence with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) technology to answer, in real time, the questions of procurement officers based exclusively on current official documents. The system reduces the time spent searching for regulations, avoids rework, supports decision-making, and strengthens the transparency and legality of government procurement processes. The initiative is aligned with the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan (PBIA) and its strategic axis No. 3, AI for Improvement of Public Services. It also operates in the public procurement dimension, aiming to incorporate AI tools into public administration routines to increase the efficiency and quality of government decisions. Unlike open AI tools available on the internet, MentorIA provides traceable responses, indicating the regulatory sources and the exact excerpt that supported each answer, ensuring greater reliability and legal certainty for procurement processes. Launched in March 2026 and available to all Compras.gov.br users, MentorIA is in its initial phase, with a focus on procurement planning. The next steps include deeper integration with procurement systems, expansion of the indexed document base, and extension of its scope to other phases of the public procurement cycle. The initiative represents a concrete step in the modernisation of Brazilian public management, contributing to more efficient procurement and higher-quality services for society. Results, outcomes and impacts Launched in March 2026, MentorIA serves all users of Compras.gov.br, the procurement portal used by civil servants across hundreds of Brazilian federal agencies. As the system is recent, quantitative results are still being consolidated. During the acceptance testing phase in December 2025, the system was validated for response accuracy based on indexed official regulatory documents. Quality is continuously monitored through user feedback using thumbs-up/thumbs-down ratings and audit logs. Expected impacts include a significant reduction in the time spent on regulatory consultation, a lower incidence of bid challenges, and greater legal compliance in the planning of public procurement processes.

title: Boardroom Primer to AI Adoption & Governance
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming a strategic capability for businesses, creating opportunities for greater competitiveness, innovation and sustainable growth while introducing new financial, operational, ethical and reputational risks. The Boardroom Primer for AI Adoption & Governance was developed by AI Malaysia to help Malaysian boards, directors and senior management navigate these opportunities and challenges through informed oversight of AI adoption and governance. The Primer provides a practical reference for business leaders to understand AI-related opportunities and risks, assess whether AI use cases align with organisational purpose and risk appetite, and consider relevant ethical, legal and governance obligations. It sets out a structured approach to responsible AI adoption covering five stages: planning and design; solution pairing; organisational readiness; verification and validation; and deployment and monitoring. The governance component further supports boards in considering AI risk, proportionality, accountability and oversight. It highlights the importance of aligning AI adoption with existing organisational governance and risk-management arrangements, including appropriate controls, human oversight, assurance, monitoring and escalation mechanisms. The Primer is intended to be adaptable across sectors and organisations of different sizes and stages of AI maturity. Launched in July 2026, the Primer was prepared by AI Malaysia Berhad, Malaysia’s national AI lead agency (formerly known as the National AI Office Malaysia), with contributions from the National AI Office AI Advisory Working Group, which convened between February and June 2025, and feedback facilitated by the Institute of Corporate Directors Malaysia. It is designed as a living document that may be updated over time in response to developments in the AI landscape, including changes in technology, governance practices and the regulatory environment.

text: Boardroom Primer to AI Adoption & Governance. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming a strategic capability for businesses, creating opportunities for greater competitiveness, innovation and sustainable growth while introducing new financial, operational, ethical and reputational risks. The Boardroom Primer for AI Adoption & Governance was developed by AI PLACE to help PLACE boards, directors and senior management navigate these opportunities and challenges through informed oversight of AI adoption and governance. The Primer provides a practical reference for business leaders to understand AI-related opportunities and risks, assess whether AI use cases align with organisational purpose and risk appetite, and consider relevant ethical, legal and governance obligations. It sets out a structured approach to responsible AI adoption covering five stages: planning and design; solution pairing; organisational readiness; verification and validation; and deployment and monitoring. The governance component further supports boards in considering AI risk, proportionality, accountability and oversight. It highlights the importance of aligning AI adoption with existing organisational governance and risk-management arrangements, including appropriate controls, human oversight, assurance, monitoring and escalation mechanisms. The Primer is intended to be adaptable across sectors and organisations of different sizes and stages of AI maturity. Launched in July 2026, the Primer was prepared by AI PLACE Berhad, PLACE’s national AI lead agency (formerly known as the National AI Office PLACE), with contributions from the National AI Office AI Advisory Working Group, which convened between February and June 2025, and feedback facilitated by the Institute of Corporate Directors PLACE. It is designed as a living document that may be updated over time in response to developments in the AI landscape, including changes in technology, governance practices and the regulatory environment

title: Government assignment to 25 Swedish national authorities to report on their use of AI
description: The Government has decided to assign 25 national authorities to report on their use of AI. The rapid development of AI provides good opportunities to improve the authorities' services, but today there is no overall picture of what the use of AI looks like.The assignment includes reporting on what collaborations exist with other authorities and what training or other competence-enhancing initiatives have been offered to the staff. The authorities must also report on the challenges linked to ethics, law and security.The assignments will give the government a better picture of how government agencies both use AI today and how to plan for its use in the future. This is a prerequisite for being able to take advantage of the opportunities and at the same time manage the risks associated with the technology. Collaborations between authorities on the development and use of AI can also lead to significant efficiency improvements. Presenting such a broad assignment to several government agencies is part of the Government's concerted effort in digitalisation policy, with the aim of ensuring Sweden's role as a leading research nation, an ambitious welfare nation and an advanced industrial nation.

title: Independent Research Fund Denmark
description: The Independent Research Fund Denmark (IRFD) plays a key role in supporting research excellence by funding investigator-driven projects across all scientific fields. As part of Denmark's broader effort to strengthen its position in artificial intelligence (AI), IRFD will launch a thematic call in 2025 focused specifically on AI research. This initiative follows the political agreement on the national research reserve and will allocate approximately 100 million DKK to support innovative, independent research projects. A central focus will be on ensuring the responsible and ethical development and use of AI.This initiative addresses the growing need for deeper scientific understanding of AI technologies and their impact on society. While AI offers many opportunities for economic growth and public service improvement, it also raises complex ethical, legal, and societal questions. The funding call aims to enable Danish researchers to explore these challenges while contributing to the global body of knowledge in AI. Researchers from universities, research institutions, and potentially interdisciplinary fields are expected to benefit from this funding opportunity.The primary objectives of the initiative are to support high-quality, bottom-up research in AI, promote responsible use of the technology, and build national capacity in this strategically important area. The initiative also aims to foster long-term knowledge generation that can inform policy, innovation, and education. By encouraging curiosity-driven and independent research, IRFD ensures that Denmark remains at the forefront of critical AI developments, not only technologically but also ethically and socially.Looking ahead, the AI-focused call may serve as a model for future thematic priorities, particularly in fields where technology intersects with society. Depending on the outcomes and interest generated by the 2025 call, IRFD may consider additional funding rounds or broader interdisciplinary approaches. The initiative reflects IRFD's evolving role in addressing complex global challenges through research, and its ability to adapt funding strategies in line with national and international priorities.

title: AI as Focus Area in the Performance Agreements With the Public Universities
description: The overall goal of having a focus on AI in the performance agreements is to increase excellence in research and teaching, to increase efficiency and effectiveness at universities through the use and utilization of AI technologies, to ensure trustworthiness and accessibility as well as security and resilience in connection with AI. In response to these requirements, the universities and the ministry agreed on a wide range of measures in the performance agreements 2025-2027. Here are some examples.Many Universities will implement new AI strategies or update existing strategies on digitalization, to develop a holistic institutional approach to the new challenges and opportunities that AI technologies bring.A key goal of the ministry is to increase the digitization and AI competencies of students, researchers and teachers to enable the safe and effective use of new, innovative technologies for learning, teaching and research. Therefore, many Universities agreed to offer new extension curricula or micro credentials courses on AI or to revise and adapt existing curricula for students, as well as to offer further training opportunities for teachers. The University Linz for e.g. plans to implement a Competence Centre for university didactics and AI-sensitive university teaching.At the same time, the cross-university project "Academics AI" was also anchored in all performance agreements (see separate measure), as was a cross-university project on further enhancing cyber security in all universities.A focus was also placed on Infrastructure (HPC) in order to further strengthen Austria as a research location in the area of AI and to enable excellent (interdisciplinary) research with and around the topic. To increase visibility and impact the University of Vienna and the Technical University of Vienna agreed to pool their resources by co-founding the Vienna Centre for AI.

title: The Government strengthens AI skills among professionals and students
description: The Government strengthens AI skills among professionals and students.AI is increasingly affecting everyday life. Professionals need up and reskilling in AI. Therefore, seven higher education institutions have been assigned to develop short courses with a focus on AI.According to the AI Commission, Sweden is lagging behind internationally in the field of AI, despite the fact that there is good basic education on innovation. AI will affect everyday life more in the future, and professional roles may change, among other things, because of increased automation. This means that those who work as, for example, nurses, teachers, or engineers may need to supplement their previous education to better meet the requirements for competence that are set because of the development of AI.Knowledge about AI among professionals can be increased through short, skill-developing courses, among other things. The Government is therefore investing so that seven higher education institutions can develop courses with a focus on AI for professionals in various sectors.Higher education institutions must report on the development of AI in education. Sweden's students need to be well prepared for future professional life and understand the opportunities and challenges of AI tools. Therefore, the higher education institutions are tasked with reporting on how they work with the development of the educational offerings regarding AI, and efforts to integrate AI elements in the courses where it is relevant. The assignment is in accordance with the recommendations of the AI Commission.

title: National Policy on Artificial Intelligence (CONPES 4144)
description: Since the formulation of the National Policy on Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence (CONPES Document 3975 of 2019), progress has been made in the construction of enabling conditions for the adoption of digital technologies. However, the country still shows low capacities for research, development, adoption and ethical and sustainable use of AI systems in strategic social, economic and environmental issues.This CONPES document formulates a national Artificial Intelligence policy whose objective is to generate capacities for research, development, adoption and ethical and sustainable use of AI systems in order to promote social and economic transformation in Colombia. To achieve this objective, the policy is structured around six strategic axes: (i) Ethics and Governance: strengthen governance mechanisms and apply ethical principles related to AI systems, to ensure responsible development and use; (ii) Data and Infrastructure: strengthen the infrastructure technology, as well as the availability, exchange and representativeness of data, fundamental for AI; (iii) Research, Development and Innovation (R&D&I): boost research, development and innovation in AI systems in a way that is reflected in knowledge productivity, and benefits for the country; (iv) Capacity Development and Digital Talent: develop the capabilities and digital talent necessary for the design, use and adoption of AI, in addition to promoting the social appropriation of knowledge of this technology; (v) Risk Mitigation: define measures that promote the identification, prevention and mitigation of risks and undesired effects related to AI systems; and (vi) Use and Adoption of AI: Promote the use and adoption of AI systems in public entities, the business fabric and the territories; (vii) Use and Adoption of AI: promote the use and adoption of AI systems in public entities, the business fabric and the territories.

title: Collection of Knowledge and Development of a Guideline on Green AI
description: Green AI is a highly relevant topic and greater attention should be paid to green AI when discussing the requirements for AI applications. In view of the ever-larger language models and their roll-out to universally accessible applications (e.g., integration into search engines) as well as their spread to even more computationally intensive modalities (e.g., generation of video content), it is to be expected that the energy needs for training and inferencing AI systems will increase sharply, and that we are currently only at the beginning of this development.There is already an understanding of how AI applications can be made more sustainable (renewable energy, less computationally intensive algorithms, new architectures such as edge AI or spiking neural networks), but many research questions are still open and to date remain underappreciated among the target group of AI developers and policy makers.The aim of this R&D service is therefore to systematically record the current state of research on sustainable AI systems and applications for specific target groups. This know-how will be used to draw up a guideline for implementing sustainable AI applications. This guideline will be made available to all projects of FFG calls relevant to AI, and to the ministries responsible for AI applications.Objectives and impact:- Answering or identifying open research questions in relation to the sustainability to the sustainability of AI- Dissemination of knowledge on how AI can be designed and used sustainably and, as a result, reducing the consumption of resources and emissions through AI systems

title: AI Monitor
description: Despite a wealth of data available on developments related to AI, this information is often not accessible in a centralised manner, thus hindering evidence-based discussion about developments related to AI. The AI Monitor seeks to address this issue by collecting and presenting quantitative data from a variety of sources, mainly publiclyavailable, and by supplementing this dashboard with information about existing initiatives which provide some form of support for actors in the Austrian AI ecosystem. In addition, qualitative assessments of the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum on the opportunities and challenges related to AI will help tomonitor these developments from multiple perspectives.The Austrian AI Monitor will be hosted on digitalaustria.gv.at and will be published in 2025 with annual updates.The AI Monitor will be able to integrate further initiatives and data points, allowing for a gradual expansion of itsscope.

title: Academic AI Services
description: The "Academic AI Services" project has three objectives:1. To create a safe environment for the testing, use and further development of (generative) AI technologies in the university context in order to allowteachers, researchers and students in the field of AI to benefit from the latest technologies. These technologies are to be made available taking into accountdata protection and information security (Academic AI).2. The provision of an open-source AI platform for the development of new AI models as well as access to the MUSICA platform for computationallyintensive tasks (e.g. training of models) (Experimental Services). But also know-how that helps with implementation on the MUSICA platform (e.g. hostingand operating training/inference/evaluation services, a comprehensive range of training courses, specific consulting). The process will be accompanied byextensive monitoring and regular audits to ensure that both the (sensitive) data, the research processes and the results are protected from unauthorized access.In order to facilitate international cooperation for researchers, it is to be ensured that the solutions developed are compatible with European developments.3. Resources to promote innovative AI projects at Universities. In these projects, universities are to work cooperatively to solve problems in teaching,research and administration with the help of AI methods. Typical projects could be chatbots, automation administration processes, preparation of lecturenotes, Student tutor, chatbots for lectures, automated creation of exam questions, automatic exam pre-correction, multilingual lecture content, furtherdevelopment in the field of learning analytics, etc

title: AI-specific programmes
description: Slovakia is responding to the growing global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) expertise by expanding its higher education offerings in this field. The increasing importance of AI across industries has created a clear need for well-trained professionals who can build, apply, and manage intelligent systems. In Slovakia, this demand is seen both in the technology sector and in areas such as healthcare, transportation, finance, and public administration. By offering more specialised academic programmes, the country is creating new opportunities for students to gain skills that are valuable in the job market while also helping to strengthen its digital economy. The main goal of this initiative is to give students structured, in-depth training in AI and related subjects like data science and intelligent systems. Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. They provide a pathway to careers in software development, machine learning, robotics, data analytics, and research, among others. Courses typically combine theoretical foundations with practical applications, helping students to understand not only how AI works, but also how to use it to solve real-world problems. According to AIpoint.SK, six universities in Slovakia collectively offer 22 AI‑specific degree programmes. These programmes cover undergraduate and graduate study in AI, data science, intelligent systems, and related areas, and are available at leading institutions such as the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Technical University of Košice, Comenius University, University of Žilina, Pavol Jozef Šafárik University, and Pan‑European University. The aim is to prepare a skilled workforce in AI and advanced data technologies aligned with industry demand and educational advancement across the country. The development of these programmes reflects cooperation between universities, government agencies, and private sector stakeholders. It also shows a clear national commitment to preparing the next generation of digital professionals. Looking forward, the initiative may grow by adding more advanced courses, increasing partnerships with tech companies, or offering new specialisations based on industry trends. As AI continues to evolve, Slovakia’s universities are positioning themselves to train students who can lead in both domestic and international innovation landscapes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Sector – Interim Report of the Inter-Agency Task Force on the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Israel's Financial Sector
description: Israel’s artificial intelligence initiative in the financial sector is a forward-looking effort to harness the potential of AI while ensuring responsible and fair use. The initiative responds to the growing interest in AI applications across banking, insurance, credit, and investment services, where the technology offers opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce operational costs, enhance access to financial services, and promote innovation. At the same time, it addresses significant risks, including algorithmic bias, lack of transparency (the “black box” problem), privacy concerns, cyber threats, and the potential for market concentration or financial instability. These challenges demand a careful and tailored approach to regulation that neither stifles innovation nor compromises consumer protection or market integrity. The key objectives of the initiative are to promote safe AI integration in financial services, ensure consumer rights and data privacy, and maintain public trust in digital finance. Led by an inter-agency task force of financial regulators, the initiative encourages a flexible, risk-based regulatory framework that adapts to the level of risk posed by specific AI applications. It emphasizes technological neutrality, proportional regulation, and alignment with global standards while advancing innovation through mechanisms like regulatory sandboxes, innovation hubs, and improved access to anonymized data. Consumer-facing protections—such as explainability of AI decisions, human oversight in critical processes, and clear disclosures about AI use—are prioritized to safeguard fairness and accountability. The initiative is expected to evolve through continued public consultation, refinement of regulatory principles, and the gradual development of sector-specific rules. While Israel does not currently adopt a single, sweeping AI law, the initiative encourages updates to existing financial regulations and policies to accommodate AI-driven services. Institutionalization will occur through regulator-issued guidelines, inter-agency coordination, and the integration of AI governance and risk management practices across financial institutions. Efforts to monitor systemic risks, such as over-reliance on third-party AI providers or disinformation threats, are also part of the long-term implementation plan. The initiative aims to scale through broader adoption of AI tools, supported by clear, consistent oversight and continuous evaluation. Since its inception, the initiative has moved from conceptual discussion to structured planning, producing two key policy documents that assess both current challenges and future needs. These reports reflect the government’s commitment to balancing technological progress with social responsibility. As AI adoption increases, the initiative’s principles and tools will be revisited and updated to ensure a competitive, inclusive, and resilient financial sector.

title: Establishment of a Moonshot AI Applied Research Consortium
description: The term Moonshot project refers to broad research efforts, at the forefront of global knowledge, which require collaboration by several different research teams. Projects may differ in nature on the range between basic and applied research, but all will have a relatively broad scope of research activity and a high rate of uncertainty about whether the challenge can be solved, or the research question answered (high risk – high gain). Such research characteristics ensure that even in case of “failure” to solve the challenge, the generated intellectual property is expected to be substantial, positioning the researchers involved at the vanguard of global research. Moreover, groundbreaking, and broad-scope research projects are expected to help draw leading global researchers, and to establish Israel’s research reserve. Various projects are to be launched by different entities that take part in the program, in accordance with the research question. Projects pertaining to the foundations of AI technology will be launched by the Planning and Budgeting Committee, projects that are more applicative will be launched by the Innovation Authority, and projects pertaining to the dual needs of the defense system will be led by the Directorate of Defense Research & Development. Each such project is expected to span several research teams from different disciplines and institutions, working together for a period of two to three years. Subjects for challenge projects will be chosen by a combination of open calls for proposals (bottom-up approach), and general guidance towards broad and relevant spheres of interest (top-down approach). The research activity’s operational mechanism will be derived from the leading entity’s toolbox. Chosen projects may include a variety of research fields, combining software, hardware, robotics including humanoid robotics, and others.

title: Increasing the number of AI experts from overseas in Israeli industry (returning residents, new immigrants, foreign experts)
description: Considering the talent shortage in AI, countries worldwide are competing for experts. As part of a call for proposals completed in 2024, the Innovation Authority chose 3 entities to locate and bring to Israel foreign AI researchers with a relevant academic education from well-known institutions and relevant work experience overseas, who wish to work in Israeli high-tech companies as AI researchers and lead their development teams. Target audiences include immigrants who are entitled to settle in Israel, Israelis who emigrated overseas and wish to return to Israel, as well as foreign experts who wish to relocate. The chosen entities will also be responsible for the AI experts’ placement and assimilation in Israel. The purpose of government support in this case is to reduce the financial risk associated with establishing an international identification, recruitment, and selection apparatus. The ultimate goal is to allow the chosen entities, after an initial time-limited governmental support, to continue and expand their effort to attract foreign talent organically, without the need for continuous governmental intervention.

title: AI Competence Center
description: The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Slovenia is preparing to launch a Competence Center for Artificial Intelligence , designed as a cornerstone of the country’s National Programme for Artificial Intelligence (NpAI) . Its purpose is to strengthen Slovenia’s position in AI development, adoption, and integration across both public and private sectors. The Competence Center will pursue several objectives: Advance AI research and expertise by supporting collaboration between academia, industry, and government. Foster innovation and encourage the development of AI-based products and services. Support SMEs through training, consulting, and test-before-invest opportunities, acting as a one-stop-shop for AI adoption. Promote economic growth by facilitating the integration of AI into industry, public services, and administration. The Center will be implemented through a consortium model , ensuring broad participation from key stakeholders. A public call was launched in December 2024 to select consortium members, expected to include universities, research institutions, private sector companies, and government actors. Looking forward, the Competence Center is set to become a national focal point for AI , aligning Slovenia’s research and innovation activities with broader European initiatives. By providing infrastructure, expertise, and support services, it is expected to: Enhance Slovenia’s competitiveness in the global digital economy, Stimulate the development of AI talent and skills, Drive cross-sectoral applications of AI in areas such as healthcare, manufacturing, smart cities, and public administration.

title: AI Innovative Lab
description: The AI Innovative Lab was established to strengthen research and development in artificial intelligence by creating a critical mass of expertise and skills . Its mission is to support high-performance applications across a wide range of AI subfields while fostering both fundamental and applied research. The lab’s work spans several priority areas : Bioinformatics and computational biology. Artificial vision and computer vision applications. Text analysis and natural language processing (NLP) . Deep learning methods driving recent breakthroughs in AI. In addition, the lab conducts research in key theoretical and applied AI domains, including: Inductive Logic Programming (ILP) . Data mining and large-scale knowledge discovery. Knowledge representation techniques. Constraint logic programming , including constraint handling rules. Automatic reasoning and inference systems. Semantic web technologies . Intelligent information integration . Expert systems and knowledge-based systems . The overarching goal of the AI Innovative Lab is to bridge theoretical advances and practical applications . By cultivating specialised expertise and addressing real-world challenges, it contributes to the development of intelligent systems that can be applied in diverse fields such as healthcare, engineering, and information systems. Looking forward, the lab aims to expand its research collaborations, strengthen interdisciplinary projects, and position itself as a centre of excellence for AI innovation. Through talent development, cutting-edge projects, and knowledge transfer, it supports both national and international efforts to advance the frontiers of artificial intelligence.

title: Romanian AI Innovation Hub for AI (HRIA)
description: The Romanian Hub of Artificial Intelligence (HRIA) is a strategic initiative designed to ensure a broad and long-lasting impact of AI across Romania’s economy and society. Recognised as a national priority, it seeks to accelerate the adoption of AI while building a competitive and collaborative research environment. HRIA is implemented as a consortium of 7 universities and 8 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) , combining academic expertise with industrial innovation capacity. The general objectives of HRIA are to: Strengthen the national AI research ecosystem by uniting academic and business efforts. Stimulate original scientific creation and innovation in AI. Transfer research results into industry and society, supporting new products and services. Build a national knowledge base that is integrated into the European Research Area . The project runs from March 1, 2025, to December 31, 2029 , during which time it will address multiple research, development, and innovation priorities. These include: Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence Intelligent and Autonomous Systems Smart Human-Computer Interfaces Hardware Technologies for AI AI in Medicine and Healthcare AI in Security and Space AI for Smart Cities AI for the Environment Development and Testing of AI Prototypes and Systems Looking ahead, HRIA is expected to serve as both a national nucleus for AI knowledge and innovation and a bridge to European initiatives . By fostering collaboration between academia and industry, it will enhance Romania’s capacity to develop cutting-edge technologies, generate economic value, and contribute to addressing global challenges through AI.

title: America's AI Action Plan
description: The Plan identifies over 90 Federal policy actions across three pillars – Accelerating Innovation, Building American AI Infrastructure, and Leading in International Diplomacy and Security – to be implemented by the Trump Administration. Key policies in the AI Action Plan include: Exporting American AI: The Commerce and State Departments will partner with industry to deliver secure, full-stack AI export packages – including hardware, models, software, applications, and standards – to America’s friends and allies around the world. Promoting Rapid Buildout of Data Centers: Expediting and modernizing permits for data centers and semiconductor fabs, as well as creating new national initiatives to increase high-demand occupations like electricians and HVAC technicians. Enabling Innovation and Adoption: Removing onerous Federal regulations that hinder AI development and deployment, and seek private sector input on rules to remove. Upholding Free Speech in Frontier Models: Updating Federal procurement guidelines to ensure that the government only contracts with frontier large language model developers who ensure that their systems are objective and free from top-down ideological bias.

title: Digital Skills Initiative
description: Austria has established a Digital Competencies Initiative (Digitale Kompetenzoffensive) as an intersectional cooperation between 4 federal ministries. The initiative focuses on the development and coordination of measures for digital literacy and skills. Under the umbrella of the initiative, the Digital Competencies and Skills strategy outlines how Austria is going to achieve more digital competencies among the citizens. Measures around AI are a major priority in the strategy. Accordingly, a specific strategy for AI literacy and skills is currently in development and has successfully kicked off with an expert event in the beginning of July 2024. Following the explicit goals and principles of the general national digital literacy and skills strategy and the national AI strategy, the AI literacy and skills strategy will focus on the inclusion of population groups with low levels of digital literacy, like the elderly and rural population, and gender diversity for AI skills, with the aim to broaden the national IT expert's pool. A number of AI workshops are already offered for free across the country as part of the general “Digital Everywhere”. AI will also be a major focus for the building-up programme “Digital Everywhere PLUS” with modular workshops, online learning, train-the-trainer concepts and other innovative teaching methods. Currently, an AI competences consultation with experts from the AI Board, the national interest groups, scientific experts in education, adult education experts and other important stakeholder groups is in progress. The results will inform the further development of the programme and flow into a white paper on AI competences as a backbone of the programme. In parallel, a scientific working group for the definition of a basic curriculum on AI has kicked off to make sure that AI courses are meeting the criteria of critical AI literacy of the population.

title: Creation of a hybrid cloud to combine registers such as AJPES register
description: Slovenia plans a hybrid cloud to make it easier for businesses to deal with the state. Today, key company data live in separate registers (e.g., AJPES, the Financial Administration, and court registers), which means firms often must repeat filings and slows administrative processes. The project addresses this fragmentation by enabling secure, unified access to those records. The main objectives are to simplify procedures for businesses interacting with the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, reduce paperwork, and improve data quality and consistency. By linking existing registers through a common cloud layer, authorities can retrieve verified information once and reuse it where legally permitted.

description: Towards the Food Factory of the Future is a roadmap by Flanders’ FOOD to modernize the agri-food sector in Flanders. The initiative targets four areas: better quality control through sensors and data, digital automation, circular use of resources, and workforce skills. Through projects and partnerships, it aims to especially help SMEs test and adopt tools like AI, machine learning, and energy-efficient systems.

title: AI for Policymaking
description: The Slovak government is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to strengthen data-driven policymaking. Public bodies hold large amounts of information, but turning this into timely insights is difficult. AI offers tools to analyse datasets more quickly, identify trends, and predict outcomes, supporting more evidence-based and effective governance. The aim is to move policymaking from reactive to proactive. Applications include labour-market analysis, health forecasting, or infrastructure planning. By modelling likely impacts, AI can help policymakers anticipate challenges and make better use of public resources. These efforts are guided by Slovakia’s national AI strategy and supported through partnerships with researchers and technology providers.

title: AEXCIA Platform
description: The AEXCIA platform is being developed to help regulators manage the growing number of consumer complaints and requests, which are often too complex and numerous for traditional systems to handle efficiently. Citizens increasingly use digital channels and social media to voice concerns, and this creates both opportunities to better understand public sentiment and challenges in processing large volumes of data. AEXCIA’s main goal is to strengthen consumer protection by automating the intake and processing of complaints while also analysing patterns in consumer behaviour. Portugal’s communications regulator (ANACOM) will use it to support supervisory work, improve oversight of service providers, and design policies that better reflect consumer needs. By reducing manual work and providing actionable insights, the tool aims to increase both efficiency and transparency.

title: National Data Strategy
description: The National Data Strategy is a key component of Portugal’s digital transformation agenda. It envisions a governance model designed to foster a collaborative and dynamic ecosystem that promotes data altruism and creates synergies among stakeholders. The strategy focuses on three main pillars: Ethical and efficient data management: Establishing robust guidelines for the ethical and efficient management of data, ensuring reliability and security throughout its lifecycle. Stakeholder collaboration: Fostering effective collaboration between stakeholders to facilitate data and resource sharing in ways that drive innovation and value creation. Continuous monitoring and impact assessment: Implementing continuous monitoring of data initiatives, using models to assess the impact of these actions on society and the economy. The strategy aims to create a data-driven economy, enhancing public sector efficiency, fostering innovation, and improving citizens' quality of life. By promoting data altruism, it encourages the sharing of data for public good, ensuring that data is used responsibly and ethically.

title: IPA AI Training Programmes
description: The Institute of Public Administration (IPA) in Bulgaria runs a comprehensive AI training initiative designed for civil servants. The program addresses the growing need for practical knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence applications within public administration and human resource management, helping to modernize governmental operations and decision-making. The primary objective of the IPA AI Training Programmes is to equip public sector professionals with practical expertise in applying AI tools to real-world administrative tasks. The program emphasizes hands-on learning, enabling participants to understand, implement, and manage AI-based solutions that improve efficiency, enhance service delivery, and support data-driven decision-making. The initiative is delivered through multiple learning formats, including self-paced e-learning modules, face-to-face training sessions, and interactive workshops. Participants explore AI use cases relevant to their work, such as automating routine administrative processes, enhancing HR management, and supporting policy analysis. The program combines theoretical foundations with practical exercises, fostering applied skills that can be directly utilized in government operations.

title: Swedish participation in LUMI hosted by CSC in Finland
description: Sweden participates in the LUMI supercomputing infrastructure, hosted by CSC in Finland, to provide researchers with access to one of Europe’s most powerful high-performance computing (HPC) systems. LUMI, the fastest supercomputer in Europe, is part of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which aims to strengthen European HPC capabilities and advance research and innovation across the continent. The initiative addresses the growing demand for computational resources for data-intensive scientific research, including artificial intelligence, climate modeling, genomics, and materials science. By leveraging LUMI, Swedish researchers gain access to cutting-edge computational power, enabling complex simulations, AI model training, and advanced analytics that would not be feasible on national infrastructure alone. Sweden’s participation is coordinated through the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS), which facilitates access for universities, research institutes, and other partners. Researchers can submit proposals to use LUMI for collaborative projects, ensuring that the system supports a wide range of scientific and technological applications.

title: Programme for AI Literacy and Skills
description: The Programme for AI Literacy and Skills in Austria is a national initiative aimed at improving AI understanding and digital competence among citizens. The programme has officially kicked off in July 2024 with an expert event and is aligned with Austria’s broader national digital literacy and skills strategy and the national AI strategy. Key objectives include: Promoting AI literacy among population groups with lower digital skills, including the elderly and people in rural areas Enhancing gender diversity in AI and technology-related skills Broadening the national pool of IT and AI experts to meet future labour market needs The programme will adopt inclusive approaches and targeted educational measures to reach underrepresented groups and ensure equitable access to AI education. It also aims to strengthen Austria’s overall digital competence, supporting the country’s innovation and competitiveness in AI-related fields.

description: The Swiss–Latvian Cooperation Programme – Pre-defined Programme Component in ICT and Smart Energy (2025–2029) aims to advance research and innovation in sustainable energy technologies. The programme focuses on improving the efficiency and stability of the Baltic electricity grid while supporting the development of advanced energy storage and hydrogen production materials. By combining expertise from academia and research organisations, the programme seeks to create practical, deployable solutions for the region’s energy sector.

title: Development and construction of a supercomputer
description: The supercomputer project in Slovakia, led by the Slovak Academy of Sciences in collaboration with Eviden and the Atos Group, addresses the growing need for high-performance computing (HPC) in research and public administration. Many scientific, administrative, and industrial tasks require computing power that exceeds what standard systems can provide, and this project seeks to fill that gap. The main objective is to develop and operate a national HPC infrastructure that is publicly accessible. This system is designed to support advanced simulations, data analysis, and modeling for a wide range of users, including universities, research institutes, public institutions, and private R&D organizations. The project involves constructing the physical supercomputing facility, installing hardware and software systems, and integrating it into the national HPC network. The Slovak Academy of Sciences provides scientific oversight, Eviden and the Atos Group contribute technical expertise in design, implementation, and operations, and various end-users from academia, government, and industry access the system for computational needs.

Many scientific, administrative, and industrial tasks require computing power that exceeds what standard systems can provide, and this project seeks to fill that gap. The main objective is to develop and operate a national HPC infrastructure that is publicly accessible. This system is designed to support advanced simulations, data analysis, and modeling for a wide range of users, including universities, research institutes, public institutions, and private R&D organizations. The project involves constructing the physical supercomputing facility, installing hardware and software systems, and integrating it into the national HPC network. The Slovak Academy of Sciences provides scientific oversight, Eviden and the Atos Group contribute technical expertise in design, implementation, and operations, and various end-users from academia, government, and industry access the system for computational needs

title: PRODIGIT project
description: The PRODIGIT project is a collaborative initiative between the Presidential Council of Tax Justice (Consiglio di Presidenza della Giustizia Tributaria, CPGT) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), aimed at modernising judicial tax proceedings through the use of artificial intelligence (AI). The project addresses key challenges in tax-related legal processes, including lengthy case handling, administrative complexity, and the need for more accurate decision-making. PRODIGIT focuses on enhancing efficiency and accuracy in judicial procedures by integrating AI-powered tools into the workflow of tax judges. The initiative employs techniques such as legal summarisation, information extraction, and data-driven analysis to assist judges in processing cases, identifying relevant information, and making informed decisions more quickly. This approach reduces the administrative burden on judicial staff while maintaining the quality and reliability of legal outcomes. The project involves close collaboration between judicial authorities, public administration, and AI experts, ensuring that technological solutions are tailored to the legal context and practical needs of the tax justice system. By embedding AI into judicial processes, PRODIGIT demonstrates the potential of AI to support public sector transformation in specialised legal domains.

title: The First Regional Forum on the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence
description: The First Regional AI Forum, held in Odesa, was launched to address the growing need for responsible and effective adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) at the local level in Ukraine. The initiative responds to the increasing relevance of AI in public administration and education, and the necessity to ensure that AI technologies are introduced in a way that respects human rights, promotes trust, and supports inclusive digital transformation. Organised by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, the forum brought together over 150 educators, public servants, digital transformation officers, and community leaders. Objectives: It served as a regional platform to present national and international frameworks on ethical AI use and offered practical tools for implementing AI in schools and public institutions. A key feature was the presentation of recommendations on AI use in education and civil service, including the Council of Europe’s HUDERIA methodology for assessing AI’s impact on human rights and democracy. Impact: This forum marked the beginning of a broader effort to institutionalise AI education and awareness at the regional level in Ukraine. Future plans include expanding the CDTO Campus AI programmes, scaling the HUDERIA methodology to more regions, and replicating the forum format in other parts of the country. The initiative helps build a foundation for informed and ethical AI transformation, with direct benefits for public administration, education, and local communities."

title: Big Course on Artificial Intelligence in Education
description: The “Big Course on Artificial Intelligence in Education” is a professional training programme designed for university lecturers in Ukraine. Organised by the NGO Progresylni with the support of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine and the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, the course builds upon the Recommendations on Responsible AI Use in Higher Education developed by the Expert Advisory Committee on AI at the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. Objectives: The programme addresses key topics related to integrating AI into teaching and learning processes. These include new pedagogical approaches, academic integrity, assessment practices, personalisation of learning, and the legal and ethical dimensions of AI use in education. Methodology: The course is delivered online and combines lectures, public discussions, and practical workshops, with participation from leading Ukrainian and international experts. Upon successful completion and passing of the final test, participants receive a certificate of professional development. The course aims to foster responsible AI use in higher education and to enhance educators’ capacity to adapt to the digital transformation of learning environments. This initiative contributes to the professional growth of Ukrainian educators, strengthens the culture of responsible AI integration in higher education, and aligns national practices with international standards of AI use in education.

title: AI Centre of Excellence under the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
description: The AI Centre of Excellence was launched in 2025 by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine as the first national institution dedicated to accelerating the development and integration of AI across public governance, defence, education, business, and healthcare. The Centre was created as part of Ukraine’s WINWIN innovation strategy 2030 and aims to enhance the country’s global competitiveness by transforming the state, economy, and society through responsible AI adoption. Key objectives: Brings together experts, infrastructure, and innovation capacity to address national priorities through applied AI solutions. Its primary focus is the development of national LLM and AI tools for the government and defence sectors. It also supports the implementation of AI in education, scientific research, and healthcare, while fostering the growth of start-ups and small and medium enterprises. Results: In its first year, the Centre launched an AI incubator and initiated the development of a pipeline for piloting AI products in the public sector. Work began on 16 AI prototypes, with several expected to advance to MVP stage and transition into full-scale products. These efforts aim to test practical applications of AI and build implementation capacity across public services. Impact: A strategic goal of the Centre is to lay the technological foundation for Ukraine’s AI sovereignty. It has begun developing national infrastructure for AI deployment and is working on the development of a national large language model (LLM) tailored for public service use. The Centre is also shaping a technological strategy focused on scaling and integrating AI into major digital platforms, such as Diia (Ukraine’s mobile app for e-governance services), Mriia (a national digital education platform), and AI Legal (a planned tool for automating legal support in the public sector), as well as AI for EU integration and acquis alignment. While specific defence applications remain confidential, the Centre is expected to contribute to the development of AI-enabled solutions in the security sector."

title: AI training courses
description: In 2022, the Maltese government signed a Memorandum of Understanding involving the Institute for the Public Service, University of Malta, MCAST, eSkills Malta Foundation, and the Office of the Prime Minister. This agreement covers three years of AI training for public officers. The aim of the training is to raise the capacity of public servants to apply Artificial Intelligence in government operations and internal processes. The training is expected to include courses at various levels, scholarships for those wishing to specialise, and collaboration with international institutions (e.g. drawing on material from Helsinki University). While there is public documentation of these plans, the precise structure of an “Introduction to AI” module—covering machine learning, applications, and fundamentals—has not been fully detailed in the sources reviewed. Some content is clearly about foundational AI knowledge, but without full breakdowns in all cases.

title: AI in tax administration
description: The Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Inland Revenue Authority) has implemented advanced AI and analytics software to strengthen tax administration and improve compliance monitoring. This initiative addresses the challenge of detecting tax avoidance and fraud within a large and complex national tax system, where manual monitoring is time-consuming and prone to gaps. The system integrates data from the Tax Registry and the Archive of Financial Relations, enabling sophisticated analysis to identify potential irregularities, anomalies, and high-risk cases. By leveraging AI algorithms, the authority can prioritise investigations, allocate resources more efficiently, and focus on cases with the highest potential impact on revenue protection.

title: EuroQCS-Poland
description: EuroQCS-Poland is a European initiative to install a quantum computer in Poland, hosted at the Poznan Supercomputing and Networking Center. The system, called PIAST-Q, is based on trapped-ion technology and offers over 20 physical qubits. It is designed to support research and innovation across science, industry, and public sectors, and will be integrated with classical supercomputing infrastructure to enable hybrid computing approaches. The project is part of a broader European effort to advance quantum technologies and is co-funded by the EU and Poland’s Ministry of Digital Affairs.

title: AI Guidelines
description: Germany has developed the KI-Leitlinien (AI Guidelines) to ensure a harmonised and responsible approach to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across federal public administration. This initiative addresses the need for a consistent framework that guides government institutions in deploying AI systems ethically, transparently, and effectively, while maintaining public trust and accountability. The primary objective of the KI-Leitlinien is to promote a value-based approach to AI adoption. title: Levente HPC
description: The Levente project is Hungary’s plan to build a powerful supercomputer with a capacity of 20 PetaFlops to boost its computing power for research and AI projects. This is important because many scientific and industrial tasks now require large amounts of computing resources, which Hungary’s current systems cannot fully support. The main goal of Levente is to provide advanced computing to universities, research centers, and industries, helping them run complex simulations and AI models more efficiently. This will support innovation in areas like healthcare, manufacturing, and technology development. Supported by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU), the project involves government bodies, academic institutions, and industry partners working together to build and operate the supercomputer. However, the project has faced delays due to economic challenges linked to the COVID-19 pandemic and geopolitical issues. Once operational, Levente will significantly improve Hungary’s ability to handle demanding research and industrial tasks. In the future, it could expand and connect with Europe’s wider supercomputing network, strengthening Hungary’s role in international research and innovation.

title: Knowledge centre for municipalities
description: Local Government Denmark (KL), the association representing Danish municipalities, has established a Digitalisation Centre to strengthen local governments’ capacity to use digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI). The centre addresses the growing need for municipalities to adapt to rapid technological change while ensuring that digital transformation creates tangible value for citizens, improves public services, and supports sustainable local development. The centre’s main objectives are to collect and share knowledge on digitalisation, support municipalities in experimenting with and adopting new technologies, and identify emerging challenges related to digital governance and innovation. It provides municipalities with practical, action-oriented guidance on key areas such as data security, IT procurement, framework architecture, and ethical AI use. By acting as a central hub of expertise, the centre helps ensure that digital solutions are implemented effectively and responsibly across Denmark’s municipalities. In addition to its advisory and coordination role, KL has launched an AI School designed for managers, executives, and elected officials. This programme aims to build understanding and leadership capacity around AI, enabling decision-makers to recognise opportunities, manage risks, and strategically integrate AI into municipal operations and services.

title: Innovative reception of the Emergency Call Center
description: The Czech Republic is undertaking a comprehensive modernisation of its Emergency Call Center system by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve its efficiency, functionality, and responsiveness. This initiative addresses the growing need for faster, more coordinated emergency responses in an era of increasing data complexity and demand for real-time decision-making. The project’s primary goal is to establish a unified, modern environment that seamlessly connects all components of the country’s integrated rescue system. This includes the development of an updated dispatcher interface, application layer, and central database—all designed to work together in a cohesive, interoperable framework. By ensuring full integration, the new system will enhance communication between emergency operators, police, fire, and medical services, enabling faster and more accurate responses to emergencies. AI plays a central role in this transformation. Advanced analytics and machine learning tools will be employed to optimise workflows, forecast resource needs, and set capacity parameters across the emergency network. These capabilities will not only improve operational performance but also help identify patterns and areas for efficiency gains, contributing to better public safety outcomes.

title: Robotics and Life
description: The subject “Robotica și viața (Robotics and Life)” is an optional subject in Romanian gymnasium (grades 6–7) offered one hour per week. It is designed as an interdisciplinary course, integrating content and skills from Mathematics, Physics, Informatics and ICT to build a broader STEM foundation. Its objectives include: Forming transdisciplinary / multidisciplinary skills in students so they can link concepts across subject areas. Encouraging technical creativity, for example by designing and building robot models and developing control algorithms. Developing algorithmic thinking, modelling, and an understanding of virtual simulations, where physical robotics kits are not available. The curriculum is competency-centered, referencing the gymnasium graduate profile, Romania’s Digital Agenda strategy, and uses existing school resources where possible (ICT labs, internet, simulators). If kits are available, physical robot-building is included, but simulations ensure the subject can be delivered in schools without extra costly resources.
