title: Frontier AI Initiative
description: The Frontier AI Initiative was introduced by the European Commission as part of the EU’s broader “Apply AI Strategy” and AI Continent policy framework. Its objective is to strengthen Europe’s capabilities in developing and governing frontier-level AI systems. Activities include convening expert forums, coordinating research investments, aligning safety and evaluation approaches, and linking existing European high-performance computing facilities with emerging AI development ecosystems. The initiative also aims to reduce Europe’s reliance on foreign frontier models by supporting domestic research capacity and enabling collaboration between public laboratories, startups and established technology companies. In addition, the programme promotes responsible development by embedding safety testing, benchmarking and governance mechanisms into the development pipeline for advanced models. The Frontier AI Initiative therefore acts as both a coordination mechanism and an enabling platform for European investment in advanced AI capabilities.

title: The Interministerial AI Assistant
description: The AI Assistant is a secure, government-wide chat tool designed for public servants. It helps users draft and improve text, summarize long documents, and answer day-to-day questions more quickly, while keeping a clear focus on safe and responsible use in a public administration context. The initiative was developed to address a growing need across ministries: many teams were exploring generative AI, but often with separate tools and duplicated technical efforts. By providing a shared assistant, the government aims to make AI easier to access for public servants, reduce fragmentation, and support productivity gains in routine tasks. In 2025, the AI Assistant was piloted across 8 ministries with up to 10,000 volunteer users. It helped public servants draft, summarize and search information faster, supporting everyday work and reducing the need for separate ministry-by-ministry tools. Impact has been tracked through user adoption (registrations and active use), usage statistics (queries, features used), and qualitative feedback from pilot administrations. Future results are expected to include wider adoption, more time saved on routine tasks, and improved consistency and security in how generative AI is used across government. Key challenges included ensuring strong security and compliance for government use, scaling computing capacity cost-effectively, and building trust among users. Another risk was fragmentation, with ministries developing separate assistants and duplicating effort. These challenges were addressed by hosting the service on secure infrastructure, monitoring usage to manage costs, and designing the Assistant as a shared tool that can evolve with ministry needs. Lessons learned include the importance of starting with clear, high-value everyday tasks (writing, summarising), providing user guidance and support, and collecting feedback early to improve the service. Success depends on reliable performance, strong governance, and gradual scaling based on real adoption. Over time, the AI Assistant is expected to expand its user base and offer more advanced features, including stronger connections to trusted public information sources and the ability to work with internal document collections. It is designed to scale progressively, in line with security requirements and real usage needs, while remaining interoperable with other government digital tools.

title: AI verkstaden - AI node for public administration
description: AI‑verkstaden is a national initiative designed to help Sweden’s public sector adopt artificial intelligence safely, efficiently and at scale. It responds to long‑standing challenges across agencies, regions and municipalities, including fragmented digital infrastructure, uneven AI competence, inconsistent data quality, legal uncertainty and unequal access to technical resources. Many smaller public organisations in particular lack the environments, support and guidance needed to use AI responsibly. Against this backdrop, AI‑verkstaden leverages rapid technological progress and Sweden’s growing need for digital sovereignty, secure data management and a coordinated approach to technology adoption. The initiative’s core objective is to provide a shared, secure national infrastructure where public actors can experiment with, develop and deploy AI solutions. This includes lab, development and production environments; a catalogue of quality‑assured AI services; and structured support that ranges from self‑service resources to expert legal, technical and change‑management advice. By enabling public actors to share models, align standards and coordinate legal and technical assessments, AI‑verkstaden reduces redundant work and promotes more coherent, efficient and trustworthy AI use across the public sector. Its broader aim is to raise AI maturity, improve service quality and strengthen Sweden’s digital resilience and civil preparedness. AI‑verkstaden is being established over multiple years (2026–2030), gradually expanding its service catalogue, infrastructure and user base. It will move from pilots and foundational support functions toward full operational capacity using a hybrid model that combines a state‑controlled “community cloud” with approved private‑sector resources. Over time, it will be institutionalised through stable governance shared between the two government agencies responsible for its oversight. Its flexible architecture ensures it can adapt to evolving technologies, regulatory requirements and user needs. Early experimentation has already demonstrated value. A pilot with the Mörbylånga municipality tested an AI service for masking personal data, showing that local actors can securely access and use AI within a governed environment. The pilot validated technical, legal and contractual processes and highlighted user support needs, helping refine requirements for future scaling. Early user feedback confirmed that the service lowered adoption barriers. These results were assessed through real‑world testing in operational settings.

title: EU Apply AI Strategy
description: The Apply AI Strategy represents the European Commission's most targeted effort to move the EU from AI development to AI deployment, with a particular emphasis on ensuring that SMEs and public sector organisations can benefit from AI. The Strategy identifies 11 priority sectors for AI integration, including healthcare, manufacturing, mobility, agriculture, energy, and public administration, and promotes an 'AI-first' organisational culture in which decision-makers are expected to consider AI as a default option when designing services and operational processes. For SMEs specifically, the Strategy connects with a broad support infrastructure: the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) network, which provides test-before-invest facilities, digital maturity assessments, and access to expertise; the InvestAI initiative (EUR 200 billion total target investment); the Digital Europe Programme (EUR 1.3 billion allocated for AI and digital skills, 2025–2027); and the AI Factories network, which gives SMEs access to high-performance computing resources. The Strategy is coordinated through the Apply AI Alliance, a multi-stakeholder forum bringing together AI providers, industry associations, academia, social partners, and civil society. France, Germany, and Italy, as G7 members, are key implementers of the Strategy, and each has developed national-level measures aligned with it.

title: Public Sector AI Community of Practice
description: The Public Sector AI Community of Practice is a centrally led professional network that connects digital practitioners across New Zealand’s wider public sector. In its first full year, membership expanded from 60 to 95 agencies nationwide, with more than 600 practitioners engaged overall. Around 200 practitioners typically join each monthly online session, and the community delivered more than a dozen sessions over the year. Its purpose is to provide a shared space where agencies can learn from one another, explore emerging technologies and strengthen capability across government. As part of the Government Chief Digital Officer’s AI Work Programme, the community’s agenda is shaped by members’ interests and feedback, ensuring sessions remain timely and relevant. Each monthly gathering is built around the themes of share, learn and connect, combining formal presentations, knowledge‑sharing updates and structured discussions. Agencies routinely present updates on their AI programmes and initiatives, offering insights into practical implementation, lessons learned and developing responsible AI practices. Deep‑dive sessions explore technical topics or emerging developments, often led by subject‑matter experts such as data platform managers and scientists who share specialist knowledge or support training. Sessions examine active AI use cases and pilots, provide visibility into early exploratory projects and highlight shifts in technology or the operating environment that affect government AI adoption. Sub‑communities have begun to form around shared areas of practice, including a growing Policy Professionals group led by practitioners in the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.

title: AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure 3.0 (ABCI 3.0)
description: ABCI 3.0 represents Japan's strategic response to growing global AI competition and the need for sovereign AI capabilities. As the third generation of ABCI infrastructure—first launched in August 2018—the system became fully operational in January 2025, providing unprecedented computing resources for AI development within Japan. In June 2025, ABCI 3.0 officially proved its status as Japan’s premier AI supercomputer by ranking 4th globally and 1st in Japan on the HPL-MxP benchmark, which measures mixed-precision AI computing performance. It also secured 15th place in the world (2nd in Japan) on the TOP500 list, reflecting its immense raw computational power. The initiative addresses Japan's critical need to reduce dependence on foreign AI technologies while developing foundation models with deep understanding of Japanese language and culture. Built by Hewlett Packard Enterprise using NVIDIA's H200 Tensor Core GPUs connected via Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking, the system delivers peak performance of 6.22 exaflops in half precision and 3.0 exaflops in single precision—representing a 7 to 13 times improvement over the previous ABCI 2.0 system. As of May 2025, more than 60 R&D projects involving foundation models, LLMs, and multimodal AI were already active under its "Accelerated Use" program. ABCI3.0 funded through METI's Economic Security Fund with an initial investment of ¥36 billion ($232 million). The infrastructure prioritizes resource allocation for public and strategic R&D purposes, particularly supporting national institutions, universities, and startups. ABCI 3.0's mission has evolved from providing general AI infrastructure to focusing on cutting-edge challenges in sovereign AI development and supporting the domestic AI startup ecosystem. The system provides relaxed usage limits compared to previous versions, including increased node allocations and extended reserved durations, enabling larger-scale foundation model development. Looking ahead, ABCI 3.0 is a cornerstone for advancing "Physical AI"—integrating real-world data like 3D point clouds and sound into multimodal foundation models—marking the next frontier in Japan's strategy to enhance industrial competitiveness through sovereign AI technology.

title: Italy AI Law 132/2025
description: Law No. 132 of 23 September 2025 (Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 224 of 25 September 2025), in force since 10 October 2025, makes Italy the first EU Member State to adopt a dedicated national AI framework aligned with the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689). Structured across six chapters and 28 articles, it establishes core principles—transparency, proportionality, security, data protection, accountability, gender equality, and non-discrimination—anchored in an anthropocentric approach preserving human oversight. It introduces sector-specific rules whereby AI may support but not replace decision-making in healthcare (with mandatory patient disclosure), justice, and regulated professions, while enabling its use in scientific research on anonymised data and requiring transparency toward workers, alongside the creation of a workplace AI Observatory. Governance assigns the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) as notifying authority and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as market surveillance authority, with financial regulators retaining sectoral oversight.

title: Virtual assistant in mObywatel
description: The Virtual Assistant is an attempt to help the citizen navigate the multitude of available public services ranging from reporting an environmental violations, to registering the birth of a child. Every year many services are introduced, changed, or retired, making it difficult for the citizen to keep track of them. The ability to ask questions in natural language makes the services more approachable, and by extension helps every citizen access everything the modern state has to offer. As a secondary objective, the initiative strives to build trusted public AI – both in the terms of the information provided by the Virtual Assistant, and by legally and technically enshrining the safety of the citizen data. The virtual assistant differs from the commercial offerings by the strict validation and verification of the knowledge sources and close integration with government databases. The answers it provides are limited to the official documentation – it is also designed not to give opinions or judgement-based advice. This ensures the assistant can be trusted to help citizens, while at the same time saving the budgetary cost of citizens asking general-knowledge questions. Furthermore, the assistant is embedded in mObywatel - the official Polish state application that lets people keep digital versions of important documents and use many public services safely on their mobiles. Therefore, if the user asks about a service or a document available in the app, the assistant can link directly to that service, ensuring seamless user experience. Finally, the Virtual Assistant is designed from the ground up to be privacy-preserving. It does not link the conversations to a user preventing any profiling. Every message goes through a multi-step process designed to purge any personally identifiable information. The LLM infrastructure is fully self-managed, to prevent external API providers from accessing the conversation data. The Virtual Assistant has been used 600 000 times in the two months from its introduction. The performance of the assistant is measured in real time, based on the user feedback (surveys after a conversation and the ability to up and downvote specific answers). Specific answers receive 62% positive votes and 38% negative, while the whole conversations have an equal split of 44% good or very good and 44% of bad or very bad. The specific rated conversations and messages are then assessed both manually and automatically by analytical and data science teams to guide the development of the system. Moreover, the project is assessed using social science frameworks, i.e: moderated workshops and unmoderated online forms.

title: Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity
description: The Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity programme is a demand-side subsidy instrument operated by the Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy (MIMIT). It provides vouchers to eligible SMEs and self-employed persons (lavoratori autonomi) to offset the cost of purchasing or subscribing to cloud computing and cybersecurity services from a register of prequalified suppliers. Eligible products explicitly include cloud SaaS solutions with integrated AI features meaning the programme directly lowers the financial barrier to SME adoption of AI-enabled software without requiring beneficiaries to procure AI separately. Supplier preregistration opened on 27 February 2026, establishing the pool of eligible vendors from which SMEs may choose; the SME application window ran from March to April 2026. The programme complements Italy's broader SME digitalisation strategy, including the national Competence Centers network and the Transition 5.0 incentive scheme.

text: Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity. The Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity programme is a demand-side subsidy instrument operated by the Ministero delle PLACE e del Made in PLACE (MIMIT). It provides vouchers to eligible SMEs and self-employed persons (lavoratori autonomi) to offset the cost of purchasing or subscribing to cloud computing and cybersecurity services from a register of prequalified suppliers. Eligible products explicitly include cloud SaaS solutions with integrated AI features meaning the programme directly lowers the financial barrier to SME adoption of AI-enabled software without requiring beneficiaries to procure AI separately. Supplier preregistration opened on 27 February 2026, establishing the pool of eligible vendors from which SMEs may choose; the SME application window ran from March to April 2026. The programme complements PLACE's broader SME digitalisation strategy, including the national Competence Centers network and the Transition 5.0 incentive scheme

title: Sectoral Workforce Solutions Program (AI-focused projects)
description: The AI stream of the Sectoral Workforce Solutions Program (SWSP) was announced in Canada's Budget 2024, allocating CAD 50M over four years (2025–26 to 2028–29) to support workers who may be impacted by AI through new skills training in potentially disrupted sectors and communities. The SWSP itself was originally established in Budget 2021 with CAD 960M over three years and has since invested over CAD 560M across 55 projects, supporting training for over 115,000 participants. The programme is administered by Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) and funds not-for-profit organisations, for-profit organisations, municipal governments, Indigenous organisations, and provincial/territorial bodies that have demonstrated knowledge of sectoral skills issues and established partnerships with national, regional, or local sectoral stakeholders. Projects must address workforce development needs in key sectors (agriculture/agri-food, construction, health, ICT, manufacturing, natural resources and environment, tourism, and transportation) and at minimum 10% co-funding from non-ESDC sources is required. The AI stream specifically targets workers facing job displacement or skills gaps due to AI adoption. Eligible activities include training and reskilling, attracting and retaining workforce, developing sector-wide standards and tools, and implementing creative workforce solutions. Funding per project ranges from CAD 5M to CAD 50M. Projects are national (spanning three+ provinces) or regional in scope.

title: MEB Smart Legislation Assistant  (AI-powered Legal Assistant)
description: The MEB Smart Legislation Assistant is an artificial intelligence–based decision support system developed by the Directorate General for Innovation and Educational Technologies to improve access to legislation within the Ministry of National Education. Ministry staff are required to consult thousands of pages of laws, regulations, circulars and guidelines in their daily work, which is time-consuming and prone to error. The initiative addresses this challenge by providing fast, reliable and transparent access to up-to-date legal information. The system allows authorised users to ask legal questions in natural language without requiring technical or legal expertise. Using advanced language models, the assistant searches official legislation sources and presents answers in a structured and understandable format. Each response is supported by direct references to the relevant legal provisions, enabling users to verify information through official sources such as mevzuat.gov.tr. Security and trust are central to the initiative. Access is restricted to authorised Ministry personnel and integrated with existing authentication infrastructure. The system operates only on verified and official legal texts and provides transparency by showing how answers are generated, including which legal documents and articles were used. The initiative is designed as a continuously evolving system. Through user feedback and performance analytics, the assistant is regularly improved to enhance accuracy, coverage and usability. In the future, the system is expected to expand its scope to include additional legal documents, institutional guidelines and internal regulatory content, contributing to a broader AI ecosystem within the Ministry.

title: AI for Growth
description: AI for Growth is a targeted federal funding programme announced under Canada's 2025 Budget and operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED). It is delivered through Canada's three National AI Institutes — Amii (Alberta), Mila (Québec), and the Vector Institute (Ontario) — as well as the Global Innovation Clusters network. The programme has three primary objectives: to increase AI adoption among Canadian SMEs by connecting them with advisory support, tools, and funding; to accelerate the commercialisation of Canadian-developed AI research by facilitating pathways from lab to market; and to strengthen business capacity to adopt domestically developed AI technologies, thereby reducing reliance on foreign platforms. SMEs are the primary target beneficiary, with support encompassing access to compute resources, AI readiness assessments, structured adoption pathways, and skills development. The programme is designed to build on Canada's existing innovation infrastructure rather than create new parallel institutions, leveraging the established expertise and networks of the National AI Institutes.

title: UK AI for Science Strategy
description: The AI for Science Strategy was published by the UK government to accelerate the integration of artificial intelligence into scientific discovery and innovation. The strategy seeks to position the United Kingdom as a global leader in AI-enabled research by investing in infrastructure, data resources and interdisciplinary collaborations. It focuses on enabling scientists to use advanced AI systems to analyse complex datasets, simulate natural phenomena and accelerate breakthroughs in fields such as life sciences, materials science, climate research and energy. The strategy promotes the creation of mission-driven research programmes where AI techniques are applied to large-scale scientific challenges, while also strengthening the computing infrastructure required to train and run advanced models. It encourages collaboration between universities, national laboratories, startups and established industry actors. In addition, the strategy emphasises responsible innovation, skills development and access to shared data resources.

title: TiNAI (Tamil Nadu Land Use Information System) (Subnational: Tamil Nadu State)
description: TiNAI (Tamil Nadu Land Use Information System) was developed to address a persistent research–policy disconnect in land-use governance. Although large volumes of spatial, environmental, and sectoral data existed across departments, they remained fragmented, limiting cross-sector interpretation and evidence-based planning. TiNAI responds to this challenge by integrating multi-sector datasets into a unified geospatial Digital Twin platform supported by artificial intelligence, enabling holistic analysis of land, climate, water, energy, agriculture, forests, disaster risks, and urban systems. The initiative aims to strengthen scientific decision-making by transforming complex spatial datasets into interpretable insights for policymakers. Through AI-assisted pattern analysis, KPI synthesis, and scenario exploration, the platform supports fiscal planning, resource optimisation, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience. TiNAI includes thematic modules such as Land Use and Land Cover (LULC), climate indicators (temperature trends, rainfall, heat stress), forest monitoring, renewable energy suitability (solar and wind potential), disaster risk (landslides, forest fires), coastal vulnerability, agriculture trends, water resource analytics, and urban growth dynamics. These modules are accessible through interactive maps, dashboards, and analytical tools that enable multi-dimensional assessment. Since its initial development as a land-use information system, TiNAI has evolved into an integrated AI-enabled spatial intelligence and Digital Twin architecture. The platform has progressively expanded its modules, analytical tools, and key performance indicators, while strengthening interdepartmental data integration. Its adoption in planning workflows demonstrates its role in supporting fiscal allocation and identifying strategic development opportunities. Looking ahead, TiNAI is expected to institutionalise cross-sector data integration further by incorporating health, housing, municipal, and additional statistical datasets. This expansion will enhance monitoring of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), disaster risk reduction frameworks, and climate resilience metrics. With an open, scalable architecture, the platform has potential for replication across other states or regions seeking integrated, AI-driven land and resource governance systems.

title: PresidencIA: Generative AI Adoption Programme for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
description: PresidencIA is a comprehensive programme designed to accelerate the responsible adoption of generative AI within the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office (Gabinete de Presidencia). While AI offers significant potential to improve public‑sector decision‑making and service delivery, many administrations lack the internal capacity, tools and infrastructure needed to adopt it safely. PresidencIA responds by combining skills development, purpose‑built applications, sovereign infrastructure and international engagement into a single, integrated approach. The programme’s first pillar focuses on community and capacity building. Through hands‑on workshops such as Whispering to AIs, Prototyping with AI and Researching with AI, several hundred public servants have developed practical skills in prompt engineering and responsible AI use. These activities prioritise experimentation and peer learning over theoretical instruction, supported by an active community of practice where staff share experiences and best practices. The second pillar delivers AI applications tailored to the Prime Minister’s Office. These include ServetIA, a research platform that produces source‑verified analytical outputs to support policy work; CiudadanIA, which automates the summarisation of citizen correspondence addressed to the President, reducing processing time and improving response quality; and GlobalAlert, which provides real‑time geopolitical monitoring and threat analysis. The programme also developed PromptAventura, a gamified AI literacy tool now validated and transferred to the government intranet. In addition, PresidencIA produced open‑source components, including an LLM evaluation workbench used to test prompts and models at scale through LLM‑as‑a‑judge methodologies. The infrastructure pillar addresses AI sovereignty and secure deployment. PresidencIA has tested open‑weight language models for on‑premises use, enabling sensitive data processing without reliance on external cloud providers. In collaboration with the government IT unit (U.TIC), the programme is assessing the feasibility of a dedicated internal AI compute cluster and fine‑tuning models for specific government use cases. Alongside domestic infrastructure, PresidencIA also pursues international engagement, positioning Spain as a strategic partner for leading AI labs and fostering collaboration on alignment, safety research and responsible deployment of frontier AI systems in government contexts.

title: Data EF AI Agent
description: The Data EF Open Data Portal serves as Cambodia’s central platform for sharing economic and financial datasets across areas such as public finance, macroeconomics, revenue collection and industry. While the portal provides extensive data access, staff and decision‑makers often struggled to translate these datasets into timely insights. Manual search, review and download processes were slow and resource‑intensive, and inconsistent metadata and complex schemas made it difficult for users to locate relevant information. These limitations reduced the portal’s effectiveness as a decision-support tool. To address this gap, the General Department of Digital Economy developed the Data EF AI Agent and integrated it into Data EF Insight, the analytics portal. The AI agent connects natural-language queries to underlying datasets through a semantic metadata layer, automatically identifying relevant data, retrieving it from the Data EF lakehouse and delivering results as tables, visualizations or concise summaries. This allows users to move directly from a question to an insight within seconds, while keeping human oversight at the center of validation and decision‑making. The Data EF AI Agent aligns closely with Cambodia’s digital transformation agenda. It supports the Digital Government Policy 2022–2035 and the Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021–2035, both of which emphasize evidence-based policymaking, data interoperability and digital government. Cambodia’s low scores on the OECD OURdata Index (0.04) and the Digital Government Index (0.2) highlight the importance of initiatives that make government data easier to access and analyze. The AI agent reduces barriers to data use, strengthens analytical capacity and advances responsible, human-centered AI consistent with OECD AI Principles. The purpose of the AI agent is to remove technical barriers and improve administrative efficiency across the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). Internal testing shows that data retrieval and summarization can now be completed in 10–15 seconds—compared to lengthy manual processes involving multiple dataset searches and downloads. Staff can explore more than 600 datasets through a single, easy‑to‑use interface, strengthening evidence-based reporting and analysis. Improvements are evaluated through workflow comparisons, usage observations and user feedback on usability and efficiency. Early results show reduced reliance on technical expertise, faster reporting cycles and stronger internal data-use capability. The initiative is expected to encourage broader adoption of data-driven governance within MEF and expand to additional use cases as confidence grows.

title: Strategy for the Use of AI in the Judiciary
description: The federal government and the states have jointly developed a strategy for the use of artificial intelligence in the judiciary. This strategy was adopted in June 2025. It sets out a comprehensive vision for the use of AI systems in the judiciary, along with the necessary action plans and measures to achieve this vision. The strategy aims to harness the opportunities offered by AI for the judiciary at federal and state levels, while taking due account of the associated risks and limitations. Notably, the strategy anticipates providing forward-looking support for judicial and administrative processes, enhancing access to justice, and promoting innovation in AI. Furthermore, the strategy aims to develop a uniform interpretation of the AI Act throughout the federal states and states in order to ensure its coherent and effective implementation within the judiciary. At the same time, it seeks to ensure the AI Act's requirements are fully implemented throughout the judicial system. Through the joint strategy and an AI platform, AI solutions initially developed by individual states within the framework of specific projects will be made available for reuse by all states and the federal government in accordance with the EfA principle ('Develop once, use everywhere'). This approach is intended to improve cost-efficiency and increase the pace of innovation within the judiciary. According to the current timetable, the conceptual implementation of the AI Strategy is expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

title: Framework for Governance of Indigenous Data
description: The Indigenous Data Sovereignty Principles are outlined by the Maiam nayri Wingara Indigenous Data Sovereignty Collective and advocate for major changes to how data about, or that may affect, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are promoted, accessed and handled. The Framework guides Australian Government agencies on how to practically implement and embed those areas of data governance where the objectives of the Indigenous Data Sovereignty movement and the Australian Government align. The Framework was developed to change current data governance practices at all stages of the ‘Data Lifecycle’, from conceptualisation (before data are collected) to dissemination and reuse. A key tenet of several actions in the Framework is the need to build capability to engage with and use data, both within the Australian Government and among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. Better use of data can then support shared decision-making at all points in the data lifecycle. The Framework is based on the principles of respect for cultural heritage, informed consent, privacy, and trust. It is informed by FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) guiding principles on data management and CARE (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics) principles which reflect the crucial role of data in self-determination. Each guideline in the Framework will illustrate which aspects of these principles have been employed. Australian Government agencies are responsible for implementing the actions where reasonably practical within their legislative obligations, and for identifying areas where it is not practical, and why (for example, due to national security, privacy, or compliance-related limitations). The Framework includes implementation guidelines that seek to influence behaviour, change current practices, and enable the Australian Public Service to work in partnership with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people at all levels. The guidelines direct Australian Government agencies to: 1. Partner with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. 2. Build data-related capabilities. 3. Provide knowledge of data assets. 4. Build an inclusive data system. Results, outcomes and impacts The intended outcomes of the Framework include: Government meaningfully partnering with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities across all stages of the data lifecycle. The APS effectively supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to use their own stories, make their own decisions, and set their own priorities. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples being able to easily access and use their own data for self-determination and community development. A more accessible and culturally competent public service that is inclusive, responsive, and transparent in relation to Indigenous data.

title: Document Register Agent
description: The DRA was developed to increase efficiency in access to records within a specific business area of the Department of Finance (Finance). Previously, staff relied on manual processes to review documents and record key details, which created barriers to consistent record keeping and made it difficult to efficiently research existing information. DRA was introduced to improve access to historical records and reduce administrative effort. The initiative combines AI with automated workflows to support staff with clearly defined tasks. When a document is saved to a designated system, DRA extracts relevant information and presents it to users for review through a structured approval process. Staff remain responsible for reviewing and approving the information before it is recorded, ensuring appropriate oversight and accuracy at all times. The objective of DRA is to improve consistency in how documents are recorded, reduce duplication of effort, and support better use of existing information within the business area it serves. By capturing information in a structured and standardised way, the initiative helps staff more easily conduct research and apply existing resources to current work. The system has been assessed as low risk, as it does not interact with the public, make decisions independently or process personal information. DRA is deliberately designed as a targeted solution tailored to the needs of a specific business area, rather than an enterprise-wide system. It reflects the Finance’s approach to using AI for well scoped, low risk, assistive purposes where there is a clear operational need. It represents the type of AI enabled solution Finance currently uses and plans to expand further in 2026 by applying similar approaches to other suitable internal processes. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative has delivered measurable productivity improvements while maintaining human oversight. Results were assessed through A/B testing, which showed that using DRA reduced the time required to extract and record key information by approximately 15–30 minutes per document compared to manual methods. When applied across typical annual workloads in the business area, this represents a meaningful reduction in administrative effort each year. Over time, these improvements are expected to strengthen record keeping, improve access to historical records, and support more consistent use of existing information resources.

title: Remote Pilot Program
description: Use-Case Examples The Ghost Nets Initiative is an Indigenous-led design of the use of drones and AI by Indigenous ranger groups in northern Australia to monitor ghost nets and marine debris. Population surveys of threatened animal species using drone-based thermal sensors. Detection of saltwater crocodiles through the development of an integrated sensor network and real-time alerts. The use of drones and AI in detecting, monitoring and controling buffel grass. Results, outcomes and impacts The remote pilot program demonstrated that drones and AI can safely and efficiently monitor remote environments, delivering better detection of ghost nets, threatened species, crocodiles and invasive buffel grass than traditional methods. Indigenous-led and ranger-delivered approaches improved coverage, accuracy and decision making while building lasting technical capability in communities and agencies. Across use cases, pilots reduced safety risks, costs and time in the field and enabled more targeted, evidence-based management actions. Overall, the program showed clear environmental, cultural and public safety benefits and provided a strong foundation for scaling these technologies into business-as-usual operations. Challenges and lessons learned The initiative faced challenges operating in remote and harsh environments, meeting aviation and safety requirements, and producing sufficiently high quality, consistent data to train AI models reliably. Building capability took time, as rangers and staff needed training, accreditation and confidence in both drone operations and AI-enabled workflows, often in areas with limited digital infrastructure. A key lesson was that early, genuine co-design with First Nations rangers was essential to ensure culturally appropriate use, trust, and Indigenous data sovereignty. The pilots also showed that success depends less on technical sophistication than on good data, simple repeatable processes, strong governance, and embedding the technology into business-as-usual decision making.

title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilisation of AI-related Technology
description: While AI technologies, including generative AI, contribute to improving citizens’ lives and advancing economic development, delays in domestic AI development and utilisation, as well as public concerns about associated risks, had become challenges. In response to these circumstances, and in order to balance the promotion of AI innovation with risk mitigation, the AI Act was promulgated and partially enforced on 4 June 2025 and fully enforced on 1 September 2025. Furthermore, the AI Basic Plan stipulated in Article 18, Paragraph 1 of the Act sets forth the following “Three Principles” and “Four Basic Policies” as fundamental guidelines for promoting research, development, and utilization of AI-related technologies. Three principles Promoting innovation while mitigating risks Agile methodology that responds to changes Promoting integrated domestic and international policies Four Basic Policies Accelerated promotion of AI deployment Strategic enhancement of AI development capabilities Leadership in AI governance Continuous transformation toward an AI society

title: Social Media Analytics for Water Sector Issues
description: The Social Media Analysis initiative was developed to bridge the gap between massive public discourse on social media and actionable institutional intelligence. Previously, monitoring citizen feedback on X was a labor-intensive manual process requiring roughly four hours daily. This initiative leverages AI and machine learning to automate this workflow, processing data through Google Cloud BigQuery and visualising results via Looker Enterprise. By doing so, it resolves the issue of "information overload" and ensures that critical beneficiary reports are never missed. The primary objective is to transform raw social data into structured business insights through several specialised layers: Spam Guard: Uses NLP to filter out advertisements, water filter promotions, and redundant bot replies. Multi-Layer Classification: The system assigns sentiment (Positive, Neutral, Negative), extracts geographic data (City and Neighbourhood), and maps posts to approximately seven business-defined problem categories. Summary Reporting: The data points are synthesised and integrated into the "Observatory Dashboard," providing a single source of truth for leadership and higher management, highlighting emerging trends and public perception. The initiative is currently fully operational and success is maintained through a combination of automated infrastructure monitoring on Google Cloud Run and continuous human-in-the-loop validation to ensure the model remains aligned with local context and evolving dialect. Future evolution of the tool is focused on horizontal and functional scaling. The roadmap includes expanding analysis to platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram, as well as incorporating video and Reels content analysis. Additionally, we aim to integrate the system directly with CRM platforms to automatically trigger service tickets from social media complaints, further closing the loop between citizen feedback and operational response.

title: H2O AI Assistant for Water Sector
description: The H2O Assistant is a purpose-built AI ecosystem designed to revolutionise knowledge management and operational efficiency within the Saudi Water Authority (SWA). By centralising access to the organisation's vast data landscape ranging from unstructured legacy documents to live Google Cloud Platform (GCP) BigQuery datasets, the assistant provides executive leadership and managers with a single, conversational interface that also supports Arabic. title: Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis
description: The process of distributing legislative bills to the thematic committees – Initial Dispatch – requires manual and technical analysis by the Clerk staff. This activity, although critical for the proper progress of legislative processing, is susceptible to inconsistencies, delays, and work overload. Additionally, the growing volume of bills makes the process increasingly challenging in terms of time and accuracy. That process is composed of five modules and implemented by AI agents that evaluate the legislative document from different perspectives: Assessment of the bill's procedural and constitutional requirements Search for similar legislative documents already being processed in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, so that, instead of having independent processing, they can be attached to a similar bill Definition of the form of analysis of the legislative matter, that is, whether by characteristic or rule it will first be evaluated by thematic committees before being voted on in plenary, or whether it is possible for the legislative proposal to become law as long as it has a conclusive opinion in the thematic committees through which it must pass. Below are the alternatives for form of bill analysis procedure: Bill subject to conclusive discussion by committees Bill subject to plenary discussion, Bill subject to internal discussions in committees. Definition of the processing regime: under Brazilian legislation, legislative matters can be processed under the following regimes: Ordinary, Priority, Urgency, Special. Distribution to thematic committees for evaluation of merit, financial adequacy, and constitutionality. In the Chamber of Deputies of Brazil there are 30 permanent committees. All these analyses approaches are supported by AI agents to choose the best option, complying with the procedural and constitutional rights and rules involved.

title: NugepIA: AI-Powered Judicial Precedent Management System (Subnational: Porto Velho)
description: NugepIA was developed by the Court of Justice of Rondônia (TJRO) to resolve critical bottlenecks in the management of binding precedents, such as IRDR and IAC, within the court’s NUGEPNAC unit. Prior to its introduction, monitoring of precedents relied on manual spreadsheets and institutional memory, creating fragmented communication, high risk of error and delays in reporting information to the National Council of Justice (CNJ). Judges’ chambers also lacked automatic visibility into suspended cases, negatively affecting productivity and legal certainty. The initiative’s core objective is to automate the NUGEPNAC workflow using the Collectivus AI tool. The system automatically extracts key procedural dates—such as suspension, judgment and finality—directly from case documents, ensuring accurate and up‑to‑date records. It applies textual‑similarity analysis to group identical or highly similar cases, alerting judges in their workspaces to repetitive litigation and suggesting links to existing or potential binding precedents. In addition, the system performs daily monitoring of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) website to track updates in constitutional‑control actions relevant to ongoing cases. Development progressed from initial mapping in February 2025 to full implementation by December 2025. Integration was completed across the PJe system, the Nugep System and the Chamber Module, eliminating manual reconciliation between platforms. This milestone institutionalised AI as a support tool for judicial decision‑making and laid the technological foundation for the broader AssessorIA platform, which now scales similarity‑analysis capabilities across the entire court. Operationally, NugepIA eliminated manual data verification and enabled automated, accurate reporting to the CNJ’s National Precedent Bank (BNP). The AI achieves over 95% precision in grouping similar lawsuits and provides direct, actionable suggestions to judges’ chambers. Impact is measured through reduced screening and verification time, continuous validation cycles parallel to development and improved visibility of first‑ and second‑instance caseloads that were previously unmonitored by the central system. Implementation addressed several challenges. Manual grouping of cases and spreadsheet‑based communication were error‑prone, and inconsistencies in procedural dates previously prevented automatic validation. These issues were resolved through full system integration and AI‑based date extraction, replacing manual review. Experience showed that successful AI use in the judiciary depends on coordinated planning between technical and legal teams, realistic timelines and continuous testing to mature similarity‑analysis functions.

title: ServetIA: AI Research Platform for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
description: ServetIA is a custom-built AI research platform developed within the PresidencIA programme to support analysis and information retrieval in the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office. Named after Miguel Servet, the Spanish polymath and pioneer of scientific inquiry, ServetIA embodies the same spirit of rigorous, evidence-based investigation applied to modern governance. Government advisors in the Prime Minister’s Office routinely research complex policy topics, prepare briefing documents, and synthesise information from multiple sources under tight deadlines. Traditional methods are slow and resource intensive. Off-the-shelf AI tools raise concerns about data privacy, accuracy, and suitability for sensitive government contexts. ServetIA bridges this gap. Built on large language model technology, it provides a complete suite of tools for research powered with AI, where staff can pose policy questions and receive structured, source-referenced responses, conduct literature review, reach consensus and generate drafts with verified citation. The platform prioritises “grounding”, ensuring outputs are anchored in verifiable sources rather than generating unsupported claims. This responds directly to the government’s need for reliable, citable information. A deep research module handles comprehensive, multi-source investigations that go beyond simple question-answering. The platform is in Beta, deployed and accessible at servetia.eu, with iterative refinements based on government user feedback. Development follows human-centred design: features are prioritised through user interviews and observation during structured Discovery phases within the Prime Minister’s Office. Technical implementation leverages both cloud-based and on-premises models. For sensitive use cases, the platform enables the use of local LLMs instead of Cloud, using open-weight models that can run on local infrastructure, supporting AI sovereignty objectives. This hybrid approach balances performance with data security requirements of a head-of-government institution. ServetIA complements a broader ecosystem within the PresidencIA programme, demonstrating how purpose-built AI tools, developed with government-specific requirements for security, accuracy, and usability, can enhance core government functions. Its architecture is modular and transferable, can be adapted to other departments and ministries, and its methodology, combining user research, iterative prototyping, and security-first design, provides a replicable model for AI tool development in government settings across countries. The tool augments rather than replaces human judgment, positioning AI as a support layer for public servants.

title: Ulysses - Consolidated summaries of legislative bills
description: Legislative consultants, staff in charge of support the laymaking drafting, assist parliamentarians in reporting on legislative bills by producing consolidated executive summaries for each bill, including its justification and other related documents: amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. The production of these summaries can take hours or days, depending on the number of amendments and bills attached to the main bill being reported. This challenge is amplified along with the bills' lifecycle, once the set of documents increases eveyday and the updated version can assume a different meaning along with the time. In some cases, the bill intends to change other bills, resulting in a complex chain of documents. The AI system uses generative AI tools to assist consultants in producing these summaries, which must be reviewed and supplemented by the consultants themselves according to thematic or contextual needs. These are the main objectives for this AI application: (i) decrease the time required to produce consolidated executive summaries from hours or days to minutes, enabling legislative consultants to work more efficiently; (ii) automatically identify and synthesize key information from all related documents to prevent oversight of critical content; and (iii) provide standardized, well-structured summaries that serve as a robust foundation for consultants to review and refine, ensuring uniformity across legislative reports. This initiative necessitates ongoing investment in ensuring the quality of both metadata and complete textual content of the legislative proposals under analysis and their respective cited legislation. Results, outcomes and impacts: A first positive impact achieved was the standardization of AI-generated summaries based on consensus obtained among the consultants who participated in the solution validation. For example, there are rules for initiating summary text, for limiting the number of words generated, for incorporating cited legislation into the summarization context, etc. We have begun collecting feedback-based measurements for ongoing investigation and continuous improvement of the deployed solution Challenges and lessons learned: Along the implementation of the AI system, it was necessary to perform extraction of textual and tabular content from documents produced in various different formats (e.g., .doc, .docx, .pdf, .tiff, among others). Some bills and regulations may contain both text and tables simultaneously. Moreover, varying context window constraints and behavioral differences were observed across different generative AI models, which required specific testing and targeted interventions to handle each encountered issue.

title: AI Chatbot for Statistical Analyses of Fiscal Data
description: The initiative addresses the growing volume and complexity of fiscal and statistical data, which increasingly challenge traditional analytical tools and constrain the capacity of public administrations to fully leverage available information for decision-making. At the same time, it capitalises on the opportunity offered by high-quality, structured public data and advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) to modernise analytical processes, strengthen evidence-based policymaking, and improve transparency in the management of public information. The initiative pursues three main objectives: to enhance the accuracy, speed, and efficiency of fiscal data analysis through AI-based tools; to support data-driven decision-making within public administration; to promote the responsible and trustworthy use of AI, in line with principles of data protection, accountability, and human oversight. To achieve these objectives, a prototype AI-based chatbot was developed using aggregated statistical data published by the Department of Finance. title: Ulysses chat
description: The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies provides a wide range of internal services that support roughly 10,000 people, including 513 deputies, parliamentary staff, public servants and outsourced workers. Its operations span broadcasting (radio and TV), news services, medical care, engineering, architecture, finance, procurement, IT, legal services, training, a legislative university, dozens of legislative committees and extensive research and library functions. This diversity generates a constant demand for rapid access to accurate institutional information. The Chamber’s traditional intranet model could no longer meet the speed and analytical depth required by employees in their daily work. As generative AI became widely used, staff increasingly turned to external platforms; however, using these tools without institutional context would require uploading large volumes of internal documents, creating risks around data privacy, rule misapplication and high duplication‑related costs. To address this, the Chamber developed Ulysses Chat—a generative AI‑based virtual assistant designed specifically for internal use and grounded in the institution’s own knowledge base. Ulysses Chat draws on a network of interconnected AI agents and operates within a governance layer designed to ensure privacy, security and responsible AI behaviour. It incorporates mechanisms for auditing, token accountability, minimising bias and hallucinations, and managing out‑of‑context queries. In its first implementation stage, the system answers questions using official institutional data, including internal standards, legislation, manuals, administrative rules, planning and budget information, logistics and human‑resources procedures, and legislative data such as bills, speeches and voting records. It also uses the Chamber’s organizational chart to contextualize information. In the current second phase, Ulysses Chat is beginning to automate selected internal processes through direct interaction with institutional systems. Across all information domains, data managers, data stewards and the Data Protection Officer oversee ongoing data‑quality monitoring.

title: BizData
description: Each year, the Ministry of Economy provides in‑person or assisted consulting to around 30,000 businesses, covering only about 5% of Israel’s entrepreneurial population. BizData was created to extend this support to the remaining majority of small and medium‑sized enterprises by delivering scalable, digital business guidance. Using conversational interaction, the system identifies the type of business, its activities, geographic context and customer base, and then provides tailored information such as comparable business characteristics, recommendations for business planning, guidance on licensing and employment, and market‑related insights. The system is built on an AI agent combined with custom databases developed specifically for the initiative and is being progressively connected to additional governmental and public data sources. This allows businesses to receive context‑specific information from a unified platform rather than navigating fragmented systems. A key technical capability enables the AI to interpret a simple verbal description of a business and match it across datasets that use different classification systems, resolving inconsistencies that previously prevented effective data integration. Less than one year after launch, BizData is used by approximately 5,500 businesses and entrepreneurs, with 60% returning for repeated use. Among survey respondents, 86% report receiving significant value from the system. Interest from other government ministries has led to discussions on expanding shared knowledge contributions, and partnerships are being explored with organisations that employ business consultants and mentors. These collaborations would allow the development of a “consultant assistant” function to support professional advisors in delivering higher‑quality guidance. Implementation presented several challenges. Business‑related datasets varied in structure and classification, requiring the development of an AI‑based matching component to align user input with reliable data sources. Additional effort was required to secure approvals from data owners to enable lawful reuse of information for public benefit. A current strategic challenge is positioning BizData as the primary digital gateway for businesses across Israel. The long‑term objective is to strengthen business resilience, support the creation of new enterprises and enable growth among small and medium‑sized firms, contributing to broader economic development. BizData is designed to evolve into the central channel through which businesses in Israel access trusted business and government information, combining scalability, accessibility and informed decision‑making in a single platform.

title: Transform Paraná Program – Integrated Ecosystem of AI, Automation, and Data Governance (Subnational: Paraná)
description: The Transforma Paraná Program establishes a statewide infrastructure for territorial and environmental intelligence designed to modernize public governance in Paraná. It responds to long‑standing structural challenges in public administration, including fragmented data across multiple systems, limited automation and heavy reliance on manual, time‑consuming processes. By combining artificial intelligence with cloud‑native architecture, the program aims to eliminate data silos and support faster, evidence‑based decision‑making across government. At the heart of the initiative is the creation of a unified Data Foundation, implemented through a Macro State Data Lake that consolidates large volumes of information under a single governance framework. This foundation standardizes metadata, ensures interoperability and embeds compliance with Brazil’s General Data Protection Law (LGPD). It enables a range of high‑impact projects, including the Paraná Mais Sustentável platform for rural digital addressing and environmental monitoring; SISTRANSITO, which uses AI to analyze more than 82,000 traffic accident reports to improve road safety; and the J.A.C.A. project, which digitizes food donations at CEASA‑PR using conversational agents to reduce hunger and food waste. The program is institutionalized through a strategic partnership between the Secretariat of Innovation and Artificial Intelligence (SEIA) and CELEPAR, ensuring that the technology is embedded in official state services and remains sustainable over time. Implementation follows a phased approach, starting with core infrastructure and pilot modules before scaling to full production. Continuous improvement is supported through automated pipelines and the introduction of an Agent Development Kit, enabling the deployment of intelligent, proactive digital services in areas such as health, education and public security. Concrete results are already visible. The Data Foundation has centralized petabytes of information, automated the analysis of 82,000 traffic accident reports and enabled the creation of unique digital addresses for 300,000 rural properties. Impact is measured through reductions in manual processing time, high levels of data structuring (exceeding 90% completeness) and the successful deployment of AI‑based conversational services for social programs. Beyond these core initiatives, Transforma Paraná supports a broader innovation ecosystem. Complementary actions include the Conecta IA program to identify operational bottlenecks, Hub GovTech Paraná to promote open innovation, the Paraná Artificial Intelligence Cup for civil servants and AI solutions applied to public security and housing programs such as COHAPAR. Together, these efforts reduce bureaucracy, increase efficiency and modernize service delivery across multiple policy domains.

title: CiudadanIA: AI-Powered Citizen Correspondence Processing for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
description: CiudadanIA is an AI initiative within the PresidencIA programme that applies generative AI to improve the processing of citizen correspondence addressed to the President of Spain through the official “Escribe al Presidente” (Write to the President) service. This channel receives thousands of letters from citizens raising concerns, making requests, and sharing opinions on policy matters. Each letter requires reading, summarising, categorising, and routing to the appropriate government department, a labour-intensive process that directly affects how quickly and effectively citizens receive responses. CiudadanIA automates the summarisation step using small language models. Rather than relying exclusively on large cloud-based AI systems, the project combined cloud with fine-tuned compact models (specifically Gemma-3-4B, quantised for efficiency) to run on local government infrastructure. This design decision was driven by two requirements: citizen letters contain personal and sensitive information, and the government’s AI sovereignty objectives call for reduced dependency on third-party systems. The fine-tuning and evaluation process was rigorous. Government staff who process citizen correspondence daily provided expert feedback on model outputs, identifying systematic errors such as hallucinated information (inventing details not present in letters), tone distortion (characterising respectful requests as demands), and omission of relevant content. This feedback was used to iteratively refine prompts and model behaviour. To support this evaluation at scale, the programme developed an open-source LLM evaluation workbench that enables systematic testing of different prompts, models, and configurations. The tool supports both cloud APIs and local models, includes batch processing for evaluating large sets of correspondence, and implements an LLM-as-a-judge methodology where one language model evaluates the quality of another’s outputs against configurable criteria (accuracy, conciseness, tone preservation). The tool also supports English and Spanish and is available for other government teams.

title: Aurora – Institutional AI Cognitive Infrastructure (Subnational: State of Rio Grande do Sul)
description: Aurora emerged as an institutional effort to mark a "new Dawn" in legal work, treating technology as a strategic teammate rather than a standalone tool. It was developed to address increasing procedural complexity, data fragmentation, and cognitive overload within the justice system of Rio Grande do Sul. Prosecutors must analyse large volumes of documents, reports, and recorded hearings across multiple systems, which limits timely action in areas such as criminal prosecution, child protection, environmental enforcement, and public integrity. The initiative seeks to strengthen institutional capacity by embedding AI as a structured and accountable capability within core justice functions. Rather than focusing solely on document automation, Aurora operates as a cognitive support infrastructure. It enables natural language interaction with procedural records, automated transcription and summarisation of audiovisual evidence, cross-referencing of testimonies across different hearings, and identification of potential inconsistencies. Integration with existing judicial back-office systems (including eProc and SAJ) reduces workflow disruption and eliminates mechanical bottlenecks from case intake to judicial submission. Aurora evolved through an internal prototyping phase in which prosecutors tested and refined prompts and transcription workflows before full deployment. This ensured alignment with operational needs and encouraged voluntary adoption. Governance is anchored in institutional policy and ICT oversight, including human-in-the-loop review, audit trails, and structured prompt curation. A collaborative prompt library enables users to share and evaluate analytical instructions, which are subsequently curated by a central body that may assign an official “Approved” designation. This transforms individual expertise into institutional knowledge while preserving intellectual autonomy. As of February 2026, Aurora has processed 13,012 hours of audio and video and supported the production of 37,028 legal documents. On February 11, 2026, it reached a historic milestone of 1,000 documents produced in a single day. System analytics indicate 1,432 unique users, reflecting strong voluntary uptake. Results are monitored through usage data and workflow indicators. In time-sensitive cases, such as sexual abuse testimonies, faster evidence analysis reduces delays and strengthens safeguards. Future impacts include expanded integration and analytical capacity to improve access to justice.

It was developed to address increasing procedural complexity, data fragmentation, and cognitive overload within the justice system of Rio Grande do Sul. Prosecutors must analyse large volumes of documents, reports, and recorded hearings across multiple systems, which limits timely action in areas such as criminal prosecution, child protection, environmental enforcement, and public integrity. The initiative seeks to strengthen institutional capacity by embedding AI as a structured and accountable capability within core justice functions. Rather than focusing solely on document automation, Aurora operates as a cognitive support infrastructure. It enables natural language interaction with procedural records, automated transcription and summarisation of audiovisual evidence, cross-referencing of testimonies across different hearings, and identification of potential inconsistencies. Integration with existing judicial back-office systems (including eProc and SAJ) reduces workflow disruption and eliminates mechanical bottlenecks from case intake to judicial submission. Aurora evolved through an internal prototyping phase in which prosecutors tested and refined prompts and transcription workflows before full deployment. This ensured alignment with operational needs and encouraged voluntary adoption. Governance is anchored in institutional policy and ICT oversight, including human-in-the-loop review, audit trails, and structured prompt curation. A collaborative prompt library enables users to share and evaluate analytical instructions, which are subsequently curated by a central body that may assign an official “Approved” designation. This transforms individual expertise into institutional knowledge while preserving intellectual autonomy. As of February 2026, Aurora has processed 13,012 hours of audio and video and supported the production of 37,028 legal documents. On February 11, 2026, it reached a historic milestone of 1,000 documents produced in a single day. System analytics indicate 1,432 unique users, reflecting strong voluntary uptake. Results are monitored through usage data and workflow indicators. In time-sensitive cases, such as sexual abuse testimonies, faster evidence analysis reduces delays and strengthens safeguards. Future impacts include expanded integration and analytical capacity to improve access to justice

title: Khmer Intelligent Document AI Agent (KIDAI-A)
description: Documents are the backbone of governance, commerce, and social life. Yet virtually all leading Document AI systems, designed for high-resource languages like English, perform poorly on Khmer, Cambodia’s official script used by over 17 million people. This creates a compounding digital divide: government officials cannot efficiently query Khmer-language policy archives; businesses struggle to automate Khmer invoice processing; and citizens face barriers accessing public information in their own language. No commercially available AI solution adequately addresses this gap. Government Use Cases in Action: 1. Admin Assistant: Summarises official letters, retrieves staff records, and answers queries about internal reports in real time. 2. Policy Assistant: Enables officials to query national AI strategies (e.g., NAIS), MEF IT frameworks, and regulatory documents conversationally. 3. Data Entry Automation: Extracts structured data from invoices, sale reports, and forms, dramatically reducing manual processing time. KIDAI-A locally hosts open-source LLMs (Qwen, Gemma, GPT-OSS variants) to ensure data sovereignty, no sensitive government data leaves Cambodia’s infrastructure. The platform is offered through Subscription (PaaS), API services (OCR, STT, MT, RAG), Knowledge Hub digitisation services, and vertical solutions. Target customers include government agencies, education and research institutes, the financial sector, enterprises, SMEs, and legal services. The team is pursuing co-development partnerships with government ministries and plans to expand KIDAI-A into a national-grade AI infrastructure for Cambodia’s digital government ecosystem. KIDAI-A represents more than a product, it is a national movement. Cambodia, like many lower-middle-income nations, faces a structural risk: dependence on foreign AI tools that neither understand Khmer culture, nor protect Cambodian data. KIDAI-A is Cambodia’s answer to this challenge, a fully sovereign AI stack designed, trained, and deployed by Cambodians, for Cambodians. Results, outcomes and impacts: KIDAI-A is actively under development with the following milestones achieved and projected: 1. Proprietary Khmer speech recognition model trained on 500+ hours of audio data, achieving high transcription accuracy for Cambodian speech. 2. In-house OCR and document layout analysis models functional for Khmer/English document extraction. 3. Working prototype deployed locally — vector store loaded with 406+ government documents, demonstrating real-time multilingual Q&A. 4. Projected impact: reduce document processing time for government staff by 60-80%; enable digital access to Khmer-language policy archives; support Cambodia’s national digitisation agenda.

title: ANAC Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2026
description: ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the formal roadmap that operationalizes the agency’s AI Policy and translates AI adoption into concrete goals, governance arrangements, actions and monitoring routines. The strategy responds to a clear opportunity and challenge: to use AI to improve internal work, digital services and regulatory performance while ensuring safety, ethics, transparency, data protection and institutional accountability. The initiative is closely aligned with ANAC’s broader institutional planning. It connects to the agency’s Strategic Plan 2020–2026, its Digital Strategy 2024–2026 and the federal digital government agenda. Its strategic vision is to achieve excellence in the broad, safe and responsible adoption of AI to advance ANAC’s mission. To support this, the strategy defines key results for staff adoption and service transformation, and organizes implementation around five objectives: integrating AI into staff activities, increasing the capacity to develop AI-enabled solutions, improving data governance, ensuring security and ethics, and optimizing AI costs. The strategy is also a governance mechanism in practice, because it assigns roles and responsibilities across the institution. ANAC’s normative framework establishes an AI governance structure involving the IT Committee, the Superintendence of Technology and Digital Transformation, the data protection officer, technical advisory units, director-linked units and AI focal points. It also created an AI core with representatives from nearly all units, who met weekly, received training and helped design the policy and strategy. This creates a cross-functional model for prioritization, oversight, risk handling, implementation support and organizational learning. Looking ahead, the initiative is designed to become more institutionalized and scalable. ANAC established a roadmap, an operational model, periodic monitoring and evaluation routines, and requirements for existing AI systems to adapt to the new rules. The strategy foresees broader uptake across internal and external services, additional specific procurements if needed, and stronger reuse of models, standards and knowledge across the agency. In this sense, the initiative is not only a strategy document, but an institutional framework for trustworthy AI adoption in a federal regulator.

title: Horizons: Empowering Educators with Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technologies
description: The Horizons Program addresses a system-level challenge arising from the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education without a structured framework to guide safe and effective adoption. As AI tools become increasingly accessible, many educators currently lack clear national guidance on how to use AI safely and effectively in teaching, assessment, and school operations. Without a coordinated national approach, AI use in schools risks becoming fragmented, inconsistent, and uneven in quality. The programme therefore establishes a shared national framework that promotes equitable access, common standards, and responsible innovation, while strengthening digital readiness and positioning schools within a data-informed education system. The programme’s primary objectives are to build practical AI competencies among teachers and school leaders, improve instructional quality and assessment design, and strengthen data-informed decision-making at school level. It prioritises applied classroom integration over theoretical awareness, enabling educators to design AI-supported lessons, enhance differentiation, streamline assessment processes, and embed ethical and responsible technology practices. It also strengthens leadership capacity to govern AI implementation in alignment with national professional standards and digital transformation priorities. Implementation follows a phased national model supported by certified trainers, structured pre–post evaluation mechanisms, and continuous quality assurance monitoring. This approach ensures consistency across regions while enabling evidence-based refinement. Over time, the programme is designed to be embedded within formal professional development systems and institutional training frameworks, supported by policy guidance and competency standards. As it scales, the initiative will expand to additional educator groups, introduce differentiated specialisation pathways, and establish communities of practice to sustain impact. Future development will deepen integration with curriculum implementation, school improvement planning, and advanced data use. Through structured institutionalisation and sustained capacity building, the programme moves beyond isolated training towards coherent, responsible, and system-wide AI integration that strengthens learning outcomes and long-term education resilience.
