title: Artificial Intelligence & The Manipulation of Human Perception within the educational program "Analyze – Decide – Act"
description: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly sophisticated, it is being weaponised to manipulate human perception at unprecedented scale and precision. Deepfake videos, voice cloning, personalised disinformation campaigns and emotion-targeted content are no longer theoretical risks but active threats affecting elections, public trust, organisational security and individual decision-making. Traditional digital literacy approaches are insufficient because they do not address AI's unique capabilities: algorithmic personalisation that traps users in information bubbles, conversational bots that simulate empathy to extract sensitive data and synthetic media so realistic that even experts struggle to detect manipulation. This educational guide aims to transform passive digital consumers into informed, critical actors capable of recognising and resisting AI-based manipulation. Its primary objectives are to: (1) explain how AI technologies work in accessible language, demystifying complex mechanisms like neural networks, large language models and emotion AI; (2) illustrate real-world manipulation scenarios including spear phishing, microtargeting, deepfakes and artificial social consensus; (3) provide concrete detection and prevention methods for individuals, educators and organisations; and (4) promote a culture of verification, critical thinking and digital responsibility. The guide specifically targets diverse audiences from schoolchildren and parents to public officials and corporate leadership, recognising that digital resilience must be built across all segments of society. Developed through collaboration between the Cloud Security Alliance Romanian Chapter, the National Cyber Security Directorate (DNSC), Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and Romanian Police, through the Crime Research and Prevention Institute, this initiative leverages institutional credibility and technical expertise. The guide is freely accessible in both Romanian and English, with practical resources including fact-checking platforms, deepfake detection tools and educational materials. Initial distribution focuses on government institutions, educational networks and cybersecurity communities, with documented engagement from law enforcement training programmes and corporate security departments. The initiative is designed for continuous evolution as AI-based threats develop. The guide emphasises five fundamental directions for societal preparedness: AI-era adapted digital education that trains users to recognise algorithmic manipulation; clear regulations to ban or regulate manipulative AI-generated content; algorithmic transparency through independent audits of AI systems; multidisciplinary collaboration between cybersecurity specialists, psychologists, educators, legal experts, and sociologists; and accessible detection and verification.

This educational guide aims to transform passive digital consumers into informed, critical actors capable of recognising and resisting AI-based manipulation. Developed through collaboration between the Cloud Security Alliance Romanian Chapter, the National Cyber Security Directorate (DNSC), Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and Romanian Police, through the Crime Research and Prevention Institute, this initiative leverages institutional credibility and technical expertise. Initial distribution focuses on government institutions, educational networks and cybersecurity communities, with documented engagement from law enforcement training programmes and corporate security departments. The initiative is designed for continuous evolution as AI-based threats develop. The guide emphasises five fundamental directions for societal preparedness: AI-era adapted digital education that trains users to recognise algorithmic manipulation; clear regulations to ban or regulate manipulative AI-generated content; algorithmic transparency through independent audits of AI systems; multidisciplinary collaboration between cybersecurity specialists, psychologists, educators, legal experts, and sociologists; and accessible detection and verification

title: National AI Index (NAII)
description: The National AI Index (NAII) aims to assess the readiness level of government entities to adopt AI technologies, monitor their progress on a periodic basis, and provide practical recommendations on strengths and potential areas for improvement for each entity, thereby supporting the development and use of these technologies at the national level. The Index consists of three main pillars, seven sub-pillars, and twenty-three domains to ensure a comprehensive measurement process. The design of the Index considers current challenges and future opportunities faced by government entities in adopting AI. The most notable of these challenges include weak alignment between AI initiatives and national priorities, limited availability of suitable data for training, variations in the readiness of technical infrastructure across entities, a shortage of specialized national talent, and a lack of unified and clear measurement standards. Index Objectives: - Aligning government efforts and priorities in the field of AI. - Providing and improving the necessary enablers for AI adoption within government entities. - Enabling the launch and adoption of AI products in key sectors and ensuring impact realization. The Index delivers results that reflect each entity's adoption level while also providing the necessary support and recommendations to strengthen their capabilities in developing effective and sustainable AI solutions and applications that directly contribute to achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. Additionally, the Index aims to empower government entities to develop AI products in priority sectors, provide the essential enablers to support the sustainability of these efforts, and maximize their impact. The Index consists of three main pillars: Directions, Enablers, and Outputs. These pillars include seven main sub-pillars, divided into 23 sub-domains covering strategic, regulatory, technical, operational, and human aspects. These components were carefully selected to provide a comprehensive and integrated view of entities’ readiness levels in the field of AI. The National AI Index classifies the maturity level of government entities in AI adoption into six main levels. Each level reflects a specific stage in the entity’s practices and development of AI capabilities, and helps define a roadmap for continuous improvement. The levels are: Level 0 - Absence of Capabilities: Score: 0% – 4.9% Level 1 – Establishing: Score: 5% – 24.9% Level 2 – Activated: Score: 25% – 49.9% Level 3 - Managed: Score: 50% – 79.9% Level 4 – Excellence: Score: 80% – 94.9% Level 5 - Pioneer: Score: 95% – 100%

title: Institutional Framework for the Progressive and Responsible Adoption of Generative AI in the Public Prosecutor's Office of the Province of Buenos Aires (MPBA) (Subnational: Province of Buenos Aires)
description: The initiative was developed in response to the growing availability of generative artificial intelligence tools and the need to regulate their use within the judicial environment in an ethical, secure and legally responsible manner. The Public Prosecutor’s Office of the Province of Buenos Aires established an initial regulatory framework defining principles, limits and responsibilities for the use of generative AI by institutional staff. The adopted strategy is based on a progressive and incremental approach. In a first stage, a controlled pilot programme was implemented in selected areas using an institutional platform (ChatIA) with access controls, traceability and human supervision. Based on the experience obtained, the regulatory framework has been adjusted and expanded, incorporating new guidelines, strengthening security measures and promoting staff training. The initiative includes continuous evaluation with the objective of gradually scaling the use of the technology, integrating it with other institutional systems and consolidating an AI governance model aligned with human rights principles, transparency and accountability. The Secretary of Innovation and Digital Experience of the Public Prosecutor’s Office of the Province of Buenos Aires was recognised with the “The Government AI 100 – 2026 Edition” award by Apolitical in the category Implementation and Adoption of AI. This distinction recognises the Secretary as one of the 100 most influential individuals worldwide in artificial intelligence applied to the public sector. The recognition highlights his leadership in promoting a strategic and responsible approach to AI adoption in the justice sector. He has promoted the adoption of people-centred technologies, led the development of the secure internal platform ChatIA, and promoted a strategic agreement with Microsoft to strengthen digital and artificial intelligence capabilities within the justice system. Apolitical is the world’s largest network of public servants, with more than 400,000 members, dedicated to strengthening government capacity globally. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative enabled the introduction of generative artificial intelligence within a controlled institutional environment, reducing the risks associated with external and unregulated platforms. It strengthened awareness of responsible AI use and generated empirical evidence for improving the regulatory framework. Impacts are evaluated through monitoring of platform usage, qualitative analysis and feedback from pilot areas.

title: Plan AI (Subnational: Greater Cambridge)
description: Public consultation is a legal requirement in planning, and public participation is critical - especially as planning issues often provoke strong local interest. However, local authorities often face an overwhelming volume of feedback, sometimes ranging from short notes to submissions of over 100 pages long. Plan AI employs large language models to summarise and analyse these responses to public consultations conducted by local authority planning departments. The tool was initially tested on three live planning consultations undertaken by Greater Cambridge Shared Planning relating to the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, Planning Obligations, and Health Impact Assessments. The trial results were striking: PlanAI generated detailed summaries of every individual submission and a compendium report for all three consultations in just 16 minutes. By contrast, human planners took over 60 hours to log and summarise the 320 public submissions, including over 18 hours creating summaries – longer would have been required if human planners had been tasked with producing an overview analysis of the consultation exercise as Plan AI does. In terms of the quality of the summaries, the project team found that there were no noticeable differences between the AI summaries when compared to the human generated ones. The AI-generated reports included descriptive statistics and analytical insights, offering a clear, data-driven overview of the submissions’ content and themes. The AI tool was developed by Professors Alex Lord, Alex Singleton and Dr Mark Green from the University of Liverpool’s Department of Geography & Planning working in partnership with the Planning Policy and Strategy team at Greater Cambridge Shared Planning. This close collaboration was an important part of the development of the AI tool in making sure that the reports that it generates were consistent with how the Councils currently report back to local communities and elected members. The next phase for the development of Plan AI will be working with five new pilot authorities selected by the national government Ministry for Housing Communities and Local Government. Results, outcomes and impacts: PlanAI has undergone rigorous testing, including an initial pilot using 300 responses from three consultations. It summarised all submissions in just 16 minutes, compared with 18.5 hours for human planners, demonstrating its potential to streamline plan making and reduce administrative burdens. The tool also has a minimal carbon footprint—roughly equivalent to sending two emails. Following GCSP’s successful use of PlanAI, the Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government has commissioned five additional pilots to assess how this purpose-built planning technology could be scaled nationally. Early results are highly encouraging, indicating that PlanAI could deliver a step change in planning practice.

title: AI-assisted tender generator solution (Hankelooja)
description: Public procurement plays a central role in how governments turn public funds into services, yet preparing procurement documents is often slow, manual, and resource‑intensive. Officials must compile technical descriptions, requirements, and evaluation criteria with great precision, even though many are not full‑time procurement specialists and may only conduct procurements a few times per year. Hankelooja was developed by the Estonian Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs to reduce this administrative burden. It is an AI-assisted tool trained on publicly available procurement data that generates structured draft documents based on a short description of the purchase. This allows officials to focus on key decisions rather than repetitive drafting and formatting. The initiative was first rolled out for small‑value procurements, which provided a low‑risk environment to test AI in real government workflows. The tool operates within the government’s secure infrastructure and uses only approved data sources, addressing data protection and trust requirements from the outset. Looking ahead, the approach behind Hankelooja can be extended to more complex procurements and replicated across other administrative processes. The initiative shows how AI can be introduced in a practical way in government, starting with a clearly defined problem, demonstrating clear value and supporting wider adoption over time. Results, outcomes and impacts Testing and early use of Hankelooja showed substantial time savings in procurement preparation. For small‑scale procurements, document drafting time was reduced by up to 70%, turning work that previously took days into minutes. The tool also improved consistency and reduced errors by using standardised structures and past procurement data. Impacts have been measured through time spent on preparation and user feedback from officials. Faster and more consistent processes are intended to allow services to be delivered sooner and reduce administrative effort. The approach is expected to scale to higher-value procurements and to other government processes with similar administrative complexity.

title: AI in the Australian Public Service (DFAT, APO, open-source)
description: This initiative brings together five complementary AI capabilities, Spark, the cables AI, an internal DFAT chatbot, the open‑source AI access, and the APO chatbot, to help staff work more effectively with information. It responds to the growing volume, complexity and pace of policy, operational and diplomatic information and the opportunity to use AI to improve productivity while maintaining security, trust and accountability in a government context. The initiative seeks to address challenges such as time lost searching for information, manually synthesising material, and navigating fragmented guidance and policy sources. Spark supports broad ideation and drafting tasks, while the cables AI enables analysis of diplomatic reporting at scale to surface themes and insights. The internal DFAT chatbot and the APO chatbot provide quick access to trusted internal and policy information, reducing reliance on informal workarounds. The open-source AI provides controlled access to open‑source AI models, enabling experimentation and learning where commercial tools may not be appropriate. Key objectives include improving staff efficiency, supporting better‑informed decision making, and building organisational capability and confidence in the safe and responsible use of AI. A further objective is to establish common governance, assurance and risk management patterns so that AI adoption is consistent, defensible and aligned with DFAT obligations rather than occurring in an ad hoc manner. Results show improved efficiency and confidence for staff, with faster access to information, reduced manual synthesis, and better visibility of themes in policy. Impacts have been mainly qualitative, informed by user feedback, adoption and usage metrics, and comparative assessments of time spent on common tasks. Measurement has focused on usage analytics, task based comparisons, and structured feedback from users and stakeholders, alongside assurance and risk reviews to ensure responsible use. Over time, the initiative is expected to deliver clearer, measurable reductions in search and analysis effort, broader uptake, and more consistent use of trusted AI tools, supporting better informed decisions and scalable, secure AI adoption.

title: Modernising CRA’s Service Feedback Program with the integration of generative AI into its national operations
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) has deployed an internal generative AI model as a tool to support employees in the completion of their duties. The Service Feedback Program, with the help of internal service experts in innovation and technology, customised the CRA model for specific implementation in the Agency’s client care program. Prior to business process enhancements and AI deployment, agents were required to manually search within existing procedure manuals for guidance, and to perform manual tasks such as letter creation, case analysis and synopsis. To increase efficiency, customisations related directly to agent responsibilities were added and included adding procedure manuals into the source database and creating dedicated prompts for common Service Feedback Officer tasks. In an environment characterised by complex procedures, high cognitive load, and diverse client and employee needs, the team standardised and simplified its business processes, successfully transforming an emerging technology into a powerful lever for greater productivity, operational efficiency, and informed decision-making support, with more than 82% of officers using the tool on a weekly basis. Prior to AI deployment, comprehensive testing was undertaken to effectively support employees in its use, and officers are encouraged to use the AI tool, but it remains optional. Feedback from employees has been very positive, with a majority of employees from a recent poll indicating user satisfaction. Initial reviews show a 42% increase in quality, which the program reports is correlated with increased client satisfaction and trust in the organisation. Before the implementation of AI and other business process re-engineering initiatives, officers typically spent 5 hours per file to complete their tasks. This time has now decreased to 3.75 hours per file, a 25% improvement in efficiency, enabling the program to expedite the service to 10,000 more clients with the same workforce. It is also worth highlighting that, in the preceding year, the program conducted a comprehensive business process review to establish standardised conditions for integrating new technologies. This effort further enhanced efficiency, contributing to an overall efficiency gain of 46% over the past two years. This initiative demonstrates in concrete terms how technological innovation can be integrated in a sustainable, responsible, and human-centred way within the Agency. The Service Feedback Program has demonstrated through business transformation and the enhancement and integration of digital tools that it is possible to transform a digital tool into a true driver of modernisation, engagement, and support for a national operational program.

title: Generative AI chatbot for taxpayer information services
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) has deployed a publicly accessible generative AI chatbot to support taxpayers in navigating tax-related information and services. The chatbot is designed to answer common, high-volume questions using authoritative CRA web content, helping users find accurate information more quickly while reducing pressure on traditional service channels. During its initial deployment period, the chatbot handled over one million chat sessions and responded to more than 1.5 million taxpayer questions, representing a significant increase in digital self-service interactions year-on-year. While the CRA does not attribute changes in call volumes directly to chatbot usage, the scale of adoption suggests meaningful demand for AI-enabled digital service delivery. The solution is designed to be modular and scalable, with strong controls to ensure transparency, appropriate content sourcing, and alignment with public-sector values. Human oversight, content governance, and clear user disclosures are integral to the design. This use case demonstrates how generative AI can enhance public service delivery while maintaining trust, accountability, and accessibility. Results, outcomes and impacts During its initial deployment, the chatbot handled over 1 million chat sessions and responded to more than 1.5 million questions. Uptake was measured through usage analytics, session volumes, and interaction counts. While call volume changes cannot be directly attributed to the chatbot, adoption levels indicate strong demand for digital self-service. Future impacts are expected to include improved access to information, increased service efficiency, and continued growth in digital engagement. Challenges and lessons learned Key challenges included ensuring accuracy, managing risks related to generative AI responses, and maintaining public trust. The CRA addressed these through clear user disclosures, limiting the chatbot to official web content, human oversight, and ongoing monitoring. Another challenge was setting appropriate expectations about the tool’s capabilities and limits. Lessons learned include the importance of strong governance from the outset, transparent communication with users, and phased implementation. Early monitoring and feedback mechanisms are critical to identify gaps and improve performance. Success depends on clear scope definition, senior leadership support, technical safeguards, and alignment with public service values such as fairness, accountability, and accessibility.

title: AI Enabled National Educators’ Competency Assessment
description: The AI-Enabled National Educator Competency Assessment was developed to address a key governance challenge: the absence of consistent, system-wide evidence on educator competencies at national scale. Prior to this initiative, workforce decisions related to professional development, performance management, and career progression relied on fragmented data sources. The Ministry of Education sought to establish a transparent, fair, and scalable national model capable of generating reliable competency insights across all Emirates. The initiative operationalises the National Educators’ Competency Framework through an AI-enabled adaptive assessment system deployed via the Kafaat talent management platform. The system applies adaptive testing methodologies that adjust question difficulty in real time and uses AI-assisted analytics to generate structured competency reports aligned to national standards. Secure digital proctoring safeguards integrity, while psychometric validation ensures reliability. AI outputs are used for decision support and are reviewed by authorised Ministry officials before they inform professional development or HR actions; access to results is role-based under Ministry data governance controls. To support national benchmarking, AI-assisted question generation has been used to develop an item bank of over 438,963 questions aligned to the competency framework; items undergo expert review and psychometric validation prior to deployment, and performance bands support consistent interpretation and targeted interventions. The assessment has been implemented nationwide across all Emirates, reaching approximately 15,000 educators across school leaders, teachers, specialists, and administrators. The first national cycle established a unified baseline of competencies. A second national cycle further embedded the system within performance management and structured career progression pathways, reflecting institutionalisation within Ministry governance processes. Within this national deployment, a focused leadership pilot of 200 educators was implemented for principals and vice-principals. Through AI-supported diagnostics, including competency benchmarking, performance simulations, and gap analysis, 97 candidates were shortlisted based on readiness indicators. Of these, 57 were identified as immediately suitable for leadership roles, while 40 were classified as high-potential future leaders and entered structured professional development pathways combining targeted training, coaching, and applied leadership practice. A rigorous post-assessment using the same AI-enabled framework validated growth and ensured objective promotion decisions. This integrated model enabled evidence-based leadership selection while establishing a sustainable talent pipeline aligned with UAE Vision 2031.

title: Use of ALIA (Spanish AI Infrastructure in Spanish and Co-Official Languages) in local entities’ intelligent assistants for citizens.
description: ALIA is Spain’s public and open AI infrastructure for Spanish and co-official languages. This ensures digital sovereignty and provides language models and related resources that public administrations, researchers and companies can use to build trustworthy AI services. Currently, every public administration that has implemented an AI-based assistant has done so by using a proprietary model (for example, ChatGPT), which not only costs money but also poses the potential risk of sending private data to companies whose values might not be aligned with public service. In order to test the usefulness of ALIA models in real-life scenarios, this initiative involves close collaboration with local entities to replace their current AI assistants with ALIA-based ones. If the project succeeds, public entities and citizens alike will benefit from a better, personalised service maintained by a free, public and sovereign infrastructure fully aligned with public service values. The project’s long-term goal is to keep making ALIA as robust and complete as possible so it can end up being used not only in every public AI project but also by companies and citizens. As an open-source "building block", ALIA also empowers the domestic economy. It allows SMEs, researchers, and developers to build specialised applications on a secure, sovereign foundation. This strategy prevents vendor lock-in, ensures that the economic and strategic value of AI remains within the national ecosystem, and guarantees that the AI tools used by the State are aligned with national values and administrative reality. Results, outcomes and impacts ALIA has established a secure foundation for AI in Spain, delivering publicly available language models and an open resource hub (ALIA Kit) with models, datasets, documentation and integration guidance for Spanish and co-official languages. Tests submitted by local entities where ALIA has been used report that the public model, while not as effective as the model it replaced, almost reaches the same number of correct answers in many cases, demonstrating that there is significant potential for the future of ALIA models. Entities have expressed their interest in continuing to use ALIA as their primary model for citizen assistance from now on.

title: REVI: Permissions with AI (Subnational: Municipality of Maipú)
description: REVI addresses structural inefficiencies in Chile’s building permit system, commonly referred to as “permisología.” Although the legal maximum timeframe for permit approval is 30 days, the real average reaches 126 days and can extend up to 249 days, generating legal uncertainty, administrative burden, and an estimated economic impact of 7.3% of GDP. The primary objective of the initiative is to improve regulatory consistency, reduce processing times, and strengthen legal certainty in municipal permit reviews. By supporting both applicants and municipal reviewers through AI assistants, REVI standardises regulatory interpretation, enhances the quality of submissions, and improves transparency in decision-making. The initial pilot began in September 2025 in the municipalities of Maipú and Providencia, later expanding to additional municipalities. Implementation follows a gradual approach and is accompanied by an impact evaluation conducted in collaboration with the University of Chile. REVI integrates with existing municipal digital platforms through a secure read-only protocol, ensuring institutional autonomy and system integrity. The long-term vision is to institutionalise REVI as part of the regular municipal permit review workflow and consolidate it as a national digital public good. By 2027, the initiative aims to be implemented in at least 55 municipalities across Chile, providing a scalable model that can be adopted nationwide to modernise regulatory processes and strengthen public trust. Results, outcomes and impacts REVI is currently in its pilot phase in Maipú and Providencia. As implementation is recent, consolidated quantitative results are not yet available. Early observations show improved completeness of applications and positive user feedback. A formal impact evaluation is underway with the University of Chile, comparing baseline processing times and file quality before and after implementation. Expected results include reductions of around 20% in review times when using Clara or Norman independently, and up to 25% when both are used together, contributing to greater regulatory consistency and transparency.

title: DCCEEW AI Ethics and Governance Framework
description: The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) initiative addresses a governance and risk gap arising from the increasing use of AI within the department, where existing enterprise risk, ICT and policy frameworks do not fully account for AI-specific risks. These include ethical risks (such as bias and unfair impacts), privacy and security risks, lack of transparency or explainability, inappropriate automation of decisions, and potential harm to public trust if AI is poorly governed. At the same time, the initiative seeks to leverage the opportunity for responsible AI adoption, recognising the benefits AI can deliver for efficiency, analysis, decision support and innovation, as well as the risk of not adopting AI where appropriate. The objectives of the framework are to: ensure AI is used in a safe, ethical, transparent and accountable manner across DCCEEW; operationalise whole-of-government AI policy and assurance requirements within departmental practice; embed risk-informed decision-making across the AI lifecycle through mandatory assessments, documentation and controls; clarify roles, responsibilities and accountability for AI use, including escalation of high-risk cases; and support public trust through transparency and disclosure of AI use. The framework is intended to be institutionalised through mandatory application to relevant AI use cases, integration with existing enterprise risk and governance arrangements, use of the AI Use Case Register, staff training, and oversight by established governance bodies. It will be reviewed at least annually and updated as technology, risks and whole-of-government policy evolve. Over time, it is expected to mature through the development of supporting guidelines for specific technologies and use cases, increased organisational capability, and closer alignment with evolving national AI assurance approaches. While departmental in scope, the framework is designed so it can be adapted by portfolio agencies, supporting broader consistency in public sector AI governance. Results, outcomes and impacts Increased engagement by staff with the document and process. More line areas have registered AI tools they are using or planning to use in the AI Use Case Register. As a result, more projects have been risk-assessed, with identified mitigation activities. Challenges and lessons learned Most line areas are asking for the guide to consider the environmental impact of GenAI.

title: IP First Response
description: IP First Response is a beta digital service developed by IP Australia to help individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises understand their options when dealing with potential intellectual property (IP) disputes. Many people facing IP infringement — whether they believe their rights have been infringed or they have been accused of infringement — are unsure where to start, what their options are, or what risks and costs may be involved. The initiative aims to reduce confusion at an early stage by providing clear, structured information about common pathways for addressing disputes and enforcing rights. The service also explores how modern technology can make government information easier to navigate and reuse. IP First Response includes an AI chatbot designed to help users find relevant information and understand possible next steps more quickly. In addition, the service provides downloadable content in formats that users can take to their preferred AI tools, allowing them to explore information in ways that suit their needs. The initiative also publishes machine-readable versions of its content to make trusted government information more accessible to developers and AI platforms. The objectives of the initiative are to improve access to clear and practical information about IP disputes, reduce the barriers individuals and businesses face when navigating complex issues, and explore how emerging technologies can support more accessible government services. The initiative also provides insights into how users interact with AI-assisted guidance, helping the organisation better understand how technology can support public service delivery while maintaining appropriate safeguards. IP First Response has been developed through an experimental innovation process, beginning with early research and concept development before progressing to a public beta service. As the initiative continues to evolve, insights from user feedback, analytics, and stakeholder engagement will inform decisions about how elements of the service could be integrated into IP Australia’s broader digital services. Lessons from the initiative are also expected to contribute to broader government discussions about the responsible use of AI to improve access to public information.

title: HackIA – AI Adoption Readiness Programme for Córdoba's Productive Sector (Subnational: Province of Córdoba)
description: Despite growing interest in Artificial Intelligence among businesses in Córdoba, a significant gap existed between awareness and effective adoption. Small and medium-sized enterprises — which represent the majority of the province's productive fabric — lacked the tools, knowledge, and connections needed to move from curiosity to concrete implementation. Most companies were using AI in fragmented, informal ways (e.g., basic use of generative tools) without a clear strategic vision or the organisational capacities required to scale AI-powered solutions. HackIA was designed to bridge this gap through a structured, territory-based programme that reached companies not only in the provincial capital but also in interior cities such as Río Cuarto, Villa María, San Francisco, and Marcos Juárez — making it one of the few AI adoption programmes to operate with a genuine territorial reach across a subnational jurisdiction. What are the objectives of the initiative? The programme has four core objectives: To raise awareness and build understanding of AI's potential applied to productive and commercial processes. To diagnose each company's organisational readiness to adopt AI technologies (AI Readiness Assessment). To develop initial prototypes of solutions to real business challenges through a corporate IAthon (AI hackathon). To generate strategic linkages between companies, technology providers, start-ups, and AI specialists through structured networking rounds. How is the initiative expected to evolve in the future? A second edition of HackIA is planned for 2026. Building on the learnings from the first cohort — which revealed that companies at similar stages of digital maturity and operating in the same sector share highly specific challenges, data structures, and adoption barriers — the 2026 edition will shift from a cross-sectoral format towards a sector-focused model. Rather than bringing together companies from across the productive fabric, each programme track will be designed around the particular logic, vocabulary, and constraints of a specific productive sector (such as agribusiness, metalworking, food processing, or logistics), enabling deeper, more contextualised engagement with AI adoption challenges that are genuinely sector-specific.

title: Consult
description: The UK government runs approximately 500 public consultations annually to gather citizen input on policy decisions. Analysing tens of thousands of written responses manually is slow, expensive, and creates a bottleneck in democratic policymaking. The process requires an estimated 75,000 working days per year, costing £20 million, and often takes months, delaying policy action and making frequent public engagement prohibitively expensive. Consult uses AI to automatically identify themes across thousands of consultation responses and categorise individual submissions, whilst keeping full human oversight at the core of the process. The tool employs a two-step approach: first generating themes from the responses, then mapping each response to relevant themes. Human analysts validate the themes and review AI categorisations, maintaining control over the analytical framework whilst eliminating time-consuming manual sorting. Results, outcomes and impacts Across seven consultations in 2025, Consult saved approximately 8,000 hours and over £250,000, whilst enabling faster policy responses to public input. For example, Consult analysed over 50,000 responses to the Independent Water Commission review in two hours (work that would have taken months manually). Evaluations have also found no evidence of additional bias. Analysis time reduced from months to hours (50,000 responses in two hours). Cost reduced from £100,000 per consultation to £240. Potential savings: £20 million annually across all UK government consultations. Performed better than the human-to-human baseline (83% vs 55% agreement). Sixty per cent of AI suggestions were accepted without changes by expert reviewers. Governments can run more consultations, respond faster to public input, and allocate analyst time to interpreting findings rather than manual categorisation, leading to more effective policymaking. Challenges and lessons learned Measure AI against realistic human baselines, not perfection. Human experts only agreed 55% of the time; AI achieving 83% exceeds typical human performance. Build public trust proactively through transparency. Consult was the first UK tool to complete an independent "Social Readiness Assessment" with public input on AI use in democratic processes. Design for human oversight at critical stages. AI categorises responses but humans validate themes and review mappings; never fully automate analysis of democratic input.

title: Minute
description: Local authorities deliver essential services to vulnerable residents through thousands of face-to-face interactions daily. Yet officers in these meetings face an impossible choice: be fully present with the person in front of them or ensure accurate documentation for case files. Traditional note-taking steals attention during the very moments when human connection matters most. This isn't just inefficient; it fundamentally undermines the trust and rapport essential to effective public service. After meetings, officers spend additional hours reconstructing conversations from fragmented notes. Minute creates the space for genuine human connection by removing the burden of documentation during meetings. The tool automatically transcribes meetings up to OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE classification, freeing front-line workers to be fully present with residents. Operating in the background on secure infrastructure, it identifies speakers, making it ideal for multi-speaker settings, captures complete discussions, and creates transcripts in flexible formats, allowing officers to focus entirely on the human interaction. In 2025, the tool was tested and consequently deployed across 22 local authorities as well as Ministerial Private Offices. Officers reported satisfaction in being able to focus on the person in front of them rather than note-taking. The code has been open-sourced on GitHub, enabling other organisations to adapt the solution. Results, outcomes and impacts All 22 local authorities that participated in the 2025 trial have deployed the tool owing to officers' reported satisfaction in enabling full attention during critical conversations with vulnerable residents. Multiple Ministerial Private Offices have adopted the tool. Code has also been published on GitHub to enable organisations to create customised versions for their specific needs, including Justice Transcribe, the Ministry of Justice's adaptation for transcriptions by probation officers. Challenges and lessons learned The 100% trial-to-deployment rate proves that solving genuine pain points and daily frustrations drives adoption far more effectively than top-down mandates. Documentation burden is universal across government, but implementation requirements vary. Open-source deployment allows organisations to adapt the tool to their own needs and nuances. It also helps accelerate delivery of solutions, while reducing duplication of effort. Leading with humanity at the centre, rather than pure productivity, can unlock genuine enthusiasm.

title: Use of AI - National Observatory of Strategic Foresight
description: The National Directorate of Strategic Foresight and Studies (DNPE) of Ceplan—the governing body of Peru’s National Strategic Planning System (Sinaplan) attached to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers—is leading an initiative to incorporate Artificial Intelligence (AI) into its technical analysis. This project uses AI chatbots (specifically GPT-4o) as methodological and editorial assistants to enhance the efficiency and quality of the National Observatory of Strategic Foresight. The AI supports the specialised team in processing technical sheets that cover conceptualisation, drivers, and strategic recommendations. Key Applications: a. Standardisation: Ensuring uniform structure across technical sheets. b. Editorial Improvement: Enhancing grammar, technical style, and conceptual precision. c. Data Extraction: Recovering text from images and charts. d. Monitoring: Automating news alerts and identifying relevant context signals. e. Content Updates: Suggesting recent evidence and references for validation. f. Analytical Support: Assisting with Stata, Python, or R code for data processing. Mandatory Human Oversight: A core principle of this initiative is that AI acts as a support tool, not an autonomous decision-maker. All AI-generated outputs are strictly reviewed and validated by the technical team to ensure veracity and methodological soundness. Technical Specifications: a. Model: GPT-4o (OpenAI). b. Capabilities: Multimodal LLM with advanced contextual reasoning and structured JSON output. c. Selection Criteria: Chosen for its stability in strategic classification and superior performance in complex comparative analysis. Results, outcomes and impacts Ceplan’s National Directorate of Strategic Foresight has achieved concrete results by integrating AI into its technical production: a. Standardisation: Improved consistency and comparability of "future events" technical sheets. b. Efficiency: Reduced time spent on editorial review and quality control, shifting focus to expert validation. c. Data Recovery: Enhanced conversion of images and scanned PDFs into editable text. d. Monitoring: Optimised daily tracking of emerging signals and news through automated, uniform reporting.

title: NegotiateCOP
description: Preparing for international climate negotiations such as the Conferences of the Parties (COP) requires delegations to review hundreds of submissions, position papers and technical documents. This process creates a significant information burden, particularly for smaller delegations with limited analytical capacity. As a result, structural disparities in resources between delegations can make it harder for some countries (especially LDCs or SIDS) to process the vast amounts of information involved in climate negotiations. NegotiateCOP was developed to address this challenge. The tool uses artificial intelligence to help negotiators quickly analyse and compare official submissions from the UNFCCC submission portal. By structuring and summarising key information from negotiation documents, it helps users identify the main priorities of different parties and understand where positions align or diverge. This allows negotiators to navigate large volumes of information more efficiently and focus their attention on the most relevant issues. The application provides AI-assisted tools to explore submissions, compare positions, and query documents, with all outputs linked to the original sources for verification. The long-term objective is to further develop NegotiateCOP as an open tool that can be freely used and further improved by governments and international partners. Its open-source design and co-development with users embody the principles of digital public infrastructure by promoting transparency, equity, and inclusive participation in climate negotiations. By making negotiation information more accessible and transparent, the initiative aims to support more inclusive, evidence-based and efficient multilateral decision-making processes, reducing barriers for smaller delegations and promoting equitable access to negotiation information. Results, outcomes and impacts NegotiateCOP enabled the analysis of more than 600 submissions from COP29 and COP30, helping users quickly identify key priorities and areas of alignment between parties. Early demonstrations generated strong interest among delegations, particularly among younger negotiators who were already familiar with AI tools. By making it easier to navigate large volumes of negotiation documents, the tool has the potential to reduce analytical barriers for smaller delegations and support more transparent and informed multilateral negotiations.

title: Path for Cohesion
description: “Hadin kai–bani fondo” (“the Path for Cohesion”) is a people-centred justice initiative in Niger addressing a major access-to-justice gap: land and shared natural resource disputes are frequent and serious, and are often managed first through customary authorities. Yet frontline actors (e.g., village and canton chiefs) and justice seekers may lack easy access to reliable, nationally aligned guidance, especially in low-connectivity and low-literacy contexts. The initiative leverages widespread access to basic mobile phones to deliver trusted guidance in voice format. The objective is to improve access to consistent, practical information that supports early prevention and resolution of disputes. The solution includes a “vocal companion”: a toll-free interactive voice service accessible from basic phones. Users call a free short code, ask questions verbally, and receive spoken, step-by-step guidance. Answers are grounded in a curated, nationally validated corpus using a constrained retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach, with pre-approved non-generative responses for sensitive topics to reduce misinformation, avoid conflicts with norms, and maintain alignment with nationally accepted guidance. The service complements customary and administrative pathways, supporting traditional leaders with updated information while preserving their legitimacy. The initiative was co-created through Niger’s 2023–2024 Justice Innovation Lab with government institutions, traditional leaders, civil society, farmers’ organisations, local authorities, and justice seekers. Governance is institutionally anchored: the Ministry of Justice leads, supported by a multi-actor committee (including ANAJJ, the Rural Code, the Association of Traditional Chiefs, and sectoral ministries). It is currently being piloted in Dosso and Tillabéri. The Ministry has launched it as a solution with potential for national scale-up and broader access for justice seekers. Future evolution is expected to include expanding language coverage beyond French, improving the voice user experience, and potentially extending content to other common dispute types, while maintaining strong national governance, validation, and review of the corpus.

title: Peruvian Tourism Facilitation Platform
description: The Tourism Facilitation Platform is a national initiative led by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Tourism of Peru (MINCETUR) to improve how travellers access official information before, during and after a trip. The project is designed as a digital public service with an AI-enabled, multilingual assistant and a curated knowledge base that brings together tourism-related guidance with information on migration, customs, health, vehicle entry and other travel procedures. Rather than asking travellers to navigate multiple institutions separately, the platform is intended to provide a clearer and more user-centred entry point. The initiative responds to a practical public-sector challenge: travel information relevant to tourists is often dispersed across different agencies, updated at different speeds and presented in formats that are not easy for travellers to understand. This can create avoidable friction, repeated queries, higher service loads for public agencies and a weaker visitor experience. MINCETUR therefore designed the initiative to strengthen facilitation, reduce information asymmetries and support safer, more predictable travel, while also improving institutional co-ordination around content, updates and service standards. Its main objectives are to: (1) provide reliable and timely travel information from official sources; (2) improve the tourist experience through simpler, multilingual and more personalised guidance; (3) support interoperability and collaboration among competent public entities; (4) promote trustworthy public-sector use of AI through human review, curated content, traceable updates and risk-aware implementation. The platform is still in development and testing, and has not yet been launched for public use. This makes the initiative especially relevant as a policy and governance entry, because it combines digital public infrastructure, AI adoption, institutional co-ordination and safeguards from the design stage. Looking ahead, MINCETUR expects to institutionalise the platform as a permanent facilitation service and progressively expand its content coverage, agency participation and service channels. Future scaling could include stronger integration with existing tourism information and protection services, broader multilingual coverage, analytics to improve service quality and the formal incorporation of operational protocols for data governance, quality assurance and responsible AI use. The initiative is also expected to generate lessons that can be replicated in other tourism and citizen-service contexts in Peru.

title: AI Literacy Framework (Subnational: Flanders Region)
description: The AI Literacy Framework was created to help public-sector employees understand and use artificial intelligence safely, responsibly and in line with the EU AI Act. Many government employees increasingly encounter AI in their daily work—whether through automated decisions, generative AI tools, or data-driven systems—yet often lack the knowledge and skills needed to interpret AI outputs, recognise risks such as bias or privacy concerns, or understand when human oversight is required. The initiative addresses this gap by providing a clear, structured approach to building AI literacy across all levels of government. The framework defines the essential competencies employees need (knowledge, skills and attitudes) captured in an ethical, government-specific competence model. It identifies three dimensions (“know why”, “know what”, “know how”) and translates them into practical capabilities such as ethical awareness, data literacy, responsible AI use, and the ability to assess AI outputs. These competencies are further operationalised through five AI personas that describe how different roles in the public sector interact with AI, from basic users to designers and strategic decision-makers. Each persona includes tailored competencies and suggested learning pathways, enabling organisations to align training, HR processes, and workforce planning with real needs. The objective of the initiative is to establish a shared and consistent foundation for AI literacy across Flemish public administrations. It supports organisations in meeting legal obligations under the EU AI Act, strengthens ethical and human-centred AI adoption, and ensures that staff are equipped to protect citizens’ rights when working with AI systems. By offering a common language, competence levels, and structured learning guidance, the framework helps HR departments, training providers, and policymakers integrate AI capabilities into organisational development, recruitment, and professional learning. Looking ahead, the framework is designed to be updated as AI technologies and regulatory requirements evolve. It will be institutionalised through integration with government-wide training programmes, ongoing collaboration with partners such as UNESCO and VAIA, and alignment with future competency frameworks on digital skills. The initiative is scalable: personas, competencies, and learning plans can be expanded, adapted for local governments, and incorporated into sector-specific policies, enabling the broader public sector to develop the workforce capacity needed for trustworthy and future-proof AI adoption.

title: Artificial Intelligence Readiness Stage Assessment
description: For this report for Mexico, the Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) is applied through the collaborative effort between UNESCO and the National Alliance for Artificial Intelligence (ANIA), with the generous participation of more than 250 individuals and organizations who contributed their experience and expertise on a wide variety of related topics. in very different ways, with the development and uses of artificial intelligence (AI).An open, plural and transparent call was made to form discussion tables with experts in the matters contemplated by the RAM. There were 18 multi-stakeholder tables organized into 6 thematic axes that included legislators, representatives of the federal and state governments, autonomous bodies, academia, experts, companies and business associations, as well as civil society organizations.This report is the result of the technical support that ANIA requested from UNESCO as of June 2023 to carry out a diagnosis of the development of AI in Mexico in order to identify the needs in terms of policies, regulation and ethical standards, as well as the design of AI governance schemes in the country. based on UNESCO's "Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence".Based on this diagnosis, understanding Mexico's strengths and challenges in AI, a list of policy recommendations was integrated from which four fundamental components emerge: 1) the development of a functional map of the ecosystem in which artificial intelligence lives and has an impact; 2) the integration of a legal framework for AI that starts from the consideration of existing applicable standards, to adapt or create what is necessary, innovating in regulatory forms; 3) create the institutional and governance design of AI that responds to the objectives and needs of public policies and regulation in this area and that involves different levels of government, academia, industry, and civil society in its decisions; and 4) issue the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, considering cybersecurity, an inclusive and human-centric ethical approach, taking into account its environmental sustainability, the attention to new educational and labor demands, as well as the need to promote infrastructure.

title: Empowering Education Leaders: A Toolkit for Safe, Ethical, and Equitable AI Integration
description: This toolkit is structured into three separate sections, each featuring modules that can be accessed in any order based on the specific needs and priorities of educational leaders:1. **Mitigating Risk: Protecting Student Privacy, Security, and Non-Discrimination (Modules 1-3)**. Understanding relevant federal laws, regulations, and guidelines is a crucial initial step for educational leaders planning to implement AI in schools. Leaders must be aware of how existing federal policies apply to their unique contexts. This section encourages leaders to explore privacy and data security obligations, the intersection of civil rights, accessibility, and digital equity with AI, and to carefully evaluate the potential benefits and risks of AI usage. It is particularly relevant for leaders aiming to proactively address issues of student safety, privacy, and security in their AI implementation plans.2. **Developing a Strategy for AI Integration in the Instructional Core (Modules 4-7)**. AI technologies have already become widespread in educational environments, making firsthand exploration essential for comprehension. Feedback from educators during listening sessions emphasized the importance of leveraging insights from previous educational technology advancements to create a clear and coherent strategy linked to the instructional core as a foundational step in AI planning, with the understanding that this strategy may need to be revised as more is learned about AI. Leaders identified three additional steps to enhance their strategy for effectively utilizing AI tools tailored to student needs: (1) engage with and inform their communities, (2) set priorities and establish a pace for implementation, and (3) support the execution of the community's strategy through a task force. This section offers resources to assist educational leaders in evaluating the evidence surrounding AI tools and guiding them through these three critical steps, making it suitable for leaders involved in or starting the strategic planning process for AI.3. **Maximizing Opportunity: Guiding the Effective Use and Evaluation of AI (Modules 8-10)**. While exploration and strategy development are vital initial phases, the Department encourages educational leaders to take an active role in directing the effective use of AI to improve teaching and student learning, whether for educator productivity or instructional purposes. Leaders highlighted three key steps for shaping AI usage: (1) fostering AI literacy among educators, (2) updating responsible use policies, and (3) creating a comprehensive system-wide plan. This section is designed for educational leaders who have established a clear strategy for AI use and are prepared to focus on guiding, shaping, and continuously assessing AI implementation.

description: The initiative aims to analyze the achievements and limitations of AI policies to date and seeks to maximize AI innovation capabilities while addressing shortcomings through a shift in policy paradigms by comprehensively considering the recent global AI market environment and Korea's potential.- Moving beyond the initial support for expanding AI infrastructure, the Korean government will focus on aiding the large-scale development and integration of AI infrastructure that private entities find challenging to tackle on their own.- In addition to fiscal investments, Korea intends to significantly improve the investment environment to encourage the private sector to invest more in AI.- Recognizing AI as national infrastructure, the government will promote a nationwide AI transition and support public-private collaboration to promote Korea's AI products and services beyond the domestic market and on the global stage.

title: ALAIT Austrian Lab for AI Trust
description: The Austrian Lab for AI Trust project (2024 - 2027) uses scientific methods to develop and test a new, interdisciplinary form of technology assessment for AI technologies that is based on the principles of trustworthy AI and pilots its application directly in society: it tests an AI Trust Lab with dialog formats and feedback loops for technology assessment in the sense of a participatory design. The project thus addresses an essential social setting for the development of social trust and governance in AI, that of the industries and professional groups that use AI, such as education, health, media or material goods production.The project consortium consists of the four partners winnovation, leiwand.ai, TU Vienna and APA, which have great scientific expertise in AI technologies, their quality assessment and social requirements for AI as well as innovative methodological approaches and a high dissemination power due to a strong anchoring in the Austrian AI ecosystem.Specifically, the R&D project will produce the following results, among others:- novel technology impact assessments for current AI technologies- AI technology profiles in visualized form, e.g. on AI chatbots or AI image recognition, which show the main opportunities and risks- Industry white papers on companies' AI requirements in connection with the implementation of standards- A new type of AI dialog format for professional groups/industries, the AI Trust Lab- For the purpose of scaling, a comprehensive AI Trust Lab network of AI-interested organizations (professional associations, companies) that conduct AI Trust Labs themselvesThrough a broad dissemination and exploitation strategy, the " Austrian Lab for AI Trust " empowers key stakeholder groups in society to deal with current AI technologies in an informed manner and to develop their own socio-technical standards for the ethical and high-quality use of AI in their respective industries and sectors.The project thus contributes to building trust in AI in three key dimensions: Creation of- transparency in the sense of accessibility of compact, comprehensive information on the effects of AI technologies- governance for the use of AI and its direct embedding and translation of standards into society and- AI literacy in the sense of acquiring knowledge and skills for dealing with current technologies.

title: AI Service Desk
description: Compliance with the AI Act is a key issue for a broad range of stakeholders who often face uncertainty and a lack of clarity on how the AI Act should be implemented. The Austrian AI Service Desk aims to help organisations achieve compliance with the AI Act and thus facilitate a smooth transition to a new regulatory framework for potential providers and deployers of AI systems. The AI Service Desk provides information on the AI Act, including through infographics, and responds to questions about its implementation, which are as a rule published after anonymisation as FAQs. Inaddition, it tenders studies on particular sectors or topics and organises events on key issues. Set up asof March 2024, the AI Service Desk has become a central contact point for regulatory questions relatedto the AI Act

title: National Digital Security Strategy
description: This strategy is based on four approaches: (1) "Whole-of-Society," which promotes multisectoral collaboration; (2) Human-Centered, which prioritizes the protection of digital rights; (3) Cyber Risk Management, which strengthens national resilience; and (4) Innovation and Capacity Development, which drives research and training in cybersecurity. It also has four specific objectives: consolidating digital security governance, improving national cyber resilience, developing the digital security workforce, and adapting and updating the cyber regulatory framework. AI plays a fundamental role in this strategy, as it aims to create strategies for the implementation of this technology with a defined risk assessment, ethical guidelines for the use of AI in digital security, the development of talent in AI applied to digital security, and the creation of frameworks for privacy protection in the context of AI and Big Data, among other goals.

title: Methodology to Identify Lessons Learned
description: Many organizations do not document or analyze their lessons learned for fear of criticism, sanctions, or simply because of time pressure on projects. This leads to the repetition of errors and the loss of opportunities for improvement. In addition, the lack of an organizational culture that encourages reflection prevents the generation of useful knowledge for future initiatives. The objective is to systematize the identification and documentation of lessons learned through artificial intelligence (AI), specifically ChatGPT, to ensure an objective, structured, and efficient process. The aim is for teams to be able to record positive and negative experiences without bias or tension, allowing for continuous improvement in project management. AI is expected to facilitate the identification of lessons learned in minutes, optimizing decision-making. In addition, the knowledge generated is expected to be reused in new projects, institutionalizing a learning management process that encompasses identification, documentation, dissemination, reuse, and evaluation. In the long term, the impact of using these lessons to improve organizational efficiency and evidence-based decision-making will be measured. Initially, lessons learned were identified through meetings between participants. However, the lack of a culture of sharing mistakes made consensus difficult. To overcome this barrier, AI was implemented to generate lessons learned objectively and without personal judgment. Today, the process has evolved into a more structured system that includes identification, documentation, dissemination, and evaluation of organizational learning.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (NAIS)
description: The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (ENIA) of Costa Rica, led by MICITT, aligns national efforts to promote the ethical, safe, and responsible use of AI, maximizing societal benefits while addressing potential risks. Validated through contributions from diverse sectors, ENIA establishes a roadmap for sustainable AI adoption and governance, positioning Costa Rica as a leader in responsible technological progress.ENIA emphasizes the integration of AI into Costa Rica's socioeconomic framework while leveraging its commitment to sustainability, equity, and human rights. The strategy highlights initiatives in talent development, including specialized AI education, reskilling, and upskilling programs, to prepare the workforce for an AI-driven economy. Building robust digital infrastructure, such as deploying 5G networks and establishing a National AI Center of Excellence, is also central to supporting research, development, and implementation of AI in strategic sectors.To mitigate AI-related risks, ENIA introduces a comprehensive risk management framework, strengthening MICITT's Cybersecurity Directorate to protect critical infrastructure and enhance resilience. On the global stage, Costa Rica advocates for ethical and sustainable AI frameworks, emphasizing regional collaboration on data management and equitable access to technology.By combining innovation, ethics, and international cooperation, ENIA positions Costa Rica to lead in shaping a future where AI advances humanity's well-being, ensuring inclusive and responsible technological progress.

title: AITHYRA Institute - Research Institute for Biomedical Artificial Intelligence
description: The AITHYRA Research Institute for Biomedical Artificial Intelligence, initiated by the Austrian Academy of Sciences and primarily funded by the Boehringer Ingelheim foundation, seeks to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence (AI) and biomedicine. The primary issue this initiative addresses is the complexity of biomedical data, which presents significant challenges in understanding and treating diseases. Traditional methods of data analysis are often insufficient in dealing with the vast and intricate datasets generated in biomedical research. AITHYRA aims to leverage the power of AI to analyse this data more effectively, thereby enabling advancements in diagnosis, treatment, and understanding of various diseases.The objectives of AITHYRA are multifaceted. Firstly, it aims to develop novel AI methodologies tailored to biomedical research, enhancing the capability to interpret complex data. Secondly, the initiative seeks to foster collaboration between different sectors, including academia, research-based companies, start-ups, and both Austrian and international universities and scientific institutions. By combining diverse expertise and resources, AITHYRA aspires to create a synergistic research environment. A key goal is to gain a deeper comprehension of biomedical interrelationships, which will help in better understanding diseases, enabling faster and more reliable diagnoses, and supporting the development of treatments for currently incurable diseases.As the initiative progresses, AITHYRA is expected to evolve by continuously integrating cutting-edge AI technology with biomedical research. The implementation involves establishing a robust infrastructure for research collaborations, attracting top talent in both AI and biomedicine, and securing ongoing funding and support from various stakeholders. Institutionalization could see AITHYRA becoming a central hub for AI-driven biomedical research in Austria and potentially on an international scale. Scaling the initiative more broadly could involve establishing partnerships with global health organizations and expanding the research network to include more international institutions, thereby amplifying its impact.Since its inception, AITHYRA has evolved by identifying key areas of biomedical research that can most benefit from AI interventions. Initial stages involved setting up collaborative frameworks and beginning joint research projects. Over time, the institute has grown in scope, incorporating more advanced AI technologies and expanding its research portfolio. Regular updates highlight progress in specific projects and breakthroughs in AI applications, demonstrating the institute's commitment to its mission. The future vision of AITHYRA includes not only advancing biomedical research but also contributing to the global knowledge pool, thereby shaping future healthcare paradigms and improving patient outcomes on a broader scale.

title: AI Advisory Board
description: The Advisory Board for Artificial Intelligence (AI Advisory Board “ KI-Beirat) was constituted on February 28th 2024. The eleven members of the AI Advisory Board are proven experts in the field of AI and have excellent knowledge in the areas of ethics, research, economics, law and technology. The AI Advisory Board will advise the Federal Government on issues relating to AI and pool knowledge on AI as a whole. An administrative support office for the AI Advisory Board is located at the Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting and Telecommunications (RTR-GmbH), which is also home to Austria's AI Service Desk.The AI Advisory Board's tasks include:- Advising and informing the Federal Government on technical, social and ethical issues relating to artificial intelligence- Observing the technological development of AI and assessing the associated opportunities and risks for Austria- Supporting the federal government in prioritizing and focusing on AI topics and measures- Strategic advice to the federal government in the context of development and implementation of Austria's AI strategy AIM AT 2020 and the associated implementation plans

title: AI Stakeholder Forum
description: The AI Stakeholder Forum, founded March 2024, consists of 30 diverse associations and interest groups: The broad range of associations covers amongst others organisations from the AI ecosystem, representatives of employers and labour, as well as organisations representing the interests of people with disabilities, youth and senior citizens. title: Data Strategy for Austria
description: Data has become a central factor in today's society and the further development of the economy. The intelligent use of data makes it possible to collect comprehensive information, generate knowledge and insights for evidence-based decision-making for policy, the economy and research. The national data strategy for Austria addresses the issues that data is too often not used and that cross-domain usability is often not possible. For that reason, the strategy provides a general strategic framework, with which the Federal Government intend to promote the exchange and broad use of data while maintaining data protection and security standards. The strategy defines three goals: develop sustainable data infrastructures and technical solutions for efficient data exchange, enable responsible data sharing and establish an innovative data culture as well as strengthen data literacy competences. 45 accompanying measures across the domains aim to strengthen the change towards proactive data use and data culture. For implementing the measures, the strategy foresees to establish a stakeholder forum, to exchange on best practices and actively engage with actors of the data economy. Additionally, the strategy foresees a cross-ministerial exchange platform to foster the sharing of knowledge between federal ministries and track the implementation of measures.

title: embrAIsme - Improving Conditions and Policies for SMEs to Embrace AI
description: The Interreg Europe project embrAIsme, led by Austria Wirtschaftsservice (aws), fosters collaboration between partners from Finland, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Bulgaria, Serbia, and Slovenia to enhance SME support for AI adoption. Running for four years from April 2024, the project is co-financed by the Federal Chancellery of Austria and aims to accelerate AI integration in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by addressing cultural resistance in SMEs, skill gaps, regulatory challenges, and limited funding access.AI offers vast potential for productivity, innovation, and competitiveness, yet many SMEs struggle with adoption due to internal resistance, lack of expertise, and uncertainty about AI's value. Structural barriers such as funding constraints, regulatory complexity, skill shortages, and insufficient infrastructure further hinder progress. embrAIsme seeks to create an enabling environment for AI adoption by improving policies, providing financial incentives, clarifying regulations, and raising awareness.The project focuses on six core intervention areas: Government Initiatives and Support, Access to Finance, Legal and Ethical Issues, Human Capital & Skills, Infrastructure and Technology Access, and Collaborative Networks and Ecosystems. Through study visits, workshops with AI experts and a strong focus on networking, policy recommendations will be provided to specific policy instruments to improve concepts and frameworks of funding opportunities and regulatory guidance needed for AI integration. By fostering knowledge-sharing, leadership engagement, and hands-on training, the initiative ensures SMEs across diverse regions benefit from AI-driven advancements.As AI adoption grows, the project will play a key role in maintaining SME competitiveness in an increasingly digital economy. Initial findings highlight cultural resistance in SMEs as a major challenge, prompting a stronger focus on leadership engagement, best-practice case studies, and AI-readiness initiatives. By continuously refining its strategies based on stakeholder insights, embrAIsme ensures that European SMEs are well-equipped to leverage AI for sustainable growth and innovation.

title: Overarching National AI Strategy
description: The usage and development of responsible AI in Denmark should be accelerated by four new national initiatives:1) The Digital Artificial Intelligence Taskforce rolling out AI solutions in the public sector on a large scale.2) A new research-based centre for advice on the responsible use of AI so that important knowledge about AI can be brought to life in governments and businesses.3) To accelerate the development of secure and transparent Danish language models to strengthen the foundation for the work on AI in companies and authorities.4) To make Danish data available open source to ensure that many more high-quality AI solutions can work in Danish.The new initiatives in this strategic endeavour do not stand alone. They should be seen in the context of the many other initiatives already in place or in the pipeline and in collaboration with leading countries and the EU. However, the new initiatives will help pave the way for more straightforward utilisation of AI across society. This is the government's ambition with the Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence Act (AI ACT)
description: The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, and will be fully applicable 2 years later on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions. It sets out risk-based rules for AI developers and deployers regarding specific uses of AI. It aims to address risks by categorising them into four different levels: unacceptable risk, high risk, limited risk, and minimal risk. The Code of Practice (published in July 10, 2025) is a voluntary tool that helps industry comply with the AI Act legal obligations on safety, transparency and copyright of general-purpose AI models. In the following weeks, Member States and the Commission will assess its adequacy. Additionally, the code will be complemented by Commission guidelines on key concepts related to general-purpose AI models, to be published still in July.
