title: "AI in Everyday Consumer Life" - Teaching Materials on Artificial Intelligence for Secondary School
description: This initiative aims to close the gap between the rapid pace of technological advancements and the more traditional structure of educational curricula. The material provides a comprehensive guide to teaching artificial intelligence in consumer contexts for students of Secondary School. It includes structured methods, lesson plans, and materials that help students explore AI's impact on everyday consumer life. Designed for Secondary school, the teaching materials aim to introduce students to the concept of AI and its applications in a way that is practical and age-appropriate. Students will begin by gathering associations about AI and learning what the term truly means. They will explore generative chatbots as tools and practice using them effectively. The materials also highlight the impact of AI on consumer behavior, including potential risks and drawbacks. Students will examine devices and applications that utilize AI, gaining an understanding of its specific functions and the societal contexts in which it is developed and applied. Finally, the materials encourage students to think critically about the future of AI, reflect on its development, and form their own perspectives on its potential impact.The main goals of the initiative are to enhance students' understanding of AI, develop practical skills such as interacting with generative chatbots, and explore the societal and ethical dimensions of AI's influence. It addresses potential challenges posed by AI, such as privacy concerns, job displacement, and algorithmic bias, by raising awareness and fostering ethical reflection. At the same time, it supports teachers by offering free, high-quality teaching materials and tools that allow them to effectively integrate AI topics into their lessons. These resources are freely available for download at www.konsumentenfragen.at, and accompanying workshops are provided to guide teachers in using the materials.Looking ahead, the initiative is set to expand. Starting in the summer semester of 2026, digital education will become a mandatory subject in schools. Materials like these will play a critical role in helping educators meet this requirement and ensure that students are equipped with essential digital competencies.

title: Enlightenment 4.0 “ Understanding AI decisions as a human being
description: The only right of affected persons under the AI Act that can be directly enforced against the deployer is provided for in Article 86, which states that persons affected by a high-risk AI-supported decision have a right to a clear and meaningful explanation of the role of the AI system in the decision-making process and of the main elements of the decision taken. This is particularly important to ensure that affected persons can understand how and why a particular decision was made. This right is of immense importance, as it often forms the basis for affected persons to be able to exercise their rights and, if necessary, assert legal claims.The project Enlightenment 4.0, commissioned by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection and led by the Research Institute - Digital Human Rights Center, aims to develop practical guidelines for dealing with the right to information under Article 86 of the AI Act. The right of access will be analyzed in conjunction with other data protection regulations, in particular Article 22 GDPR and Article 15 (1) (h) GDPR. A first interim report on the theoretical foundations of the right of access has already been prepared and will form the basis for the creation of a practical guide.

The only right of affected persons under the AI Act that can be directly enforced against the deployer is provided for in Article 86, which states that persons affected by a high-risk AI-supported decision have a right to a clear and meaningful explanation of the role of the AI system in the decision-making process and of the main elements of the decision taken. This is particularly important to ensure that affected persons can understand how and why a particular decision was made. This right is of immense importance, as it often forms the basis for affected persons to be able to exercise their rights and, if necessary, assert legal claims.The project Enlightenment 4.0, commissioned by the PLACE Federal Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection and led by the Research Institute - Digital Human Rights Center, aims to develop practical guidelines for dealing with the right to information under Article 86 of the AI Act. The right of access will be analyzed in conjunction with other data protection regulations, in particular Article 22 GDPR and Article 15 (1) (h) GDPR. A first interim report on the theoretical foundations of the right of access has already been prepared and will form the basis for the creation of a practical guide

title: Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence “A more robust foundation for the responsible development and use of AI in Denmark"
description: The usage and development of responsible AI in Denmark should be accelerated by four new national initiatives:1) The Digital Artificial Intelligence Taskforce rolling out AI solutions in the public sector on a large scale.2) A new research-based centre for advice on the responsible use of AI so that important knowledge about AI can be brought to life in governments and businesses.3) To accelerate the development of secure and transparent Danish language models to strengthen the foundation for the work on AI in companies and authorities.4) To make Danish data available open source to ensure that many more high-quality AI solutions can work in Danish. The new initiatives in this strategic endeavour do not stand alone. They should be seen in the context of the many other initiatives already in place or in the pipeline and in collaboration with leading countries and the EU. However, the new initiatives will help pave the way for more straightforward utilisation of AI across society. This is the government's ambition with the Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence.

title: AI subject curricula: Artificial Intelligence - From Theory to Practice
description: "Artificial Intelligence “ From Theory to Practice" is a national-level educational initiative in Croatia that aims to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) and its practical applications. Launched in response to the growing demand for digital and AI-related competencies in the workforce, this initiative seeks to equip secondary school students and teachers with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in AI technologies. By integrating AI into the formal education curriculum, the project addresses a critical skills gap and prepares the next generation for active participation in the digital economy.The primary objectives of the initiative are threefold: first, to raise awareness and understanding of AI among students and educators; second, to build technical skills and critical thinking around the development and use of AI tools; and third, to promote ethical and responsible AI practices. To achieve these goals, the program offers a comprehensive AI curriculum co-designed with academic experts, industry stakeholders, and education authorities. It includes modules on machine learning, data analysis, computer vision, and natural language processing, supported by real-world case studies and interactive learning platforms.Initially piloted in a select number of schools, the initiative has gradually expanded nationwide, reaching hundreds of educators and thousands of students. Teachers undergo specialized training and certification to ensure consistent, high-quality delivery of content. The program also incorporates feedback loops, allowing continuous refinement based on classroom experience and emerging technological trends. Furthermore, partnerships with universities, tech companies, and government bodies enhance the program's relevance and scalability.Looking ahead, "Artificial Intelligence “ From Theory to Practice" is positioned to serve as a model for regional and international replication. Its future evolution includes integrating AI into other STEM subjects, scaling the program to primary education, and aligning with broader EU digital education strategies. As AI continues to reshape economies and societies, Croatia's early investment in AI literacy through this initiative represents a forward-thinking approach to national capacity-building and digital inclusion.

title: Mandatory Guardrails for Safe and Responsible AI
description: The potential for Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve social and economic well-being is immense. AI development and deployment is accelerating and is already permeating institutions, infrastructure, products and services. This often occurs undetected by those engaging with it.The Australian Government's consultations on safe and responsible AI have shown that our current regulatory system is not fit for purpose to respond to the distinct risks that AI poses. Internationally, governments are reforming existing regulations and introducing new regulations to address the risks of AI, with a focus on creating preventative, risk-based guardrails that apply across the AI supply chain and throughout the AI lifecycle. To unlock innovative uses of AI we need a modern and effective regulatorysystem.In the Australian Government's interim response to the Safe and Responsible AI in Australia discussion paper, a commitment was made to a develop a regulatory environment that builds community trust and promotes AI adoption. The guardrails outlined complement those in the Voluntary AI Safety Standard, and set clear expectations from the Australian Government on how to use AI safely and responsibly. They aim to address risks and harms from AI, build public trust and provide businesses with greater regulatory certainty. Implementing the Voluntary AI Safety Standard now will help businesses start to develop practices required in a future regulatory environment.Consultation on the proposed mandatory guardrails is now closed.Government is now considering the feedback received and next steps.

title: Vision on Generative AI
description: Specific areas mentioned include: Safety: Ensuring the safe development and use of generative AI, including mitigating misuse, accidents, and systemic safety risks. Justice: Ensuring lawful development and application that takes into account existing laws and regulations, equal opportunities, and non-discrimination. Well-being and autonomy: Promoting applications of generative AI that serve human well-being and secure human autonomy. Sustainability and prosperity: Encouraging generative AI that contributes to sustainability and increases prosperity. These policy areas imply a wide spectrum of actions, from promoting innovation (e.g. by pilots and promoting an AI-ecosystem) and education to engaging in international collaborations and enforcing and implementing regulation. The goal is to find a balance between leveraging the benefits of generative AI and managing the risks and challenges. The development of the government-wide vision on generative AI was characterized by an open approach with a wide range of involved stakeholders. These stakeholders ranged from experts in various domains to the general public, and their input was collected and assessed in various ways. Key points of this approach include: Sectoral Sessions: Between June and November 2023, multiple sessions were held in sectors such as public administration, healthcare, employment, and the economy. During these sessions, input for the vision was collected, and it was continually checked that the vision covered the correct aspects. These conversations will continue into 2024. Collaborations: In collaboration with the ECP (Electronic Commerce Platform) and the Dutch AI Coalition (NL-AIC), meetings were organized with stakeholders from the media, higher education, healthcare, and the police to discuss ethical dilemmas surrounding generative AI. Awareness and Impact Analysis: Sessions were organized with Dutch citizens to raise awareness about generative AI and to gain insights into how people perceive the impact of generative AI on their lives and the role of the government in integrating this technology into society. Broad Representation: A working group on generative AI was set up with participants from various ministries, provinces (IPO), and municipalities (VNG) to ensure that the vision reflects a broad perspective on generative AI. Advisory Group: An advisory group with members representing diverse societal perspectives was established to test the vision from various angles. This approach underscores the importance of inclusivity and collaboration with a broad range of stakeholders to arrive at a well-supported and informed vision on generative AI.

These stakeholders ranged from experts in various domains to the general public, and their input was collected and assessed in various ways. Key points of this approach include: Sectoral Sessions: Between June and November 2023, multiple sessions were held in sectors such as public administration, healthcare, employment, and the economy. title: Law 5142/2024 Completion of land registration, simplification of procedures, use of artificial intelligence and provisions for the operation of the Hellenic Land Registry Cadastre", other provisions of the Ministry of Digital Governance.
description: The Hellenic Cadastre, responsible for managing property records, previously encountered delays and inefficiencies due to the manual processing of paper documents for property transactions. This often meant citizens were waiting months or even years to legally own their property. To overcome these challenges, the cadastre developed a system to automate the reading and categorization of property contracts, apply the relevant legal rules, and then generate assessments for approval using AI.Law 5142/2024 addresses inefficiencies in land registration and leverages AI to enhance the accuracy and speed of cadastral processes. It aims to modernize the Greek Cadaster, ensuring legal security and reducing bureaucracy.Objectives:Complete land registration and simplify procedures.Integrate AI to improve cadastral accuracy and speed.Enhance legal security and reduce long-term legal disputes.The new AI tool, which is already in pilot operation, can read the text of the contract in natural language, identify the type of transaction, identify the elements required under legal rules, apply an automatic completeness check of the elements of a contract, such as updates and ENFIA declaration, as well as generate an automatic recommendation to the supervisor to approve or reject elements of the contract. This results in significant time and cost savings for the State, as a process that currently costs 15 euros could cost as low as 30 cents.It is noted that the final decision will continue to be taken by the competent supervisor, but the AI tool will greatly facilitate his/her work by providing a ready-made recommendation that will highlight exactly the points of the contract that need attention.The new tool was created by the Ministry of Digital Government at no cost, is very simple to use and was implemented using Microsoft Azure Open AI technology. The development and hosting of the system was supported by Microsoft, ensuring the high technological quality and reliability of the tool.The framework can scale by expanding its AI capabilities and integrating additional public services, fostering broader digital transformation across Greece.Since its enactment, the law has seen updates to align with the EU's AI Act and other international standards, ensuring continuous improvement and relevance. Regular updates and enhancements have been made to improve the system's efficiency and user experience.

title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard
description: The 10 guardrails at a glance:1. Establish, implement and publish an accountability process including governance, internal capability and a strategy for regulatory compliance.2. Establish and implement a risk management process to identify and mitigate risks.3. Protect AI systems, and implement data governance measures to manage data quality and provenance.4. Test AI models and systems to evaluate model performance and monitor the system once deployed.5. Enable human control or intervention in an AI system to achieve meaningful human oversight across the life cycle.6. Inform end-users regarding AI-enabled decisions, interactions with AI and AI-generated content.7. Establish processes for people impacted by AI systems to challenge use or outcomes.8. Be transparent with other organisations across the AI supply chain about data, models and systems to help them effectively address risks.9. Keep and maintain records to allow third parties to assess compliance with guardrails.10. Engage your stakeholders and evaluate their needs and circumstances, with a focus on safety, diversity, inclusion and fairness.

title: Twelfth Development Plan (2024-2028)
description: The Development Plan aims to provide a long-term perspective and unity of purpose for all members of society. The development process has followed a holistic approach based on the principles of human orientation, participation, inclusiveness, accountability, and transparency. The Plan was developed through a participatory approach with contributions from the public sector, private sector, civil society representatives, and academic circles. During the preparatory phase, 60 specialized commissions and 27 working groups were established, and approximately 8,500 people participated in the meetings. title: Regulatory Sandbox for AI
description: As part of Denmark's national digitalization strategy, the Danish Agency for Digital Government and the Danish Data Protection Agency have launched a regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence. This initiative aims to help organizations navigate complex legal requirements while developing or deploying AI solutions, particularly focusing on data protection and compliance with upcoming EU legislation, such as the AI Act. The sandbox addresses the growing need for clarity around how existing and emerging laws apply to AI, ensuring innovation is both responsible and legally sound.The main goal of the initiative is to support the development and use of high-quality, trustworthy AI by providing tailored, hands-on guidance in a controlled environment. Participating organizations receive project-based advice on how to align their AI projects with GDPR requirements and, eventually, the AI Act. By offering legal certainty and regulatory insight early in the development process, the sandbox helps reduce risks, prevent project abandonment, and shorten the time from innovation to implementation.Initially, the sandbox focuses on GDPR compliance as a foundational element for responsible AI. As the European Union finalizes and enforces the AI Act, the sandbox will expand its scope to include guidance on this regulation as well. This approach ensures that both private companies and public authorities can adapt to the new rules gradually, building capacity and confidence in applying legal principles to real-world AI use cases.Looking ahead, the sandbox is expected to grow into a permanent mechanism for fostering responsible AI innovation in Denmark. The model may also serve as a blueprint for similar initiatives across Europe or within specific sectors, such as health, finance, or public services. By institutionalizing regulatory support and promoting cooperation between developers and authorities, the sandbox represents a proactive, future-oriented approach to AI governance that balances innovation with legal and ethical responsibilities.

title: FAIR-AI - Fostering Austria's Innovative Strength and Research excellence in Artificial Intelligence
description: FAIR-AI focuses on the requirements of the upcoming European AI law and the obstacles to its implementation in the day-to-day development and management of AI-based projects and its AI law-compliant application. These obstacles are multi-faceted and arise from technical reasons (e.g. intrinsic technical risks of current machine learning such as data shifts in a non-stationary environment), technical and management challenges (e.g. the need for a highly skilled workforce, high initial costs, and project management-level risks), and socio-technical application-related factors (e.g. the need for risk awareness in the application of AI, including human factors such as cognitive biases in AI-assisted decision-making).In this context, we consider the detection, monitoring and, when possible, anticipation of risks at all levels of system development and application as a key factor. In this regard, FAIR-AI follows a methodology to disentangle these types of risks. Rather than demanding a general solution to this problem, our approach takes a bottom-up strategy by selecting typical pitfalls in a specific development and application context to create a collection of instructive, self-contained use cases, which are implemented in research modules, to illustrate the intrinsic risks.We go beyond the state of the art to explore ways of risk disentanglement, prediction, and their integration into a recommender system capable of providing active support and guidance.FAIR-AI focuses on the requirements of the upcoming European AI law and the obstacles to its implementation in the day-to-day development and management of AI-based projects and its AI law-compliant application. title: AI implementation plan for 2024 and the following years
description: The federal government's national strategy for artificial intelligence (AI) was published in 2021 under the title Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030). In principle, the AI strategy is an agile strategy that can be further developed against the backdrop of rapidly changing technological, legal and social developments.In this sense, the AI Implementation Plan 2024 is not only a first interim report, but also a supplement to and specification of the AIM AT 2030. The implementation plan contains 47 measures and AI projects from all twelve federal ministries that are being implemented or planned in the short to medium term. The measures presented are based on four horizontal and four vertical priorities:Horizontal priorities (guiding principles of all measures): Trustworthiness of AI; Resilience and security of and through AI; Climate neutrality and sustainability of and through AI; Technology sovereignty and business locationVertical priorities (specific application domains): Research, innovation and business; Education and skills; Administration and citizen services; Governance and strategies.Examples of some of the 47 measures in the 2024 Implementation Plan include: AI focus in the 2025–27 performance agreement for public universities; Establishment of an “Austrian Competence Center for Digital Farming”; Preparation of an AI Hub Austria in the area of research and innovation; AI literacy focus of the digital competence offensive; Improvement of digital administrative services through AI-supported tools, such as testing an LLM chatbot for questions about ID Austria; Creating a suitable legal framework for AI in the healthcare sector.

title: AI Upskilling Fund
description: The UK government announced a £7.4 million pilot scheme to subsidise the cost of AI skills training for SMEs in the Professional Business Services sector. Of this, £6.4 million of grant funding is available. This pilot is funded through the £37.5 million Labour Market Evaluations and Pilots fund (LMEP), announced by the Chancellor at Spring Budget 2023.Eligible businesses can apply for up to 50% of the cost of AI skills training. This training should support employees to develop their technical skills and/or understanding of AI, helping them develop, deploy, or use AI in their role.Evidence shows that a lack of AI skills in businesses is hindering AI adoption, in part due to low investment in AI upskilling by UK businesses. This is particularly true in smaller companies. The pilot aims to increase AI adoption and productivity by incentivising greater employer-led investment in skills and training. Eligible businesses could apply for funding for up to 50% of the cost of AI skills training and other AI upskilling activities. The training should support employees to develop their technical skills and/or understanding of AI, helping them develop, deploy, or use AI in their role.Specifically, the objectives of the pilot are to:(1) Stimulate employer investment in AI training.(2) Address AI skills gaps in the UK workforce that are limiting AI adoption.(3) Measure the impact of AI upskilling on business productivity and outcomes.

title: Assuring a Responsible Future for AI
description: AI is transforming the way we live and work, and rapid developments in its capabilities provide exciting new opportunities to improve the lives of UK citizens.AI has the potential to radically transform public services across the UK, driving a modern digital government which gives people a more satisfying experience and their time back. It also has an important role to play in realising this government's 5 missions to rebuild Britain, including building a National Health Service (NHS) fit for the future and kickstarting economic growth. AI is already providing new ways to identify and treat disease and is transforming the speed and accuracy of diagnostic services. There are early indications that the UK AI market could grow to over $1 trillion (USD) by 2035, demonstrating its enormous economic potential.However, to fully realise its potential, AI must be developed and deployed in a safe and responsible way with its benefits more widely shared. Like all technological innovation, the use of AI poses risks; for example, bias, privacy, and other socio-economic impacts like job loss. Identifying and mitigating these risks will be key to ensuring the safe development and use of AI and driving future adoption.AI assurance provides tools and techniques to measure, evaluate and communicate the risks posed by AI across complex supply chains. It can help to demonstrate the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems, and their compliance with existing ” and future ” standards and regulations. AI assurance is therefore a key driver of safe and responsible¨AI innovation. The UK government is taking action to realise the benefits of AI and ensure it is developed and deployed safely, equitably, and responsibly across Britain.The UK government will look to mitigate the risks associated with AI and drive adoption of safe and responsible AI by maximising future growth of the UK's AI assurance market. Our proactive, targeted actions will increase demand and supply in the UK market and unlock its global potential.

title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: Open consultation
description: Two major strengths of the UK economy are its creative industries and AI sector. Both are essential to drive economic growth and deliver the government's Plan for Change.The UK government is determined to build on the strengths of the UK AI sector, and will set out an ambitious roadmap leveraging AI to grow the economy and improve public services through the AI Opportunities Action Plan (AIOAP).The UK government also recognises the continued economic and cultural contributions of our world-leading creative industries. Copyright is a key pillar of our creative economy. It exists to help creators control the use of their works and allows them to seek payment for it. However, the widespread use of copyright material for training AI models has presented new challenges for the UK's copyright framework, and many rights holders have found it difficult to exercise their rights in this context. It is important that copyright continues to support the UK's world-leading creative industries and creates the conditions for AI innovation that allows them to share in the benefits of these new technologies.This consultation seeks views on proposals to deliver against the government's objectives for this area, which are:(1) Boosting trust and transparency between sectors, by ensuring AI developers provide right holders with greater clarity about how they use their material.(2) Enhancing right holders' control over whether or not their works are used to train AI models, and their ability to be paid for its use where they so wish.(3) Ensuring AI developers have access to high-quality material to train leading AI models in the UK and support innovation across the UK AI sector.Additionally, the consultation addresses other emerging issues, including copyright protection for computer-generated works, and the issue of digital replicas.As AI evolves rapidly, the UK's response must adapt. The consultation is an opportunity for anyone with an interest in these issues to share their views and provide evidence regarding the economic impact of these proposals. During the consultation, we will also run wider engagement activity to help ensure that the full range of views is heard.

text: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: Open consultation. Two major strengths of the PLACE economy are its creative industries and AI sector. Both are essential to drive economic growth and deliver the government's Plan for Change.The PLACE government is determined to build on the strengths of the PLACE AI sector, and will set out an ambitious roadmap leveraging AI to grow the economy and improve public services through the AI Opportunities Action Plan (AIOAP).The PLACE government also recognises the continued economic and cultural contributions of our world-leading creative industries. Copyright is a key pillar of our creative economy. It exists to help creators control the use of their works and allows them to seek payment for it. However, the widespread use of copyright material for training AI models has presented new challenges for the PLACE's copyright framework, and many rights holders have found it difficult to exercise their rights in this context. It is important that copyright continues to support the PLACE's world-leading creative industries and creates the conditions for AI innovation that allows them to share in the benefits of these new technologies.This consultation seeks views on proposals to deliver against the government's objectives for this area, which are:(1) Boosting trust and transparency between sectors, by ensuring AI developers provide right holders with greater clarity about how they use their material.(2) Enhancing right holders' control over whether or not their works are used to train AI models, and their ability to be paid for its use where they so wish.(3) Ensuring AI developers have access to high-quality material to train leading AI models in the PLACE and support innovation across the PLACE AI sector.Additionally, the consultation addresses other emerging issues, including copyright protection for computer-generated works, and the issue of digital replicas.As AI evolves rapidly, the PLACE's response must adapt. The consultation is an opportunity for anyone with an interest in these issues to share their views and provide evidence regarding the economic impact of these proposals. During the consultation, we will also run wider engagement activity to help ensure that the full range of views is heard

title: GenAI Team at the CaMiNO
description: The main tasks of the Team established by the Regulation No. 166 of the Rector of the University of Lodz Rector of 29 September 2023 include: analysis of trends related to the development of generative artificial intelligence and assessment of their relevance to the education sector and the conduct of research; close cooperation with external experts and institutions working for the responsible and ethical development of generative AI, including in particular the education and research sectors; identification of opportunities and possibilities for the use of generative AI tools at the University of Lodz, as well as potential threats resulting from their development for the scientific and research, teaching and administrative processes carried out at the university; analysis of the needs and expectations related to the development of generative artificial intelligence of all members of the academic community (students, researchers, teaching and administrative staff); promotion of knowledge of generative AI tools and the conditions for their use (legal, ethical, cultural, etc.) in the teaching, research and administrative processes among members of the academic community and recommendation of forms and tools to improve skills and competences within this area; promotion of good national and international practices in terms of using generative AI tools in the teaching, research and administrative processes. title: Digital Task Force for AI
description: The Digital Task Force for AI in Denmark was established to address the challenges and opportunities presented by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies. The initiative seeks to ensure that Denmark remains at the forefront of AI innovation while promoting ethical, responsible, and inclusive AI adoption across public and private sectors. It aims to tackle issues such as data privacy, AI governance, transparency, and the impact of AI on society and the labour market.The primary objectives of the Task Force include developing national strategies and guidelines that support trustworthy AI, fostering collaboration among government agencies, academia, and industry, and promoting public awareness and education about AI technologies. By coordinating efforts across sectors, the initiative works to create an AI ecosystem that balances innovation with ethical considerations, ensuring AI benefits all citizens and respects fundamental rights.Looking forward, the Digital Task Force for AI is expected to evolve into a permanent body that continuously monitors AI developments and advises policymakers on emerging risks and opportunities. It will institutionalize AI governance frameworks and encourage the integration of AI in public services while maintaining transparency and accountability. The initiative also plans to expand its outreach, facilitating international cooperation and knowledge exchange to strengthen Denmark's position in the global AI landscape.Since its inception, the initiative has grown from a coordinating task force to a more structured and collaborative platform involving diverse stakeholders. It has contributed to national AI policies, supported pilot projects, and enhanced dialogue on AI ethics and regulation. Ongoing updates reflect the fast-paced AI environment, ensuring that Denmark's approach remains adaptive and proactive in addressing new technological and societal challenges.

description: The Agency for Digital Governance (DIGG) and the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) will develop guidelines to promote the efficient, safe and ethical use of generative AI in public administration. The guidelines will serve as a guide and support in the use of generative AI for employees at government agencies, municipalities and regions from legal, security and ethical perspectives. In order to increase the use of AI in public administration, it is also important that people in management functions have access to the support needed to use the technology. The guidelines will therefore also serve as a methodological support and, based on legal, security and ethical aspects, provide guidance for the operations' assessments of whether and, if so, how generative AI should be used. In this respect, the guidelines will also support public administration in taking advantage of generative AI in a way that fosters innovation and development. However, the guidelines developed within the framework of the assignment should not target the use of generative AI in education or research. If the authorities deem it appropriate, the guidelines can be supplemented with training material or a sample catalogue, to show the possibilities of using generative AI in public administration. The activities conducted in public administration are very broad, which means that generative AI is already used to varying degrees. Internal guidelines or recommendations for generative AI have been developed to varying degrees within different government agencies, which can contribute expertise and experience of the use of generative AI in public administration. The purposes of the use of generative AI in public administration differ between different activities. In addition, depending on their size, the businesses have different conditions for promoting the use of AI on their own. The authorities must therefore conduct a dialogue with the relevant public and private actors during the implementation of the assignment. The work on the guidelines will make use of already existing knowledge support, e.g. The trust model for AI managed by DIGG. The guidelines shall be based on current regulations and be based on the state's core values in order to create trust, transparency and build trust. In so far as the guidance relates to data protection, it is produced and decided by the IMY in its capacity as an independent data protection authority. However, DIGG will coordinate the authorities' work to develop the guidelines. The assignment will also contribute to increasing the level of knowledge about the opportunities and limitations of AI in public administration. During the implementation of the assignment, DIGG will offer competence-enhancing initiatives to smaller actors in public administration in order to promote the administration's appropriate and efficient use of AI. DIGG can offer smaller municipalities, regions and authorities support in how they can use AI.

instrument: Principles/guidelines/frameworks for trustworthy AI
oecd_principles: 2.3 Shaping an enabling interoperable governance and policy environment for AI
organisation: The Swedish Government, the Swedish Agency for Digital Governance and the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection

title: AI Regulatory Sandbox
description: The AI Regulatory Sandbox, developed in collaboration with the European Commission, is a digital space that seeks to connect competent authorities with AI development companies to jointly define best practices when implementing future European AI regulation, and ensure its application.The AI Sandbox will be implemented by two focus groups and they will work on the publication of initial guidelines. The initiative will include a quality label. Final deliverables with the implementation guidelines, the good practices and the lessons learnt developed in the sandbox, will be published during the Spanish Presidency of the UE Council.The initiative has the following objectives:Connect competent authorities with companies developing AI and together find the best way to operationalize the future obligations of the AI regulation in easy-to-follow & future-proof good practice guidelines and other supporting materials.

title: University-Business Chairs on AI
description: The National IA Strategy (ENIA) Measure N. 9 establishes the objective to "Promote a wider range of AI-oriented training in vocational and university education and training", and within the Action Line N. 2, the strategy plans to "Promote the development of digital skills, strengthen national talent and attract global talent".This measure will reinforce AI research activities, creating a solid knowledge body to nurture training offer in different fields. It also aims to strengthen dissemination activities, public-private collaboration and the promotion of teaching in the field of AI, thereby helping to place Spanish universities at the technological forefront.The initiative has the following objectives:Creation of a set of university-business chairs to develop the application of AI, both at national and international levelsPromoting the development of AI scientific research with a multidisciplinary approach, and the development of research projects that be transferred to industryPromoting knowledge transfer between universities and companies at a transversal level in health, sustainability, rights or the data economy

title: AI factory - Pharos
description: The Pharos project will serve as a hub for academia, research, the public sector, and private enterprises, aiming to develop innovative AI-driven services. Its focus will span the sectors of Health, Culture and Language and Sustainability. In doing so, it will play a crucial role in fostering the growth and ongoing support of an innovative and competitive ecosystem of startups and SMEs.The project has a total budget of 30 million, funded 50% by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking and 50% by National Resources. The project is scheduled to commence in March 2025, with a total duration of 36 months.This initiative is a flagship project under the Blueprint for Greece's AI Transformation, developed by the High Level Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence (AI) The project will leverage the high-performance computing infrastructure of the DAEDALUS supercomputer, enabling seamless collaboration with other European infrastructures. The cooperation amongst AI Factories across countries, will ensure the collective data produced can be utilized for the benefit of all European citizens.An ecosystem of innovative best practices will be developed in Greece that will:Enhance competitiveness by providing advanced computational resources, access to big data, and specialised human expertise.Support the development of reliable AI services aligned with European AI regulations (AI Act).Promote innovation in the targeted key industrial sectors, i.e. sustainability, through satellite data analysis for natural resource management and mitigating the effects of climate change.Invest in human capital via training programs, fostering academic collaborations, upskilling and attracting talent in the AI domain.Ensure innovation by connecting with EDIHs, Data Spaces, National Competence Centers (NCCs), and key projects such as DeployAI, ALT-EDIC4EU, LLMs4EU, amongst others.Foster a cross-border innovation ecosystem through AI, delivering widespread benefits for all EU countries.The Pharos project will be managed and operated by the National Infrastructures for Research and Technology (GRNET), operating under the auspices of the Greek Ministry of Digital Governance. It is coordinated by a consortium of partners which include the National Centre for Scientific Research DEMOKRITOS (NCSRD), the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), the Athena Research Center, and the GrowthFund, in close collaboration with the Special Secretariat of Foresight of the Government.Affiliated Bodies include: a) The National Center for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH), b) Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (AUTH), c) National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA), d) Foundation for Research and Technology - Hellas (FORTH), e) University of Piraeus (UNIPI), as well as the National Documentation Centre (EKT) and IDIKA S.A., both operating under the auspices of the Greek Ministry of Digital Governance.

title: Slovene Early Stage Innovation Fund
description: This equity financing programme, offered by the Slovene Enterprise Fund , targets innovative SMEs with strong growth potential and an international orientation. Its main goal is to accelerate the development and scaling of companies that are advancing Slovenia’s green and digital transformation . Key features include: Equity capital provision – offering funding to early-stage and growth-phase SMEs that might otherwise face difficulty accessing traditional financing. Target beneficiaries – innovative micro, small, and medium-sized companies contributing to sustainability, digitalisation, and technological innovation. Focus on global growth – supporting start-ups and scale-ups that aim to compete and expand internationally. Alignment with national and EU priorities – advancing both green transition goals and digital economy objectives , in line with EU frameworks. Through this initiative, the Slovene Enterprise Fund helps companies: Access capital for product development, market expansion, and innovation . Enhance competitiveness and technological capabilities . Contribute to national strategic goals , including sustainability, digitalisation, and global economic integration. This programme complements Slovenia’s broader ecosystem of start-up and innovation support, working alongside initiatives such as P2 , Digital Transformation incentives , and SID Bank equity financing to provide a comprehensive set of funding instruments for high-tech and innovative SMEs.

title: #BeDigitalTogether
description: The #BeDigitalTogether initiative in Belgium focuses on fostering a more diverse and inclusive digital workforce , with a particular emphasis on artificial intelligence and related technologies. By targeting underrepresented groups, the programme aims to create equal opportunities for participation, learning, and career advancement in the tech sector. Key objectives include: Reducing barriers to entry for underrepresented populations in the digital and AI workforce. Promoting equitable access to training, mentorship, and employment opportunities . Raising awareness about the importance of diversity in technology and AI development. Supporting a sustainable and inclusive tech ecosystem , which leverages diverse perspectives for innovation. Through workshops, outreach, and networking initiatives, #BeDigitalTogether helps build a more inclusive digital landscape in Belgium , ensuring that AI and other emerging technologies benefit from a broader range of skills, experiences, and viewpoints .

title: Schoolpackage AI
description: The Schoolpackage AI programme, led by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) , seeks to integrate artificial intelligence into the educational system . Its objective is to build foundational AI literacy among students while equipping teachers with the knowledge and tools to incorporate AI in their teaching. Key elements include: Pilot programmes in selected schools , which are scientifically monitored to evaluate effectiveness and outcomes. Use of AI tools in teaching , including generative AI applications, to enhance learning experiences. Teacher training and support , ensuring educators are prepared to guide students in AI-related subjects. Research on AI in education , promoting evidence-based strategies for integrating AI technologies into curricula. The initiative aims to prepare students for a digital future , fostering AI literacy and understanding from an early age. By combining hands-on experience, teacher training, and research, Schoolpackage AI supports Austria’s goal of creating a digitally competent and AI-aware generation .

title: AI Radar
description: The AI Radar initiative, coordinated by Austria Tourism , is designed to prepare the tourism sector for the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence . It provides structured training, awareness, and networking opportunities to help tourism businesses and professionals understand and use AI technologies effectively. Key objectives include: Monitoring AI innovations and identifying their potential applications in tourism. Recognising trends and experimenting with new technologies to anticipate future developments. Strengthening skills and capacities of tourism professionals through regular (online) webinars and workshops . Developing prototypes and promoting networking to encourage collaboration between businesses, experts, and innovators. By combining training with trend analysis and prototype development, AI Radar helps Austria’s tourism industry to adopt AI-based solutions more quickly and confidently. The programme thus contributes to future-proofing the sector , improving competitiveness, and enhancing the visitor experience through smarter, more efficient, and innovative services.

title: Research and innovation bill
description: The Swedish Government has presented the Research and Innovation Bill 2024 , which represents the largest investment in research and innovation in the country’s history . The bill aims to ensure that Sweden remains a leading knowledge nation and a hub for innovation and advanced technologies. Key elements include: Funding for excellent research – significantly increased and long-term support for world-class research projects. Increased and competitive funding for higher education institutions – to strengthen their research capabilities and improve international competitiveness. Enhanced research infrastructure – investments in cutting-edge laboratories, data facilities, and national research resources. Investments in groundbreaking technologies – support for emerging and transformative technologies, such as artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and advanced life sciences . Objectives: Consolidate Sweden’s position as a global leader in science, innovation, and technology. Provide sustainable and competitive funding for universities and research institutes . Facilitate the development of high-impact research infrastructures . Support breakthrough technologies that address societal and environmental challenges. This new bill underscores the Swedish Government’s commitment to research excellence and to fostering an environment where cutting-edge innovation – including in AI – can thrive.

title: Initiatives to help start-ups and/or scale-ups access financing
description: Spain has established multiple public funding instruments to stimulate innovation across all technological sectors, including artificial intelligence. These initiatives are designed to provide capital, co-investment, and participatory financing to companies at different stages of development, from early-stage start-ups to growth-focused SMEs. Key programmes include: Next Tech Fund – €4 billion to support early-stage and high-tech companies, including AI ventures. Co-investment Fund (FOCO) – €2 billion for co-investment in innovative companies, leveraging private sector funding. INNVIERTE programme – supports the growth of innovative enterprises through venture capital and seed investments. Fond-ICO Global – €4.5 billion in financial instruments to back technology-driven projects. ENISA participatory loans – targeted loans for SMEs and start-ups to foster innovation and competitiveness. Women’s Digital Entrepreneurs – €51 million dedicated to supporting female-led digital and technology initiatives. These initiatives aim to: Accelerate digital and technological transformation , including AI adoption. Enhance access to capital for innovative projects and companies. Promote gender equality in entrepreneurship , particularly in the digital sector. Foster public–private collaboration , combining government support with private investment. Together, these funding instruments create a robust innovation ecosystem , encouraging technological advancement and the integration of AI across Spanish industry and society.

title: AI4ES (Network of Excellence in AI)
description: The AI4ES Network of Excellence aims to aggregate and harmonise Spain’s capacities, infrastructures, and R&D activities in artificial intelligence and data analytics . By uniting leading technological centres, it fosters collaboration and accelerates the translation of research into real-world applications. The network is coordinated by the Instituto Tecnológico de Informática (ITI) and includes: Fundación CTIC Centro Tecnológico Eurecat Tecnalia Together, these centres mobilise nearly 300 professionals with research and technical expertise across multiple sectors, providing a strong foundation for multi-sector R&D projects in AI and data analytics. Key objectives of AI4ES include: Boost Spain’s data- and AI-based economy by facilitating knowledge and technology transfer to the productive fabric. Strengthen national infrastructures and capacities in AI and data analytics. Promote collaboration between research centres and industry , enabling innovative products and services. Support the development of advanced digital skills and the uptake of AI across sectors. Through this initiative, Spain positions itself to expand its AI ecosystem , create synergies between research and industry, and enhance competitiveness in Europe’s digital economy

It aligns with Spain’s broader strategy to invest in emerging technologies and strengthen the connection between science and industry. Once operational, Spain Neurotech is expected to contribute to medical breakthroughs , new AI models inspired by the brain , and the training of highly skilled researchers in this rapidly evolving field.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
description: The two Slovenian EDIHs form part of the European Digital Innovation Hub network funded under the Digital Europe Programme and national support. They serve as regional one-stop shops to accelerate the digital transformation of SMEs, start-ups, scale-ups, and public sector organisations , with a strong emphasis on AI and other enabling technologies. Smart, Resilient and Sustainable Communities (SRC-EDIH): SRC focuses on state and local governments as well as SMEs, supporting them in testing products, solutions, and components in real environments. It helps organisations upgrade their digital processes and business models while aligning growth with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) . Core areas of support include High-Performance Computing (HPC), AI, cybersecurity, robotics, and blockchain technologies , with particular targeting of the manufacturing and public services sectors. DIGI-SI: DIGI-SI aims to foster the digital transformation of SMEs, start-ups, scale-ups, and public administration in four strategic priority areas: Agri-food, Health, Tourism, and Manufacturing . It provides services in AI, cybersecurity, HPC, and advanced digital skills , with tailored support for food producers, healthcare providers, tourism operators, and manufacturing firms . Both hubs play a dual role: Technology adoption – providing expertise, testing facilities, and infrastructure. Access to finance – supporting AI start-ups and scale-ups in connecting with investors, funding schemes, and EU programmes. Together, SRC-EDIH and DIGI-SI enhance Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem , ensure SMEs and start-ups can benefit from the latest digital technologies, and strengthen the country’s integration into the European digital single market .

title: Legal Guide for Designing Regulatory Sandboxes
description: The Regulatory Sandbox Legal Guide is a legal and policy tool developed to support Israeli regulators in creating structured mechanisms for safe experimentation with innovative technologies. It responds to a critical governance challenge: how to regulate fast-evolving sectors such as artificial intelligence, digital finance, and health innovation within legal systems that are often rigid, outdated, or fragmented. The guide enables regulators to authorize time-bound testing environments in which companies can trial new business models or technologies under supervision, subject to partial regulatory exemptions and risk controls. Beyond outlining the core principles of a regulatory sandbox — such as eligibility criteria, clear objectives, and institutional accountability — the guide focuses on the legal design of sandbox regimes. It provides structured legislative models that can be embedded in both primary and secondary laws, and includes examples from existing Israeli statutes to support tailored implementation. It stresses the need for legislative clarity and normative certainty, while also enabling proportional regulatory discretion and adaptive oversight. The guide is designed to promote innovation while protecting the public interest. It establishes a process of learning-based regulation, allowing adjustments grounded in real-world experience. The sandbox model fosters dialogue between regulators and innovators, builds institutional capacity, and helps reduce uncertainty in the face of novel and complex technologies. Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to expand through the enactment of a cross-sectoral statutory framework, empowering the establishment of dedicated sandboxes via secondary legislation and through other coordinated efforts by an inter-ministerial team promoting regulatory experimentation. Over time, the sandbox model may serve as a stepping stone toward broader innovation-friendly reforms, including adaptive regulation and dynamic oversight mechanisms. The guide reflects an evolving shift in regulatory governance — moving from static rulemaking toward flexible, learning-oriented approaches — and is expected to shape how Israeli regulators engage with uncertainty, technological complexity, and cross-sector innovation.

text: Legal Guide for Designing Regulatory Sandboxes. The Regulatory Sandbox Legal Guide is a legal and policy tool developed to support PLACE regulators in creating structured mechanisms for safe experimentation with innovative technologies. It responds to a critical governance challenge: how to regulate fast-evolving sectors such as artificial intelligence, digital finance, and health innovation within legal systems that are often rigid, outdated, or fragmented. The guide enables regulators to authorize time-bound testing environments in which companies can trial new business models or technologies under supervision, subject to partial regulatory exemptions and risk controls. Beyond outlining the core principles of a regulatory sandbox — such as eligibility criteria, clear objectives, and institutional accountability — the guide focuses on the legal design of sandbox regimes. It provides structured legislative models that can be embedded in both primary and secondary laws, and includes examples from existing PLACE statutes to support tailored implementation. It stresses the need for legislative clarity and normative certainty, while also enabling proportional regulatory discretion and adaptive oversight. The guide is designed to promote innovation while protecting the public interest. It establishes a process of learning-based regulation, allowing adjustments grounded in real-world experience. The sandbox model fosters dialogue between regulators and innovators, builds institutional capacity, and helps reduce uncertainty in the face of novel and complex technologies. Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to expand through the enactment of a cross-sectoral statutory framework, empowering the establishment of dedicated sandboxes via secondary legislation and through other coordinated efforts by an inter-ministerial team promoting regulatory experimentation. Over time, the sandbox model may serve as a stepping stone toward broader innovation-friendly reforms, including adaptive regulation and dynamic oversight mechanisms. The guide reflects an evolving shift in regulatory governance — moving from static rulemaking toward flexible, learning-oriented approaches — and is expected to shape how PLACE regulators engage with uncertainty, technological complexity, and cross-sector innovation

title: R&D projects for smart specialisation and specific economic objectives

Key objectives of this initiative include: Promoting applied research in priority technology areas such as artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, quantum technologies, and digital solutions. Supporting technology development from conceptual stages to validated prototypes, bridging the gap between research and practical application. Enhancing Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by funding projects with high potential for industrial and societal impact. Fostering collaboration among universities, research institutes, and industry partners to strengthen national R&D capacity. Through these measures, Slovenia aims to align its research investments with European and national priorities , encourage innovation-driven growth, and ensure that emerging technologies contribute to sustainable economic and societal development. Looking forward, the strategy is expected to expand the scope and scale of applied R&D , create new opportunities for knowledge transfer, and position Slovenia as a competitive player in the European technology landscape, particularly in AI and other advanced digital technologies.

title: Gravity and Strategic projects
description: The Gravity Projects initiative is a Slovenian national programme designed to accelerate innovative and high-impact research in strategically important technology areas. The initiative supports four consortia of researchers , each dedicated to a different thematic domain: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor technologies Language technologies Quantum technologies These projects target research and technological development at TRL 1/2 to TRL 4/5 , covering early conceptual work through experimental validation and prototype development. This enables the transition from fundamental research to applied solutions that can have tangible societal and industrial impact. The initiative is co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation , ensuring that national priorities are aligned with research investments. Key objectives include: Advancing cutting-edge research in emerging and strategically important technologies. Fostering collaboration among universities, research institutes, and industry partners. Strengthening Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by supporting projects with high scientific and economic potential. Facilitating technology transfer from research outputs to practical applications in industry and public services. Looking forward, the Gravity Projects are expected to create sustainable centres of expertise in each of the four thematic areas. The initiative also aims to build national and international research networks , attract top talent, and enhance Slovenia’s position in global innovation and digital transformation.

title: EUROPEUM-EDIC
description: The European Blockchain Partnership (EBP) and the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) have been established as a European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (EDIC) to accelerate the use of blockchain across Europe. This initiative seeks to provide trustworthy, cross-border digital public services by leveraging decentralised technologies. The project pursues several core objectives: Facilitate cross-border cooperation among public authorities to deploy and scale blockchain solutions across the EU. Ensure interoperability of blockchain solutions at multiple levels — protocol, smart contract, and application. Foster integration with other key digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data spaces, and cybersecurity. Enable innovation-friendly conditions by supporting collaboration with blockchain and non-blockchain initiatives, as well as with other EDICs. By advancing European blockchain services , the initiative is expected to: Increase trust and transparency in digital transactions across member states. Support efficient and secure public services , such as digital identity, document verification, and supply chain monitoring. Provide a foundation for innovation ecosystems , allowing SMEs, startups, and public bodies to develop applications that rely on secure decentralised infrastructure. Over time, the EBSI EDIC is intended to become a pan-European blockchain infrastructure , supporting both the public sector and private innovation. Its role in promoting interoperability and cooperation with other digital fields will ensure that blockchain is not developed in isolation but as part of a broader European digital ecosystem .

title: CitiVERSE
description: The Connected Local Digital Twins for CitiVERSE (LDT CitiVERSE EDIC) is a European initiative designed to connect existing local digital twins and establish the foundation of the EU CitiVERSE. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a city’s physical assets, processes, and systems , combining real-time data, analytics, and AI to create models that simulate urban dynamics. The CitiVERSE initiative pursues several key objectives: Integration of local digital twins into a Europe-wide network, enabling knowledge-sharing and interoperability. Use of AI-driven simulations to test scenarios such as the effects of traffic flow changes on air quality, congestion, and decarbonisation efforts. Application of generative AI and virtual reality tools to enhance citizen participation, making consultations on urban planning more engaging and easier to understand. By focusing on smart city development , CitiVERSE enables municipalities to: Improve urban decision-making with real-time and predictive modelling. Foster sustainable and climate-friendly solutions , aligned with EU Green Deal goals. Strengthen citizen engagement by providing accessible and immersive digital tools. In the longer term, the CitiVERSE project is expected to evolve into a pan-European platform for digital urban innovation. It will support cities in scaling and integrating digital twin solutions , while ensuring interoperability across borders. The initiative also acts as a testing ground for cutting-edge generative AI applications , positioning Europe at the forefront of AI-driven smart city technologies.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
description: The European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Slovakia are part of the EU-wide initiative under the Digital Europe Programme that helps businesses and public sector organisations accelerate digital transformation. In Slovakia, these hubs provide test-before-invest services , training, and access to expertise, with a focus on artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies. The Ministry of Investment, Regional Development, and Informatization of the Slovak Republic oversees their implementation and launch. The Slovak EDIHs include: HealthHub – Centre of Innovative Health Care : Supports hospitals and healthcare facilities in digital transformation and innovation. Cassovium : Creates a unique platform for the implementation and development of digital technologies in Eastern Slovakia. Expandi 4.0 : Assists SMEs in digital transformation by guiding them through innovation processes and developing the skills needed for success. Hopero : Helps companies and public institutions prepare and implement AI projects, secure funding, and connect with innovators in Slovakia’s ecosystem. SCDI (Slovak Centre of Digital Innovations) : Focuses on SME digitalisation with emphasis on environmental sustainability, workforce development, and the digital technology industry. KInIT (Kempelen Institute of Intelligent Technologies) : An independent, non-profit institute that advances research in AI and computer science, bridging expertise across public and private sectors. Together, these hubs play a crucial role in: Supporting SMEs and public organisations in adopting AI and digital tools. Strengthening Slovakia’s innovation ecosystem by linking research, industry, and government. Improving competitiveness and resilience across sectors, including healthcare, manufacturing, and public services. Building skills and training for digital and AI adoption. Looking forward, the Slovak EDIHs are expected to expand their services, strengthen international cooperation within the EU-wide network of hubs, and contribute to making Slovakia more competitive and innovative in the digital age.

title: Alliance for Language Technologies - European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (ALT-EDIC)
description: Slovenia actively participates in the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC) , a joint initiative addressing the scarcity of high-quality European language data for training artificial intelligence systems. This is a strategic step for both Slovenia and the European Union, as the majority of current AI language models are based on English and non-European data sources. The objectives of ALT-EDIC include: Developing shared European infrastructure for language technologies. Creating large language models (LLMs) specifically tailored to European official and regional languages . Promoting linguistic diversity and ensuring smaller languages are represented in AI systems. Advancing Europe’s AI sovereignty by reducing dependence on non-European AI technologies. For Slovenia, participation in ALT-EDIC supports both national and European strategic goals: Strengthening local AI research and development capacity , particularly in natural language processing (NLP). Supporting public services, SMEs, and industries in adopting advanced language technologies. Contributing to the preservation and digitalisation of the Slovene language , ensuring it remains part of cutting-edge AI systems. Looking ahead, ALT-EDIC is expected to become a pan-European hub for language technologies , fostering collaboration among member states, research institutions, and private sector stakeholders. Slovenia’s role in the consortium provides access to infrastructure, shared datasets, and expertise, positioning the country as an active contributor to the development of European multilingual AI ecosystems .

title: AI in Primary and Secondary school
description: The “AI in Primary and Secondary Education” initiative is a national pilot designed to bring AI into Italy’s school curriculum . It forms a key part of the AI Strategy 2024–2026 and responds to the country’s need to address the digital skills gap in education. Beginning with the 2024–2025 academic year , 15 schools across Calabria, Lazio, Tuscany, and Lombardy will test AI-integrated lessons. The pilot will: Equip students with foundational knowledge of AI and essential digital competencies Use AI tools as virtual assistants to facilitate personalised learning experiences Support teachers in developing tailored educational approaches that meet diverse student needs This initiative is also intended to scale up in the coming years as part of Italy’s broader push to promote advanced technologies in education . By embedding AI early into learning environments, Italy aims to prepare a new generation of students for an increasingly digital economy and society.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC)
description: The National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC) is a national initiative in Greece aimed at familiarising middle and high school students with artificial intelligence and developing practical skills in emerging technologies. Organised by the ARCHIMEDES Unit of the Athena Research Center , the competition is held in collaboration with: Hellenic Society of Computer Scientists and Professionals in Communications (GCP) Hellenic Society for Artificial Intelligence (EETN) Institute of Educational Policy (IEP) The competition introduces participants to modern AI techniques and applications , including: Machine learning Computer vision Natural language processing Students work on real-world challenges based on these technologies, gain experience collaborating with industry experts , and build teamwork and problem-solving skills . Top-performing students have the opportunity to represent Greece at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence , raising the country’s profile in global AI education and innovation. Future outlook: Expansion of the competition to include more schools and students nationwide Broader partnerships with industry and academia to deepen mentoring and resources Continued alignment with international standards in AI education and competitions

title: AI Guidelines for Education System

It aims to: Support teachers and school leaders in understanding how AI tools can enhance teaching and learning. Ensure the ethical and safe use of AI , including privacy, security, and fairness considerations. Provide practical recommendations for incorporating AI-based educational resources, platforms, and tools into curricula. Equip students with basic knowledge about AI and its implications to build digital literacy and critical thinking skills . The guidelines act as both a policy and practical tool , encouraging schools to experiment with innovative technologies while safeguarding ethical standards and data protection . Over time, they are expected to evolve alongside advances in AI and Bulgaria’s broader digital education strategy.

title: Recommendations on AI in education, teaching and training
description: The initiative focuses on creating clear recommendations for the use of artificial intelligence in education, teaching, and training . It responds to the growing role of AI in schools and educational institutions, aiming to ensure that AI tools are used responsibly, safely, and effectively. The initiative also seeks to increase understanding of AI among educators and learners. The main objectives of the recommendations are to: Enhance knowledge and awareness of AI in educational contexts. Promote responsible and safe use of AI tools by teachers and students. Support equality in learning , ensuring all learners can access the benefits of AI technology. The initiative is being developed collaboratively by the National Agency for Education and the Ministry of Education and Culture, reflecting a coordinated approach that includes policymakers, educators, and experts. The recommendations will provide guidance for schools, training institutions, and educational organisations across Finland. In the future, the recommendations are expected to be integrated into educational policies and teaching practices . As AI continues to evolve, these guidelines may expand to include new technologies and applications, helping Finland maintain a safe, innovative, and inclusive learning environment for all students.

title: “Digital problem solving” in Preparatory Adult Education (FVU)
description: In January 2024, Denmark updated its Preparatory Adult Education (FVU) curricula to include a focus on digital problem solving , with specific attention to generative AI. The initiative addresses the need to equip adults, particularly low-skilled learners, with practical digital skills that are increasingly relevant in daily life, work, and study. The curriculum aims to help students: Understand generative AI and its basic concepts. Recognize practical applications of AI in personal and professional contexts. Identify possibilities and limitations of AI tools for solving everyday tasks. Apply AI tools to tasks related to employment, further education, or private life. While the main target group remains low-skilled adults, the educational offer has been expanded to a broader audience. This ensures more learners have access to essential digital skills that support employability and personal development. The initiative also reflects a broader trend in adult education towards integrating digital literacy and AI awareness into foundational programmes. Over time, the curriculum is expected to evolve, incorporating more interactive tools, practical exercises, and guidance to help learners effectively navigate AI technologies in their personal and professional lives.

title: Legislative amendments for road transport automation
description: The initiative seeks to create a legal framework for automated road transport in Finland, ensuring that emerging technologies can be safely and efficiently deployed. The ministry prepared a memorandum assessing necessary legislative amendments, which was made available for public and stakeholder comments until 17 May 2024. Key objectives of the initiative include: Updating road transport laws to accommodate automated vehicles Ensuring safety and regulatory compliance while supporting innovation Incorporating stakeholder feedback into the legislative drafting process Following the consultation, officials at the Ministry of Transport and Communications will continue drafting the legislation. The goal is to submit a government proposal to Parliament during the autumn 2025 session, establishing a clear, robust, and forward-looking framework for automated road transport in Finland. Future outlook: Adoption of modernised transport legislation that supports automation Enhanced safety and operational standards for automated vehicles Creation of an enabling environment for innovation and commercial deployment in Finland’s transport sector

description: This joint project is part of Germany’s New Vehicle and System Technologies programme and is funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK). Its main goal is to develop and train generative AI models that can accelerate the safe and large-scale deployment of automated and autonomous vehicles. The project tackles several key challenges: Overcoming technical and operational barriers to autonomous driving Creating foundation models for self-driving systems using generative AI Pooling proprietary datasets from multiple companies for the first time to train large, high-quality AI models collaboratively The initiative is also designed to strengthen Germany’s position in AI-powered mobility innovation, by promoting cross-industry collaboration and reducing duplication of effort in data collection and model training. title: Training scholarships
description: Spain faces an important challenge and opportunity as technology rapidly reshapes its economy and society. Fields like artificial intelligence (AI), data processing, and advanced computing are playing an increasingly central role across industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, and cybersecurity. However, Spain, like many countries, needs more highly trained experts to fully take advantage of these technologies and drive innovation. This program directly addresses that need by providing 374 scholarships for in-depth training in AI and several related high-tech areas. The program’s main goal is to support students, researchers, and professionals over four years of study and research in fields that are crucial for Spain’s technological future. Besides AI, it includes disciplines like massive data and information processing, high-performance computing, cloud computing, cybersecurity, biotechnology, medical devices, medical imaging, robotics, and quantum technologies. By focusing on these key sectors, the initiative aims to build a strong, specialized workforce ready to contribute to Spain’s scientific progress and economic competitiveness. Managed by government agencies or educational institutions in Spain, the scholarships provide recipients with the financial resources to fully commit to their training and research projects. This helps ensure that talented individuals can develop deep expertise without financial barriers. The program’s structure supports long-term skill development, recognizing that mastery in these complex, interdisciplinary fields takes time and dedicated effort.
