title: Camilla - Digital Assistant for Public Sector Competitions
description: Camilla is a generative-AI virtual assistant promoted by Formez PA in close collaboration with CSI Piemonte. Formez PA, as the in-house agency of the Department for Public Administration, leads the initiative on the policy and service side, while CSI Piemonte provides and operates the underlying AI platform and conversational technology. Camilla addresses key challenges in Italy's public recruitment landscape, where digitalisation has increased competition volume and complexity while shortening timelines, often overwhelming candidates with fragmented information. By leveraging generative AI, the initiative taps the opportunity to provide immediate, intuitive access to up-to-date details on competitions managed by RIPAM and Formez PA and hosted on the inPA Portal, Italy's unified gateway for public sector recruitment. This responds directly to user difficulties in navigating notices, schedules, and applications, reducing barriers to merit-based participation. Formez PA, as RIPAM's operational arm, a role recently enhanced under the 2025 Decreto PA framework, launched Camilla to streamline these processes. The AI assistant draws from a real-time knowledge base via inPA APIs, offering 24/7 text and voice support for queries on open competitions, eligibility, and submissions. A monitored back office refines prompts and content for accuracy, ensuring reliable guidance. Core objectives include enhancing user navigation, cutting staff workload on support tickets, and elevating inPA's digital service quality, aiming for higher satisfaction, fewer inquiries, and broader adoption. Future evolution focuses on scalability and institutionalisation. The knowledge base will expand from central and regional competitions to encompass all inPA publishers, including agencies, municipalities, and provinces, supported by enhanced APIs, automated verification, and capacity-building for administrations. With monitoring and reporting in place, Camilla is positioned to become a permanent national tool, handling thousands of parallel competitions and evolving via user feedback into a cornerstone of efficient, transparent public recruitment.

title: AI Brownfield Site
description: The initiative addresses Austria’s persistent challenge of high land consumption, around 6.5 hectares per day, far exceeding national sustainability targets. A major opportunity lies in reactivating brownfields: previously industrial or commercial sites that are unused or underused. Earlier studies estimated up to 10,000 such sites nationwide, yet no comprehensive, publicly accessible dataset existed. Against this backdrop, the initiative seeks to leverage AI-based image analysis to systematically identify brownfields across Austria and support more sustainable land use, prioritising redevelopment over new land conversion. The project’s core objective is to create the first nationwide, data-driven brownfield map using optical remote-sensing data. By applying a trained AI classification system to orthophotos, approximately 65,000 industrial and commercial sites larger than 1,000 m² were analysed. About 4,700 brownfields, sites with very high prediction confidence, covering roughly 4,000 hectares were published on the public WebGIS platform and made available as open government data. The initiative aims to support municipalities, planners, investors, and policymakers in prioritising land recycling, aligning with national commitments to reduce soil sealing and promote redevelopment over new zoning. By making the data publicly accessible through www.brachflaechen-dialog.at and data.gv.at, the project institutionalises a standardised, repeatable method for monitoring brownfield potential. Looking ahead, the initiative is designed for continuous evolution and long-term integration into Austria’s land-use governance. Since one-third of the country is re-photographed annually, updated orthophotos will feed into the system, enabling regular refreshes of the brownfield map. This creates a dynamic monitoring tool rather than a one-time inventory. Through institutionalisation within the Federal Ministry and ongoing technical updates, the initiative is positioned to become a permanent, scalable instrument for reducing land consumption and promoting sustainable spatial development.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Courts
description: Use of AI Tools by Courts to Enhance Court Operations: This document examines benefits and challenges, sets out guiding principles, and highlights key steps in the adoption of AI tools by courts. It focuses on AI tools used for administrative or legal research and analysis purposes, rather than on AI tools and issues related to decision making, evidence, electronic disclosure or substantive law. Use of AI Tools by Court Users to Help them Participate in Court: This document examines the benefits and challenges of using AI by court users to assist them in participating in court proceedings. It addresses considerations relevant to 1) the development and monitoring of guidelines by courts on the subject, and 2) responsible use of AI by court users. Both documents were developed as non-binding guidance to assist courts across Canada in developing their own policies, frameworks and tools governing the use of AI by courts or court users. As such, the Action Committee does not actively monitor their implementation and institutionalisation. The Action Committee supports Canada’s courts in their modernisation efforts. It provides guidance for addressing challenges, and highlights opportunities and innovative practices to modernise court operations and improve access to justice for court users. In this case, the non-prescriptive guidance covers the use of artificial intelligence by courts to enhance their operations and the use of artificial intelligence by court users to support their participation in court proceedings. Given the non-binding nature of this guidance, there is no formal measuring of results and impacts.

title: AI Copilot for the National Post Provider
description: Posta Kopilot is an AI-powered mobile application designed to enhance the efficiency of manual mail sorting at the National Post of Serbia (Pošta Srbije). Serbia's national postal service handles over 2.1 million pieces of mail daily, and a significant portion of the sorting process remains manual. Sorting mail traditionally requires extensive knowledge of postal codes, delivery routes, and address structures, which can take new employees several months to acquire. The application uses artificial intelligence to recognise and interpret address information, then guides workers on correct sorting decisions in real time. This reduces dependency on memorised knowledge, accelerates onboarding for new staff, and makes the sorting process both faster and more accurate. The initiative was developed through Serbia's Innovation Fund GovTech programme, which connects private technology companies with public sector institutions to solve operational challenges using innovative technologies. LambdaWorks, a digital product agency, led product development, covering product management, design, backend and frontend engineering, and infrastructure. Key outcomes include a greater than 20% increase in manual sorting efficiency and a reduction in employee onboarding time from several months to a few weeks. These improvements directly affect daily processing of 2.1 million plus mail pieces, lowering training costs, accelerating workforce readiness, and yielding tangible financial savings for Serbia's postal infrastructure. The project also surfaced important lessons. User adoption and change management were significant challenges; introducing an AI tool into frontline workflows required careful attention to usability and trust-building, achieved through intuitive UX design and iterative testing with postal workers. Securing budget for ongoing operation within public sector procurement constraints was a further hurdle. Close collaboration between the technology partner and Pošta Srbije proved essential for aligning the solution with real operational needs, and the GovTech programme model demonstrated its effectiveness as a vehicle for delivering practical AI solutions in the public sector. Looking ahead, Posta Kopilot has the potential to scale to additional postal facilities across Serbia and could serve as a replicable model for other national postal services facing similar manual sorting challenges. Its modular design supports adaptation to different operational environments.

title: AI for resilient digital  government services (Subnational: Province of Cordoba)
description: The Province of Córdoba’s citizen‑facing digital infrastructure supports services such as digital identity (Ciudadano Digital – CiDi), online procedures, payments and public information portals for more than 3.8 million residents. Ensuring their continuous availability has become a major governance challenge. To strengthen resilience, the Sub‑secretariat of Technological Infrastructure developed an autonomous AI‑agent ecosystem that monitors, diagnoses and supports incident resolution across the province’s cloud environment. Operating across 66 AWS accounts, the system provides continuous monitoring, faster response times and full auditability of every automated action, directly improving the reliability of essential public services. The solution is built as an ecosystem of AI agents running on AWS, using Anthropic’s Claude models through Amazon Bedrock so that all inference remains within the province’s cloud environment. Claude Sonnet performs minute‑by‑minute monitoring and first‑line analysis, while Claude Opus conducts deeper diagnostics and produces technical reports. Applications are evaluated across five dimensions—connectivity, HTML structure, content integrity, error detection and external resources—to generate a configurable health score. When the score drops below the alert threshold, a specialized agent initiates a structured seven‑stage workflow covering detection, diagnosis, planning, execution, validation, resolution and closure. All steps are documented in real time, and automated summaries are shared with technical and executive stakeholders. The architecture was designed with transparency and accountability at its core. All inference takes place within Córdoba’s AWS boundary, with CloudTrail logging and IAM‑based access controls aligning the AI layer with existing infrastructure governance. This ensures that every AI‑driven action is auditable to the same standard as any other infrastructure change, a requirement that shaped the model and platform selection. The broader initiative forms part of Córdoba’s strategy to reinforce resilient digital‑government infrastructure in an increasingly digital society. The project’s development independently arrived at a “read‑only first” deployment model, prioritizing diagnostic capability before allowing any automated changes. This approach was later validated externally when AWS announced its DevOps Agent in December 2025 with an identical philosophy—confirming Córdoba’s alignment with global best practice in responsible agentic AI. The province is committed to regional knowledge sharing. An interactive infographic documents the workflow, and the team is prepared to share its risk matrix, governance framework and 23‑item documentation standard with peer governments.

title: AI Proof of Concept trajectory
description: Public administrations often struggle with a lack of internal technical expertise. This leads to heavy reliance on expensive external IT vendors and slows down the adoption of new technologies. To resolve this, FOD Financiën launched a bottom-up innovation initiative aimed at testing internal AI proofs of concept (POCs) to optimise daily administrative processes. Concurrently, as the subgroup lead for Belgium for internal AI upskilling within the European Fiscalis network, we leverage this local initiative to address a broader opportunity: helping member states achieve AI independence. The primary objective is to significantly raise AI maturity by empowering government employees to propose, test, and evaluate AI POCs safely. Rather than outsourcing, we focus entirely on building internal expertise and proprietary, reusable assets like our in-house FinGPT platform, data extraction components, and anonymisation tools. A critical, parallel objective tied to our Fiscalis leadership is defining specific internal AI roles and upskilling staff accordingly. This ensures our organisation, and eventually other member states, has the precise competencies required to execute small AI projects autonomously without vendor lock-in. Over time, what began as a modest POC track managed by four part-time employees has grown into a structured, driving force for digital transformation. We now have a dedicated internal AI team of eleven people operating in an iterative three-month cycle designed to fail fast or scale fast. The internal enthusiasm has snowballed, as evidenced by our most recent call which generated 50 new bottom-up proposals. With 25 tested use cases to date, FOD Financiën currently holds the highest number of tested AI use cases among Belgian federal departments. In the future, the initiative will be deeply institutionalised through the formal appointment and continuous training of dedicated AI personas across various departments. Because our operational costs remain exceptionally low, with recent POC cycles incurring infrastructure costs of less than 60 euros, we can continuously reinvest in internal knowledge building. The modular nature of our AI components ensures high transferability. We plan to scale our successful POC frameworks and upskilling methodologies to other Belgian government departments and share them across European member states through the Fiscalis network, fostering widespread, vendor-independent AI maturity.

title: Indonesia’s Healthcare AI Task Force
description: Indonesia’s Healthcare AI Task Force is a national working group established by the Ministry of Health Republic Indonesia to respond to the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and its potential impact on healthcare delivery. The initiative addresses the need for clear coordination, governance, and ethical guidance so that AI can be used to improve efficiency, accuracy, and access to health services, while safeguarding patient rights, data protection, and public trust. The Task Force seeks to leverage AI as an opportunity to strengthen Indonesia’s health system through better use of health data and digital innovation. It focuses on priority health challenges such as disease screening, early risk prediction, clinical decision support, and national health programmes, while also responding to the broader opportunity to build domestic capacity in health-related AI research and development. By bringing together policymakers, clinicians, researchers, and industry, the initiative aims to bridge gaps between innovation and real-world health needs. The main objectives of the initiative are to develop policy recommendations for the responsible use of AI in healthcare, identify and promote high-impact AI use cases, and ensure that AI development and deployment are ethical, accountable, and aligned with national laws and strategies. The Task Force also plays a coordinating role, facilitating collaboration across sectors and supporting pilot implementations in areas such as medical imaging, genomics, virtual health assistance, and medical devices. Currently, the Task Force has three main tasks: producing AI for healthcare regulation, building AI healthcare use cases and holding a global Healthcare AI Hackathon. The AI for healthcare regulation has become part of Indonesia's National AI Strategy with three priority cases: tuberculosis screening, stunting prediction, and the national Free Health Check-Up. The AI healthcare use cases focus on genomics, healthcare imaging AI, and large language models. Indonesia has successfully held a global Healthcare AI Hackathon with participants from ten countries and 278 teams. The winners then became part of the Healthcare Sandbox under supervision of the Ministry of Health Republic Indonesia. Going forward, the Healthcare AI Task Force is expected to be institutionalised as a key mechanism for guiding AI adoption within Indonesia’s health system. Its work will inform regulations, standards, and implementation frameworks, while successful pilots can be scaled nationally through integration with existing digital health platforms and programmes. Over time, the initiative is designed to evolve from coordination and experimentation towards broader, system-wide adoption of AI that supports better health outcomes and more resilient health services.

title: Guidelines for the Use of Hyper-scale AI in the Public Sector
description: Results, outcomes and impacts This guideline contributed to mitigating adoption risks in the early-stage market for generative AI in the public sector by defining business models and presenting diverse use cases to support adoption. Specifically, an information session attended by approximately 250 public sector officials was held, and 10 generative AI companies were identified and matched with public sector organisations. The guideline is expected to be revised in line with future developments in AI. Challenges and lessons learned When producing and disseminating content on AI technologies through guidelines, the rapid pace of technological advancement may result in the inclusion of technologies that have already become outdated. Nevertheless, it is considered meaningful to document and preserve the technological legacy.

title: The AI Lab (Subnational: Brisbane, QLD)
description: The NIISQ AI Lab explores how AI can address real-world challenges and create opportunities for staff, participants, and stakeholders. Its primary goal is to develop safe, practical AI solutions that reduce administrative burdens, enhance efficiency, and allow staff to focus on higher-value tasks. By fostering curiosity and collaboration, the AI Lab empowers teams to test, learn, and adapt to emerging technologies while aligning with organisational priorities. Using a structured experimentation framework, the AI Lab conducts agile, short-term testing to uncover challenges and opportunities. Cross-functional teams, including data scientists, developers, policy experts, and subject matter specialists, collaborate to solve complex problems from diverse perspectives. Successful implementations include generative AI for invoice processing, natural language analytics for insights, and tools to boost staff productivity. These solutions have delivered measurable outcomes, such as significant time savings, improved decision-making, and reduced manual workloads, benefiting internal teams and external stakeholders. Unsuccessful experiments that do not meet clear success metrics do not move to implementation, saving the Agency time and money and also creating greater trust in new technologies with end users. The AI Lab plans to institutionalise AI adoption by integrating experimentation into business-as-usual operations. Collaboration with teams like People Strategy and Development ensures staff are educated, supported, and engaged in the AI journey. Adhering to Queensland Government AI Principles, the Lab addresses data privacy, ethics, and governance challenges while exploring new technologies and scaling promising solutions. This positions the AI Lab to expand its impact across the organisation, driving transformative change. The NIISQ AI Lab exemplifies a forward-thinking approach to AI adoption in government agencies, setting a benchmark for safe, structured, and inclusive implementation. By focusing on business problems, experimentation, collaboration, and governance, the Lab is building internal AI capabilities, fostering a future-ready workforce, and delivering innovation with measurable outcomes.

title: Intelligent Complaint Analysis System (SIAR)
description: Consumer complaints filed with businesses through our institution are our primary input for identifying non-compliance and infringements of the Chilean Consumer Protection Law. However, their manual analysis is slow and resource-intensive. During mass-impact events with a high volume of complaints (typically between 3,000 and 12,000), manual processing becomes unsustainable, compromising the timeliness and effectiveness of our institutional response. Traditionally, an official requires eight to 31 business days to analyse this volume. This limitation was starkly exposed during the 2024 power outage that affected nine regions nationwide due to adverse weather, generating an unprecedented volume of complaints against electricity companies—specifically 32,753 in a matter of days. Even with a dedicated team of four officials, manual analysis would have taken at least 21 business days. The core problem lies in the inability to quickly assess the true impact of these emergencies, identify specific patterns of harm, and generate timely evidence for protection actions. This bottleneck historically left consumers vulnerable and without prompt solutions. The main challenge was to overcome this structural limitation: we needed a way to rapidly process massive complaint volumes to expedite decisions and ensure compliance with consumer protection regulations. To solve this, we developed the Intelligent Complaint Analysis System (SIAR, for its Spanish acronym). SIAR leverages artificial intelligence to automate complaint analysis. Using semantic analysis, Python, and specialised natural language AI models, SIAR deepens the evaluation process to quickly detect new issues and severe cases (such as the loss of food or medicine in a power outage). Crucially, the model was trained directly by expert officials using established legal criteria and consumer protection regulations, ensuring the AI's outputs are highly accurate and institutionally reliable. Regarding SIAR’s future evolution, its high adaptability drives two strategic lines of action: internal scaling and external replicability. Internally, the tool has already transcended its original emergency-response purpose. Currently in production, SIAR now features a user-friendly interface for non-technical staff, removing the need for programming skills. As we prepare to launch internal training, the system will be integrated into daily administrative workflows, automating routine tasks to ensure high-standard analysis during both national contingencies and normal operations. Externally, its replicability has been actively explored in other public institutions that, as part of their core business, must analyse large volumes of text-based data—such as the National Migration Service. This dual expansion demonstrates its immense potential to scale, transform mass case management, and ultimately deliver faster, data-driven justice across the broader public sector.

title: SuperNOC: ZENiA (Subnational: Genoa)
description: ZENiA is the new virtual assistant of the Municipality of Genoa, based on artificial intelligence and integrated into the institutional website. Designed for citizens, residents, businesses, and anyone who needs information about municipal services, ZENiA allows users to quickly find content, contacts, offices, and procedures. Thanks to its advanced architecture, it does not just respond: it guides users in submitting reports, requests for assistance, and booking appointments with the relevant offices. It is accessible via both text chat and voice, making it an inclusive tool for people with disabilities. The project stems from the need to make access to municipal services easier, faster, and more intuitive. The municipality wanted to respond to a concrete need of citizens: to find reliable information without difficulty, overcoming linguistic and technological barriers. The opportunity is twofold: on the one hand, to improve communication between citizens and the administration, and on the other, to promote a more modern, transparent, and digital public administration. The decision to offer ZENiA in nine languages—Italian, English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Romanian, Bengali, and Urdu—reflects the municipality's desire to ensure equal access to services for all communities present. Based on Microsoft technology (OpenAI 4.1o) and funded by European funds from the National Metro Plus and Medium-Sized Cities South 2021–2027 Program, ZENiA analyses the contents of the institutional website and provides accurate, consistent, and reliable answers. Users can also interact by authenticating themselves with SPID, CIE, or CNS for personalised services. The added value lies in the chatbot's ability to guide the user step by step, reducing search times, errors, and operational difficulties. The ability to interact via voice further enhances accessibility, making ZENiA a truly inclusive tool geared towards digital innovation in the city. In the coming years, ZENiA is expected to evolve into a fully integrated digital access point for municipal services. The Municipality plans to expand its capabilities by gradually connecting the virtual assistant to additional back-office systems, enabling users to complete more procedures entirely online and receive personalised updates on their requests. The initiative is designed to become an institutional component of Genoa’s digital ecosystem, embedded in service processes and adopted as a standard communication channel with citizens. Its scalable architecture also allows broader future deployment: ZENiA could be extended to mobile apps, integrated into smart city platforms, or replicated by other administrations, positioning Genoa as a reference model for AI-enabled public service innovation.

title: Building regulations copilot (BR Copilot)
description: The Architecture Regulation Copilot is an AI-enabled regulatory information platform that consolidates and structures dispersed building-related laws, administrative rules, and local ordinances in Korea. It supports users in searching, understanding, and applying building regulations in a clear and systematic manner. The system structures legal data at the clause level and provides integrated regulatory information through natural language processing (NLP)-based query search and keyword search functions. It also includes address-based search features that allow users to identify applicable land-use regulations, permitted building uses, and development restrictions. Through real-time linkage with the Ministry of Government Legislation, the platform ensures up-to-date legal information and enables integrated access to acts, enforcement decrees, enforcement rules, notices, and local ordinances. In addition, it enables responses based on public complaint cases, official Q&A from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and judicial precedents to support regulatory interpretation. The initiative establishes a digital regulatory support system that enables regulators, permit authorities, professionals, and the general public to systematically access and use building regulations. Results, outcomes and impacts An integrated clause-level regulatory database with NLP Q&A and address-based inference lets a single query return acts, decrees, rules, notices, ordinances, precedents, and administrative interpretations. Real-time updates keep regulations current, and automated similarity detection flags overlapping or conflicting provisions in advance. These features reduce omissions, improve consistency in administrative decisions, speed permit reviews, increase operational throughput, and support better compliance outcomes. Future impact will be measured by quantitative indicators: reduced search time, fewer repetitive inquiries, and shorter administrative processing durations.

title: Ariana (Subnational: Montevideo)
description: This virtual assistant for construction permits (Ariana) seeks to facilitate consultation on the regulations governing construction permits in Montevideo. Ariana is an assistant based on generative artificial intelligence and is used by professionals, technicians and officials to make queries in natural language. Its goal is to facilitate administrative management and reduce errors in the presentation of procedures, acting as a support tool for the management of construction permits. Currently, phase one of the project has been published with a corrective and evolutionary maintenance scheme. In the future, it is planned to expand its scope by integrating a broader spectrum of regulations and extending its response capacity to other issues beyond the architectural and urban-planning field within the Municipality of Montevideo. Results, outcomes and impacts Because the project is currently in an early design phase, aspects related to tangible results and impacts have not yet been addressed operationally. Currently, evaluation methodologies and metrics are being defined that will allow monitoring of the evolution of the tool once implemented, focusing on institutional efficiency and user experience. One of the main objectives for the evolution of this tool is to observe a positive impact both at the institutional level and on external users. It is expected to optimise the comprehensive management of permits. Challenges and lessons learned The main risk identified is the need to generate internal capacities for the sustainability of this type of emerging technology. To mitigate this risk, technical training tasks for officials of the Municipality of Montevideo are incorporated into the assistant's evolution planning. A fundamental lesson has been the need to define comprehensive indicators of success. It is not enough to measure the reduction of face-to-face consultations to optimise the team's time; it is essential to include the perception of the citizen and their level of satisfaction with the response received.

title: AI Governance Framework of Madrid: Institutionalisation, Ethics and Oversight for the Public Use of Artificial Intelligence (Subnational: Madrid)
description: Madrid’s AI Governance initiative was created to address the growing need to co-ordinate AI systems and to ensure their safe, ethical and rights-based use. Before its creation, AI projects emerged in a fragmented way across departments, making it difficult to ensure transparency, oversight and alignment with European requirements. The City Council designed a comprehensive framework to guide the full lifecycle of AI systems and guarantee a digital transformation centred on people and public value, and it set this out in the ‘Artificial Intelligence Roadmap at the Madrid City Council’. The model has three dimensions. The procedural dimension defines norms, risk assessments, human oversight, ethical validation and data protection protocols. The structural dimension assigns roles and capabilities, with the Digital Office defining strategy, IAM as a technological enabler, and units such as Data Protection, Legal Services and Madrid Talento ensuring compliance and workforce training. The relational dimension operates through MAIA, a corporate group created in 2024 bringing together over 90 professionals to co-ordinate use cases and collaborate with universities, companies and other administrations. The governance framework includes instruments such as the municipal algorithm registry, a standard lifecycle, ethical safeguards, legal assurance and an indicator dashboard. It aligns with the EU AI Act, the Spanish Digital Rights Charter and the OECD AI Principles, ensuring safety, transparency, traceability, explainability and non-discrimination. It also supports continuous adaptation to the fast-changing landscape of generative AI. Implementation is embedded within the Madrid Capital Digital strategy and materialised through more than 40 real AI projects across taxation, mobility, environment, social services, participation, tourism, urban planning, cleanliness, cybersecurity and accessibility. Examples include the Tax Laboratory, SIVPICA, PALOMA, the Mobility Big Data Platform, the Digital Twin, Decide Madrid with AI, the air quality system, the smart cleaning vehicle and VisitMadridGPT, as well as predictive models of the Madrid Transport Company (Empresa Municipal de Transporte). More information about the use cases is available on the website. To strengthen governance, two working groups have been created: the AI Governance Working Group and the Madrid Artificial Intelligence (MAIA) Working Group. The model will evolve through a new AI Committee, expanded methodologies, a reinforced algorithm registry, periodic audits, stronger alignment with the AI Act and increased citizen engagement. It is designed as a permanent, scalable and replicable governance mechanism.

title: LibrAIfy: Digitisation of Textual Cultural Heritage - Improving the Quality of OCRed Texts
description: Our initiative was oriented towards the application of modern AI technologies to the digitisation of Serbian textual cultural heritage. This process poses significant challenges due to the variable quality of scanned material, historical language use, and authentic printing practices often reflected in distinctive typography, decorations, and complex layouts. Although AI tools offer vast potential, they are rarely suitable for off-the-shelf use and require careful domain and language adaptation. Building on open-source tools rooted in AI subfields such as computer vision and natural language processing, and informed by recent academic advances, our team developed a technology pipeline suitable for image enhancement, layout segmentation, optical character recognition (OCR), and post-OCR text correction and improvement. Thanks to the partnership with the National Library of Serbia, the solution was tested and evaluated on a representative collection of historical periodicals, resulting in the digitisation of more than 16,000 documents and over 400 GB of material. The initiative was important for two main reasons: (1) it supports the preservation of culture and language while providing access to a vast body of historical, cultural, and social content important for the education of the general public and for research; (2) it contributes to the creation of resources essential for the progress of local language technologies and the development of AI-based tools for text representation and understanding. As such, it brought valuable and extensive experience working with historical documents and provided deeper insight into the state of the technology, particularly in OCR and post-OCR processing for low-resource languages. Accordingly, the objectives of the initiative were: Establishing a suite suitable for technology benchmarking; Developing a Serbian-focused post-OCR tool to mitigate inaccuracies in modern OCR solutions; Creating additional high-quality, diverse resources to support local language technology development and language model training. Given that our partner, the National Library of Serbia, is continuously engaged in digitisation activities, diverse metrics and user feedback can be systematically collected and leveraged for ongoing software improvement and adaptation to broader, more varied scenarios, enhancing its applicability across other local digitisation centres. The initiative was also recognised and strongly supported by the UNDP Digital, AI, and Innovation Hub, bringing global visibility and opening opportunities for collaboration with communities worldwide.

title: Schrijfkader – AI-Assisted Writing Support for Government Officials (Subnational: Municipality of Tilburg)
description: Governments rely heavily on written documents for policymaking, decision-making and communication with citizens. Civil servants spend significant time drafting policy proposals, council documents, internal reports and formal correspondence. These documents must follow strict administrative and legal standards while remaining clear and understandable for decision-makers and the public. Schrijfkader was developed to support civil servants in this process by providing AI-assisted writing support directly within Microsoft Word. The tool offers contextual suggestions while documents are being written and helps users improve structure, clarity and tone. It can also support compliance with organisational writing frameworks and legal communication standards used by public administrations. The initiative was co-developed with the Municipality of Tilburg and further refined in collaboration with the Province of South Holland and other Dutch public sector organisations. Development focused on building a practical solution that integrates into existing government workflows rather than requiring new systems or complex changes to existing processes. Human oversight remains central: the tool provides suggestions, while civil servants remain fully responsible for decisions and final content. The initiative aims to reduce administrative workload, improve the readability and consistency of government documents, and support more transparent communication with citizens. As adoption expands, the approach demonstrates how AI can support everyday administrative tasks within government in a responsible and practical manner. Schrijfkader continues to evolve as additional public organisations participate and new functionalities are introduced. Because the tool is designed to integrate with commonly used software and organisational writing frameworks, the approach has strong potential to scale to other governments facing similar challenges in administrative writing and document production. Results, outcomes and impacts Early implementations suggest that Schrijfkader can significantly reduce the time required to draft and revise government documents while improving clarity and consistency. Users report fewer editing cycles and improved adherence to organisational writing guidelines. The tool is currently implemented or piloted across multiple Dutch public sector organisations. Initial evaluations rely on user feedback, document quality reviews and time-saving estimates. As adoption expands, further evaluation will focus on measurable indicators such as drafting time reduction, document readability improvements and productivity gains for civil servants.

title: AI Skills for Business Competency Framework
description: The framework outlines the essential knowledge, skills, personal attributes, and behaviors necessary to effectively address practical challenges and demonstrate competence in both personal and professional contexts. It is designed for the following groups:1) **AI Citizens**: Individuals in the public who may engage with organizations utilizing artificial intelligence. The framework clarifies the understanding of AI, focusing on its capabilities, opportunities, and risks, thereby equipping AI Citizens with a realistic perspective on AI usage.2) **AI Workers**: Employees whose roles are not primarily centered on data but may still be influenced by these technologies. The framework aids AI workers in recognizing the efficiency and productivity enhancements that AI can offer in their jobs.3) **AI Professionals**: Individuals whose main responsibilities involve data and AI, such as data analysts, machine learning engineers, and data ethicists. The framework delineates the essential cross-disciplinary competencies needed to collaborate effectively within teams and across their organizations.4) **AI Leaders**: Senior personnel responsible for the acquisition and governance of AI solutions. The framework assists them in anticipating the implications of emerging technologies, including their effects on the workforce, and in overseeing the responsible and safe implementation of AI in complex organizational environments.The framework consists of five dimensions, each representing a set of competencies and behaviors across five key areas.**Dimension A: Privacy & Stewardship**. This dimension focuses on data security and protection, encompassing the design, creation, storage, distribution, and associated risks.**Dimension B: Specification, acquisition, engineering, architecture, storage, and curation**. This area addresses the collection, secure storage, manipulation, and curation of data, along with competencies related to data management and analytical techniques, including handling issues arising from the (mis)use of sensitive data.**Dimension C: Problem definition & communication**. This dimension emphasizes the ability to identify and articulate a problem clearly, understand how artificial intelligence can contribute to potential solutions, and effectively communicate this knowledge to diverse audiences.**Dimension D: Problem solving, analysis, modeling, visualization**. This area involves the knowledge and application of various mathematical, statistical, and computing tools and methods to define and analyze problems and present solutions.**Dimension E: Evaluation and Reflection**. It is crucial for all professionals in data science and AI to have a solid grasp of the ethical principles guiding their work and to take responsibility for the integrity of the models they develop.

title: Bill of Rights of the Person in the Digital Environment
description: Therefore, the function of this document is to establish guidelines, instruments, indicators, goals, strategies, codes of good practice, models and comprehensive, systemic, continuous and evaluable policies aimed at meeting the objectives of said regulations, which implies that this document is more of a code of good practice than a binding one.This takes into account, among other things, that the development of Artificial Intelligence has allowed the storage of amounts of information unimaginable to the human mind and, from this, predictive profiles of individual or collective behavior can be generated and, in gloomy scenarios, it can be possible not only to predict, but also to generate and implement consumption or behavioral models in important sectors of society.That is why the inclusion of a chapter dedicated to the ethical use of Artificial Intelligence is innovative. Where, without a doubt, it is reiterated that the use of AI has become increasingly recurrent: social networks, applications and programs, scientific research and even medical applications. Given this importance, we must be aware of the need to have a specialized legal framework; However, and in view of the rapid development of this technology, it is practically impossible to point out specific rules “ which provide for each and every one of the legal cases that could occur “ but the regulatory development must be aimed at providing for general cases.Based on the above, the following rights were recognized in the respective chapter: the first of them is that of the use of artificial intelligence centered on the person, which implies the respect, protection and promotion of human dignity and the rights of the person in the use of AI, which is why it was established that the use of such technology must, always, to promote the healthy and integral development of all.Secondly, the inclusion of the right to privacy and protection of personal data with a focus on AI was considered necessary. This right has several dimensions.The third right is related to transparency and access to information in use of AI. In this regard, it was considered necessary to establish the right of every person to receive information related to decision-making by AI, and that such information, invariably, makes known who is the person responsible for its use. Similarly, developers are expected to adopt transparency measures aimed at specifying the way in which these systems work and the factors considered for decision-making or specific predictions.The last right is safety in the use of AI, where it is enshrined that the measures implemented for this purpose must guarantee both personal integrity and human rights through the prevention and elimination of risks.

title: AI4Dev Reference Group
description: Key functions of the AI4Dev Reference Group will include mitigating the risks of AI by undertaking analysis and mapping out emerging trends of frontier technologies. Additionally, the Reference Group will serve as a sounding board and advisory panel on how to leverage AI and other frontier technologies towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030 in Nigeria. Further, it will provide advice to the broader development community in Nigeria and the UN leadership on measures to mitigate any risks associated with the uptake of these frontier technologies. Finally, the AI4Dev Reference Group will work as a Research and Development platform for policy makers, development partners and the entire UN System in Nigeria to better track and monitor trends, signals and advise on opportunities for AI.

title: Tech Trends Position Statement: Generative AI
description: This position statement examines the evolving landscape of generative AI, providing an overview of the generative AI lifecycle, examples of its use and misuse, and consideration of online safety risks and opportunities.The paper includes steps industry can take to prevent online safety risks of generative AI and improve user safety and empowerment. It also sets out eSafety's current tools and approaches to generative AI, which includes education for young people, parents and educators; reporting schemes for serious online abuse; transparency tools; and the status of mandatory codes and standards. The position paper was released in August 2023 was developed following significant consultation with experts in generative AI including academics and NGOs.The initiative has the following objective(s):Outline Office of the eSafety Commissioner's (eSafety's) approach to generative AI.

description: To foster the conditions for the development of the digital transformation strategy, there is a broad regulatory framework, but it is worth highlighting the Executive Decree N.41248, which establishes the High Level Commission of Digital Government, which will act as a consultative body for the development of the national strategy for the implementation of the public policy of digital government, and Law N.9943, which establishes the National Agency of Digital Government, as the executing body for interoperability and strategic projects in this area.There is a strategic framework within the institution that focuses on the development of the Costa Rican society and economy, which is the National Policy for the Knowledge-Based Society and Economy (PNSEBC); the plans of each vice ministry with a sectoral vision focused on their areas of work, such as the National Plan for Science, Technology and Innovation (PNCTI), the National Telecommunications Development Plan (PNDT), the National Cybersecurity Strategy and the Bioeconomy Strategy.In this way, the Digital Transformation Strategy seeks to be transversal to these planning instruments, developing digital government and governance components through its strategic axes.

title: Guidelines: Use of AI-Based Tools in Final Papers
description: The žGuidelines for the Use of AI-Based Tools in Final Papers by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research aim to address both opportunities and risks associated with generative AI, such as ChatGPT. The initiative ensures that AI tools are responsibly used and transparently documented while preventing misuse or academic dishonesty.Key measures include: Transparency in Use: Students must explicitly indicate if and how AI tools were used. Final papers require an updated declaration of originality, including details about AI usage. Unified Citation Rules: Standardized citation guidelines for AI-generated content are provided and mandatory. Accompanying Protocols: Students document all tools used in a process log. Supervision Protocols: Teachers track the work process and identify potential misuse of AI tools during supervision. Assessment Rubrics: Projects are evaluated through rubrics that integrate presentation, discussion, and work process, ensuring the written product is not the sole basis for assessment. Focus on Discussion: During presentations and discussions, targeted questions help uncover potential AI-assisted sections.These measures promote ethical use of AI, equip students with critical skills to navigate AI technologies, and ensure integrity in final papers.

title: AI Badge for eEducation Schools
description: The network eEducation Austria, comprising over 4,100 schools (including 1,400 Expert or Expert+ schools), introduces the AI Badge to enhance digital and AI literacy in schools. This initiative builds upon the network's existing badge system, which tracks digital activities and supports schools' progression from Member to Expert and Expert+ status.The AI Badge emphasizes: School Development: By integrating AI-related activities into the autonomous school development process, the initiative ensures that AI becomes a strategic focus at the local school level. Sustainable Engagement: Schools are required to engage with AI topics and complete at least one AI Badge by the end of the 2024/25 school year. Involvement of leadership: The initiative encourages school leadership to prioritize and sustain AI-focused initiatives, fostering awareness and readiness among educators and students alike.By implementing the AI Badge, eEducation Austria aims to ensure that attention is directed toward AI at the school level, where its impact is most critical. The initiative strengthens the role of AI as a key component of school development and prepares students for the demands of a digital future.

title: AI Pilot Schools: Learning and Teaching with AI Tools
description: The initiative žAI Pilot Schools, spearheaded by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research, examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools. The project involves three empirical phases: Baseline Survey (2023/24): A comprehensive questionnaire was distributed to assess the status quo of AI usage in Austrian schools. This survey combined rating scales and open questions to gather insights into the existing knowledge and tools available. Focus Survey (2024): Building on the initial results, a second quantitative survey titled žAI Pilot Schools in Focus documented teachers' experiences with AI technologies in their classrooms. Ongoing Documentation (2024): Teachers were provided with a structured template to record their qualitative experiences with AI-based learning tools throughout 2024.The surveys and documentation are conducted online, ensuring direct communication with the participating pilot schools. Data from the surveys have been analyzed using SPSS, while the qualitative documentation is being evaluated with MAXQDA software. These insights aim to support evidence-based recommendations for AI integration in education, enhancing teaching practices and student learning outcomes in the digital age.

title: Digital Administration Manual: AI, Ethics and Law – Practical Manual for Public Administration, Version 2.0
description: The Digital Administration Guide 2.0 aims to address the dual challenge of harnessing the opportunities presented by digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), while mitigating their associated risks. As AI systems become increasingly integrated into public administration, they offer significant potential to enhance efficiency, transparency, and citizen-centric services. However, these advancements also pose challenges related to ethical concerns, data protection, fairness, and the potential for bias. The guide serves as a practical framework to help public administrators navigate these complexities while maintaining public trust and adherence to legal and ethical standards. The main objective is to help public servants make well-founded decisions on whether and under which conditions AI should be used. The guide is intended for all public employees, including policy and service owners, project teams, IT, procurement, legal services, data protection and information security. It supports assessment across the full lifecycle, from early planning to procurement, deployment and review, as well as documentation of key decisions and safeguards. At its core, the guide offers a decision tree and a checklist with a criteria-and-measures catalogue (EKIV). These tools help teams assess requirements and safeguards relating to transparency, non-discrimination, data protection, human oversight and documentation. Version 2.0 covers generative AI and quantum AI and incorporates relevant obligations and risk considerations under the EU AI Act. It also includes the Federal AI Guidelines as practical recommendations for responsible use. The guide is a "living document," designed to evolve continuously through feedback from practitioners, advancements in technology, and regulatory updates. It is non-binding, and there are no concrete plans to introduce it as a mandatory, government-wide requirement. The Federal AI Guidelines, which are part of the manual, are planned to be used by federal ministries, within their respective remits, as a key reference for AI use. Seminars and an e-learning format support practical application. The approach may scale through voluntary uptake, reuse of the tools and training materials, and integration into project and procurement practices. Results, outcomes and impacts Results so far focus on capacity building and wider recognition. The Federal Administration Academy (VAB) seminar PM 215, based on the Practical Guide, has run four times since 2023, with 98 participants; the related e-learning module has 1,262 bookings. Impacts are tracked through registration and booking counts and standard course evaluations. The Austrian Court of Audit referenced the Practical Guide as an orientation tool for assessing ethical issues in AI use and recommended strengthening its uptake across ministries.

title: Implementation Plan for Nationwide Diffusion of AI into Everyday Life
description: Since the launch of ChatGPT in November, 2022, the competition over LLM among global tech giants is fierce; the US, EU, UK and other major players are actively discussing how to shape new norms and ensure safety regarding AI in order to address the technology's potential risks and misuses/abuses. Although Korea is relatively late to the competition, it is fast developing and securing its own LLM, backed by bold corporate ambitions and government support, creating synergies with the country's strengths in semiconductors, platforms and ICT infrastructure. The Korean government is providing support to boost AI application in specialized areas, promote mutual cooperation between large corporates and SMEs, and ensure world-class AI safety and trust so that Korean companies can lead the global market.

title: Strategy to Realize Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
description: There are high hopes for the potential benefits created by generative AI such as ChatGPT, while concerns are growing over AI-induced risks related to safety. Major countries and international organizations, recognizing that ensuring AI trust as a prerequisite to the development of AI industry, proposed guidelines and other voluntary measures to ensure AI safety. The initiative is aimed at addressing AI's innate technological limitations, including bias and the lack of transparency, as well as its potential risks, such as malfunction and failures.

title: Imagine AI for Dignity: Feminine Visions for Regeneration
description: The Austrian Foreign Ministry's initiative, "Imagine AI for Dignity & Creative Democratic Futures," is a key component of the national AI strategy aimed at exploring innovative ways to utilize AI in a manner that honors human dignity and the environment while fostering the creative evolution of liberal democracies. Central to this initiative is the exhibition "Imagine AI for Dignity - Feminine Visions for Regeneration," which presents forward-thinking perspectives on AI's role amid the interplay of digital humanism, democratic principles, and ecological progress. The exhibition responds to the pressing need for a fundamental societal transformation and technological advancement, drawing on concepts from critical posthumanism to envision what "regeneration" might entail in the context of contemporary technologies.Through visual art and media theory, the exhibition seeks to uncover innovative solutions to today's challenges, emphasizing empowerment, ecological regeneration, democratic values, and an inclusive future. It poses questions about what an AI influenced by feminine principles could resemble and what alternative visions for a regenerative future might arise from such an approach. Given that individuals identified as FLINTA/ female often face disproportionate impacts from bias, climate change, and technological advancements, a feminine perspective on digital humanism, the climate crisis, and democratic processes is crucial. This initiative advocates for the integration of care, healing, and sustainable practices into technological development rather than a complete rejection of technology.In light of the threats to liberal democratic values, the exhibition underscores the importance of designing and regulating AI technologies to enhance rather than compromise democratic principles and fundamental rights. As digital technologies reshape society, it is vital to evaluate them through a democratic lens. The project serves as a call to harness digital technologies in a manner that promotes an expanded humanism, which encompasses both human rights and ecological sustainability.Curated by experts Claudia Larcher and Eva Fischer, the exhibition is set to open on March 15 or 16 at the NIROX Art Center in South Africa's Cradle of Humankind, in collaboration with the Austrian Cultural Forum Pretoria. This exhibition, along with the curators' residency, workshops with students from the University of Pretoria and the University of Johannesburg, and the opening performance, is part of a broader project scheduled from March 10 to 20, 2025. Future plans include showcasing the exhibition at Austrian Embassies and Cultural Fora in sub-Saharan Africa, with a return to Austria in 2026, involving the UNESCO Chair for Digital Humanism at TU Wien and the University of Applied Arts Vienna, along with its Angewandte Interdisciplin.

title: National AI Strategy 2.0
description: The recent breakthroughs in AI demand a renewed focus by Singapore to refine our national strategies for AI:Greater capabilities. AI is now more powerful and accessible. We therefore need to work with producers and users of AI in a more concerted manner, because responsible development and deployment do not happen by chance.Greater concerns. There are growing concerns over the safety and security risks of AI, particularly Generative AI models. These range from fears over malicious attacks on AI models, to the current inscrutability of large language models (LLMs), which calls into question the validity, credibility, and legality of their output. Such concerns have garnered attention from many around the world.There are also new competitive realities around AI:Resources and talent for AI are scarce. These are concentrated within a few companies and countries, intensifying economic competition, as well as geostrategic and resilience risks.Other smaller countries are also moving quickly to attract AI investments and talent. While acquisitions for AI may be costly, they can confer enduring value and deepen capabilities, if properly integrated within the ecosystem.We will therefore make three shifts from our first National AI Strategy:From Opportunity to Necessity. People must know AI, not just see it as a good to have. We need both technical experts and savvy users to maximise AI's potential for Singapore.From Local to Global. Our people and businesses should operate with the ambition to be world-leading in AI. Singapore should be well-connected to global innovation networks, working with the best to overcome complex challenges surrounding AI today (e.g. energy, data, and ethics). Singapore must contribute to AI breakthroughs and products that the world values.From Projects to Systems. For AI to have widespread and positive impact on our economy and society, Singapore has to move beyond flagship National AI Projects. We will take a systems approach, bringing together stakeholders within and outside Singapore to add to our resources, capabilities, and infrastructure, accelerate the exchange of ideas, and administer AI-enabled solutions at scale.The initiative has the following objectives:1. Excellence. Singapore will selectively develop peaks of excellence in AI, to advance the field and maximise value creation.2. Empowerment. We will raise up individuals, businesses, and communities to use AI with confidence, discernment, and trust.

description: The impact of AI is not limited to only telecom sector. title: Approach Document for India: Part 3 - Adopting Framework - A use case approach on facial recognition technology
description: As a follow-up to NSAI, stakeholder discussions on the suggested method for the responsible use of new technologies were launched in 2019 in partnership with the World Economic Forums. It culminated in 2021 with the publication of a two-part approach document outlining principles for the responsible design, development, and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) in India, as well as enforcement measures for operationalising these principles (RAI principles).Against the backdrop of a growing clamour for developing governance and regulatory frameworks to reduce the possible hazards of AI while maximising its advantages for the most significant number of people, they set these RAI principles. These are safety and reliability, inclusivity and non-discrimination, equality, privacy and security, transparency, accountability, protection and reinforcement of positive human values.Furthermore, the proposed method needs to be tested in a use case to determine the recommended approach's efficacy and identify associated challenges. Therefore, facial recognition technology (FRT) has been selected as the first use case to examine the previously stated RAI principles and operationalisation mechanism.

title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
description: The initiative has the following objectives:In undertaking this voluntary commitment, developers and managers of advanced generative systems commit to working to achieve the following outcomes: 1. Accountability “ Firms understand their role with regard to the systems they develop or manage, put in place appropriate risk management systems, and share information with other firms as needed to avoid gaps.2. Safety “ Systems are subject to risk assessments, and mitigations needed to ensure safe operation are put in place prior to deployment.3. Fairness and Equity “ Potential impacts with regard to fairness and equity are assessed and addressed at different phases of development and deployment of the systems.4. Transparency “ Sufficient information is published to allow consumers to make informed decisions and for experts to evaluate whether risks have been adequately addressed.5. Human Oversight and Monitoring “ System use is monitored after deployment, and updates are implemented as needed to address any risks that materialize.6. Validity and Robustness “ Systems operate as intended, are secure against cyber attacks, and their behaviour in response to the range of tasks or situations to which they are likely to be exposed is understood.

title: Guide on the use of Generative AI
description: The Guide is intended to clarify when and how federal public servants can use generative AI tools. It encourages their use while identifying key risks and challenges and providing best practices for both everyday users and departments looking to deploy tools. It also presents responsible-use principles to help ensure that public servants use the tools ethically and in line with Government of Canada values and ethics. The Guide seeks to raise awareness and foster co-ordination among federal institutions. It highlights the importance of engaging key stakeholders, including legal counsel and privacy and security experts, before deploying generative AI tools for public use or using them for purposes such as service delivery. It is not mandatory, and data on its use are not collected. Many departments have used the Guide to inform their own generative AI policies. The Guide will be updated regularly to keep pace with regulatory and technological change as federal departments use and experiment with AI. A principles-based approach helps the guidance remain relevant as capabilities evolve. Developing it openly, with input from inside and outside government, provided a fuller picture of generative AI risks, challenges and best practices. The Guide also incorporates flexibility because generative AI risks are context-specific. Departments can interpret its principles to suit their own contexts.

title: Australian Framework for Generative AI in Schools
description: In February 2023, Education Ministers agreed that responding to the risks and harnessing opportunities for Australian schools and students arising from generative AI technologies is a national education priority. title: Algorithms Research
description: On 15 March 2022, the House of Representatives' Select Committee on Social Media and Online Safety (the Committee) tabled its final report on its Inquiry into Social Media and Online Safety (the Inquiry). The Inquiry looked at the use of algorithms on social media platforms and the harms and benefits they give rise to. The Report recommended a review of the use of algorithms by digital platforms, to consider possible regulatory options on algorithms, and the government's capability to address AI and other emerging tech regulation. title: Safe and Responsible AI in Australia: Interim Response
description: In 2023 the Australian Government consulted the public on its Safe and responsible AI in Australia discussion paper, which sought views on how the government can mitigate any potential risks of AI and support safe and responsible AI practices. On 17 January 2024 the government published its interim response to this consultation. Rather than move immediately to legislative approaches, the Government response outlines the need for further work on options, including through existing legislative reform agendas. This will include:o considering options for mandatory guardrails for those who develop or deploy AI systems in legitimate, but high risk settings.o considering further opportunities to strengthen existing laws to address risks and harms from AI.The initiative has the following objective(s):Outlines the government's aim to ensure the development and deployment of AI in high-risk settings is safe and reliable, and use in low-risk settings can continue to flourish largely unimpeded.

title: mAigov
description: mAigov is an AI-powered digital assistant integrated into Greece's unified public administration portal, gov.gr. Launched in December 2023 by the Ministry of Digital Governance, mAigov aims to streamline citizens' interactions with public services by simplifying access to information and procedures.mAIgov initiative seeks to resolve the inefficiencies in public service delivery and leverage the opportunity to enhance digital governance. It aims to make public services more accessible, efficient, and user-friendly through the use of AI technology.Objectives:Improve the quality, speed, and accessibility of public services.Enhance citizen interaction with government services.Promote transparency and accountability in public administration.Key Features of mAigov:Natural Language Processing: Users can engage with mAigov through text or voice inputs in natural language, allowing for intuitive searches of the services they require. The assistant is trained on over 1,600 services available on gov.gr and more than 3,270 administrative procedures from the National Register of Administrative Procedures, "MITOS."Multilingual Support: To accommodate a diverse user base, mAigov supports interactions in 25 languages, including the 24 official languages of the European Union and Albanian. This feature is particularly beneficial for Greeks living abroad and non-Greek-speaking individuals seeking information on Greek public services.User-Friendly Interface: Accessible via mobile devices and computers, mAigov provides a straightforward and friendly interface. Users can submit inquiries and receive guidance on locating the services they need. At the end of each interaction, users have the option to evaluate their experience, contributing to the system's ongoing improvement.Scalability and Performance: In its beta phase, mAigov can handle up to 240 conversations per minute in Greek, with each session limited to five minutes to ensure efficient service. A queuing mechanism manages user traffic, maintaining service quality during peak times.mAIgov goes through continuous updates and integration with more government services.mAIgov platform can scale by expanding its language capabilities and integrating with additional public services. This will allow broader access and improved service delivery for both Greek citizens and international users.Since its launch, mAIgov has evolved by increasing its language support to 25 languages and expanding its service offerings. It has seen significant user engagement and continuous improvements based on user feedback.Results: Over 1.6 million interactions with the bot, since its launch.

title: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligece Regulation and Ethics
description: The AI Policy identifies seven main challenges arising from the use of artificial intelligence in the private sector (discrimination, human oversight, explainability, disclosure of AI interactions, safety, accountability and privacy). To address these challenges, and consistent with the approach taken by the OECD AI Recommendations, the AI Policy sets forth common policy principles and a number of practical recommendations.The main recommendation are: Adopting sectoral regulation Promoting consistency with existing regulatory approach of leading countries and international organizations Adopting a risk-based approach Using "soft" regulatory tools intended to allow for an incremental development of the regulatory framework Fostering cooperation between the public and the private sectors.The initiative has the following objectives:The AI Policy provides guidelines and instructions for sectoral regulators when addressing the regulation of AI in the private sector. While some parts of the AI Policy can be natively applied to the public sector as well, a full discussion of the required adaptations and modifications is out of the scope of this Policy. The government's policy on public sector applications of AI is being developed separately.With respect to private sector applications, the AI Policy is premised upon the concept of "Responsible Innovation", which captures the need to support innovation while simultaneously fostering accountability and ethically-aligned design and uses of AI. While private sector innovation and ethics (or regulation) are often perceived as conflicting with one another, responsible innovation views these two goals as synergistic and mutually complementary. The AI Policy applies this concept to the entire lifecycle of AI applications, with a special focus on use and deployment.

title: The Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications Education Intelligence
description: The Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications by the Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA) is intended to be a guide for the development, evaluation, and accreditation of higher education programs in AI, serving as a reliable, primary reference recognized in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Recognized scientific methodologies were considered in the preparation of the framework. Thus, an integrated methodology that combines the descriptive, historical, and predictive approaches was adopted. The framework is designed to be flexible and general to keep pace with the rapidly developing nature of the field, empowering educational and training institutions to foster development and creativity. The framework focuses on the specifications of study plans for academic and training programs in the field of AI, as well as ensuring the quality of such programs. Also, it specifies the certificates granted in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia based on global benchmarks and explains the general learning outcomes for the graduates of these programs.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024–2030
description: This National Artificial Intelligence Strategy serves as the cornerstone for the implementation of a public AI policy that encompasses the public and private sectors and all stakeholders. It aims to enhance Uruguay's sustainable development across all dimensions, contributing to inclusive economic growth, the country's environmental sustainability, and the strengthening of its sovereignty.To this end, the National Strategy establishes the foundations for national AI governance based on a multi-stakeholder approach. It ensures the capacities needed to harness AI for the development of various economic sectors and to achieve a more egalitarian and inclusive society. The Strategy builds upon and simultaneously promotes the progress made by the country in digital transformation, research, and innovation.The Strategy aligns AI policy with the National Cybersecurity Strategy (2024“2030), the National Digital Citizenship Strategy for an Information and Knowledge Society (2024“2028), and the National Data Strategy (2030), co-created alongside this document.In the public domain, it provides sustainability to the achievements realized through the AI Strategy for Digital Government (2020) and aims to deepen these efforts by advancing the use of AI to improve public services and the management of public entities.It lays the groundwork to foster and optimize public and private investment, enabling the country to develop the necessary infrastructure and capacities for AI deployment across both public and private sectors. The Strategy acknowledges the significant challenges Uruguay faces in this area, considering the scale of its economy and national budget.The Strategy does not overlook the risks AI poses to society, human rights, and democracy. On the contrary, it establishes the foundations to address these risks appropriately and effectively, outlining various action lines aimed at developing regulatory frameworks and the necessary capacities while promoting collaboration among all stakeholders.The approved Strategy is based on 10 guiding principles in accordance with article 74 of Law No. 20.212, of November 6, 2023. It also contains 12 lines of action organized into 3 Pillars: Governance, Capabilities for AI and Sustainable Development and the creation, monitoring and review process statement.

title: DAEDALUS Hypercomputer
description: The new supercomputing system, capable of executing more than 60 petaflops or 60 million billion calculations per second (aggregated performance), will drive European innovation and support scientific advancements. It will enable new applications across a wide range of fields including engineering, chemistry and health sciences. DAEDALUS supercomputer will be available to serve a wide range of users, no matter where in Europe they are located, in the scientific community, industry and the public sector. Access to the computing resources of the new machine will be jointly managed by theEuroHPCJU and the DAEDALUS consortium in proportion to their investment.The system will be managed and operated by GRNET S.A. The National Infrastructures for Research and Technology, in Athens, Greece, operating under the auspices of the Greek Ministry of Digital Governance. It will be installed in the new data centre located in the building of the former Power Station of the Lavrion Technological Cultural Park of the National Technical University of Athens. The total investment for Daedalus, including the infrastructural modifications of its host building, is valued at approximately 50 million. The funding comprises resources from Greece's National Recovery and Resilience Plan Greece 2.0, supported by the European Union's NextGenerationEU initiative, alongside contributions from the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU).This initiative underlines the government's strategy to enhance Greece's public digital infrastructure, which forms part of its broader Digital Transformation Plan for 2020-2025. One of Daedalus's core objectives is to support an array of complex research activities. The supercomputer's hybrid architecture, combining high-density CPUs and accelerator units, is optimized for diverse applications spanning artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and big data analytics. Its capabilities will facilitate advancements in natural language requests, personalized medicine, spatial planning, fire protection and disaster response as well as smart mobility and autonomous vehicle technology.For scientists in computational fields such as chemistry, physics, and biology, the supercomputer offers unprecedented resources to expedite research cycles, simulate complex phenomena, and conduct large-scale experiments previously constrained by limited computational power.The installation of Daedalus marks a significant step forward for Greece's digital strategy. By hosting one of Europe's most powerful supercomputers, the nation is poised to enhance its competitive edge in scientific research and technological development. This strategic initiative sets the stage for Greece to emerge as a leader in high-performance computing, securing its place in the rapidly evolving landscape of global technology.
