title: Application Laboratory for AI and Big Data (AI Lab)
description: The AI lab located at the Federal Environment Agency started its operations after its official opening in October 2023.The two central tasks of the AI lab are the modernization and digitalization of the environmental administration and the development of AI and data-based applications to support the agencies in the jurisdication oft he BMUV in their enforcement and research tasks.With currently 32 employees, the AI lab has built up substantial "in-house" expertise, particularly in the areas of data, data analysis, and AI, in order to anchor data-based and modern working within the authorities - from automated processes to new work methods. Regarding concrete applications, todate more than 70 AI application cases have been identified in various areas through the cyclical "Use Case Discovery Process" developed specifically for the AI lab, twenty of which are currently being implemented or have been finished.The data-based insights gained from the Use Cases in the AI Lab can serve as a basis for political decisions by the BMUV and the Federal Government. Results are also made available to the public and enable a deeper understanding of complex environmental and transformation processes.The establishment of the AI lab was decided as a measure within the environmental policy digital agenda of the BMUV and anchored in the updated AI strategy 2020 and the federal government's data strategy 2021. The AI lab is being financed with a total of 26.4 million for a limited period from 2021-2025. Future financing from 2026 is not yet secured.

title: Clusters of Excellence
description: COE Bilateral Artificial Intelligence:The Bilateral research project, coordinated by the Johannes Kepler University Linz, combines research in two fields of artificial intelligence: sub-symbolic AI (machine learning) and symbolic AI (knowledge representation and reasoning). The project aims to bringing together both approaches, with the common goal of developing the foundations of Broad AI. Broad AI could be capable of coming to its own conclusions and demonstrating comprehensive cognitive abilities. While existing AI programs like ChatGPT are currently causing a sensation, they ultimately only evaluate existing data. New AI systems could plan better, adapt quickly to changing situations, and become creative in a broader sense.COE Quantum Science Austria:The Cluster of Excellence Quantum Science Austria aims to advance basic research in quantum science and expand the frontiers of knowledge, making it a driver for future innovations. Its focus is on fundamental questions about the quantum nature of space, time, and gravity, new paradigms in quantum information science, and the physics of quantum many-body systems. Its research potential lies also in the highly innovative field of next generation high performance computing, quantum computing and their combination.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Centers
description: Taking into account the progress made in Colombia concerning the adoption of Artificial Intelligence systems and the contribution they can make to accelerate accurate decision-making based on data and evidence, as well as the priorities established by the National Government on this issue and channeled by the Ministry of ICT, it has been proposed that the country will be able to adopt Artificial Intelligence systems that can be used to accelerate decision making based on data and evidence.That has been channeled from the ICT Ministry, and the creation of artificial intelligence centers has been proposed. These Centers will be essential articulators for the strategy of digital ecosystems being consolidated at the national level.These AI Centers will foster the development and/or evolution of AI systems for decision-making on public issues, strengthen the regulatory sphere, and promote the articulation between actors, strategies, and resources aimed at promoting public innovation. While these will be AI Centers for the entire digital innovation ecosystem, they will be directly supported by the ICT Ministry, and their themes will be related to the development of public challenges and the strengthening ofstate capacities that translate into improved service delivery to the Colombian population.

title: National Programme for Transparency and Protection of Personal Data in the Use of Artificial Intelligence
description: Given the exponential growth in the integration of artificial intelligence solutions in different sectors, the Agency of Access to Public Information (AAIP) has developed a programme to focus on the potential social, economic, cultural and environmental risks that need to be studied and addressed to avoid bias and discrimination.This programme promotes analysis processes, regulation and capacity building to accompany the development and use of AI. It is aimed at public and private entities that use automated decision making systems with AI applications.It has the following lines of action: Observatory on AI, to monitor regional and global progress in the regulation of technological developments based on AI and promote algorithmic. transparency; Governance and social participation, to promote joint work with government bodies of technological and legal governance ; and capacity building, to provide training and technical assistance on transparency and protection of personal data in the use of the AI and awareness campaigns, media and information literacy.The expected evolution of the programme is to be integrated into a broader national AI strategy, in order to ensure synergy with other initiatives of the national public administration.

title: RETECH IA
description: The RETECH IA programme is part of Spain’s broader Territorial Networks of Technological Specialisation (RETECH) framework, coordinated by the Government of Spain (Gobierno de España) . It is designed to connect regions, institutions, and companies to develop and implement artificial intelligence solutions with national and European impact. Key aspects include: 13 flagship projects (see Box 1) covering different domains and use cases of AI, from research to applied innovation. Interregional cooperation – building synergies between Spain’s autonomous communities and avoiding duplication of efforts. Public–private collaboration – involving technology centres, companies, universities, and public administrations. Support for scaling and deployment – helping AI projects move from pilots to full-scale implementation. The main objectives of RETECH IA are to: Strengthen Spain’s AI capabilities at a territorial level. Encourage shared infrastructures, data spaces, and standards . Facilitate cross-regional knowledge transfer and innovation . Align national efforts with the EU’s Digital Europe Programme and other European initiatives. By aggregating resources and expertise across regions, RETECH IA accelerates the adoption of AI technologies and contributes to Spain’s leadership in the European digital economy.

title: Strengthen and retain specialised IT talent and skills
description: The national IT education strategy is designed to address the shortage of specialised IT skills in Denmark and to ensure the workforce is prepared for a technology-driven economy. It focuses on: Expanding continuing and further education programmes in IT, enabling professionals to update and deepen their technical competencies. Enhancing professional Master’s programmes in IT education , ensuring high-quality advanced training aligned with industry needs. Attracting and retaining international students , supporting their integration into the Danish labour market to strengthen the pool of skilled IT professionals. Aligning educational pathways with emerging technology trends , including digitalisation, AI, cybersecurity, and advanced computing. Through these measures, the strategy seeks to boost Denmark’s IT workforce , maintain global competitiveness, and address the country’s demand for highly qualified technology professionals .

title: Recommendations on AI based tools for examinations in primary, lower and upper secondary school
description: In May 2023, the Ministry of Children and Education set up an expert group to examine the implications of AI-based tools in primary, lower, and upper secondary school examinations . This group: Developed recommendations issued in April 2024 on how to integrate AI-based tools into assessments. Proposed the use of different testing methods to better evaluate students’ knowledge, skills, and ability to critically use digital tools. Highlighted the importance of aligning examinations with real-world digital competencies , ensuring students are not only knowledgeable but also able to apply and reflect critically on technology use. Provides a foundation for the Ministry’s future work in shaping policies and frameworks on AI and digital tool use in education. This initiative marks a proactive approach to digital-era assessment , aiming to ensure that educational evaluations remain relevant and equitable in a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

title: Allowance for the payment of digital training courses
description: This initiative, launched under the RRF , is designed to expand access to digital and AI training for individuals across the Czech Republic. It: Subsidises course fees , covering up to 82% of costs (maximum ~EUR 2,000 per person over three years), reducing financial barriers to upskilling. Is administered via the “I’m in a Course” platform , which acts as a one-stop shop for available training opportunities. Encourages participation in digital and AI-focused courses , from basic digital literacy to advanced AI programming and applications. Aims to support lifelong learning and workforce adaptability , equipping people with in-demand skills needed for the green and digital transitions. By reducing costs and centralising course offerings, the initiative broadens participation in digital upskilling , helping individuals and employers respond to rapid technological change.

description: The programme is designed to equip students with highly specialised knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence, data analytics, and Big Data technologies . Comprehensive AI and Big Data curriculum : Students gain theoretical knowledge and practical experience in machine learning, data processing, and AI applications . Industry-relevant training : Focused on professional readiness , the programme prepares graduates for careers in data science, AI development, and related sectors . description: The INSAIT Explorer Programme is designed to nurture exceptional students in computer science and AI through a unique integration of academic study and hands-on research. Key features include: Bachelor’s degree integration : Students complete a four-year undergraduate programme at Sofia University while participating in research at INSAIT. Advanced AI curriculum : Covers machine learning, robotics, quantum computing , and other emerging technologies. Research opportunities : Fellows work alongside researchers on cutting-edge AI projects , gaining practical skills and experience. Industry-supported : Funded through donations and partnerships with private sector companies, ensuring exposure to real-world applications. Talent cultivation : The programme aims to develop future leaders in AI and technology in Bulgaria, bridging the gap between education, research, and industry. By combining rigorous academic study with applied research , the INSAIT Explorer Programme creates a pipeline of highly skilled AI professionals , positioning Bulgaria as a competitive player in the global AI and technology ecosystem.

title: The National AI Policy
description: The vision of the strategy is to become a global center for AI research and innovation. The mission is to leverage AI to power economic growth, improve quality of life and position Rwanda as a global innovator for responsible and inclusive AI. Six priority policy areas have been identified to accelerate the responsible development and deployment of AI across the nation. These priority areas are categorised as enablers, accelerators or safeguards. Priority areas categorised as enablers are 1) 21st century skills and high AI literacy, and 2) reliable infrastructure and compute capacity, and 3) robust strategy. Priority areas categorised as accelerators are 1) trustworthy AI adoption in the public sector, and 2) widely beneficial AI adoption in the private sector. The priority area categorised as safeguard is practical ethical guidelines. The National AI Policy includes the recommendation to establish a Responsible AI Office (RAI Office) during the first year of this policy, housed within MINICT. The RAI Office will have the coordinating responsibility of driving the AI policy Implementation Plan. The RAI Office is to be given the mandate to implement the National AI Policy by coordinating stakeholders across institutions and championing the responsible development and deployment of AI across the Rwandan public and private sectors. Beyond domestic engagement, the RAI Office may participate in global AI governance efforts, e.g. by the OECD/Global Partnership on AI (GPAI), ITU, and UNESCO. Besides, the RAI Office will be tasked with the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the policy, the integration of the implementation plan in regional-level policies and actors, as well as with leading communications around the National AI Policy. Rwanda has a momentous opportunity to leverage advancements in AI to achieve national objectives outlined in Vision 2050. By launching the Responsible AI Office, coordinating key actors and driving action, MINICT accelerates AI adoption in Rwanda to achieve objectives linked to sustainable and inclusive development and capacity building in Rwanda.

title: PoVejMo
description: The PoVejMo programme is a Slovenian research and innovation initiative focused on adaptive natural language processing (NLP) with large-scale language models. The programme is implemented via a public call for co-funding of longer-term, large collaborative research and innovation projects, targeting Technical Readiness Levels (TRL) 3–6 , which cover experimental proof-of-concept through to prototype validation. Key objectives of the programme include: Advancing research in NLP by leveraging AI to create models capable of understanding and generating human-like language. Promoting collaborative innovation by funding multi-institutional projects that involve universities, research institutes, and industry partners. Strengthening Slovenia’s AI ecosystem , particularly in the field of language technologies. Bridging fundamental research and applied AI solutions , enabling technologies that can be deployed in industry, public administration, and services. The initiative is overseen and co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation , ensuring alignment with national research priorities and European AI strategies. Through PoVejMo, Slovenia seeks to enhance its capacity in AI-driven language technologies , support interdisciplinary collaboration, and strengthen the country’s position in the European AI landscape. Looking forward, the programme is expected to foster scalable AI language solutions , contribute to digital innovation in society and industry , and support researchers in developing cutting-edge tools that are both technically advanced and practically applicable.

title: COFUND SMASH project
description: The SMASH programme (funded under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND Actions) is an intersectoral, career-development training initiative designed to attract international talent and support Slovenia’s digital and scientific ambitions. Coordinated by the University of Nova Gorica , with key partners including the University of Ljubljana, the Jožef Stefan Institute, the Slovenian Environment Agency, and the Maribor Institute of Information Sciences , the programme integrates advanced research infrastructures and interdisciplinary collaboration. The core goals of SMASH are to: Recruit 50 top postdoctoral researchers from around the world, with a focus on both global talent and Slovenian researchers working abroad. Leverage machine learning, AI, and the Vega supercomputer to conduct research across disciplines, from natural sciences and engineering to social sciences and humanities. Strengthen Slovenia’s research ecosystem , embedding international expertise and fostering cross-sectoral collaboration. Beyond research, the programme also aligns with national talent and innovation policies . With support from the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation , two complementary projects have been launched: Developing a mechanism to attract foreign and returning Slovenian experts , enhancing Slovenia’s competitiveness in global digitalisation trends. Creating an analytical model for evaluating policy measures that support the return of highly educated Slovenes. Looking forward, the SMASH programme is expected to have a long-term impact by: Increasing Slovenia’s visibility and integration within international research networks. Supporting the next generation of AI-driven research across diverse fields. Enhancing national innovation capacity through talent retention, institutional collaboration, and cross-border knowledge exchange. By combining world-class research infrastructure with targeted policies for talent mobility, SMASH represents a strategic investment in both Slovenia’s scientific future and its role in shaping Europe’s digital transformation.

title: Digital Competences and Basic Knowledge of Computer and Information Science
description: As digital technologies become more central to education, there is growing recognition of the need to improve students’ digital skills from an early age. Many school systems face challenges in adapting their teaching methods and curricula to support this shift. In Slovenia, the Ministry of Education has taken steps to address this issue by launching targeted public tenders to support innovative projects in schools. The aim is to build and test new ways of teaching digital skills — especially digital literacy and foundational knowledge in computer and information science — in real classroom settings. The Ministry has run two public tenders to fund experimental projects in selected schools or groups within schools. These projects are designed to explore new methods for developing digital competences and computer science knowledge, particularly in departments or learning groups that take an innovative approach to teaching. The goal is not only to improve students’ technical understanding but also to strengthen problem-solving, logical thinking, and digital creativity. This approach supports a more hands-on and engaging learning experience that reflects how digital technologies are used in everyday life and in the workplace. The selected projects are carried out in cooperation with educational institutions, teachers, and subject experts. Each participating school or department proposes its own concept for how digital competences will be taught and tested, often using new tools, interdisciplinary methods, or flexible teaching formats. The Ministry supports these efforts by funding their implementation and evaluation. Over time, the results of these experimental efforts help the Ministry identify effective practices and consider how they might be scaled across the education system. Looking forward, these projects may influence broader curriculum reforms or lead to the development of new national standards for digital competence education. By testing ideas on a smaller scale first, the Ministry can better understand what works in different educational contexts. This initiative reflects Slovenia’s wider goal of preparing students for a digital future — not just by giving them access to technology, but by teaching them how to use it meaningfully and confidently in all areas of life.

title: CitCom.ai TEF
description: CitCom.ai (Smart Cities & Communities TEF) is designed to support the development and deployment of AI/robotics solutions in urban environments by offering real-world testing and experimentation. It addresses the challenge that many AI innovations are developed in laboratory settings but struggle to meet technical, societal, regulatory, or environmental requirements in actual city settings. By bridging that gap, it helps ensure that AI systems work reliably among people, infrastructure, mobility systems, and public spaces. Its objectives include: Validating new AI algorithms and robotics hardware/software. Providing guidance on ethics, compliance, regulations (including upcoming EU AI-related laws) to ensure innovations are lawful and socially acceptable. Assessing risks and opportunities of AI in urban and communal settings (mobility, connectivity, power systems, public spaces) to inform both innovators and policy makers. Facilitating ecosystem engagement—connecting innovators, public authorities, R&D institutions, and citizens—to foster collaborative development and responsible adoption. In its implementation, CitCom.ai operates through a consortium spanning 11 EU countries and several partner nodes (“super-nodes”) grouped by thematic focus (Power, Move, Connect) that cover various spatial and sectoral sub-nodes. It offers services such as testbeds, living labs, digital twins, virtual and physical validation environments, and guidance on complying with relevant regulatory frameworks.

title: NAVAJO
description: NAVAJO is a pilot project designed to enhance smart mobility by deploying an autonomous shuttle service in Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve. Its main purpose is to test and validate autonomous transport technologies and assess how they can be integrated into existing urban mobility frameworks. The initiative supports: Evaluation of safety, reliability, and efficiency of autonomous shuttles in real-life conditions Development of guidelines and best practices for incorporating autonomous vehicles into public transport networks Demonstration of smart mobility solutions for medium-sized cities Funded under Digital Wallonia’s “Intelligent Territories (Territoires Intelligents)” call for projects, NAVAJO helps the Walloon Region explore how innovative technologies can improve connectivity, sustainability, and public transport options. Looking ahead, the project may inform the wider rollout of autonomous shuttles and other intelligent transport systems across the region. Insights gained from NAVAJO will support urban planners, policymakers, and transport operators in designing future mobility solutions.

title: Flemish Task Force on Automated Driving
description: The task force was created as a collaboration platform by the Flemish Departments of Economy, Science, and Innovation (EWI) and Mobility . It brings together research institutions, innovation actors, mobility stakeholders, and logistics operators to strengthen cooperation on automated and connected transport systems in Flanders. Its main goals are to: Foster an ecosystem for shared automated road mobility Accelerate development and deployment of autonomous driving technologies Connect key actors across research, policy, and industry to stimulate innovation Although not yet a formal project, the task force has been proposed for funding under a cross-border Interreg initiative , which is currently under evaluation. If funded, it could become a major driver for cross-border testing, policy alignment, and large-scale deployment of autonomous and shared mobility solutions in the region. Looking ahead, the task force is expected to expand partnerships , develop pilot projects , and strengthen the regulatory and innovation environment for autonomous mobility in Flanders and neighbouring regions.

title: Cross-cutting platform of artificial intelligence applied to the agri-food sector
description: The Cross-cutting platform of AI applied to the agri-food sector (Proyecto PAN) is a regional consortium initiative launched in 2023. It aims to create a transversal AI platform that integrates various stakeholders, technologies, and services to enhance the agri-food value chain. By leveraging disruptive technologies, the platform seeks to improve efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in agriculture and food production. Key objectives include: Promoting the use of AI and advanced technologies across the agri-food sector Fostering collaboration between companies, research centres, and public institutions Enhancing innovation and competitiveness in regional and national agri-food industries The platform operates as a shared ecosystem, allowing stakeholders to exchange data, tools, and best practices. It also facilitates research, pilot projects, and knowledge transfer, ensuring that AI solutions can be applied effectively in real-world agricultural and food production settings. Future outlook: Scaling AI adoption across multiple agri-food sub-sectors Expanding regional and national collaboration networks Driving digital transformation and sustainable innovation in the sector

title: Strategic plan for the common agricultural policy for the 2023–2027 period
description: The Slovenian Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy (2023–2027) is designed to modernise agriculture through the adoption of digital technologies and advanced production methods. The strategy provides targeted support for farmers and agribusinesses to implement AI and machine learning solutions in their production and processing activities. Key objectives of the initiative include: Supporting investment in modern machinery and equipment with integrated IT solutions Promoting precision agriculture techniques for better resource management and productivity Encouraging sectoral interventions in fruit and vegetable growing to enhance digitalisation and innovation Integrating AI and machine learning into production and processing processes to optimise operations The plan also emphasises collaboration between farmers, technology providers, and research institutions to ensure that digital solutions are both practical and effective. By funding these modernisation efforts, Slovenia aims to increase the competitiveness and sustainability of its agricultural sector. Future outlook: Broader adoption of smart farming practices across the country Enhanced digital skills and AI capabilities among farmers and agribusinesses Strengthened alignment between technology, innovation, and sectoral development priorities

title: Green.Dat.AI
description: GREEN.DAT.AI is a Horizon Europe research and innovation project focused on creating energy-efficient, large-scale data analytics services that can be directly integrated into AI-based industrial systems . By reducing the environmental footprint of data management, the project combines technological advancement with sustainability. The project demonstrates its new analytics services across four industries — Smart Energy, Smart Agriculture/Agri-food, Smart Mobility, and Smart Banking — and six different application scenarios (pilots) to showcase their efficiency and scalability. This approach leverages European Data Spaces to ensure secure, interoperable, and cross-sectoral data usage. In Slovenia , the Innovation Technology Cluster (ITC) , a national business support organisation, is responsible for coordinating and implementing two pilots : Smart farming optimisation through digital twins Smart water management Future outlook: Broader roll-out of green data analytics solutions across European industries Increased energy efficiency and lower environmental impact of AI-based data systems Strengthened cross-border collaboration and use of European Data Spaces for sustainable digital transformation

It directs funding to projects that help agriculture and forestry meet new challenges, from climate change to sustainability. Key areas of focus include: Adaptation to climate change in agricultural and forestry sectors Efficient management of natural resources and production inputs Conservation of biodiversity and adoption of environmentally friendly practices Implementation of innovative technologies and processes to reduce greenhouse gas emissions Production of healthy agri-food products and promotion of the circular economy Digitalisation of agricultural and forestry activities The plan encourages collaboration between research institutions, agricultural organisations, and technology providers , ensuring that innovative solutions are effectively transferred to practice. By funding projects in these priority areas, ADER 2026 helps strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of rural areas. Future outlook: Continued support for innovative, environmentally friendly practices Greater emphasis on digitalisation and climate-smart technologies A stronger, evidence-based approach to sustainable agriculture and forestry

description: The AI4EOSC project aims to enhance the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) ecosystem by integrating services related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning . By leveraging EOSC infrastructure, the project provides researchers and practitioners with advanced tools for data-driven applications. A key component is the agricultural scenario-pilot developed by the Wielkopolska Agricultural Advisory Center (WODR) in Poznań together with the Poznań Supercomputing and Networking Center . This pilot focuses on: Predicting risks of diseases and pests in agricultural crops Determining plant growth phases using AI models Supporting farmers and advisors with actionable insights for crop management The project’s objectives are to: Expand the EOSC ecosystem with AI-enabled services Facilitate applied research in agriculture using AI and machine learning Strengthen collaboration between research centers and agricultural practitioners Future outlook: The AI4EOSC project is expected to scale by incorporating additional agricultural scenarios, integrating more AI models, and expanding services across Europe, promoting sustainable and precision agriculture through AI-driven insights.

title: Supply of robotics and STEM equipment for education
description: The programme supports schools nationwide by supplying robotics kits to kindergartens, elementary schools, and high schools. These kits include hardware and software that allow pupils to build and program complete projects, combining hands-on learning with digital problem-solving. Its main objectives are to: Introduce robotics and coding into early education Encourage STEM skills development among children and teenagers Provide equal access to modern educational tools in schools across the country By equipping classrooms with robotics kits, the initiative helps teachers integrate interactive, project-based learning into their lessons. It also supports the development of critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration skills that are essential for future careers. In the future, the programme may expand the range of kits and training offered, ensuring that both teachers and students can keep pace with technological advances and develop the competencies needed for a digital economy.

title: A central AI Educational Platform
description: The initiative is a flagship project of the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation . It is designed to operate as a shared virtual space where AI experts from academia and industry collaborate to produce high-quality educational resources . Its main objectives are to: Foster collaboration between universities, research institutions, and industry experts in AI Develop and share educational material to enhance AI training and awareness Build a sustainable ecosystem for AI education that supports Greece’s digital transformation goals By creating a centralised digital hub for AI learning materials, the initiative seeks to ensure broad access to up-to-date knowledge and best practices. This approach is expected to strengthen Greece’s ability to train AI professionals , increase industry–academia cooperation , and develop a skilled workforce to support the country’s AI-driven future. Looking ahead, the project aims to expand the range of educational materials , involve more institutions, and potentially integrate with European-level AI education initiatives. This would position Greece as a regional leader in AI education and skills development .

title: SME: Digital and Denmark’s Export and Investment fund (EIFO) digitalisation support for small businesses
description: Small and medium-sized firms often lack the resources to make full use of digital tools like AI. To address this, Denmark’s Export and Investment Fund (EIFO) supports SMEs with grants for expert advice on digitalisation and AI, as well as subsidies for investments, training, and management development. Since May 2023, EIFO has also worked with the European Investment Fund to make financing more accessible, unlocking more than DKK 300 million for smaller firms to upgrade their digital capacity. EIFO combines grants, loans, equity, and guarantees to help companies adopt new technologies and build skills. In 2024, it invested in nearly 80 companies and over a dozen funds, including in AI infrastructure. Over time, EIFO’s support is expected to reach more sectors and firms, spreading digital know-how and strengthening Denmark’s competitiveness in the digital economy.

title: Digital Decade: no one is left behind
description: The Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA) in Lithuania launched the project “Digital Decade: no one is left behind” to address the digital exclusion of seniors. Many older citizens face difficulties using online services or recognising online fraud, which limits their ability to benefit from digital tools and puts them at risk. The project’s main goal is to ensure that seniors can access digital services confidently, safely, and with a clear understanding of their consumer rights. The initiative works as a multi-year tour across Lithuanian communities, where CRA experts meet seniors directly, offer practical training, and provide guidance on everyday digital tasks. Participants learn how to use online services more easily, how to stay safe from scams, and where to seek help if needed. Over time, the project plans to expand its outreach, ensuring that more communities benefit and that seniors are better integrated into the country’s digital transformation.

title: Developing AI solutions at all education levels
description: Lithuania’s Ministry of Education, Science and Sport is leading a reform to bring artificial intelligence into classrooms at all levels of education. The initiative responds to the growing need for students and teachers to understand and use AI in a safe, informed way. Its main objective is to apply international recommendations on AI in schools and ensure that lessons integrate these tools responsibly and effectively. The programme is coordinated with the National Education Agency and the Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Association, which provide consultations, guidance, and teacher training. This support helps educators learn how to use AI in teaching while addressing ethical and safety concerns.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
description: Czechia hosts several European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that help businesses and public institutions adopt advanced digital tools. Many organisations, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, face barriers such as high costs, limited expertise, and uncertainty about how technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) or high-performance computing (HPC) can be applied. The hubs address this by offering a safe space to test solutions, build skills, and access expert guidance before making large investments. One example is EDIH CTU at the Czech Technical University in Prague, which supports AI and HPC applications. It provides consultations, training, and access to powerful computing resources so organisations can experiment with practical uses of AI. Another is the EDIH Testbed for Industry 4.0, which focuses on advanced manufacturing. Here, companies can trial robotics and automation technologies, working directly with researchers to solve production challenges and train staff in new methods. Over time, Czech EDIHs are expected to deepen their links with the wider European network, giving local firms access to shared expertise across the EU. This scaling up will make it easier for Czech industry to adopt digital tools and remain competitive, resilient, and innovative.

title: Digital entrepreneurship programme for schoolchildren in grades 5-8 of the Ministry of Economy and Innovation
description: Lithuania’s Ministry of Economy and Innovation has launched a Digital Entrepreneurship Programme to address the lack of early exposure to digital and entrepreneurial skills among pupils in grades 5–8. Many students at this age miss the opportunity to connect computer science with creativity and business thinking. The programme aims to fill that gap by designing a clear methodology for teaching digital entrepreneurship that is both practical and engaging. The initiative works by developing integrated lessons that combine computer science, problem-solving, and entrepreneurship, tailored to young learners. Delivered in schools with support from trained educators, it encourages students to apply digital tools in creative ways while learning the basics of entrepreneurship. Over time, the programme plans to scale up across Lithuania, ensuring that more pupils gain the confidence and skills needed to participate in a digital economy.

title: European Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) Manufacturing
description: In Czechia, the Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) for manufacturing brings together three universities to help modernize production through artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics. Czech manufacturers, like many across Europe, face pressure to remain competitive while dealing with rising costs, supply chain disruptions, and the need for more sustainable processes. The TEF gives them access to advanced testing spaces where new technologies can be tried out in realistic industrial settings before being adopted on the factory floor. The main goal is to strengthen the resilience and flexibility of Czech industry. By supporting AI-driven automation, the TEF helps production lines adjust quickly to market changes, reduce errors, and manage resources more efficiently. Local companies can present specific challenges to the facility and receive support from researchers and engineers in designing practical solutions. At the same time, the project provides training opportunities so that workers gain the skills needed to use these tools effectively. As part of a wider European network, the Czech TEF will benefit from shared expertise and common standards developed across the EU.

title: Web-based advice on AI in education
description: The rise of AI tools like generative chatbots brings both new chances and challenges for schools. Teachers and school leaders need guidance on how to use these tools responsibly while avoiding problems like cheating or privacy issues. To help with this, the National Agency for Education has created a web-based support tool for educators and school administrators. The tool’s main goal is to provide clear advice on the risks and benefits of AI in schools. It helps users understand how AI can support learning and what steps to take to ensure ethical use and protect academic integrity. It covers practical topics like digital skills, data privacy, and responsible AI use in teaching. Developed by the National Agency for Education, the tool is freely available online and designed for teachers, school leaders, and school providers. It is regularly updated to reflect changes in AI technology and real experiences from schools, helping educators adapt and use AI in a safe and effective way.

title: A joint project of the education and learning programme "Vedliai" and "Lietuvos Junior Achievement" (LJA)
description: This joint initiative by the education programme Vedliai and Lietuvos Junior Achievement (LJA) addresses the gap in practical digital and entrepreneurial education for young students in Lithuania. Many pupils in grades 5–8 are not exposed early enough to how computer science and entrepreneurship can connect to real-world opportunities. The project aims to change this by offering integrated lessons that combine coding, digital creativity, and business thinking in ways that are accessible and engaging. The programme is delivered directly in schools, supported by trained teachers and mentors who adapt the lessons to pupils’ age and interests. By blending computer science with entrepreneurship, it equips students with both technical and problem-solving skills while encouraging creativity and teamwork. Over time, the project plans to expand to more schools across Lithuania, ensuring that a larger share of pupils gain the knowledge and confidence needed to participate in the country’s growing digital economy.

title: State programme for developing, attracting and retaining talent – specific call on AI
description: The promotion of the consolidation of researchers' professional careers, encouraging the creation of permanent positions within their host institutions and supporting the start or strengthening of a research line through the funding of an individual R&D&I project, as well as the adaptation and renovation of spaces and laboratories and the improvement of equipment necessary for its implementation. Within the general objective of promoting the professional career consolidation of researchers in any thematic area, this call specifically supports the consolidation of researchers whose field of study falls within a strategic area related to either Artificial Intelligence (AI) or microelectronics and semiconductors (Chips), for which an additional budget will be allocated. The eligible activities under this initiative include: a) An incentive for the creation of a permanent position in the principal investigator’s area of expertise, if applicable. b) The implementation of an individual R&D&I project led by the principal investigator. c) The adaptation of spaces, renovation of laboratories, and improvement of equipment necessary to launch or strengthen the principal investigator’s research line.

title: AIAMO Mobility Data Hub & Services
description: The AIAMO initiative , led by the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) in Germany, addresses the challenge of providing reliable, sustainable mobility while supporting climate protection goals. The initiative focuses on creating a data-sovereign platform that integrates multiple mobility services and makes them accessible to SMEs and smaller municipalities. Key objectives include: Simplifying data collection in the mobility sector to generate actionable insights Supporting environmentally friendly and multimodal traffic management Enabling SMEs and cities to access research findings and deploy AI applications for improved mobility Implementation revolves around an interconnected integration zone , where trusted AI applications provide guidance for mobility solutions and ensure that SMEs and municipalities can make informed, sustainable decisions. The initiative combines data integration, AI-driven analytics, and practical service deployment to foster smarter, greener urban mobility. Future outlook: Expanded use of AI for traffic and mobility optimisation across smaller cities and regions Enhanced access to market-ready AI solutions for SMEs Contribution to Germany’s climate protection and sustainable transport goals

title: TRANSPORT 2030
description: The TRANSPORT 2030 programme is a national initiative aimed at promoting applied research and development in the transport sector. Managed jointly by the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic and the Ministry of Transport, it provides funding and coordination to drive innovation across road, rail, air, and water transport. Its objectives include: Advancing AI-based automation and digitalisation in transport systems Supporting the development and testing of advanced transport technologies Encouraging collaboration between research institutions, businesses, and public authorities Strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of the Czech transport sector The programme funds projects across all modes of transport, ensuring that innovative solutions are shared and scaled throughout the industry. By prioritising AI and digitalisation, TRANSPORT 2030 helps modernise infrastructure, improve safety, and enhance efficiency in both passenger and freight transport. Looking ahead, the initiative aims to continue expanding support for pilot projects, integrate emerging technologies such as autonomous mobility and smart infrastructure, and build a stronger link between research outcomes and real-world implementation.

description: he Ministry of Education has launched a national initiative to improve the skills of professionals and managers working in education. This initiative focuses on three key areas: sustainable development, financial literacy, and digital skills, which includes training in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). The aim is to prepare educational staff to better respond to current and future challenges by giving them the knowledge and tools they need to lead, teach, and support students in a rapidly changing world. At its core, the initiative addresses the growing need for schools and educational institutions to keep up with major societal and technological changes. Issues like climate change, economic inequality, and the digital transformation are shaping how we live and work. Education systems play a key role in preparing future generations to deal with these challenges. However, many educators and school leaders feel they lack the specific training to teach about sustainability or manage digital tools like AI effectively. By offering targeted training, this initiative helps bridge that gap. The programme is designed for both professional educators—such as teachers and trainers—and for those in leadership or administrative roles within education. It offers training modules, workshops, and courses that cover sustainable development goals (SDGs), basic and advanced financial literacy, and a broad set of digital skills, including an introduction to artificial intelligence. While details may vary by region or institution, the training is typically delivered by certified providers or in cooperation with universities and public education institutes. Participants not only gain technical knowledge but also explore how to apply it in practical, classroom-based or institutional settings. In the future, the programme is expected to expand, both in terms of content and scale. As digital tools and AI technologies evolve, so will the training materials, ensuring that educators stay up to date with the latest developments. There may also be efforts to extend the reach of the programme beyond formal education settings—such as into vocational training or adult education. Overall, the initiative lays the groundwork for a more resilient, future-ready education system by investing in the people who shape it.

title: Requalification of Women in ICT Professions
description: The initiative offers both short-term (15 hours) and long-term (24 hours) training programmes for various ICT professions, including: • Cybersecurity Specialist • Data Analyst • IT Support Specialist • IT Project Manager • UX Designer • AI Specialist The primary goal of this initiative was to enhance digital literacy, encourage greater interest among women in ICT careers, and provide training that would enable participants to pursue careers in the ICT sector. The initiative achieved positive results, with over 500 women participating in the training programmes. Women over the age of 18 could apply without any additional requirements. Many of these participants reported an increased interest in digital technologies and pursuing careers in this field. A total of 23 training sessions were conducted as part of the initiative, including four specifically focused on AI. The AI Specialist training programme was completed by 89 participants. The AI Specialist curriculum training included several key topics in: the fundamentals of AI and its primary applications, future development opportunities, as well as the basics of machine learning, deep learning, and neural networks. For the longer training programmes, they had to include additional topics, e,g. understanding algorithms for data analysis. In addition to these training programmes, the initiative also featured events specifically focused on ICT skills for women. These events aimed to showcase various ICT roles, career paths, and opportunities for education and certification. They also offered networking opportunities within the ICT community, job search support, and options for further training, mentorship, and ongoing support. The initiative, in place since 2023, is financed through the national budget with EUR 2.95 million, with approx. EUR 22k focused on AI.

title: Science, Technology and Society university programmes
description: The initiative involves two Swedish universities working to connect technology education and research with the broader societal and policy implications of technology. As technology becomes increasingly central to daily life and industry, it’s important for students and researchers to understand not just how to build new systems, but also how those systems affect society, ethics, and policy decisions. This initiative addresses the challenge that technical education often focuses heavily on the skills to create technology, but less on reflecting about its consequences or how it should be governed. At Uppsala University, this challenge is met through complementary programmes designed to teach students in technology-related fields about the societal and policy impact of the technologies they study. These programmes aim to broaden students’ perspectives, encouraging them to think about how technology influences people, communities, and decision-making processes. The goal is to prepare future engineers and technologists who are not only skilled in their craft but also aware of the responsibilities they have as creators and users of technology. At the University of Gothenburg, there is a dedicated research group focusing on the relationship between technology and society. This group studies how technological developments interact with social systems, policy frameworks, and ethical questions. Their work helps inform both academic understanding and public debate, ensuring that technological progress is considered alongside its wider effects. These efforts reflect a growing awareness in Swedish higher education of the need to combine technical skills with societal insight. By educating students and conducting research that spans technology and policy, these universities are helping shape a generation of professionals who can contribute to technology development in ways that are socially responsible and informed by real-world impact. Over time, these initiatives may expand, involving more students and researchers, and fostering stronger links between universities, policymakers, and industry.

title: Analysing the impact of AI on educational programmes
description: The Swedish government has asked two important agencies—the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ) and the Swedish National Agency for Higher Vocational Education (MYH)—to work together on understanding how artificial intelligence (AI) might affect education at universities and polytechnics. This initiative addresses a key challenge: as AI rapidly changes many industries, there is uncertainty about how education systems should adapt to prepare students with the right skills for future jobs. By analyzing these changes, the agencies aim to help education providers align their programs with the evolving demands of the labor market. The main goal of this effort is to study how AI impacts the types of skills students will need when they graduate. This means looking at current university and vocational programs and evaluating whether they are keeping pace with technological advances and labor market needs. The agencies want to identify any gaps or opportunities in education offerings so that graduates can be well-prepared for new roles created or changed by AI. Ultimately, this helps ensure that Sweden’s workforce stays competitive and ready for future challenges. To carry out this work, UKÄ and MYH will collect information from various sources including employers, educators, and students. They will analyze trends in AI technology, the evolving job market, and education curricula. By bringing together knowledge from both higher education and vocational training sectors, the agencies can provide a comprehensive view of the situation. This collaboration also ensures that recommendations will consider the full spectrum of education pathways.

instrument: Monitoring the impact of AI in the labour market

title: AI Cluster
description: As part of France’s National AI Strategy, €560 million was allocated in 2023 to train both AI specialists and “AI+X” professionals who combine AI with expertise in other fields. A central element of this effort is the AI Cluster initiative, which brings together nine universities and grandes écoles to serve as hubs of excellence in AI education. The clusters aim to raise the quality and scale of AI training, ensuring that France develops a broad talent base capable of advancing research and supporting industry. They provide initial education for students, continuous training for professionals, and foster collaboration between academia and business to align skills with economic and societal needs.

title: AI use in processing VAT returns
description: FURS - the Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia - handles large volumes of VAT returns, where manual checks alone can miss patterns and slow responses. To address this, FURS applies advanced AI and predictive analytics to spot risk signals in filings more quickly and consistently. The objective is straightforward: make controls more effective and efficient. By prioritizing cases with a higher probability of errors or fraud, FURS can focus audit resources where they matter most, aiming to increase both the number of effective controls and the share of additionally identified irregularities. In practice, predictive models analyze VAT-return data and related variables to produce risk scores. These models are integrated into FURS’s business processes so caseworkers see ranked alerts and supporting indicators rather than raw data. Human officials still make decisions; the models help them triage, standardize checks, and improve overall throughput.

instrument: AI use cases/projects in the public sector

title: Coordination Mechanisms for the Sharing of Energy (COOMEP)
description: The COOMEP project focuses on creating transferable knowledge and expertise to support coordinated energy management among groups of households. By employing AI proxies, the initiative allows households to automate and optimise energy usage according to collective and individual needs. Key objectives include: Promoting sustainable energy consumption at the household level Using AI-driven tools to optimise energy sharing and reduce inefficiencies Encouraging collaboration and knowledge exchange between participating households The project provides insights into how AI can facilitate energy coordination, helping communities make smarter energy decisions while reducing overall consumption. COOMEP also generates lessons that can be replicated and adapted in other regions or countries seeking similar energy efficiency solutions.

title: Net Zero Cities
description: The Net Zero Cities pilot in Slovenia (2023–2025) focuses on improving urban mobility and data-driven city management across Ljubljana, Kranj, and Velenje. The initiative upgrades the cities’ digital platforms by integrating data from public transport operators and other sources, while installing additional sensors and equipment for more accurate and comprehensive data collection. Key objectives include: Enhancing the accuracy of traffic and mobility data Integrating multiple data sources to create unified platforms for urban mobility management Developing MaaS mobile applications to improve public transport access and efficiency The pilot allows city planners, transport operators, and citizens to make better-informed decisions. It also supports Net Zero goals by promoting sustainable mobility and reducing emissions through smarter transport solutions.

title: Strengthening the Digital Skills of Civil Servants
description: The Administrative Academy, part of Slovenia’s Ministry of Public Administration, has launched a training programme to strengthen the digital skills of civil servants. Many public officials face challenges in adapting to rapid technological change, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence. By addressing these gaps, the programme ensures that the public sector can adopt new technologies effectively and responsibly. Its main objective is to improve both basic digital competences and more advanced skills, with a focus on AI. Training is delivered through the Administrative Academy and is co-financed by the Republic of Slovenia, the Ministry of Public Administration, and the European Union’s NextGenerationEU fund.

title: Tampere City Lab
description: The main objective of this project is to speed up the responsible use of AI in urban life by connecting developers with real infrastructure and data. The Lab reduces risk for both companies and public bodies while ensuring innovation is shaped by real city needs. The initiative offers both virtual and physical testbeds. Virtual tools include Tampere’s IoT platform with sensor data, analytics, and development toolkits. Physical environments include Hervanta for autonomous vehicles, Tyyppaamo for energy and building systems, and the Nokia Arena for event-related solutions. Alongside access to these facilities, the Lab provides project support, partnerships, and guidance on intellectual property. Tampere City Lab is also part of the EU-wide Citcom.ai network, which links similar testing facilities across Europe and enables shared learning and collaboration.

title: Smart Traffic Analysis and Traffic Safety (STATS)
description: The STATS project in the Netherlands focuses on applying AI and data science to improve urban traffic safety. By analysing traffic patterns, the project identifies risks for cyclists and pedestrians and develops strategies to prevent accidents. Key objectives include: Monitoring and analysing traffic flows using AI and computer vision Enhancing pedestrian and cyclist safety in urban environments Providing data-driven insights for local authorities to make streets safer The project combines real-time traffic data, AI algorithms, and urban planning expertise to detect potential hazards and inform city safety measures. Collaboration between municipalities, research institutions, and technology providers ensures that solutions are practical and scalable.

title: Open Government Action Plan
description: The Open Government Action Plan 2023-2027 aims to make government data more open and accessible to the public. It focuses on improving transparency, ensuring governments are accountable, and encouraging citizens to participate in decision-making. The plan recognizes that sharing data openly helps build trust between governments and people. To reach these goals, the plan promotes the use of open data, making it easier for anyone to access and use government information. This includes updating digital platforms and improving how data is organized and shared. The initiative involves various government bodies working together, often alongside civil society and private partners. Building on previous efforts, the plan continues to expand open data availability and citizen engagement, helping governments become more open and responsive to public needs.

title: Smart LED Light
description: The AI-powered smart lighting system in Latvian cities is designed to enhance road safety and traffic management through real-time monitoring. By integrating AI with street lighting infrastructure, the system can automatically detect and record a range of traffic violations, including: Crossing intersections at a red light Improper use of public transport lanes Unauthorised stopping at junctions Non-compliance with other traffic signals The initiative serves multiple objectives: Supporting traffic law enforcement by providing accurate and automated violation data Improving urban mobility through analysis of traffic patterns and violations Enhancing public safety in busy city areas Implementation relies on the integration of AI algorithms with smart city infrastructure, enabling continuous monitoring without requiring extensive human supervision. The collected data can also inform urban planning decisions, such as adjusting signal timing or redesigning intersections to improve safety and traffic flow. Future outlook: Expansion to additional cities and urban areas across Latvia Integration with other smart city services for holistic urban management Use of data for predictive traffic control and long-term mobility planning

title: Winter Road Maintenance Using AI in Kuldīga Municipality
description: The Winter Road Maintenance Using AI initiative in Kuldīga Municipality applies artificial intelligence to optimise winter road maintenance. By analysing real-time road conditions, the system predicts where and when maintenance actions are needed, helping municipalities allocate resources more effectively. Key objectives include: Real-time assessment of road conditions during winter Predictive recommendations for maintenance actions to prevent accidents and improve road safety Interactive mapping to visualise AI-generated guidance for local authorities and maintenance teams Facilitating collaboration between municipalities and road maintenance providers The initiative demonstrates how AI can improve public service efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. By integrating predictive analytics and interactive visual tools, the programme supports better decision-making for winter road management.

title: Testing authorisation regime and connected vehicle technology pilot
description: The CAM Interdepartmental Steering Group, established in November 2023, coordinates efforts across government departments to support the safe deployment of connected and automated mobility (CAM) technologies. One of its primary tasks is to develop a testing authorisation regime for CAM vehicles operating on public roads. The ongoing pilot project is a key component of this initiative, aiming to test and validate Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS), which enable vehicles to communicate with each other and with traffic infrastructure. Key elements include: Participation of 1,500 drivers to gather real-world data and insights Testing of connected vehicle technology on public roads Evaluation of safety, reliability, and user experience for automated mobility solutions The initiative fosters collaboration between government authorities, transport agencies, technology providers, and road users, ensuring that regulatory frameworks and technical standards support both innovation and safety. Future outlook: Implementation of a formal testing authorisation framework for CAM Expansion of pilot projects and deployment of C-ITS solutions Strengthening of policy and technical readiness for wider adoption of connected and automated mobility in public transport and road networks

It also serves as a pilot for smart city mobility, demonstrating how autonomous technologies can integrate into public and private transport networks. title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
description: Slovakia’s European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) help public bodies and businesses adopt AI and other digital tools. Many administrations lack expertise and struggle to test solutions before use; the hubs act as one-stop shops, offering guidance, pilot projects, and training. Their main objectives are to provide “test-before-invest” services, build staff skills, and connect public organisations with researchers and technology providers. This supports more efficient service delivery - for example through AI-based document handling, data analysis, or cybersecurity tools - while reducing risks and costs. The Slovak network includes the SKAI-eDIH led by the Kempelen Institute of Intelligent Technologies, as well as hubs like the Center for Innovative Healthcare (CIH) and Cassovium in Eastern Slovakia.

title: DigitalLead
description: DigitalLead is Denmark’s national cluster for digital technologies and part of the country’s business promotion system. It was created to bridge the gap between companies developing digital solutions and sectors that need help adopting them, such as healthcare, energy, and manufacturing. The cluster’s aim is to boost digital innovation across the economy. For tech developers, it offers access to networks, research, and funding opportunities. For other industries, it provides guidance on identifying and testing solutions, ensuring digital tools are effectively applied. DigitalLead brings together businesses, entrepreneurs, universities, and knowledge institutions through joint projects, training, and matchmaking activities. This creates pathways for research results and new ideas to be turned into practical services and products.

title: ION
description: Romania’s ION is an AI “counsellor” launched in 2023 to improve how the government listens to citizens. Developed with the Bucharest-based company Humans.ai and local researchers, it was presented by the prime minister as the world’s first AI honorary government adviser. The tool gathers input directly from citizens through an online platform and also scans social media to track public concerns. Using natural-language processing, it identifies key topics and measures sentiment, offering officials a quicker view of what matters to the public. A mirror-like installation also allows people to leave messages in person. ION’s main goals are to strengthen citizen engagement, reduce the delay in detecting issues, and bring real-time evidence into policymaking.

title: Caixa Geral de Aposentações AI Virtual Assistant
description: The General Retirement Fund (CGA), which manages pensions for Portuguese public sector employees, has introduced an AI-based virtual assistant on its portal. The tool was created to address the high volume of recurring questions about pensions, documents, and procedures, which often caused delays on phone and email channels. The assistant’s main role is to answer FAQs instantly, guide users to relevant forms or services such as CGA Directa, and ensure replies are consistent. By working around the clock, it reduces waiting times and improves navigation, while also collecting insights into which topics generate the most confusion

title: Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure
description: The Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure project is implemented by the Institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences. It addresses the need for secure and reliable communication channels, which are critical for data in research, government, and industry. It works by applying principles of quantum physics, such as quantum key distribution, to protect information against interception or tampering. The Institute of Physics leads the design, testing, and deployment, collaborating with national research institutions and technology partners.

title: Medresyst
description: The rise in life expectancy and lifestyle changes has led to an increase in complex diseases like cancer, diabetes, and neurological disorders, burdening healthcare systems. MedReSyst focuses on 4P medicine (Personalized, Preventive, Predictive and Participatory). It leverages network medicine by integrating biological, environmental, and clinical data with artificial intelligence to customize care, identify risks and predict treatment responses. This initiative is based upon three strategic pillars : -Acquisition of Multimodal Data: Collecting biological, exposomic, clinical, and imaging data through specific cohorts in collaboration with international bio-banks. -AI Modeling: Developing explanatory models of pathogenesis to enable more personalized, effective treatments with fewer side effects. -Personalized Clinical Strategies: Designing integrated screening, diagnostic, and treatment workflows for precision medicine, reducing costs, and improving care quality. MedReSyst develops AI models with continuous learning, fostering a virtuous cycle between experts and technology for more transparent and flexible AI use in medicine.

title: DeepGreen
description: The DeepGreen project addresses the need for AI systems that can run directly on small, low-power devices. Traditional AI often relies on cloud computing or large data centers, which are not suitable for devices like sensors, wearables, or industrial equipment that require fast, local processing. This creates a barrier to using AI in many real-world applications where speed, privacy, or limited connectivity are concerns. In response, DeepGreen partners launched the Eclipse AIDGE platform in 2023 — the first open-source software platform dedicated to embedded AI. It allows developers to design, train, and deploy AI models directly on hardware devices, without sending data to external servers. The platform supports energy-efficient AI and helps reduce latency while improving data security. Being open source, it is freely accessible and can be adapted by developers, researchers, and companies of all sizes. The platform was developed through collaboration between research institutions, technology companies, and open-source communities. It includes tools for building AI models, testing their performance, and running them on different types of hardware. This helps make embedded AI easier to develop and more reliable in everyday use. By connecting expertise from various fields, the DeepGreen project has created a practical tool for applying AI outside the cloud directly where data is generated and decisions need to be made.

title: National Health Data Infrastructure
description: Austria is developing a national platform to make better use of health data that has already been collected. This is known as "secondary use" of data — using information not to treat individual patients, but to help improve public health policies and healthcare planning. At present, much of this data is stored separately by hospitals, insurance providers, and health authorities, making it difficult to get a complete picture of the healthcare system. This new platform aims to solve that problem by bringing data together in a secure and coordinated way. Recent legal changes require several public bodies to work together on this project. These include the national government, the provinces (Länder), regional health insurance funds, and the main social insurance organisation. Together, they are responsible for setting up and running the platform. The main goal is to allow public health authorities to analyse anonymised health data so they can make better decisions — for example, to track how diseases spread, improve the quality of care, or identify where the health system needs more support. Although still under development, the platform will be built with strong protections for privacy and data security.

title: Digital Nose
description: The Digital Nose project tackles a core forestry challenge: early, non-invasive detection of tree stress and pest outbreaks. Its goal is to build an AI-enabled early-warning system that helps forest managers react sooner to drought, disease, and insect attacks—key for climate-smart forestry. How it works: sensors capture stress-related volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from trees and insect pheromones, while imaging records typical damage patterns. AI models fuse these signals to flag emerging problems before they become visible at scale, with the goal of enabling targeted interventions and reducing losses.

title: Develop and upscale quantum compute capacity
description: Quantum computing represents a new frontier in technology, promising to solve complex problems that are beyond the reach of today’s classical computers. Recognizing this opportunity, the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland announced plans to develop a quantum computer with at least 50 qubits by 2025. This initiative addresses the challenge of advancing Finland’s technological capabilities and securing a position at the forefront of quantum research, which has the potential to revolutionize fields such as medicine, materials science, and cryptography. The Finnish government supports this vision by dedicating significant funding to accelerate the project. In its 2023 budget session, the government allocated 70 million euros to VTT, with the goal of scaling up the quantum computer from 50 qubits to 300 qubits by 2027. Increasing the number of qubits is essential because it directly improves the computing power and practical applications of quantum machines. This funding reflects a strong commitment to boosting Finland’s innovation ecosystem and ensuring that the country remains competitive in this highly strategic area. The initiative involves combining quantum computing with existing high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Specifically, the plan is to connect the quantum computer to LUMI, one of Europe’s most powerful supercomputers, to create a national quantum computing environment. This connection will allow researchers to use both classical and quantum computing strengths, supporting advanced simulations and data processing tasks. The collaboration between VTT, the government, and HPC infrastructure operators exemplifies a coordinated effort to build a robust ecosystem for future technologies.

title: EUCAIM project
description: Sweden is actively participating in the EUCAIM (European Federation for Cancer Images) project, a pivotal initiative under the European Cancer Imaging Initiative, which is a cornerstone of Europe's Beating Cancer Plan. This project aims to establish a pan-European digital infrastructure that facilitates the secure sharing and analysis of cancer-related imaging data, thereby enhancing the development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in oncology. The primary objective of EUCAIM is to create a federated platform that integrates anonymized cancer images and associated clinical data from diverse sources across Europe. This infrastructure will support the development, benchmarking, and validation of AI models for precision medicine, ultimately leading to improved diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment strategies for cancer patients. In Sweden, the initiative is coordinated by Umeå University, with significant contributions from Region Västerbotten, Uppsala University (SciLifeLab), Linköping University, and Karolinska Institutet. These institutions are instrumental in providing access to high-quality imaging data and clinical expertise, ensuring that the platform is both clinically relevant and scientifically robust. Vinnova, Sweden's innovation agency, is co-funding the Swedish participation, with a total investment of SEK 12.4 million allocated to the project.

title: Clarence
description: Clarence is a Luxembourg sovereign cloud operated by a joint venture between LuxConnect and Proximus Luxembourg. The platform is built on Google’s Distributed Cloud Hosted technology (sovereign controls without external operator access) and targets government and regulated sectors needing confidential workloads, including AI.

title: National Reference Centre for semantic resources of the Ministry of Health
description: Spain’s National Reference Centre for Semantic Resources (SNOMED CT), managed by the Ministry of Health, is designed to ensure semantic interoperability across the National Health System (SNS). The centre manages and distributes SNOMED CT clinical terminology, promoting its adoption and use within health information systems nationwide. Main Functions: License Management: Administers SNOMED CT licenses for users in Spain. Content Distribution: Publishes and distributes both the official SNOMED International content and Spain-specific extensions, including reference sets and a Spanish-language lexicon. Support and Training: Provides official training on SNOMED CT and offers technical support and consultancy for SNS users. International Collaboration: Serves as Spain’s point of contact with SNOMED International and participates in working groups to develop and improve clinical terminology.

title: ARTIQ - AI Centres of Excellence
description: The ARTIQ programme, launched in 2023 by Poland’s National Science Centre (NCN) and the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR), is aimed at boosting the country’s capacity in advanced AI research and development. One of the key projects under this scheme is led by AGH University of Science and Technology, which secured funding to establish a specialised research team working on next-generation AI systems. The winning project, titled “Integrating Reasoning, Learning, Optimization and Interpretability for Accelerated Commercialization of Next-Generation Intelligent Software Systems”, reflects the initiative’s focus on bridging fundamental AI research with practical applications. By combining areas such as machine reasoning, machine learning, and optimization with interpretability, the project seeks to strengthen both scientific knowledge and pathways for AI commercialisation. Through such efforts, ARTIQ intends to reinforce Poland’s role in the European AI research landscape, while also creating opportunities for translating academic advances into market-ready solutions.

title: MEGALITH project
description: The MEGALITH project is a research initiative focused on preserving Malta’s ancient megalithic temples through the use of AI and simulation techniques. By training AI models on historical and simulated data, the project can predict how stones will degrade under varying meteorological conditions and climate change scenarios. Key objectives include: Assessing environmental impacts on megalithic structures Predicting stone degradation over time to inform conservation strategies Supporting preservation planning with data-driven insights The project combines expertise from heritage conservation, AI, and environmental science. The AI models allow researchers and policymakers to evaluate the effectiveness of preservation measures before implementation, reducing risks and costs.
