title: AI Research Institute (ICIA)
description: The AI Research Institute (ICIA) at Cluj-Napoca Technical University (UTCN) represents a major investment in Romania’s artificial intelligence ecosystem. Officially inaugurated with its first symposium in October 2024 , the institute is part of the Romanian AI Hub and was constructed between 2023 and 2024, with additional facilities still under development. Its mission is to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure and expertise to generate innovative AI-based solutions for both industry and society. ICIA is equipped with cutting-edge research infrastructure, including: High-performance computing (HPC) systems. Specialised servers for deep learning and Big Data storage. Advanced platforms for modelling, simulation, optimisation, and design. The institute’s research addresses a broad range of domains, such as: Internet of Things (IoT) and cyber-physical systems. Autonomous and connected mobility and smart city applications. Sensors and integrated circuits for intelligent systems. Advanced multimedia data processing (text, voice, video). Social and service robotics , with AI applied to non-industrial robotics. Cybersecurity and civilian space applications . Smart agriculture (e-agriculture) through robotics and digital technologies. E-administration and e-governance . E-health , including early diagnosis, telemedicine, and software modelling. Human–machine communication technologies , supported by AI and natural language processing. The goal of ICIA is not only to advance scientific knowledge but also to create practical solutions that can be applied across strategic sectors. By combining advanced computing power with interdisciplinary expertise, it fosters innovation and strengthens Romania’s contribution to European and global AI research. Looking forward, ICIA is expected to become a hub for collaboration between academia, industry, and government, serving as both a training ground for highly skilled AI specialists and a platform for developing technologies with real-world impact.

Advanced research in key emerging fields. Practical solutions that address real-world challenges faced by industry and society. Beyond strengthening institutional performance, the project also seeks to increase Romania’s visibility in the global research community. The labs serve as a platform for interdisciplinary collaboration, where academic researchers, industry partners, and policymakers can work together to design and test innovative solutions. Looking ahead, ICIINNOLAB is expected to play a central role in shaping Romania’s digital transformation. By combining expertise across multiple technology domains, the initiative will foster innovation, encourage cross-sectoral applications, and provide a foundation for future national and European projects in disruptive technologies.

title: Research in areas of strategic interest
description: The “Research in Areas of Strategic Interest” programme is one of ten programmes under Romania’s National Research, Development and Innovation Plan (PNCDI IV) 2022–2027 . It aims to boost the participation of Romanian research organisations in international projects while driving progress in fields that are strategically important for the country’s development. Within this framework, Subprogramme 9.8 – Artificial Intelligence is dedicated specifically to advancing AI research and applications. The AI subprogramme seeks to: Support cutting-edge AI research, development, and innovation in Romania. Develop cross-applicable AI solutions that can benefit multiple sectors, from healthcare to culture and administration. Encourage the widespread adoption of AI to create added value in economic, social, cultural, and public sectors. Strengthen the national AI ecosystem and align it with international standards and initiatives. To achieve these goals, the subprogramme funds a wide range of projects, including: Research, development, and innovation (RDI) projects. Advanced research centres in AI. AI-based application development and industrial management solutions. Testing and validation platforms. Participation in global AI initiatives and projects. Public–private RDI partnerships. Data set management and processing platforms. Projects promoting AI in society. Pilot projects and joint research between Romanian diaspora experts and local researchers. Strategic projects for the long-term development of the national AI ecosystem. The Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation has committed to launching dedicated AI calls under this subprogramme, with research activities coordinated by the newly established National Authority for Research . Through this effort, Romania aims to create an integrated, well-funded AI research environment that both supports domestic innovation and increases the country’s visibility and competitiveness in the global AI landscape.

title: Institute for AI Mihai Drăgănescu
description: The “Mihai Drăgănescu” Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence, based in Bucharest, is a national centre dedicated to advancing knowledge and innovation in AI. Its mission is to combine fundamental and applied research to strengthen Romania’s role in the global AI research landscape. The institute is named after Mihai Drăgănescu, a leading Romanian scientist, and builds on his legacy of connecting science, technology, and society. Research at the institute spans several domains, including: Machine learning and data-driven models Natural language processing (NLP) and computational linguistics Intelligent systems and decision-making technologies Robotics and autonomous systems Computer network architectures supporting the knowledge society The institute works at the intersection of theory and application, producing both academic contributions and real-world innovations. Its researchers develop methodologies, tools, and prototypes that can be applied across industries, while also training the next generation of AI specialists. Looking forward, the institute aims to deepen international collaboration, strengthen interdisciplinary projects, and expand its role in supporting Romania’s digital transformation. By combining cutting-edge research with practical solutions, the institute positions itself as a key player in shaping how AI contributes to economic and social development.

title: National Test Beds Network
description: The National Test Beds Network in Portugal complements the country’s Digital Innovation Hubs by creating spaces where new AI and digital solutions can be tested in real-world conditions. It was established to respond to the need for safe, practical environments that allow businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), to experiment with emerging technologies before deploying them more widely. The initiative has three main objectives: Accelerate AI and digital adoption through targeted testing and experimentation programmes. Provide infrastructure and technical support so that companies can trial new products, services, and processes in realistic settings. Promote collaboration among companies, universities, and research centres to modernise strategic sectors of the economy. Implementation focuses on bringing together public and private actors, ensuring that companies of different sizes and technological maturity levels have access to cutting-edge resources. By enabling practical experimentation, the network reduces the risks of innovation and increases the chances that AI solutions can be effectively integrated into business operations. Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to expand in scope, building stronger institutional frameworks and extending access to more regions and industries. By scaling further, the National Test Beds Network could help Portugal establish itself as a leader in AI-driven transformation and enhance the competitiveness of its companies at both the national and European levels.

title: REASSURE
description: The REASSURE project, launched in 2022 in Belgium, focuses on improving the reliability and efficiency of sustainable energy systems through advanced data analytics. Its primary goal is to provide tools that allow energy operators to assess and optimise the performance of energy networks under varying conditions. Key objectives include: Developing a context-aware data analytics toolkit for energy systems Integrating predictive models to anticipate potential issues and improve reliability Optimising energy efficiency and sustainability across networks The toolkit combines real-time data analysis with contextual information to ensure energy systems are robust, adaptable, and resilient. REASSURE supports decision-making for energy operators and policymakers, helping them manage both current operations and future energy challenges.

title: Slovakia	Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030
description: The Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030 sets out a comprehensive roadmap for modernizing Slovakia’s transport sector using AI and digital technologies. It emphasizes the systematic development of Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) to enable real-time traffic management, automation, and operational efficiency across all transport modes. Key objectives include: Road transport: Developing peripheral infrastructure on highways and major roads to support intelligent transport technologies Rail transport: Modernizing the European Railway Traffic Management System (ERTMS) and the European Train Control System (ETCS) to improve automation and safety Water transport: Implementing River Information Services (RIS) with AI-driven systems for better navigation and operational efficiency Multimodal transport: Enhancing AI-based models for planning and operational coordination across transport modes The plan reflects Slovakia’s commitment to adopting AI technologies in line with broader EU standards and objectives, aiming to increase safety, optimize traffic flows, and improve overall transport functionality. Implementation involves collaboration between national authorities, infrastructure providers, and technology developers to ensure cohesive and efficient deployment of AI solutions.

title: Central Government Guidelines on Cloud Policies
description: In 2023, Finland’s Ministry of Finance updated the central government’s guidelines on the use of cloud services. These changes respond to the growing need for more flexible, efficient, and secure digital systems across public administration. As government operations become increasingly digital, cloud services offer opportunities to improve service delivery, reduce costs, and support remote access. At the same time, these changes raise important questions about data protection, especially when handling confidential or sensitive information. The main goal of the updated policy is to promote a “Cloud First” approach. This means that cloud-based solutions should be the default choice when public authorities plan new digital services or update existing systems. However, the policy also makes clear that security and legal requirements must always be met. Special attention is given to how public and confidential data is stored and managed in cloud environments, to ensure that information is handled responsibly and in line with national and EU data protection laws. The updated guidelines provide practical support for government departments and agencies. They include rules on risk management, supplier responsibilities, and technical requirements for cloud use. The policy encourages organisations to evaluate the benefits and risks of cloud services early in the planning process. It also promotes cooperation between different public bodies to share knowledge and develop common practices. These updates build on earlier cloud strategies and reflect Finland’s broader digital goals. As more government services move online, the new policy framework helps ensure that cloud adoption happens in a secure, consistent, and well-governed way across the public sector.

title: Digital Compass/data policy
description: Finland’s Digital Compass is a national plan that defines how the country manages its digital transformation, with a strong focus on data. It addresses the need for clear and coordinated rules around how data is collected, shared, and used. As digital services become a bigger part of everyday life, there is growing pressure to make sure that data is handled in ways that are safe, efficient, and fair for everyone—from individuals and businesses to public institutions. One of the key objectives of the initiative is to make data more available and easier to use while protecting privacy and personal rights. The plan supports the use of open data, where possible, to help improve public services and support innovation. At the same time, it sets clear expectations around data security, transparency, and ethical use. The goal is to allow both public and private sector actors to use data in ways that create value without compromising trust. The Digital Compass brings together a wide range of participants. It is led by the Finnish government, but involves collaboration with municipalities, companies, researchers, and civil society. The policy also aligns with wider European efforts to create a more unified and secure digital space. Through shared rules and coordinated action, the initiative helps ensure that data can flow between sectors and across borders, when appropriate, under common standards. The approach is practical and structured. It includes steps like developing national data spaces—systems that allow different organisations to access and share data more effectively—and improving digital infrastructure to support this. It also promotes training and awareness so that organisations understand how to manage data responsibly. By setting out clear roles, goals, and tools, Finland’s Digital Compass helps make the country’s digital landscape more connected, secure, and useful.

title: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery
description: The Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery initiative leverages AI and computer vision to systematically map urban infrastructure. Using street-level imagery, the system identifies assets such as traffic signs, waste bins, and storm drains, and assigns precise geospatial coordinates to each item. Key objectives of the initiative include: Creating a comprehensive geospatial database of city assets Supporting municipal operations, planning, and maintenance through accurate and up-to-date information Enabling integration with other information systems for enhanced city management The initiative facilitates data-driven urban management by allowing city authorities to quickly locate and monitor assets, plan maintenance schedules, and optimise resource allocation. By combining AI detection with geospatial mapping, the programme reduces manual surveying costs and improves the accuracy of asset inventories. Future outlook: Expansion to additional types of urban assets Integration with smart city platforms for real-time monitoring Enhanced predictive maintenance and planning capabilities using AI-generated insights

title: Technology Incubation Project
description: The Technology Incubation programme in Czechia supports early-stage start-ups and spin-offs in fields like AI, mobility, space, and sustainability. It was created to address the lack of early funding, mentoring, and customer access that often prevents young teams from growing. By 2025, the aim is to help around 250 start-ups bring new products and services to market. Selected start-ups receive non-equity grants, tailored mentoring, and access to specialised hubs across the country. New cohorts are admitted in waves, and AI has emerged as one of the strongest tracks with dozens of projects already in incubation. The long-term plan is to build a national ecosystem where successful alumni and investors feed back into supporting the next generation of start-ups.

description: Partly implemented through the National Plan for Language Technologies, which encompasses all initiatives related to developing language technologies and AI in Spanish and co-official languages, in particular: Linguistic corpora will be developed made up of texts of different kinds (novels, plays, film scripts, press news, etc.), but also that consider singing, oral or sign language, including terminologies and the generation of a metasearch engine for terms as well as technologies for the extraction and processing of neologisms (TeresIA project). Support for the Spanish Language and Artificial Intelligence Project (LEIA) to create a language data bank, enriched with contributions from the autonomous communities. Projects underway include AINA (Catalan), GAITU (Basque), NÓS (Galician) and VIVES (Valencian). Related initiatives concern the development of testing and validation of language models through actions led by the Royal Language Academy and the National Observatory on Society and Information Society (ONTSI, project ODESIA). Development of the ALIA language models, which will contribute to developing a GenAI foundation for the implementation of public administration use cases, AI services within the Spanish AI Factory, and the Spanish GenAI ecosystem more broadly.

title: National Strategy for Quantum Technology
description: In 2022, the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science published a research mapping focused on quantum science and technology. This study showed that Danish quantum research is considered world-class in several areas and enjoys strong international recognition. Quantum science holds great promise for advancing computing, communications, and other technologies, and Denmark’s strong position highlights its potential to contribute significantly to these fields. The main goal of the mapping was to assess Denmark’s strengths and identify opportunities in quantum research. This helps guide national policies and funding decisions to support and grow the country’s expertise in this important area. By understanding where Denmark stands globally, the government can better target investments and collaborations. Over the past ten years, Danish research institutions have increased their quantum activities significantly. New research groups have been formed, and several top international researchers have been recruited. Universities and research centers across Denmark have created a vibrant environment for quantum research, often collaborating internationally. The Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science supports this work by monitoring progress and providing strategic backing.

title: Data strategy for local governments
description: Since 2001, Denmark’s central, regional, and local governments have worked together to create digital strategies that guide the development of a modern public sector. These strategies, agreed upon through multi-year plans, aim to make government services more efficient and accessible by coordinating digital efforts across different levels of government. The initiative addresses the need for better access to and sharing of data within the public sector. Standardizing data is essential for smooth communication and collaboration between various government bodies, which ultimately helps provide better services to citizens. In 2022, the association of Danish municipalities (KL) introduced a data strategy asking local governments to make their data available in a standardized way. This encourages greater efficiency, transparency, and easier access to information for both the public and businesses. Going forward, the initiative will continue to evolve by expanding cooperation and improving how data is shared and used across all levels of government. This ongoing effort ensures that Denmark’s public sector stays prepared to meet future challenges with better digital tools and services.

title: Mobility Innovation Hub
description: The Mobility Innovation Hub serves as a central platform for innovation in sustainable mobility within Czechia’s National Technology Incubation framework. It was created to address pressing challenges in transportation by promoting the development of advanced mobility solutions. Its main goals are to: Foster collaboration between start-ups, established companies, and research institutions Accelerate innovation in sustainable and smart mobility technologies Support the development of solutions in urban transportation, electrification, autonomous vehicles, and smart mobility systems The Hub functions as a bridge between research and industry, enabling new technologies to move from concept to market faster. By providing access to expertise, networking, and funding opportunities, it helps Czech companies and innovators remain competitive in the fast-evolving mobility sector. Future outlook: Expansion of innovation support services to more start-ups and SMEs Strengthening Czechia’s position in European mobility and transportation innovation networks Continued focus on green and digital transformation in transport

title: Danish Data Portal
description: Datavejviser.dk is a platform created to help people find and use data collected by public authorities in Denmark. The initiative recognizes that while a lot of data is available, it can be difficult for users to locate the right information or understand where to get it. By providing a clear, centralized directory of datasets, Datavejviser.dk makes it easier for businesses, researchers, government workers, and citizens to find the data they need and use it effectively. The main goal of the platform is to improve transparency and support innovation by making public data more accessible. It does this by listing and describing data from many government agencies and linking users directly to the sources. This way, users don’t have to search through multiple websites or databases. Instead, they can use the platform as a one-stop resource to discover data on topics like the environment, economy, demographics, and more. Datavejviser.dk works by collecting information about datasets available across the public sector and organizing them in a simple and consistent way. It uses standard formats to make sure the data is easy to find and compatible with different systems. The Danish Agency for Digital Government manages the platform, regularly updating it and responding to user feedback. This approach helps ensure that the platform stays relevant and continues to meet the needs of its users. Looking to the future, the platform plans to expand its offerings and improve its features. It aims to include more datasets and improve user interaction by listening to what people want and need. By doing so, it hopes to encourage greater use of public data in areas such as research, business innovation, and public planning. Overall, Datavejviser.dk is a step toward making government data more open, useful, and aligned with the needs of society.

title: Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
description: France and Germany have established a binational call for projects on artificial intelligence (AI), aiming to strengthen cooperation on critical challenges such as risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience. This initiative reflects both countries’ commitment to joint innovation, cross-border collaboration, and applied AI research. Among the selected projects is RenovAIte, which seeks to transform the way housing and road renovation is planned and executed. Its main features include: Developing AI-based software to support renovation at scale Covering the entire value chain, from data acquisition and analysis to decision-making tools Providing tailored solutions for engineering firms, housing services, and road management authorities The project contributes to greater efficiency, sustainability, and cost-effectiveness in infrastructure management. By applying AI, RenovAIte enables smarter resource allocation and reduces environmental impact while improving service delivery for citizens.

title: CONTRAILS project Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
description: The CONTRAILS project is carried out under the France–Germany Call for Projects on AI technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience (2022). It aims to combine trusted artificial intelligence techniques with physical modelling to advance understanding of condensation trails (contrails) and their role in climate change. The project pursues several objectives: Improve identification and characterisation of contrails through AI-supported analysis Enhance data assimilation and prediction models to forecast contrail formation and persistence Provide tools to assess the impact of contrails on the climate Support future trajectory optimisation tests designed to prevent or minimise contrail formation By coupling AI technologies with environmental and atmospheric models, CONTRAILS contributes to climate mitigation strategies in aviation. It also demonstrates how cross-border collaboration can accelerate innovation in AI for climate resilience and risk management.

title: Seerlinq
description: Seerlinq is a Slovak company that uses machine learning to analyse physiological data for cardiovascular care. It addresses the challenge that effective diagnosis and treatment of heart conditions often require complex interpretation of patient data. The company’s main objective is to provide tools that personalise diagnostics and treatment, improving accuracy and patient outcomes. Its solutions work by applying advanced algorithms to patient data, helping clinicians make informed decisions tailored to individual patients. Seerlinq collaborates with healthcare providers to integrate these tools into clinical workflows. By enhancing precision and personalisation in cardiovascular care, it supports better and more efficient patient management.

title: National Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Node and 1+ Million Genome Project
description: Romania is joining the European effort to share genome and clinical data through its involvement in the European Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI), part of the wider 1+ Million Genomes (1+MG) initiative. This effort addresses the challenge that many countries have useful genetic and health data, but lack the systems and connections needed to use them safely across borders. By building its own infrastructure, Romania aims to make its data usable for research, medical advances, and improved patient care, while respecting privacy and legal rules. The main goals are to enable secure access to high-quality human genome data and matching clinical information; to align Romania’s systems with agreed European standards so data can talk to each other; and to support national research and health services in using genome information for better diagnosis, treatments, and prevention. It also seeks to strengthen Romania’s role in European genomics, helping Romanian institutions participate fully in transnational research and healthcare innovations. Romania has institutions like the Genomics Research and Development Institute and the Authority for Digitization of Romania participating in GDI. There is coordination with the “Carol Davila” University of Medicine and Pharmacy and the National Genomic Research Network. The plan is to establish a “National Mirror Group” or equivalent body, build or upgrade national genome data hubs, and ensure these meet legal, technical, and ethical standards required by the European framework (like data protection, data quality, interoperability). Romania contributes its existing genome datasets and clinical data under these conditions.

instrument: Initiative to promote data access and sharing

title: D4Health Tirol
description: This Austrian project aims to make better use of health data by securely linking information from hospitals, telemedicine services, and the national death registry. At the moment, these data sources are separate, making it hard to apply machine learning or artificial intelligence effectively in healthcare or research. The project addresses this by building a federated infrastructure, which allows data to be used across systems without moving or duplicating it. The main goal is to support AI-based research and improve routine care, such as predicting health risks or personalising treatment. Data stays with the original institutions, but can be accessed securely under strict rules to protect privacy. Hospitals, digital health providers, researchers, and public authorities are all involved in building and using this system.

title: Transitional study support
description: In 2022, the government launched a new program to help working adults improve and update their skills, not limited to artificial intelligence but covering a wide range of subjects. This initiative addresses the growing need for people to adapt to changes in the job market, where new technologies and shifting industries require continuous learning. Many professionals find it difficult to balance work and study because of financial constraints, so this program aims to make it easier for adults to return to education without losing their income security. The main goal of this initiative is to support adults aged 27 to 62 who want to re-skill or broaden their knowledge. It gives them a chance to study for up to two years while providing financial assistance to reduce the risk of losing income during this time. For the first year, participants receive a study grant equal to 80% of their previous salary, making it possible to focus on learning without serious financial pressure. After the initial year, they can apply for a student loan to continue their studies for an additional year if needed. The program works by offering direct financial support to eligible adults who choose to study. It is designed to be flexible, allowing people to pursue education that matches their career goals and the demands of the labor market. The government manages the program, likely in cooperation with educational institutions and financial agencies that handle grants and loans. This setup encourages more adults to take part in lifelong learning, whether by attending universities, polytechnics, or other training programs. this initiative has the potential to scale up and adapt as the needs of the workforce change. It provides a foundation for continuous professional development that can help individuals stay relevant in a rapidly evolving job market.
category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
instrument: Collaborations with stakeholders to ensure a fair transition in the labour market
oecd_principles: 1.1 Inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being

title: Acceleration strategy dedicated to the agritech industry
description: France’s agritech acceleration strategy uses AI and France 2030 funding to promote digital farming and data platforms. A central project is Agdatahub, a neutral data intermediary that enables farmers, co-operatives, and agri-food companies to share information securely with clear consent rules. The platform underpins services like traceability, decision support, and interoperability, and is aligned with European initiatives such as Gaia-X and AgriDataSpace. Supported by national funding and private investment, Agdatahub is expanding from national deployment to a role in EU-wide data spaces, positioning France as a leader in agricultural data governance and innovation.

title: Finnish Bioeconomy Strategy
description: The goal of Finland’s Bioeconomy Strategy 2022–2035 is to to strengthen bio-based industries while steering the country toward its goal of climate neutrality by 2035. The strategy identifies digitalisation and AI as key tools to raise efficiency, cut emissions, and create more value from renewable resources. It promotes innovation in areas such as new bio-based materials, advanced processing methods, and sustainable forestry and agriculture. By supporting the development of new products and services, the strategy aims to diversify the economy while reducing dependence on fossil-based raw materials. Implementation involves collaboration between ministries, research bodies, and industry actors, with measures to foster R&D, scale up pilot projects, and integrate digital tools into bioeconomy sectors. In this way, the strategy links Finland’s climate goals directly with industrial competitiveness and technological development.

title: Testing and experimentation facilities
description: France participates in the EU network of Testing & Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) to help companies trial AI in real-world settings and de-risk deployment. title: Transitional study support
description: In a rapidly changing job market, many adults need to update or learn new skills to stay competitive and meet the demands of evolving industries. This challenge is not limited to technology fields like artificial intelligence but affects a wide range of professions. To support working professionals in this transition, the government introduced a study support program in 2022. The program aims to help adults between the ages of 27 and 62 take time to study and expand their skills without losing financial stability. The main goal of the program is to make it easier for adults to return to education and improve their qualifications, whether they want to specialize in new areas like AI or pursue other fields. To do this, the program offers financial aid that covers part of the individual’s income during their studies. Specifically, for the first year of study, participants receive a grant equal to 80% of their previous salary. This support helps reduce the financial risks involved in leaving work temporarily to focus on learning. After this initial year, those who want to continue their education can apply for a student loan to help cover the costs for a second year. This initiative involves the government working together with educational institutions and financial agencies to manage the program and provide funding. Eligible adults can apply for this support and choose study programs that fit their career plans and the needs of the labor market. By providing both grants and loans, the program offers a flexible way for professionals to reskill or upskill in a way that suits their individual situations. The initiative reflects a commitment to lifelong learning, helping workers remain employable and productive as industries evolve, especially with the ongoing impact of technologies like artificial intelligence.

text: Transitional study support. In a rapidly changing job market, many adults need to update or learn new skills to stay competitive and meet the demands of evolving industries. This challenge is not limited to technology fields like artificial intelligence but affects a wide range of professions. To support working professionals in this transition, the government introduced a study support program in 2022. The program aims to help adults between the ages of 27 and 62 take time to study and expand their skills without losing financial stability. The main goal of the program is to make it easier for adults to return to education and improve their qualifications, whether they want to specialize in new areas like AI or pursue other fields. To do this, the program offers financial aid that covers part of the individual’s income during their studies. Specifically, for the first year of study, participants receive a grant equal to 80% of their previous salary. This support helps reduce the financial risks involved in leaving work temporarily to focus on learning. After this initial year, those who want to continue their education can apply for a student loan to help cover the costs for a second year. This initiative involves the government working together with educational institutions and financial agencies to manage the program and provide funding. Eligible adults can apply for this support and choose study programs that fit their career plans and the needs of the labor market. By providing both grants and loans, the program offers a flexible way for professionals to reskill or upskill in a way that suits their individual situations. The initiative reflects a commitment to lifelong learning, helping workers remain employable and productive as industries evolve, especially with the ongoing impact of technologies like artificial intelligence

title: eHealth Strategy
description: Slovenia's eHealth Strategy for 2022–2027, titled “eHealth for a Healthier Society” , is a comprehensive initiative developed with support from the European Commission’s Structural Reform Support Programme. The strategy outlines the objectives and priorities for the development of eHealth in Slovenia, focusing on enhancing patient care, improving system efficiency, and facilitating data-driven decision-making. Key Objectives: Unified Electronic Health Record (eHealth Record): The strategy emphasizes the introduction of a single electronic health record system, aiming to centralize patient data, enhance accessibility, and improve the continuity of care across the healthcare system. National Telehealth Framework: A national telehealth framework is being designed to facilitate the provision of remote healthcare services, ensuring broader access to medical consultations and reducing geographical barriers to healthcare delivery. Legislative Reforms: The strategy includes the amendment of related legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system, streamline data flows, and ensure compliance with data protection regulations. System Integration and Interoperability: Efforts are underway to optimize, integrate, and connect existing information systems and databases, enhancing the efficiency of management and control processes within the healthcare sector. Data Security and Governance: The strategy prioritizes the enhancement of data security measures and the establishment of robust governance frameworks to safeguard patient information and ensure the responsible use of health data. Strategic Vision: By 2027, Slovenia aims to have a patient-centered, secure, interoperable, and efficient digital health ecosystem. The strategy seeks to empower citizens and health professionals through digital tools, improve population health, and promote trust in digital services. It aligns with broader EU frameworks such as the European Health Data Space and the Digital Decade 2030 objectives, contributing to the modernization and digitalization of the healthcare system in Slovenia. Implementation and Oversight: The Government Office for Digital Transformation, soon to become the Ministry of Digital Transformation, plays a pivotal role in coordinating the digitalization efforts. The strategy emphasizes the importance of a dedicated management structure, specialized workforce, and active involvement of all relevant stakeholders to ensure the successful implementation and sustainability of the eHealth initiatives.

title: Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Ireland
description: Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Ireland is the Irish arm of the European GDI project which aims to create federated genetic data infrastructures across Europe to allow for safe and secure sharing of genomic data. A federated genetic data infrastructure will allow countries taking part in the project to collaboratively share data while storing the data in their own country. This ensures data privacy and protection. Access to analyse the data will only be granted to individuals after a review process. Ireland has committed to the onboarding stage of the overall European GDI project, which means that over the next 4 years we will develop a proof-of-concept infrastructure that will be tested using artificial genetic data first. This is to ensure that the infrastructure works correctly and is safe and secure.

title: New Energy
description: Launched in 2022, the New Energy (Nowa Energia) programme is a national initiative to drive innovation and sustainability in Poland’s energy sector. It provides financial and strategic support to both entrepreneurs and local government bodies, helping them test and implement modern energy solutions. The programme has two main thematic areas: Smart Cities for Growth – developing technologies that enhance urban sustainability and efficiency through smart energy systems. Self-Sufficient Energy Clusters – supporting local communities and municipalities in building decentralised, renewable-based energy systems to increase resilience and reduce reliance on external supply. Key objectives include: Encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation in the energy sector Supporting local governments and public service providers in sustainable transformation Strengthening energy self-sufficiency and resilience across regions Promoting the development of green technologies aligned with EU sustainability goals

title: Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS)
description: The Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS) is a state-owned initiative created to strengthen the country’s data ecosystem and promote the secondary use of data for research, innovation, and policy. Its mandate is to act as a trusted intermediary that facilitates secure data sharing between public institutions, private organisations, and research actors. By setting governance frameworks, providing technical infrastructure, and ensuring compliance with ethical and legal standards, LNDS seeks to unlock value from public sector data while maintaining strong safeguards on privacy and security. The service also supports Luxembourg’s ambition to position itself as a hub for responsible data-driven innovation.

National Telemedicine Framework: A national framework for telemedicine services is being designed to facilitate remote consultations and healthcare delivery, improving access to services across the country. Legislative Reforms: The strategy includes revising existing legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system, streamline data flows, and ensure secure data exchange. Implementation and Expected Outcomes: The strategy aims to optimize and integrate existing health information systems, improve data security, and enhance the efficiency of healthcare management processes. By 2027, PLACE seeks to establish a patient-centered, secure, and interoperable digital health ecosystem that aligns with PLACE frameworks such as the PLACE Health Data Space and the Digital Decade 2030 objectives. Governance and Stakeholder Involvement: A hybrid governance model will be established, balancing national standardization with local autonomy. A Central National Unit (CNU) will coordinate efforts, supported by advisory and executive boards that include key stakeholders from healthcare providers, policymakers, and payers

title: ROBUST
description: The ROBUST consortium, which began in 2022, is a major European research effort spanning ten years that is designed to strengthen the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems. With 54 partners drawn from universities, research institutions, industry, and civil-society organizations, the initiative brings together a wide spectrum of expertise. Its goal is to improve AI across five core dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. One important strand of work is to formalize notions of reliability in AI using flexible contracts or guarantees, so that users and developers can trust behaviour in changing environments. The consortium also develops methods, tools, and frameworks aimed at building trust—for instance by making AI decisions more interpretable, robust to faults, and verifiable.

title: Start-up Ecosystem Support
description: The Startup Ecosystem Support initiative in Bulgaria is designed to strengthen the country’s entrepreneurial environment, with a particular focus on innovation, technology, and artificial intelligence (AI). It addresses key challenges faced by start-ups, including limited access to funding, mentorship, and supportive policy frameworks, which can hinder the growth and scaling of early-stage companies. The initiative provides targeted support for entrepreneurs, including guidance on business development, access to venture capital, and facilitation of connections with investors and industry partners. By improving the availability of resources and knowledge, it helps start-ups implement innovative technologies and develop AI-based products and services. A central goal of the programme is to foster a robust and sustainable start-up ecosystem in Bulgaria. This involves not only supporting individual ventures but also shaping policies that encourage entrepreneurship, reduce barriers to market entry, and stimulate collaboration between start-ups, research institutions, and established companies. By enhancing access to capital, expertise, and supportive frameworks, the initiative seeks to position Bulgaria as a competitive hub for high-value start-ups. It promotes growth and development across multiple industries, strengthening the country’s capacity for innovation and contributing to broader economic and technological advancement.

title: Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT)
description: The Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT) is a leading research institute in Bulgaria, established through a partnership with ETH Zurich and EPFL. Representing one of Eastern Europe’s most ambitious AI and computer science initiatives, INSAIT addresses the growing need for advanced research, technological innovation, and talent development in AI across the region. INSAIT has achieved several notable milestones, including the development of BgGPT, a state-of-the-art language model, and the establishment of deep-tech AI ventures that translate research breakthroughs into practical applications. The institute conducts cutting-edge research in areas such as GPT models, computer vision, robotics, and quantum computing, positioning Bulgaria at the forefront of AI innovation in Eastern Europe. As a member of the European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS) network, INSAIT fosters collaboration with leading AI research centres across Europe, ensuring knowledge exchange, high-quality research outputs, and access to advanced computational resources. The institute also emphasises interdisciplinary approaches and partnerships with industry, supporting technology transfer and the practical deployment of AI solutions.

title: Quantum Computing Research and Development Programme
description: The NQSTI is a three-year programme with a total funding of €115.9 million under the NRRP, specifically aligned with the European Union’s NextGenerationEU framework. The initiative encompasses three main action lines: Enhancing Research Infrastructure Developing state-of-the-art facilities and platforms for quantum research, including integration with high-performance computing infrastructures and the European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI). Fostering Collaboration Between Academia and Industry Establishing a network of national quantum institutes to optimize resources, bridge research with industry, and stimulate industrial innovation through joint laboratories and prototyping. Developing Innovative Research Models Implementing new standards, training programs, and fostering the creation of spin-offs and start-ups, particularly focusing on the southern regions of Italy to promote balanced regional development. description: The PSN was established by the Department for Digital Transformation under the Presidency of the Council of Ministers to consolidate and modernise Italy’s public administration infrastructure. It is operated by Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., a public-private company owned by TIM, Leonardo, CDP (through CDP Equity), and Sogei. Its mission is to host the critical and strategic data and services of central and local government bodies, including health services (ASL) and major municipalities, in a secure and resilient environment. The PSN currently operates four data centres: Acilia and Pomezia (Lazio) Rozzano and Santo Stefano Ticino (Lombardy) These centres are built to high standards of reliability, security, and energy efficiency (green design, certifications, redundancy) to support continuity, disaster recovery, and sovereignty of public data. Under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), one of the PSN’s goals is to have 75% of Italian public administrations migrate to cloud services by 2026. As of December 2022, the PSN infrastructure was declared operational at the four sites, and migrations of public administrations are underway.

title: National Strategic Hub
description: The PSN was officially activated on 21 December 2022 under Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), as part of Mission 1, Component 1, Investment 1.1 (“Cloud PA / Polo Strategico Nazionale”). Its aim is to provide public administrations—including central administrations, Local Health Units (ASLs), and the main regional/local administrations—with cloud infrastructure meeting high standards of security, sovereignty, operational continuity, and environmental sustainability. Key features include: Ownership and governance via Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., a special purpose company jointly owned by TIM, Leonardo, Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (CDP via CDP Equity), and SOGEI. Four data centres located in Acilia and Pomezia (Lazio), and Rozzano and Santo Stefano Ticino (Lombardy), designed with high availability, fault tolerance, and elevated environmental standards. Strong emphasis on digital sovereignty, meaning the infrastructure is intended to be independent of non-EU entities for critical services, with certified high security, resilience, and compliance with cloud-first principles. The initiative also encompasses migration support: administrations whose infrastructures are considered insecure or critical are prioritised for migration to the PSN. By 2026, the goal is for 75% of Italian public administrations to be using cloud services, including via PSN. Recent developments include AgID (the Agency for Digital Italy) formally joining or migrating some of its services to the PSN cloud under an agreement signed in May 2024. This migration follows the “cloud-native” and “cloud-first” architectural model, ensuring equivalence in functionality and architecture

title: European Health Data Space for Secondary Use @CY CY-EHDS-2ND
description: Cyprus is working to improve how health data is shared and used within the country and across Europe by joining the European Health Data Space (EHDS). Health data, like medical records and test results, can help improve patient care and support medical research, but sharing it safely and securely has been a challenge. To tackle this, Cyprus is setting up a National Health Data Access Body (HDAB) under the National eHealth Authority (NeHA). This body will manage access to health data, making sure it is shared responsibly between healthcare providers, researchers, and across borders. The goal is to enhance health services, speed up medical innovation, and improve health policy decisions. The HDAB will work with hospitals, government agencies, and other partners to ensure privacy and consent rules are respected. It will also support cross-border healthcare, helping patients get care abroad with their data shared safely. Over time, Cyprus plans to expand this system, making health data more useful and accessible, while strengthening its role in Europe’s health data network.

title: Digital Wallonia Strategy on Digital Administration
description: The Digital Wallonia Strategy on Digital Administration is a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming Wallonia into a fully digital region by 2024. This strategy focuses on innovating public services, fostering collaboration through open data, and serving as a testing ground for scalable digital solutions. It is structured around five key themes: Digital Uses, Smart Territory, Digital Economy, Digital Innovation, and Digital Administration. A central component of this strategy is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance mobility-related services. AI technologies are being applied to improve traffic management and urban planning, aiming to create more efficient, sustainable, and citizen-centric urban environments. For instance, the Smart Region project, launched in 2019 with a budget of EUR 4 million, seeks to propose a new model of governance for Walloon cities to transform them into Smart Cities. This initiative rethinks the experience of public administration offered to citizens. The DigitalWallonia4.ai programme plays a pivotal role in supporting AI adoption across public organizations. It provides resources and support mechanisms to assist in the digital transformation, enabling the development of AI-driven solutions that address regional challenges.

title: European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Brussels
description: The European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Brussels supports small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in adopting sustainable digital innovation, including artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies. The initiative addresses the challenge that many SMEs face in developing digital capabilities necessary to drive competitiveness, sustainability, and resilience in a rapidly changing industrial and societal landscape. The primary objective of the hub is to strengthen the digital skills and technological adoption of Brussels’ industrial sector, which is predominantly composed of SMEs. Strategic goals include fostering economic growth, facilitating social and environmental transitions, and supporting post-COVID recovery by enhancing the capacity of companies to implement innovative, digital solutions. EDIH Brussels is implemented through a partnership of Agoria, Sirris, BeCentral, Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB), and Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). Together, these partners provide SMEs with a comprehensive service ecosystem that includes training, experimentation, technology demonstrations, and access to expertise. The hub currently serves over 1,500 companies, helping them explore AI applications, optimize processes, and develop innovative products and services.

title: Flanders AI-EDIH
description: The Flanders AI European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) is designed to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the region. The initiative addresses the challenge that many SMEs face in integrating AI into their operations due to limited expertise, infrastructure, and access to practical support. The primary objective of the hub is to provide a neutral, integrated, and accessible service ecosystem where SMEs can explore, experiment with, and implement AI solutions. By offering technical guidance, training, access to AI tools, and collaborative support, the hub helps companies understand how AI can improve efficiency, innovation, and competitiveness across sectors. title: AI Fund
description: Belgium’s Federal Public Service for Policy and Support (FPS BOSA) has established the AI Fund to support applied research in artificial intelligence. The initiative addresses the need to accelerate AI development in strategic domains that are critical for public services, economic growth, and societal well-being, ensuring that research efforts align with national priorities. The primary objective of the AI Fund is to finance applied AI research projects in areas identified by the National Convergence Plan, including health, cybersecurity, and broader AI development. By providing targeted funding, the initiative encourages collaboration between academic institutions, research centers, and industry, fostering the creation of innovative AI solutions that can be deployed in real-world contexts. The fund operates through a competitive application process, inviting researchers and institutions to submit proposals aligned with priority domains. Selected projects receive financial support, technical guidance, and opportunities for knowledge exchange, ensuring that outcomes contribute effectively to Belgium’s AI ecosystem and public sector modernization.

title: National Health Strategy 2030
description: Priority 4, called “Electronic Healthcare,” aims to improve how health care uses digital technology to better diagnose and treat major diseases. Right now, health systems often struggle to share important medical information quickly and safely, which can slow down care and create risks for patient privacy. The initiative’s main goal is to create one digital platform that connects doctors, hospitals, labs, and patients, making communication smoother and health data easier to access and use. It also focuses on protecting sensitive data and ensuring health workers have the skills to use these new tools effectively. This platform will allow different health care providers to share information securely, helping doctors make faster, more accurate decisions. It involves health authorities, medical professionals, IT experts, and patients working together. The plan is to start with key diseases and regions, then gradually expand the system and train more staff. Over time, this digital health network will grow to cover more services and improve care quality, making the healthcare system stronger and more responsive to patient needs.

title: Establishing a pro-innovation approach to regulating AI
description: The initiative sets out the UK Government’s emerging approach to regulating AI in a way that supports innovation while addressing risks and protecting public trust. It identifies the need to adapt existing regulatory systems to keep pace with the rapid development of AI technologies, which present both economic opportunities and challenges such as bias, safety risks and lack of clarity in current legal frameworks. The approach aims to improve clarity and coherence in regulation, thereby supporting business confidence and investment. A key element of the initiative is the introduction of cross-sectoral principles covering areas such as safety, technical security, transparency, fairness and accountability. These principles are intended to guide how AI systems are developed and used, while allowing flexibility for regulators to tailor implementation to the context of different sectors. The approach also emphasises proportionate and risk-based regulation, encouraging lighter-touch measures such as guidance or voluntary actions before introducing stricter requirements. The initiative involves engagement with a broad range of stakeholders, including regulators, industry, academia and civil society, and invites feedback to inform further development. It also highlights the importance of international cooperation, noting plans to work with global partners and standards bodies to promote interoperable and responsible AI governance.

title: Public Services Recommendation
description: The initiative addresses the challenge of service discovery in large digital government portals. In the gov.br ecosystem, citizens face a catalogue of more than 5,000 public services delivered by multiple federal agencies, which historically made it difficult to identify the most relevant services for their needs. The initiative applies artificial intelligence to analyse users’ navigation behaviour within the portal and their use of other federal digital public services. Based on these signals, the system recommends services in real time, embedded in the user journey. This reduces friction in navigation and supports a more intuitive and personalised experience for citizens seeking public services. The initiative has been institutionalised as part of Brazil’s national digital government platform and is continuously improved through iterative model updates and monitoring of user-interaction metrics. Over time, the solution is expected to evolve by incorporating additional behavioural signals and improved semantic understanding of services, while maintaining alignment with data-protection, privacy and transparency requirements. The architecture is designed to be scalable across federal services and replicable for other public-service portals. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative has improved service discovery and user experience. On average, recommended services are accessed around 4.5 million times per month. In the last six months, the most frequently accessed service through the recommendation feature was the document-signing service. Because recommended services are more contextualised for users, the conversion rate for starting a service is higher than the portal average, reaching 73.82%. Results are monitored using portal analytics, access logs and service-start metrics. Challenges and lessons learned Challenges include ensuring consistent metadata quality across more than 5,000 services, integrating data from multiple systems, and aligning AI-driven personalisation with privacy and data-protection requirements. Operational risks included biased recommendations and the underexposure of relevant but less frequently accessed services. The initiative is evolving the AI model to improve relevance ranking and semantic understanding of public services, supported by iterative experimentation and continuous monitoring of user metrics. This requires data governance, controlled model updates with human oversight, and testing before wider rollout. Lessons learned include the importance of data governance for service catalogues, transparent recommendation criteria, cross-agency coordination, and incremental deployment with continuous evaluation. Sustainability depends on high-quality service metadata, privacy-by-design, institutional ownership of the model and ongoing monitoring to mitigate bias and performance drift over time.

title: Prediction of daily inflows in the reservoirs at the Drina River basin based on Artificial Intelligence – DrinaAI
description: The initiative uses artificial intelligence to improve the prediction of daily water inflows into reservoirs in the Drina River basin. It was developed to address limitations of traditional hydrological forecasting, which often struggles with missing data, changing weather patterns, and the increasing variability of water conditions. By integrating machine learning with historical inflow patterns, meteorological variables, and reservoir levels, the initiative enhances accuracy and supports more informed planning in water and energy management. Its main objectives are to provide more reliable inflow forecasts, enable better operation of reservoirs, and strengthen decision making for hydropower, flood preparedness, and drought management. The system applies time series analysis, regression techniques, and neural networks, combined with robust data preprocessing and feature engineering. Validation using real-world data from multiple reservoirs shows that the approach outperforms traditional methods and adapts effectively to varying hydrological conditions. The initiative also creates opportunities to expand AI based forecasting to other river systems facing similar challenges. Since many basins require improved predictive tools, the underlying framework can be adapted to additional datasets and institutional settings. As a result, the initiative has the potential to contribute to broader, cross-basin improvements in environmental planning and resource management. In the future, the initiative is expected to evolve through ongoing refinement of predictive models, deeper integration with hydrological monitoring infrastructure, and sustained collaboration with sector experts such as the Jaroslav Černi Water Institute. These partnerships support long term institutional adoption and scale up. Over time, the system could be embedded into routine operational processes across Serbia’s water sector and extended to regional partners, helping to strengthen resilience and promote evidence-based management of rivers and reservoirs. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative has achieved more accurate daily inflow forecasts than traditional methods, confirmed through validation using real reservoir data and comparative performance metrics. This has improved planning for water and energy management. Future impacts include more reliable reservoir operation, better flood and drought preparedness, and the ability to scale the AI model to other river basins.

title: Sindh Cloud First Policy (Subnational: Province of Sindh)
description: The Province of Sindh, Pakistan, recognised that fragmented on-premises ICT infrastructure across its public sector entities created inefficiencies, security vulnerabilities, and barriers to adopting modern technologies such as artificial intelligence. Public sector organisations were operating in silos with small server clusters that lacked the compute capacity, scalability, and data consolidation necessary for AI-driven analytics, predictive modelling, and intelligent public service delivery. In response, the Government of Sindh issued the Sindh Cloud First Policy in July 2022, formulated by the Information Science and Technology Department. The policy mandates that all new ICT investments by provincial public sector entities must prioritise cloud-based solutions. A dedicated Cloud Acquisition Office has been established to facilitate the transition, overseeing the design, procurement, migration, and management of cloud workloads. The Office works in liaison with the federal National Cloud Office and the Sindh Procurement Regulatory Authority to ensure compliance with accreditation standards and procurement best practices. The policy also restricts new investments in fragmented ICT infrastructure such as standalone data centres and server rooms, redirecting resources toward shared, scalable cloud environments. This consolidation of compute demand across provincial entities is designed to achieve economies of scale, lower ICT costs, and create an interoperable ecosystem where AI-enabled solutions can be developed, tested, and replicated across departments. Only cloud service providers accredited by the National Cloud Office are eligible for government contracts, and service level agreements are monitored for compliance. Looking ahead, the policy positions Sindh as an AI-ready province by ensuring that cloud infrastructure, data accessibility, and procurement frameworks are in place to support emerging AI workloads in areas such as public health, education, tax administration, and citizen services. The shift from capital to operational expenditure models and the pay-as-you-use approach further enable agile experimentation with AI tools without large upfront investments. The policy is issued in continuation of the Pakistan Cloud First Policy approved by the federal government in February 2022, ensuring alignment between provincial and national digital transformation strategies.

title: Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls
description: The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies defined that all bills presented by parliamentarians are systematically made available to receive citizens' contributions through e-polls. There are about 16,000 proposals per year, and some of them receive more than 1,000,000 suggestions/comments from citizens during the weeks of greatest discussion on the topic. It was observed that merely knowing the percentage of citizens who were for/against a legislative bill is not sufficient to improve the legislative text. Therefore, it was necessary to add an analysis of a free field in the e-poll through which citizens are invited to leave their comments and opinions. A human full analysis on these opinions is practically impossible, due to the large number and the timeliness with which parliamentarians need to position themselves in debates regarding those bills. The "Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls" algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them and showing how distant the opinion groups are from each other. title: Khmer eKYC OCR API — AI-Powered Identity Document Recognition for Cambodian Citizens
description: Background and problem Reliable Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for Khmer-script documents has historically been unavailable, creating a significant bottleneck in Cambodia's digital transformation. Financial institutions, public agencies, and businesses were forced to rely on manual data entry for identity verification, a slow, error-prone, and costly process. TSC's response to this gap, the Khmer eKYC OCR API, earned the Best R&D Award 2023 from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunication (MPTC) of Cambodia, recognising it as the country's most impactful research and development achievement of the year. What the initiative does TSC's AI team built the eKYC OCR API from the ground up using deep learning models, extracting structured data from Cambodian National IDs (Khmer and English), Passports (MRZ and biographical), and Driving Licences. The API is available entirely free of charge via CamDX, Cambodia's national data exchange platform, to all 45+ registered members, including banks, insurance companies, microfinance institutions, and government bodies. Both public- and private-sector CamDX members can access it freely. Notably, it powers CamDigiKey, Cambodia's official government single sign-on (SSO) app, enabling citizens to authenticate and access public digital services such as online business registration using their national identity documents. Objectives Eliminate manual identity data entry; accelerate eKYC compliance for NBC-regulated institutions; deliver inclusive digital services in Khmer; provide a sovereign, locally-hosted alternative to foreign OCR; and democratise access by offering the API free of charge through CamDX, removing cost as a barrier to digital transformation for all member organisations. Future evolution Having surpassed 8 million processed requests (Khmer ID card images or passport images) with zero cost to integrators, TSC will continue expanding document coverage, growing the CamDX member base, and deepening integration with Cambodia's national digital identity infrastructure. Provincial government adoption and ASEAN-level replication are key targets for 2026 and beyond.

title: AI in Production Network
description: The ProKI-Netz (Demonstrations- und Transfernetzwerk KI in der Produktion, or AI in Manufacturing Demonstration and Transfer Network) was established by the BMFTR as part of Germany's AI Action Plan to bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and SME adoption in manufacturing. The network consists of multiple regional demonstration and competence centres (Demonstrationszentren) co-located at universities with focus on production technologies across Germany, each demonstrating AI applications in specific production domains (e.g. quality control, predictive maintenance, process optimisation, robotics, digital twin). SMEs can visit demonstration centres, obtain technology consulting, access hands-on pilot projects, and receive support for implementing AI solutions in their own production environments. The network also provides training events, qualification programmes, and matchmaking between AI solution providers and manufacturers. Target audience: German SME manufacturers, particularly those in traditional industrial sectors beginning their AI adoption journey.

title: Cambodia Digital Government Policy 2022-2035
description: The process of building a digital government in Cambodia is still in an early stage, as the digitalization of ministries and institutions has not yet been fully harmonized. Most systems focus on developing applications to facilitate the work without having a strategy for long-term digital transformation and without considering the efficiency and effectiveness that data centralization provides. The development of digital government in Cambodia faces many challenges, which are the weaknesses of the digital government system, including digital connectivity infrastructure that does not yet cover the entire country, problems with quality of services and access to financial resources, overlapped digital systems in ministries and institutions that were created according to individual needs, and the lack of a common national platform. Another weakness is the lack of a national data center for storing data and providing computing resources, while all ministries and institutions have almost no infrastructure and technical capacity for ensuring digital security. The vision of this policy is to “establish a digital government to improve the citizens’ quality of life and build their trust through better public service provision.” To achieve this vision, the Cambodia Digital Government Policy 2022-2035 has set out 10 strategies: first, the establishment and improvement of digital connectivity infrastructure; second, the establishment and improvement of digital payment system infrastructure for public services; Page vii third, the establishment and strengthening of digital security infrastructure; fourth, the development of postal service infrastructure; fifth, the organization of digital government governance; sixth, the digital transformation of the government and public services; seventh, the development of digital human capital; eighth, the promotion of digital research and innovation; ninth, the organization of collaborations with digital technology companies; and tenth, the promotion of digital start-ups. Under the 10 strategies above, there are 83 priority actions comprising various projects. Overall, selecting priority actions for the development of digital government demonstrates the interconnection, complementation, depth, and conformity with the clear strategies in line with concrete objectives and goals towards complete digital transformation as set out by the Royal Government for 2035. Furthermore, the implementation of those priority actions will be in line with the master plan that has a precise roadmap fueled by strong political will to achieve success, efficiency, and effectiveness. Each priority action is accompanied by concrete measurement indicators in the clear planning phases, with the ministries and institutions responsible for implementing those priority actions.

title: Digital Decade Policy Programme 2030
description: The Digital Decade Policy Programme 2030 provides the European Union with a coordinated framework to steer and monitor progress towards shared digital objectives by 2030. It is built around four core areas: digital skills, digital infrastructures, the digitalisation of businesses, and the digitalisation of public services. Within this framework, artificial intelligence is explicitly recognised as a key digital technology alongside cloud computing, edge computing and advanced connectivity, and as a critical enabler of economic transformation, sustainability and innovation. From an infrastructure perspective, the programme highlights the importance of strong capacity to process large volumes of data through sustainable digital infrastructures, including high‑performance computing, cloud and edge facilities. These elements are presented as foundational for AI development and deployment, particularly for data‑intensive applications and advanced AI systems. The programme also links AI and digital infrastructure to the European Green Deal, emphasising the need for energy‑ and resource‑efficient digital technologies and infrastructures. The programme encourages coordinated action by Member States, including the development of multi‑country projects and joint investments in strategic digital capacities that support AI, such as computing infrastructure and advanced semiconductor technologies. It establishes monitoring and governance mechanisms to track progress towards digital targets, identify strategic dependencies and support the Union’s digital sovereignty in an open manner. Overall, the Digital Decade Policy Programme positions AI not as a standalone policy area, but as a cross‑cutting capability embedded in skills, infrastructure, business transformation and public‑sector digitalisation across the EU.

title: National Integrated Cyber Infrastructure System (NICIS)
description: NICIS is South Africa’s national framework for delivering shared cyberinfrastructure to the research and education communities. It integrates high‑performance computing capability, high‑speed network capacity and a national research data infrastructure into a hierarchically organised system that connects local resources with globally connected infrastructures, enabling seamless access for users across disciplines. Through this integrated approach, NICIS brings together national supercomputing facilities, research data services and advanced research and education networks as a coordinated platform. The initiative is designed to promote scientific and industrial development by supporting data‑intensive research, skills development and innovation, and by enabling South African researchers and institutions to participate effectively in national, regional and international research collaborations.

description: This circular addresses the growing use of AI in consumer services, which brings both benefits and risks. The Circular interprets existing Chilean laws to ensure AI systems respect rights like transparency, freedom of choice, safety, and data protection. It supports responsible innovation and aligns with Chile’s National AI Policy and international best practices.

title: LANTA Supercomputer
description: LANTA's architecture comprises 346 compute nodes, 31,744 CPU cores, 704 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, a 200 Gbps HPE Slingshot network, and a 10-petabyte parallel storage system. The system employs liquid cooling technology that reduces energy consumption by 33% compared to conventional air-cooled systems, earning it the 24th position on the Green500 list in 2022 and the 91st in 2025, alongside rankings of 70th and 199th on the TOP500 list for the same years, holding the top position in ASEAN in its debut year. LANTA underpins national projects across several sectors. In AI, it powered the development of Pathumma LLM, an open-source generative AI, and ThaiLLM, a national foundation model tailored to the Thai language and culture.
