title: VitrineGov – Brazil’s Public Sector Innovation Platform
description: VitrineGov is a public-sector innovation platform led by Brazil’s Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services (MGI). It was created to solve a structural government problem: valuable innovations are often developed inside one agency, but remain fragmented, weakly documented and hard for other institutions to understand, trust and reuse. VitrineGov addresses that gap through a full curation cycle that prospects initiatives, screens submissions, conducts pre-selection, interviews teams, documents implementation journeys, publishes accessible one-page public summaries and monitors continuity, results and replication potential. Artificial intelligence is embedded in this workflow through Veridia, the AI engine used by the curatorial team. Rather than replacing public servants or making binding decisions automatically, Veridia strengthens expert review. It helps to analyse initiative submissions considering VitrineGov’s five criteria — creativity, relevance, results, adaptability and continuity — while organising evidence, testing the correlation between public problem and solution, preparing the semi-structured interview, and producing auditable outputs such as evidence comparisons based on interview transcripts, complementary risk matrices and capability-building pathways. What makes VitrineGov distinctive is that AI is not treated as an isolated chatbot or productivity shortcut. It is part of a governed public methodology inspired by knowledge-conversion logic: tacit knowledge from teams and programmes is converted into explicit, reusable public assets. Each published initiative becomes a one-page, one-click reference for peer learning, visibility, mentoring and adaptation. The platform therefore delivers not only recognition, but also a practical transfer mechanism that lowers the cost of replication across agencies. VitrineGov is already active on the Ministry’s website and connected to the National Programme for Management and Innovation (PNGI), which gives it national scale. Its next phase is to deepen analytics, expand monitoring, strengthen auditability and widen federative reuse across more organisations, states and municipalities. In the long term, the ambition is to make public innovation searchable, comparable, trustworthy and transferable at scale — so governments spend less time reinventing solutions and more time adapting what already works.

title: AI4IA@EU - Artificial Intelligence for Better Regulation in the EU
description: Regulatory impact assessment is a fundamental task within the EU's “Better Regulation”. Through it, governments can anticipate whether new legislation will impose unnecessary bureaucracy and administrative burdens upon society. A more efficient, timely, and less human-resource-intensive impact assessment process is needed, while maintaining its robustness and increasing transparency. Using AI allows for a faster estimation of the administrative burdens within national legislation and transposed EU legislation. Additionally, the proof of concept that has been produced facilitates the comparison between the administrative burdens of various legislative texts. The goal is to help identify an increase in obligations among national legislation and “gold-plating” instances between EU directives and transposed legislation. Concretely, AI is leveraged to alleviate the impact assessment experts' task of personally reviewing each passage in the transposed legislation. Instead, NLP model(s) are trained to identify and categorise the existing administrative obligations. Once the AI’s output is produced, the calculation of the administrative burdens is also streamlined by the system through a programmatic implementation of the Standard Cost Model methodology. Results, outcomes and impacts The most visible outcome was the development of a prototype platform to support a more robust and effective impact assessment process. IA4EU delivered clear results: strengthened institutional capacity to use AI in public policy analysis, decision-support prototypes, and greater efficiency in data collection and processing. These impacts were measured through pilot testing, model performance indicators, comparative analysis, and user feedback. Expected future impacts include the continuation of pilot testing of this tool to support and strengthen impact assessment exercises. This will enable increased automation and expansion to new thematic areas, generating measurable gains in time efficiency, analytical quality, and information coverage.

title: AI-supported Local Tax Inspection for Fair and Sustainable Municipal Governance (Subnational: Alicante)
description: Local governments rely on property taxation to finance essential public services. However, undeclared constructions and outdated cadastral information undermine fiscal equity, generate legal disputes and weaken citizen trust. In territories with high urban dynamics, such as the Province of Alicante, these discrepancies accumulate over time due to fragmented administrative systems and limited inspection capacity. The initiative was developed to address this structural governance challenge. Its objective is to support municipalities in applying property taxation more fairly and consistently, in line with the principle of equal treatment of taxpayers. Artificial intelligence is used as a decision-support tool to help identify potential inconsistencies between declared property data and physical reality. Machine learning models analyse cadastral records, building permits and geospatial information to detect patterns that may indicate undeclared constructions or changes of use. The system does not automate tax decisions. Instead, it generates explainable alerts that are reviewed and validated by trained public officials before any administrative action is taken. This supports due process, accountability and full human oversight. The initiative is embedded within a shared public data infrastructure that allows municipalities — particularly smaller ones — to access advanced analytical capabilities that would otherwise be unavailable. Over time, the model is being institutionalised as part of routine inspection workflows and can be extended to additional municipalities and territorial contexts. By strengthening evidence-based decision-making, the initiative aims to contribute to fairer taxation, improved legal certainty and more sustainable local governance. Results, outcomes and impacts The initiative has improved municipalities’ capacity to detect undeclared constructions and inconsistencies in property records. It has contributed to fairer taxation, reduced information asymmetries and strengthened legal certainty. Tangible outcomes include the identification of hundreds of previously undeclared or incorrectly registered properties. The initiative supports sustainable municipal revenues and increases transparency and trust in local tax administration.

title: Community Innovation Laboratories
description: The LINC initiative, a national network of Community Innovation Labs in Costa Rica, was created to address unequal access to digital technologies and advanced technical training across regions. Many communities, particularly outside major urban centres, have limited opportunities to develop practical skills in emerging technologies. LINC responds to this gap by providing open, equipped spaces where students, teachers, entrepreneurs, and small businesses can access hands-on learning in areas such as robotics, 3D printing, digital fabrication, basic artificial intelligence, and creative problem-solving. The main objective of LINC is to strengthen digital and technical skills linked to future employment and local economic development. By combining equipment, structured training programmes, and guided mentoring, the initiative promotes practical learning and encourages innovation at the community level. It also supports teachers and local leaders so that knowledge can be replicated and sustained within schools, small businesses, and local organisations. In doing so, LINC contributes to national priorities related to digital transformation, education, and productivity. Since its launch, LINC has expanded geographically and in the range of services offered. What began as a pilot effort has grown into a distributed national network, reaching thousands of beneficiaries each year and integrating more advanced technologies over time. The initiative has also strengthened co-ordination with public institutions and local governments to align training activities with regional development needs. Looking ahead, LINC is expected to further institutionalise its operations through standardised training pathways, stronger monitoring of outcomes, and expanded partnerships with the private sector and academia. Scaling will focus on increasing territorial coverage, deepening advanced digital skills, and ensuring long-term financial and operational sustainability, so that communities across the country can continue to benefit from inclusive access to technology and innovation. Results, outcomes and impacts Since 2022, 7,921 people have been trained through 21 operational LINC labs nationwide, with 4,419 beneficiaries in 2025 alone. Over CRC 2,000 million has been invested in equipment and training. Results include expanded access to digital skills in underserved regions and stronger local innovation capacity. Impact is measured through participant records, territorial coverage and training outputs. Seven additional labs are being equipped, with expected growth in beneficiaries and advanced skills development.

title: AI Center
description: The AI Center (Argentina) is a collaborative project led by the Argentine Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation in partnership with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). Launched in 2021, the initiative aims to build national capacity in artificial intelligence by creating a dedicated AI center aligned with international standards and best practices. This center will support AI research, innovation, and policy development to foster the adoption of AI technologies across public administration and industry.By strengthening institutional frameworks and promoting knowledge sharing, the initiative seeks to position Argentina as a regional leader in AI. It focuses on enhancing AI skills, encouraging responsible and ethical AI use, and supporting sustainable economic and social development through advanced technologies. The project is funded through non-reimbursable technical cooperation and is a key component of Argentina's broader AI strategy.

title: AI Policy Forum
description: In order to support the cross-departmental implementation of the national AI strategy an inter-ministerial working group, the AI Policy Forum, was set up at the end of 2021, chaired by the Federal Chancellery (BKA) and the Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK). With members from all federal ministries, the AI Policy Forum contributes to a broad coordination of the federal government in the field of artificial intelligence. Its tasks include, among other things, coordinating AI implementation measures in the ministries, connecting experts in their specialist areas and the exchange of information on developments in the field of AI. The AI Policy Forum also contributes to shaping the content of the AI strategy and implementation plans and provides support with the implementation and ongoing and the ongoing monitoring of the AI measures contained therein. The AI Policy Forum Network Meeting is an annual series of events to which administration, academia, the business community and the interested public are invited to discuss developments in the field of AI and exchange information on current projects and topics.

title: National Bioethics and Techno-ethics Committee (Substitue of National Bioethics Committee)
description: The Commission is an advisory body to the State in the fields of life sciences and new technologies in general. Its mission is to investigate the ethical, social and legal aspects and implications in the fields of, in particular, biology, biotechnology and biology, biotechnology, medicine and genetics, and new technologies such as artificial intelligence, advanced algorithms and robotics.In May 2023 the National Commission for Bioethics & Technoethics (law 4780/2021) appointed a High-level Expert Group of Artificial Intelligence, in order to contribute significantly to the elaboration of Recommendations on ethical issues of Artificial Intelligence applications and generally of digital transformation. The Expert Group consists of reputable scientists from various fields of knowledge.The Commission's esponsibilities:(a) to formulate proposals for overall policy and concrete actions, guidelines, and opinion on matters relating to its mission,(b) represent the country in international organisations(c) develop initiatives to raise public awareness(d) participate in legislative committees or give an opinion on relevant provisions before they are tabled,(e) examining the adaptation of national legislation to international and Union law and proposing regulations on matters relating to its mission,(f) draw up and submit reports in accordance with Article 34,(g) set up working groups on matters related to its mission, composed of specialised public-sector staff or private experts, define the way in which they are organised and operate organise their organisation and structure and monitor their work; and(h) organise events on issues relevant to its mission organise, organise and conduct meetings on matters relating to its mission.In December 2024 the National Commission for Bioethics and Technoethics hosted a Meeting of the National Ethics Councils (NECs) and Chairs of the European Group on Ethics and New Technologies (EGE) in Athens.In March 2024 the National Bioethics and Technoethics Commission published its OPINION on the applications of Artificial Intelligence in health in Greece. It is the first official Greek document which comprehensively addresses the specific issue of the impact of the development and use of AI applications in health. The subject is topical, insofar as, on the one hand, remarkable relevant research initiatives are being taken, and, on the other hand, more and more AI applications are being established in clinical practice. Having already appointed a High-Level Expert Group of AI for its continuous support in AI issues and having organized repeated hearings of scientists and representatives of stakeholders, the Greek Commission in this Opinion maps the ethical issues raised by the applications of AI, approaches them through a set of ethical and operational-procedural principles, and formulates valid and feasible proposals for the harmonious integration of the AI applications in the Greek healthcare provision system.

title: AI, Data and Robotics Partnership in Horizon Europe
description: The AI, Data and Robotics Partnership is one of the 46 candidate Public Private Partnerships in the upcoming Framework Programme. The impetus for starting the preparatory work on this Partnership came by the European Commission, which adopted in 2018 the Coordinated Plan on Artificial Intelligence announcing the intention to establish a Public Private Partnership on AI, in order to increase available financing for AI in Europe. The document called for private sector partners to commit high levels of investments and referred to the cooperation between BDVA and EuRobotics in this area as a basis to build on for the new Partnership.The initiative has the following objectives:To boost European competitiveness, societal wellbeing and environmental aspects to lead the world in researching, developing and deploying value-driven trustworthy AI, Data and Robotics based on fundamental European rights, principles and values.To provide strong leadership that is rooted in the widespread deployment of AI, Data and Robotics in sectors and regions across Europe.

title: Serving Confidence in AI by Deal
description: Artificial Intelligence “ AI- is disrupting work, as a whole, and raising new questions about skills, ethics, transparency, use of data, creation, capture and sharing of the value which is produced. Answering these questions requires reinventing social dialogue, so that it takes up the two key dimensions that are, on the one hand, the question of data and AI as a mode of production, calling for a renewed sharing of thiseconomic value created and, on the other hand, the issue of data and AI as a boostfor the development of skillsin occupation and in local professionals.To initiate this renewed social dialogue, the SeCoIA project brings together various French and European partners, led by the CFE-CGC, the French union for managers, engineers, qualified technicians and employees in the public and private sector : the Union of Proximity Companies (U2P), the Italian Confederation of Managers (CIDA), the Institute of Economic and Social Research (IRES) at the service of French trade unions, as well as the association ASTREES, a member of the SOS group, which deciphers the transformations of work and employment, and invents and disseminates innovative social practices in France and Europe. The project also involves the European Confederation of Executives (CEC), the Swedish managers' organization (Ledarna), the Italian Giacomo Brodolini Foundation (FGB), the NGO AlgorithmWath, and the Trade Union Advisory Committee to the OECD (TUAC).The partners intend to expand their community to active and plural actors (providers, customers, suppliers, AI user platforms) aiming at gathering about 60 members who can embody the different interests impacted by the development of the data economy and AI.The project is planned over a two-year period and will consist of three phases :Contribute to a betterunderstanding and appropriation of data and AI issues and impactsPrefigure a new collective bargaining process involving the different stakeholdersFormulate generic and disseminatedrecommendations for developing an enriched social dialogue.

title: European Public Procurement Data Strategy
description: Today the public procurement data landscape consists of multiple sources of data that is generated at various stages of the procurement process (i.e. in the pre-award, award and post-award phases) by actors at all levels of government across Europe (local, regional, national and EU-level). The Public Procurement Directives have established a framework for data sharing at EU level that specifies obligations for information on public procurement procedures to be shared when the value is above a specific threshold. Contracting authorities can share information on procedures below the threshold value at EU level on a voluntary basis or publish these on national portals (e.g. open data portals), however, such data can also be kept in national databases that may not be directly openly accessible. In addition, there are tertiary data sources that can enrich the view on public procurement data when integrated appropriately, such as data from various government registers (e.g. contract registers, business registers, social security, tax, etc.) as well as private sector data (e.g. private databases containing financial information and corporate ownership links, sectorial information, geospatial data, etc.). Bringing together these sources can open a wide array of possibilities for further data analytics and the use of more advanced analytics capabilities (including Artificial Intelligence capabilities) to gain more insights from the vast amount of data that is generated in the domain of public procurement.The initiative has the following objectives:The European Public Procurement Data Strategy (European PPDS) will define the building blocks and objectives for an end-to-end digital Common European Public Procurement Data Space, with the aim to bring together EU public procurement data, national public procurement data and other datasources so that informative and analytical power of otherwise dispersed data repositories can be enriched. The European PPDS will establish a set of initiatives and a roadmap to meet that objective in line with the Digital Public Procurement Policy in the EU, the EU public procurement legal framework, and the European Strategy for Data.According to the European strategy for data (Feb 2020): The data spaces for public administrations will [¦] focus on law and public procurement data, while a data initiative for public procurement should cover žboth the EU dimension (EU datasets, such as TED) and the national ones

title: Brazilian AI strategy
description: The EBIA is part of a series of technology-related initiatives that have been implemented in Brazil during the past years, including the Brazilian Strategy for Digital Transformation (E-Digital), and General Data Protection Law (LGPD), amongst others. After two years of a public consultation that gathered around 1000 contributions, as well as a consultancy in AI hired by the Federal Government, the Brazilian AI Strategy was released. title: Hellenic National Bioethics Commission
description: The Committee is composed of eleven (11) scientists of recognised competence in areas relevant to its mission and responsibilities. In selecting the members of the Commission, care is taken to ensure, as far as possible, a balanced representation of the sciences and humanities. The members of the Commission are appointed by decision of the Prime Minister. In the case of the President, the Parliament is consulted in advance, in accordance with the specific provisions of its Rules of Procedure. The term of office of the members of the Committee is four years and may be renewed only once.In May 2023 the National Commission for Bioethics & Technoethics (law 4780/2021) appointed a High-level Expert Group of Artificial Intelligence, in order to contribute significantly to the elaboration of Recommendations on ethical issues of Artificial Intelligence applications and generally of digital transformation. The Expert Group consists of reputable scientists from various fields of knowledge.The Commission has the following responsibilities:(a) to formulate proposals for overall policy and concrete actions, as well as relevant guidelines, and to give its opinion on matters relating to its mission,(b) represent the country in international organisations on matters relating to its mission,(c) develop initiatives to raise public awareness on issues related to its mission,(d) participate in legislative committees on matters relating to its mission or give an opinion on relevant provisions before they are tabled,(e) examining the adaptation of national legislation to international and Union law and proposing regulations on matters relating to its mission,(f) draw up and submit reports in accordance with Article 34,(g) set up working groups on matters related to its mission, composed of specialised public-sector staff or private experts, define the way in which they are organised and operate organise their organisation and structure and monitor their work; and(h) organise events on issues relevant to its mission organise, organise and conduct meetings on matters relating to its mission.In December 2024 the National Commission for Bioethics and Technoethics hosted a Meeting of the National Ethics Councils (NECs) and Chairs of the European Group on Ethics and New Technologies (EGE) in Athens.In March 2024 the National Bioethics and Technoethics Commission published its OPINION on the applications of Artificial Intelligence in health in Greece. It is the first official Greek document which comprehensively addresses the specific issue of the impact of the development and use of AI applications in health. The subject is topical, insofar as, on the one hand, remarkable relevant research initiatives are being taken, and, on the other hand, more and more AI applications are being established in clinical practice.

title: Act Amending the Road Traffic Act and the Compulsory Insurance Act (Autonomous Driving Act)
description: The Autonomous Driving Act is one of several measures to create a legal framework to implement the German federal government's 2015 Strategy for Automated and Connected Driving. Since 2015, the Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure has authorized testing of automated and connected vehicles under real-life conditions. In June 2017, Germany amended its Road Traffic Act to allow drivers to transfer control of their vehicles to highly or fully automated driving systems and for those vehicles to be used on public roads.

title: Law on the Disclosure of Data Ethics Policy
description: On 26 May 2020, the Danish Parliament passed an amendment to the Danish Financial Statements Act, which means that large companies that have a policy for data ethics must supplement the managements report with an account of the companys policy for data ethics. The statement must contain information about the companys work with and policy on data ethics issues. If the company does not have a policy for data ethics, the managements report must include a statement explaining why they do not. The law enters into force on 1 January 2021, and a guide for businesses on how to include data ethics in their annual reports is in development.The initiative has the following objectives:To foster transparency regarding the companies work with data ethics.

title: Approach Document for India: Part 2 - Operationalizing Principles for Responsible AI
description: Drawn up across Parts 1 and 2, the strategy for Responsible AI consolidates several best practices to ensure that AI solutions are socially conscious and travel beyond the digital divide. The strategy builds upon the pervasive approach of AI for All, first discussed in the NSAI, to bring under its ambit, an accountable and utility-maximising approach to deploying AI solutions. The essence of AI for All includes within itself the maxims, Good AI for All, and AI for Good, which the strategy for Responsible AI sets to work on.In Part-1 of the Responsible AI paper released in February 2021, the various systems and societalconsiderations of AI systems have been studied and the principles for Responsible AI are outlined.Objectives:To identify broad areas for Government intervention and an institutional mechanism to support the implementation.To explore the institutional mechanisms for operationalizing the principles of responsible AI across private sector and research institutions.

title: Digital Transformation Guidelines
description: The Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021“2027 is Latvia's national policy framework guiding digital development across society, the economy, and public administration. The initiative was designed to address key challenges and opportunities in digitalisation, including the low level of digital technology adoption among businesses, lack of ICT specialists, and the need for more efficient, user-friendly public services. It builds upon Latvia's National Development Plan (NDP 2027) and aligns with EU strategies, including the Digital Europe Programme and Sustainable Growth Strategy, to support a digitally empowered and inclusive society.The Guidelines set five main development priorities: digital skills and education; digital security and trust; access to telecommunications and computing; digital transformation of the economy and public administration; and innovation, ICT industry, and science. Objectives include expanding broadband access, increasing public use of e-governance services, improving digital literacy, supporting SMEs with digital tools, and encouraging greater collaboration between the public and private sectors. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that all citizens can participate in and benefit from digital technologies throughout their lives.The initiative is being implemented through coordinated efforts between ministries, municipalities, the private sector, and NGOs. Funding comes from a mix of EU funds, state budget allocations, and private investment, with annual budget reviews to prioritise digital initiatives. One notable success has been the communication and training campaign My Latvia. Do it Digitally!, which helped over 6,000 professionals guide citizens in using e-services. However, gaps remain in SME digital adoption and ICT workforce capacity, both of which are key focus areas moving forward.Over time, the Guidelines are expected to evolve based on progress reviews and funding opportunities. Implementation is supported by strategic governance mechanisms, including cross-sectoral working groups and performance indicators. As digital technologies continue to advance, Latvia plans to strengthen its digital ecosystem, promote innovation, and increase competitiveness, while ensuring no one is left behind in the digital transition. These efforts aim to build a resilient, open, and future-ready society by 2027 and beyond.

title: Plans for Regional Diffusion of AI
description: The Plans for Regional Diffusion of AI in Korea aim to address the growing economic disparity between the capital region and non-capital areas, where industrial growth has slowed and challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic have further strained local economies. While the capital region benefits from concentrated AI capabilities and investment, many regions face difficulties in adopting and benefiting from AI technologies. This initiative seeks to bridge this gap by promoting AI innovation tailored to the specific needs of regional economies, thereby revitalizing local industries and communities.The primary objective of the initiative is to link and integrate diverse regional AI policies and projects, including those under Korea's broader Digital New Deal strategy, to create a cohesive and effective AI ecosystem across the country. By fostering collaboration between regions, the initiative aims to maximize the impact of AI-driven development and support the creation of sustainable jobs, improved services, and enhanced productivity outside the capital area. The initiative also seeks to build local AI capacity through investment in infrastructure, talent development, and innovation hubs.Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve through closer coordination among regional governments, central ministries, and private sector stakeholders. Implementation will focus on institutionalizing collaborative frameworks that allow for continuous sharing of resources, expertise, and best practices. Expansion plans include scaling successful pilot projects and strengthening support systems to ensure equitable AI access nationwide. This long-term approach aims to reduce regional disparities and promote balanced economic growth driven by AI technologies.Since its inception, the initiative has adapted to emerging challenges such as the COVID-19 crisis, which highlighted the urgent need for digital transformation in all regions. Over time, the scope has expanded from pilot efforts to more comprehensive regional cooperation, reflecting a commitment to inclusive AI development. Continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms are being established to assess progress and guide future enhancements, ensuring the initiative remains responsive to the evolving needs of Korea's diverse regions.

title: Implementation Strategy for Trustworthy AI
description: The Implementation Strategy for Trustworthy AI in Korea addresses critical challenges related to the ethical use of artificial intelligence, such as algorithmic bias, privacy risks, and the potential misuse of AI technologies. As AI becomes more deeply integrated across industries, these risks have raised social concerns that could hinder public acceptance and the sustainable growth of the AI sector. This initiative seeks to resolve these issues by establishing a clear framework that promotes responsible AI development and use, fostering trust among users, developers, and policymakers alike.The main objectives of the initiative include developing concrete ethical standards for AI, creating guidelines that support the private sector in implementing trustworthy AI practices, and promoting education and awareness around AI ethics. By providing these resources, the government aims to help organizations build AI systems that are transparent, fair, and privacy-respecting. This, in turn, supports innovation while minimizing harm, ensuring that AI technologies contribute positively to society.Looking forward, the initiative is designed to evolve through continuous engagement with stakeholders including industry players, academia, civil society, and regulatory bodies. Implementation will be institutionalized by integrating the ethical standards into regulatory frameworks and industry best practices. Over time, the initiative expects to scale by influencing not only national AI policies but also contributing to international standards and cooperation on trustworthy AI. Periodic updates will reflect technological advances and societal changes to maintain relevance and effectiveness.Since its inception as part of Korea's National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in 2019, the initiative has progressed from establishing foundational ethical principles to concrete implementation strategies introduced in 2021. This evolution highlights the government's commitment to proactive governance and continuous refinement of policies to keep pace with rapid AI development. By fostering an ecosystem of ethical AI innovation, Korea aims to strengthen its position as a global leader in AI technology that prioritizes social trust and responsibility.

title: National AI Research Resource Task Force
description: The National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) Task Force convened its fourth virtual public meeting on 31 December 2021 to further develop a vision and implementation plan for a national cyberinfrastructure that would expand participation in AI innovation to researchers and communities currently lacking resources to pursue cutting-edge research. Through provision of computational, data, and training resources and a strong governance model, a NAIRR could fuel breakthroughs in areas ranging from climate change to healthcare, and facilitate groundbreaking research in foundational areas of AI such as auditing, testing and evaluation, bias mitigation, and security. The Task Force is working toward consensus recommendations on a NAIRR implementation plan and roadmap that will be provided to Congress in 2022.The initiative has the following objective(s):To serve as a Federal advisory committee to help create and implement a blueprint for the National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) ” a shared research infrastructure providing AI researchers and students across all scientific disciplines with access to computational resources, high-quality data, educational tools, and user support.To provide recommendations for establishing and sustaining the NAIRR, including technical capabilities, governance, administration, and assessment, as well as requirements for security, privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties.To submit two reports to Congress that together will present a comprehensive strategy and implementation plan ” an interim report in May 2022 and a final report in November 2022.

title: NSF Program on Fairness in AI
description: The NSF Program on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence addresses critical challenges related to bias, transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in AI systems. As AI technologies increasingly impact society, concerns over unfair treatment, discrimination, and opaque decision-making processes have grown. This initiative aims to foster research that develops methods and tools to detect, mitigate, and prevent unfairness in AI algorithms, ensuring that AI systems are equitable and trustworthy for all users.The primary objectives of the program include advancing fundamental understanding of fairness in AI, promoting interdisciplinary research combining computer science with social, behavioral, and economic sciences, and supporting the development of frameworks that enable explainability and accountability. By encouraging collaboration among diverse academic fields, the initiative seeks to create AI systems that respect social values and protect against unintended harmful consequences.Looking forward, the program is expected to evolve by integrating emerging research findings into practical applications, influencing policy, and setting standards for ethical AI deployment. Continued funding and collaboration with industry partners like Amazon will help institutionalize these efforts, expand research capacity, and scale innovations broadly across sectors. The program's outputs are anticipated to shape future AI development toward more inclusive and responsible technologies.Since its inception, the initiative has grown to support a wide range of projects and foster a vibrant research community focused on AI fairness. Periodic updates and expanded funding opportunities reflect the evolving landscape of AI challenges and the increasing importance of embedding fairness as a core principle in AI systems worldwide.

description: The Federal Trade Commission approved a series of resolutions that will enable agency staff to investigate conduct in core FTC priority areas over the next ten years. title: Human-centred Artificial Intelligence for Human Resources: A Toolkit for Human Resources Professionals
description: The World Economic Forum created the Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence for Human Resources project in response to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in human resources (HR). While improving and addressing key issues in HR in important ways, this technology has also raised well-justified concerns about its use. The project convened a multistakeholder community of experts to create a practical toolkit for the responsible use of AI in HR, including Turkish representatives, which was tested with HR professionals in a variety of organizations around the world.The initiative has the following objectives:- To equip HR professionals with a basic understanding of AI to assist them in their efforts to assess AI-based tools- To provide guidance on the responsible and ethical use of AI in HR- To help organizations use AI-based HR tools effectively

title: Action Plan on Human Rights
description: The reformative spirit that has been maintained since 2002 without interruption has been tangibly set forth through the legislative amendments in the field of human rights. Throughout this process the presumption of innocence, one of the universal principles of law, has been established as an essential value to be borne in mind by judicial authorities at all stages. In this scope, certain amendments have been passed, especially recently, oriented at protecting personal data and guaranteeing the right of individuals not to have their honour and reputation tarnished as a criminal.Furthermore, in addition to amendments that expand the scope of rights and freedoms through a detailed screening over the legislation, another goal is to be able to offer public services in an accessible, accountable, equal, transparent and fair manner. Thus, the standards on human rights and freedoms will be raised higher, as a natural result of which a new momentum will be gained in the process of strengthening democracy with a focus on citizen satisfaction. Similarly, while the public sector's digital transformation will continue to be implemented with greater success via the e-government project on the one hand, the opportunities for political participation will be promoted in conjunction with this transformation, on the other. In this scope, digital negotiation methods will be developed with the use of new information and communication technologies.The initiative has the following objectives:Aim 8: Protecting vulnerable groups and strengthening social wealth - Goal 8.10: Protection of Human Rights in Digital Environment and Against Artificial Intelligence Applications (Around the 11 main principles which make up the backbone of the Plan, a total of 9 aims, 50 goals and 393 activities are set. The issues related to artificial intelligence are discussed under this aim.)

title: National AI Strategy
description: Within the scope of National AI Strategy preparations; In addition to public institutions and universities, interviews were conducted with representatives of the private sector, NGOs and international organizations on physical and online platforms, workshops were held and the evaluations of field experts in different disciplines were taken. In this context, the National AI Strategy was given its final form, taking into account the global trends shaped by the paradigm shift that emerged with AI in economic and social life, as well as the current situation and development goals of our country. In this direction, the vision of the National AI Strategy is determined as generating value on a global scale with an agile and sustainable AI ecosystem for a prosperous Turkey. The National AI Strategy; to realize this vision, has been designed around 6 strategic priorities, both in line with national policies and needs and taking into account the AI strategy recommendations of international organizations.The initiative has the following objectives:Strategic Priority 1: To train AI experts and increase employment in the domain.Strategic Priority 2: To support research, entrepreneurship and innovation.Strategic Priority 3: To facilitate access to quality data and technical infrastructure.Strategic Priority 4: To regulate to accelerate socioeconomic adaptation.Strategic Priority 5: To strengthen international co-operation.Strategic Priority 6: To accelerate structural and labour transformation.

title: AI Governance Guideline for Executives
description: Important milestone of the initiatives:2021: Thailand AI Ethics Guideline received approval from the cabinet.2022: Establishment of the National AI Committee, chaired by the Prime Minister2022: Thailand National AI Strategy and action Plan 2022-2027 received approval from the cabinet.2022: Establishment of the AI Governance Clinic (AIGC) under the Electronic Transactions Development Agency to lead AI governance promotion effort.2023: Publication of the AI Governance Guideline for Executives which helps facilitate understanding and practical implementation of the AI Ethics Guideline.2023-present: AIGC publicizes and offers training programs related to the AI Governance Guideline for Executives to the public. BackgroundAI technology has increasingly played a significant role in the daily lives of humans, leading to global concerns regarding its potential impact on ethics, morality, privacy, and security. These concerns further extend to questions of accountability when AI is utilized to assist in or make decisions on behalf of humans. Consequently, the governance of AI applications, known as AI governance, or the principles governing the responsible use of AI, has emerged as a critical issue that organizations must address within their specific contexts. Although Thailand AI Ethics Guideline has been available since 2021, its widespread implementation remains limited. The AI Governance Guideline for Executives was developed to offer a more practical and easily understandable guide on AI governance for organizational leaders to voluntarily follow.The initiative has the following objectives:AI Governance Guideline for Executives aims to provide a practical and comprehensive framework for implementing AI technology in a responsible and ethical manner while maintaining business objectives.

Slovenias National Programme on AI (NpAI) is in line with certain key goals from the Digital Slovenia 20320 Development Strategy (DS2030), which defines the strategic goals of digitalisation in Slovenia until 2030. Within this approach, some sectors have been identified as the most promising for the use of AI, thus have been prioritized for the direct support of uptake of AI. These include health, industry 4.0, language technologies and cultural identity, public sector, sustainable food and environment and spatial planning.

title: Taxonomy of Driving Automation for Vehicles
description: China's Taxonomy of Driving Automation for Vehicles initiative addresses the growing need for a standardized and unified classification system to define and regulate the levels of vehicle driving automation. As autonomous driving technologies continue to evolve rapidly, the absence of a clearly defined framework posed challenges for technology development, legal enforcement, industry coordination, and consumer understanding. This initiative seeks to close that gap by establishing a comprehensive taxonomy aligned with international developments but tailored to China's regulatory, technological, and societal context.The primary objective of the initiative is to set clear definitions for the different levels of driving automation”from Level 0 (no automation) to Level 5 (full automation)”based on the functions performed by the automated system versus the human driver. This classification supports regulatory consistency, facilitates compliance with safety standards, and enables communication among automakers, suppliers, policymakers, and the public. It also promotes transparency in advertising and product labeling to prevent consumer misunderstanding or overestimation of system capabilities.Over time, the initiative is expected to evolve in line with advancements in AI, sensor technologies, and vehicle connectivity. As part of its institutionalization, the taxonomy has been incorporated into national standards such as GB/T 40429-2021, which came into effect in 2021. This standard outlines six levels of automation and provides terminology and technical definitions in alignment with both ISO and SAE international standards, while allowing for adaptations to China's infrastructure and governance systems. Future updates are anticipated as technology matures, especially to accommodate new forms of mobility and smart infrastructure integration.The initiative has been developed and updated through collaborative efforts involving national regulators, technical standardization committees, research institutions, and major Chinese automotive companies. It complements broader national goals under initiatives such as Made in China 2025 and the development of intelligent connected vehicles (ICVs). By establishing a robust foundation for automated vehicle classification, China aims to foster innovation, ensure road safety, and maintain its leadership position in the global autonomous driving ecosystem.

description: Studies are carried out to establish the Center of Excellence of Data Analytics within the Ministry of Trade. Turkiye created scenarios related to the field of duty of our Ministry in the Center of Excellence of Data Analytics. Turkiye uses AI and ML technology on the data in these scenarios. Scenarios are made up of subjects that fall under the ministry's field of activity. There are special working teams for these scenarios. The project's key activities are forecasting, technological solutions, text mining in free text fields, early warning/alarm, simulation, data quality studies on various datasets, predictive models (using the methods of ML, AI, etc.), social network analysis, chatbot/assistant, and dashboard design. The Easy Export Platform enables our small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), co-operatives, and entrepreneurs to access all the information that they need via a single platform in the most up-to-date form (including the large-scale data provided with ML algorithms). It makes a significant contribution to our country's export vision.The initiative has the following objectives:- To collect, process, and protect the data of domestic and foreign trade and customs procedures in safe environments.- To support policymakers with tools such as scenario creation, simulation, and forecasting.

title: Digital Rights Charter
description: This text is based on the significant progress already made in Spain in the recognition of digital rights, including Title X of Organic Law 3/2018 of 5 December on the Protection of Personal Data and the guarantee of digital rights and the recently approved Royal Decree-Law 28/2020 of 22 September on distance work.The initiative has the following objectives:The objective of the Charter is descriptive, prospective and assertive. Descriptive of the digital contexts and scenarios that determine conflicts, sometimes unexpected, between rights, values and goods that have always existed, but which require new consideration; this mere description helps to visualise and become aware of the impact and consequences of digital environments and spaces. Prospective in anticipating future scenarios that can already be predicted. Assertive in the sense of revalidating and legitimising the principles, techniques and policies that, from the very culture of fundamental rights, should be applied in present and future digital environments and spaces.

title: Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence
description: The Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence is Denmark's flagship initiative for advancing world-class AI research that addresses major societal challenges. Established in 2021, the centre was created through a unique collaboration between the Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, five major private foundations, and Denmark's leading universities. With a total funding commitment of 47 million (DKK 354 million) over 13 years (2021-2034), the centre aims to position Denmark at the forefront of responsible, human-centred AI development.The centre focuses on a broad spectrum of AI-related topics, from technical advancements in machine learning and deep learning to cross-disciplinary research on the ethical, legal, and societal dimensions of AI. Its research agenda is built around three pillars: people, design, and societyensuring that AI technologies are not only powerful but also trustworthy, inclusive, and aligned with democratic values. The initiative addresses the growing need for AI solutions that are transparent, explainable, and designed with human interests in mind, especially as AI becomes more integrated into decision-making in areas like health, education, and governance.The University of Copenhagen hosts the centre, which operates in partnership with four other Danish universities: Aalborg University, Aarhus University, the Technical University of Denmark, and the IT University of Copenhagen. This multi-institutional setup fosters strong national collaboration and builds a comprehensive research ecosystem. In addition to conducting high-impact research, the centre is also committed to talent development, policy engagement, and public outreach, helping to shape both academic and societal understanding of AI in Denmark and beyond.Over time, the Pioneer Centre is expected to evolve into a globally recognized hub for AI research and innovation. Its long-term funding and multi-stakeholder foundation provide a stable platform for growth, including opportunities for international collaboration, interdisciplinary expansion, and deeper integration with public and private sector challenges. By bridging academic excellence with practical application and ethical foresight, the Pioneer Centre is setting a model for how advanced AI research can serve the public good.

title: National Program for Artificial Intelligence
description: The National Program for Artificial Intelligence relies on a central directorate and on theimplementation capabilities of its member organizations. Its operations include coordinating the work of all relevant governmental entities. The Program is intended to create a toolbox and organizational environment that will later facilitate AI development and the securing of Israel's leading status, alongside incremental establishment of the necessary regulatory mechanisms, while fostering responsible AI usage. It relies on a comprehensive view of all relevant aspects, including technological infrastructure, talent, investment in basic and applied research, encouraging innovation, and promoting AI usewithin the public sector.The program has five main objectives:1. Reinforcing AI infrastructure and research “ by means such as establishingcomputational infrastructures, encouraging groundbreaking basic and appliedresearch, expanding the domestic AI talent pipeline across academia and industry,promoting data infrastructures and data accessibility, and developing naturallanguage processing (NLP) infrastructures in Hebrew and Arabic.2. Creating leaps in AI adoptions in high-tech industry “ by forming regulatorysandboxes in highly regulated fields that present a high financial potential, supportingpilot-stage projects, realizing the potential of Israel's unique data assets, andimproving the capability of domestic industry to attract the best AI minds from aroundthe world.3. Implementing AI in public sector “ implementing knowledge, capabilities, and toolsin national and municipal government. Improving public service, streamliningprocesses, and improving decision-making processes based on data and technology.4. Securing Israel's global geo-technological position in AI “ Preserving andexpanding Israel's technological sovereignty and qualitative edge; deepening strategicpartnerships “ via joint research and dual-use technology development; PositioningIsrael as a regional AI hub and trusted partner; Actively participating in internationalforums to shape global AI standards and regulatory frameworks, to influence thefuture of AI and maintain Israel's freedom of action.5. Promoting AI at the national level “ Maximizing the societal and economic benefitsentailed in AI, by promoting comprehensive preparation and adaptation plans bygovernment ministries in their domains. Equipping the public and workforce with AI relevant skills, in aspects of education, employment, regulation, Responsible andtrustworthy AI, and others.It should be noted that this paper does not pertain to defense preparations as they relateto AI, and that such aspects are handled separately by the responsible entities.

description: The Law establishes among others, the following obligations: maintaining records of processed personal data, designation of a personal data protection officer, carrying out personal data protection impact assessments, provision of information during personal data collection, notification of personal data breach and communication of it to data subjects, and the implementation of appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure security of personal data. description: The AMI-CMA initiative seeks to transform digital and AI education in France by supporting original curricula across secondary and higher education. The programme focuses on preparing individuals for widespread adoption of digital tools in professional environments and addressing the gap between training supply and labour market demand . Projects are selected through evaluation by an international and independent jury . Key objectives of the programme include: Supporting the creation of new digital and AI training curricula at all education levels Contributing to diagnostics of digital training demand and supply in France Preparing individuals for professional use of digital technologies and AI Examples of funded projects: MACMIA: Organises training courses for technicians, engineers, and managers with dual skills in AI and “Industry of the Future.” It also covers dual skill areas such as embedded AI & intelligent mobility , AI & Health , and AI & Distribution . AISorb: Develops training at the intersection of AI and social sciences and humanities (SHS) to improve employability in professions transformed by AI. Future outlook: Expand the reach and impact of AI and digital training to 400,000 learners annually by 2030 Strengthen the alignment between education, skills development, and professional needs Foster innovation in curricula to ensure French students and professionals acquire skills relevant to a digital and AI-driven economy

description: The Digital Service Bundle for Continuous Learning is designed to offer a flexible, customer-oriented service package that crosses administrative boundaries. Its main goals are to: Support individuals in maintaining and developing their skills throughout their careers Help people make informed education and career decisions Align labour market demand with education supply AI technologies are integrated into the service bundle to enhance personalisation, guidance, and the delivery of learning services. The Digivisio 2030 programme complements this effort by bringing existing online digital competence courses into a common digital platform for higher education institutions. Key features include: AI-supported guidance and counselling services for students Facilitating digital skill development across higher education Promoting accessibility and standardisation of online learning Both initiatives are funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) , ensuring resources for implementation and expansion. The Service Centre for Continuous Learning and Employment (SECLE) focuses on bridging gaps between labour market needs and employee skills . Its activities include: Conducting foresight analysis to anticipate skill needs Procuring AI-related training for SME personnel Supporting integration of AI skills into academic curricula Future outlook: Expansion of digital platforms and services for lifelong learning Broader adoption of AI-driven personalised learning tools Enhanced alignment between education, workforce skills, and market needs Together, these initiatives aim to strengthen employability, support lifelong learning, and prepare individuals and organisations for evolving labour market demands.

title: Women in Digital
description: The “Women in Digital 2021–2026” strategy provides a coordinated framework to promote gender diversity in Belgium’s digital economy. Its key features include: Strategic coordination: Managed by the Federal Public Service (FPS) Economy as an intersectoral plan. Five strategic objectives: Increase the number of women graduating in digital fields. Promote integration of women into the digital workforce. Support retention of women in digital jobs through targeted policies. Challenge stereotypes and create role models to inspire girls and women. Bridge the gender gap in specific groups, including vulnerable populations. Cross-sectoral collaboration with education providers, businesses and civil society to implement actions. Monitoring and evaluation to track progress and adjust measures where needed. Through these measures, Belgium seeks to create a more inclusive and balanced digital sector , encouraging more women to study, enter, and remain in digital and AI-related careers .

title: Priority 1 of the EU Funds for Smart Economy 2021–2027
description: The project is fully consistent with EU priority objectives. The role of EIB support is to facilitate the financing of the related operational programmes and support their implementation within the shared management policy and legal framework; and ultimately to support the achievement of i.a. the redress of regional imbalances, the implementation of the Pillar of Social Rights, and the strengthening of the economic, social, and territorial cohesion of the Union. Poland - outside of Warsaw region - is designated an EIB Cohesion Region. The project therefore supports the strengthening of the EU's economic, social, and territorial cohesion. As for the sectorial public policy goals of the EIB, the multi-sector project is expected to contribute to Innovation, Digital and Human capital (IDHC, 54%), Sustainable Cities and Regions (SCI, 19%), Sustainable Energy and Natural resources (SENR, 19%), and SME development (8%). In the area of IDHC, the projects will increase the level of RDI, innovation enabling infrastructure, education and training, and healthcare which will lead to positive spill overs throughout the national economy. Under SCI, the project will support balanced territorial development, including the upgrading, replacement and reorganisation of urban infrastructure and public facilities which will positively impact quality of life for inhabitants. Concerning SENR, the project will further unlock the potential for energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy. The project will also protect the environment, biodiversity, and ecosystems, and through climate adaptation and disaster prevention invest in more resilient infrastructure, which reduces the risk of harm to life, property, and public services in the event of disaster. Finally, the project eases financial constraints for SMEs that arise from information asymmetries caused by the lack of track record for such companies and high screening costs for small investments.

title: Edge Learning Lab of AI Sweden
description: Sweden has developed an extensive ecosystem of test facilities that enable researchers, companies, and public organisations to develop, test, and validate AI technologies in real or simulated environments. These facilities cover a wide range of sectors and technology areas, providing infrastructure and expertise for experimentation, prototyping, and scaling AI solutions. A prominent example is the Edge Learning Lab at AI Sweden . This facility is designed as a cutting-edge testing environment where researchers and innovators can explore the possibilities and limitations of decentralised and edge learning , a critical area for next-generation AI applications. By enabling experimentation at the edge rather than in centralised systems, it supports innovation in areas such as autonomous vehicles, smart cities, and IoT-based services. Key features of Sweden’s AI test-facility ecosystem include: Specialised environments for AI testing, including decentralised and edge AI. Support for collaboration between researchers, industry, and the public sector. Infrastructure for experimentation and scaling , from prototypes to full-scale systems. Promotion of innovation through real-world testing conditions and knowledge sharing. By providing these facilities, Sweden is strengthening its position as a hub for AI development and experimentation , ensuring that new AI systems and applications can be safely, efficiently, and ethically tested before large-scale deployment.

title: Initiatives to help SMEs adopt digital or novel technologies including AI
description: Spain has developed a range of programmes to help companies adopt digital technologies and accelerate their innovation capabilities. These initiatives target different aspects of digital transformation, from training and advisory services to fostering collaboration between start-ups and established companies. Key programmes include: Digital Kit & Kit Consulting – provide SMEs with consultancy, guidance, and support for implementing digital tools and strategies. Activa Startups – promotes collaboration between innovative start-ups and established companies to drive technology transfer and innovation. Generación Digital Pymes – equips SME employees with the skills, knowledge, and tools needed to implement digital transformation within their organisations. Objectives of these programmes are to: Support digitalisation and innovation across SMEs and other companies. Encourage collaboration between start-ups and established companies with growth potential. Develop digital skills among employees to ensure effective technology adoption. Promote the growth of “new generation” companies , enhancing competitiveness and productivity. Although these initiatives are technology-agnostic , they include support for AI adoption , making it challenging to isolate AI-specific funding. Nevertheless, they provide an essential ecosystem for SMEs and companies to experiment with and integrate AI technologies alongside other digital solutions.

title: High-tech equity financing programme
description: Following a previous initiative by the Slovene Enterprise Fund (2014–2020), the SID Bank continues to support Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by providing equity-based funding to start-ups and scale-ups. The programme targets companies developing high-tech solutions, including those using artificial intelligence, advanced digital technologies, and other innovative products. Key features of the programme include: Equity financing instruments: seed capital and convertible loans that provide flexible funding while sharing risk between investors and the company. Target beneficiaries: innovative start-ups and scale-ups with high-growth potential in technology-driven sectors. Purpose: accelerate development, enable commercialisation of new products, and support company growth. Alignment with national strategies: complements other Slovenian programmes for SME digitalisation, R&D, and AI adoption. Through this initiative, the SID Bank helps Slovenian start-ups access capital that may be difficult to secure from traditional financing channels, while fostering innovation, technology-driven growth, and international competitiveness.

title: P4D grants for digital transformation
description: This initiative aims to help micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Slovenia adopt digital technologies and improve competitiveness. Grants can be used for technology investments, digital strategy development, software and hardware implementation, and upskilling staff. Key features of the programme include: Funding amount: up to €100,000 per enterprise. Target technologies: digital tools, advanced technologies such as AI, automation, data analytics, and cloud solutions. Scope of support: includes purchases of ICT equipment, software development, robotic process automation, AI systems, cloud services, digital marketing, and staff training. Implementation: delivered jointly by the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport and the Slovene Enterprise Fund , in alignment with EU guidelines for SME digitalisation. Through this programme, Slovenian SMEs are empowered to: Modernise business processes and adopt AI-driven solutions. Increase productivity and competitiveness in domestic and international markets. Strengthen workforce digital skills , ensuring sustainable technology adoption. The initiative supports Slovenia’s broader strategy for digital transformation, innovation, and economic growth , making SMEs more resilient and technologically capable.

title: Aid scheme for the digitalisation of SME
description: As part of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) , Component 9 – Investment 3: Private Sector Aid Schemes was launched to accelerate the digital transformation of Romania’s small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This initiative recognises that SMEs form the backbone of the economy, but often lack resources to access and implement cutting-edge technologies. By combining financial support with clear eligibility criteria, the programme seeks to foster both technological adoption and innovation-led growth. The sub-investment is structured around two main instruments : Grants for the development of advanced digital technologies – targeted at entrepreneurs who are building solutions in fields such as: Artificial intelligence (AI) Data and cloud computing Blockchain High-performance and quantum computing Internet of Things (IoT) Cybersecurity 2. Grants of up to EUR 100,000 per enterprise for digital adoption – supporting SMEs in integrating new technologies into their operations. Eligible expenses include: Purchases of ICT hardware and software licences. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and software automation tools. Blockchain and artificial intelligence systems. Machine learning, augmented reality, and virtual reality applications. Cloud services and IoT solutions. Development of company websites. Staff training in the use of IT equipment. Advisory services and technical assessments for digital readiness. The overall objective is to strengthen the competitiveness of SMEs by enabling them to adopt and create digital solutions that increase efficiency, productivity, and innovation capacity. Looking ahead, this investment is expected to deliver long-term benefits for the Romanian economy by: Creating a more digitally skilled workforce. Enhancing SME participation in the digital single market. Supporting the growth of local digital technology providers. Facilitating the integration of Romanian SMEs into European and global value chains. By targeting both the supply side (entrepreneurs developing advanced technologies) and the demand side (SMEs adopting digital tools), the initiative ensures a balanced and sustainable approach to digitalisation.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
description: Romania is home to seven European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) established under the Digital Europe Programme , with five explicitly focused on artificial intelligence (AI): eDIH-DIZ, TDIH, DIH4Society, FIT EDIH, and CiTyInnoHub . These hubs act as regional one-stop shops that help businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and public administrations take advantage of digital and AI technologies to improve their products, services, and operations. The initiative is financed through the Smart Growth, Digitalization and Financial Instruments Programme 2021–2027 , co-funded by the European Commission and the Romanian Government (Ministry of European Investments and Projects) . By combining European and national resources, the programme ensures that SMEs and other organisations can access high-quality expertise, training, and technological infrastructure. The main objectives of Romania’s EDIHs are to: Support digital transformation of SMEs through applied training, testing, and consultancy. Promote AI adoption in diverse sectors of the economy. Offer access to advanced facilities and expertise , such as test-before-invest environments. Facilitate collaboration between academia, businesses, and government institutions. Boost competitiveness by making advanced digital technologies more accessible. Looking forward, the hubs are expected to expand their role in scaling AI adoption nationwide, increasing cross-border cooperation within the European EDIH network, and contributing to a stronger innovation ecosystem in Romania. Their impact will be particularly important in helping SMEs integrate AI into real-world applications, thus enhancing productivity and competitiveness at both national and European levels.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs
description: The purpose of EDIH HPC4Poland is to increase the competitiveness and innovation of North West Poland (NUTS1) manufacturing companies and public organizations by increasing awareness and availability of advanced digital tools and services based on safe, reliable and efficient High Performance Computing (HPC), including: cloud simulations (PaaS), sensor systems (IoT), AR/VR/MR, collaborative robots, AGV, AMR, additive technologies, AI and Big Data analysis. title: INNOAIR
description: The INNOAIR Project is an innovative urban mobility initiative led by the Municipality of Sofia . It aims to reduce air pollution and traffic congestion by introducing AI-enabled, sustainable transport services . The project is supported by the Urban Innovative Actions programme under the European Regional Development Fund , which funds experimental solutions to urban challenges. Core elements of the project include: Optimising public transport routes based on real-time passenger demand using AI algorithms Launching an on-demand electric minibus service with flexible routes tailored to user needs Connecting underserved peri-urban areas to Sofia’s metro system, improving accessibility and reducing car dependency Integrating booking and payment via the BUSINN app , which links seamlessly with Sofia’s public transport system These measures not only improve the efficiency of public transport but also contribute to cleaner air, lower carbon emissions, and a more inclusive transport network. Future outlook: Expansion of on-demand AI-powered services to other areas of Sofia Integration of additional sustainable mobility solutions such as shared electric vehicles and micro-mobility options Providing a model for other European cities looking to adopt similar AI-driven approaches to public transport and environmental improvement

title: Innocities
description: Finland’s InnoCities initiative intends to tackle a common challenge: research and innovation activity is often fragmented, making it hard for regions to build globally competitive strengths. By coordinating funding and collaboration across all Finnish university and university-consortium cities, the programme seeks to pool capabilities, focus on shared priorities, and turn research into impactful solutions for businesses and society. The main objectives are to strengthen regional innovation ecosystems, deepen cooperation between cities, universities, companies and public actors, and grow specific competence areas where Finland can compete internationally. Long-term agreements between the state and InnoCities set clear expectations for results and ensure that research, development and innovation (RDI) spending produces measurable impact across regions. In practice, implementation is largely financed through the EU’s 2021–2027 programme period for sustainable urban development.

title: Digitisation of Railway and Road Infrastructure – Digitisation of Road Traffic
description: The Digitisation of Railway and Road Infrastructure – Digitisation of Road Traffic project (2021–2025) is led by Slovenia’s Ministry of Infrastructure. It leverages digitalisation and data-driven management to optimise traffic flows and improve the safety of road networks.

title: Advanced digital skills training program for civil servants
description: As part of its Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP), Romania is investing in advanced digital training for civil servants to accelerate public sector digitalisation. Many institutions lack in-house expertise for IT and data operations, slowing reform and leaving them dependent on external providers. The program aims to train 32,500 officials, including 2,500 senior staff, in areas such as database and system management, business and data analysis, and programming. By developing these skills internally, the government hopes to build a more resilient, capable workforce for ongoing digital transformation. The initiative is coordinated by the National Agency for Civil Servants with training providers like the National Institute of Administration. It runs until June 2026 and is tied to specific milestones under the RRP.

title: PlanAPP Project
description: The PlanAPP / IA2AI project was created to make regulatory impact assessments in Portugal more reliable and efficient. Many laws are passed without fully anticipating their costs or side effects, which can weaken trust and create unnecessary burdens. By introducing AI into the process, the project helps analysts test draft legislation more quickly, spot risks, and compare alternatives before decisions are made. Led by PlanAPP, Portugal’s public administration centre for planning and foresight, the initiative builds on earlier work by the Technical Unit for Legislative Impact Assessment. It works in partnership with Nova Information Management School and other experts to design AI tools that support ministries and agencies. The project began under EU funding and has since been integrated into PlanAPP’s broader work. It aims to extend use across more policy areas and levels of government, improving regulatory quality at both national and European scales.

title: National Strategy for Research Data Management
description: Research today generates large amounts of data that need to be carefully managed to ensure quality, transparency, and usefulness. Without clear guidelines, researchers and institutions can struggle to store, organize, and share their data properly. To tackle this, Denmark created a National Strategy for Research Data Management, and DeiC leads the effort to put this strategy into practice. The strategy targets research institutions like universities and the organizations that fund research. Its main goal is to promote better data management so that research data becomes easier to find, access, and reuse. This aligns with the FAIR principles—making data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable—which help improve the transparency and impact of Danish research. DeiC coordinates the work by collaborating with universities, funders, and other partners to develop tools, guidelines, and funding methods that encourage good data management. It supports training, sets standards, and helps build systems to store and share data securely. This national effort ensures that researchers across Denmark follow common practices, making research data a valuable shared resource.

title: Autonomous mobility projects PRISSMA Project - Research and Investment Platform for the Safety and Security of Autonomous Mobility
description: The PRISSMA Project (Research and Investment Platform for the Safety and Security of Autonomous Mobility) is designed to support the development and validation of automated road transport systems. Its goal is to ensure that autonomous vehicles operate safely within predefined routes or areas. AI is integrated as part of the overall system-of-systems concept, allowing individual components to be tested and verified within a broader transport network. Key objectives of the project include: Verifying the safety and reliability of automated transport systems Integrating AI components into autonomous mobility platforms Supporting innovation in autonomous transport through targeted research and investment The project is part of a wider AI Challenge organised by the Innovation and Industry Fund, which selects and supports high-impact AI projects. Since its inception, five major AI-related challenges have been addressed under this initiative, demonstrating a strong focus on applied research and practical implementation. Future outlook: Expansion of autonomous mobility testing and validation in real-world environments Continued integration of AI-driven safety and monitoring systems Strengthened collaboration between industry, research institutions, and funding bodies to accelerate innovation in autonomous transport

description: The Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI are designed to build a world-class training and research environment for artificial intelligence. Students benefit from high-level academic instruction, while industry fellows bring practical expertise to teaching and collaborative projects. By combining scientific excellence with practical application, the Konrad Zuse Schools support the training of future AI experts , strengthen Germany’s AI research capacity , and enhance the international visibility of its AI ecosystem. Looking ahead, the schools aim to expand their network of industry partners, broaden their programme offerings, and continue attracting top-tier international students and researchers to Germany.
