title: National IT Academy project on the creation of study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence
description: Slovakia is actively working to improve education in artificial intelligence (AI) at its universities to better prepare students for a future where digital technologies are increasingly important. Many higher education institutions currently lack up-to-date resources and courses focused specifically on AI, which limits students’ ability to develop the relevant skills needed in this fast-growing field. This gap presents both a challenge and an opportunity. By providing new courses, Slovakia can help students become qualified AI professionals who contribute to the country’s economic and technological growth. Subjects include such as the basics of artificial intelligence, an introduction to neural networks, more advanced topics on neural networks, and programming languages used for AI development. The goal is to offer students a strong foundation in both AI theory and practical skills. These courses are designed to be accessible for students from various technical backgrounds, helping to build a wider pool of specialists who understand AI technologies and how to apply them in real situations. In collaboration with the Digital Coalition, the Government of Slovakia supported the implementation of the national “IT Academy − Education for the 21st Century” project to educate the top ICT specialists, prepare the pilot projects for digital transformation of the education system and schools to identify and enhance the digital economy competencies, digitally transform the vocational education and training at all its levels of education, including the higher vocational education and post-secondary specialized education, with the option to offer a free choice of educational path by choosing the bachelor’s higher education degree, or by recognising tertiary education completed with the possibility of a smooth transition to higher university study of the second degree. This initiative brings together universities, government bodies, and industry experts to ensure the new study materials are accurate and relevant to the needs of employers and society. Universities pilot these new subjects and give feedback to improve the materials. Teachers receive support to help them introduce these courses effectively. Cooperation among different partners helps make sure the reforms are well coordinated and meet the standards expected in modern digital education. Looking ahead, the project aims to grow and adapt as AI technology evolves. This could include creating more advanced courses or introducing new topics like AI ethics, industry-specific applications, or ongoing training for current professionals. The broader educational reform linked to the “IT Academy − Education for the 21st Century” project supports this growth by promoting digital transformation across all levels of education. Slovakia hopes to build a workforce ready to meet future challenges and opportunities in AI and the digital economy.

title: AgrarIA: AI applied to the value chain ​​of agricultural production 2050
description: The project is focused on assessing the applicability and viability of AI alongside other advanced technologies in agriculture. It seeks to create innovative solutions that improve productivity, sustainability, and efficiency across different stages of agricultural production. Key potential initiatives include: Development of new natural products for pest and disease control, offering alternatives to chemical synthesis while maintaining effectiveness Use of collaborative robotics to optimise product transformation and processing phases Application of quantum computing for managing and analysing satellite imagery to optimise agricultural production Implementation of digital twins to enhance energy efficiency in refrigeration and storage facilities The project encourages collaboration between research institutions, technology providers, and agricultural stakeholders to ensure practical, scalable solutions. By integrating cutting-edge technologies, it aims to modernise agriculture while promoting sustainability and competitiveness. Future outlook: Adoption of AI-driven and technology-enhanced production methods across farms Increased efficiency, sustainability, and resilience in agricultural operations Development of new methodologies that can be scaled and applied to various crops and production systems

title: Area Monitoring System (AMS)
description: The Area Monitoring System (AMS) , deployed by the Agency for Agricultural Markets and Rural Development in Slovenia, is a software-supported platform that uses processed satellite images from Sentinel and commercial providers to monitor agricultural areas. By applying machine learning algorithms , the system determines the status and changes of agricultural surfaces over specific periods, improving the accuracy and efficiency of monitoring. In early 2024, the Ministry of Agriculture established a special project group to explore the introduction and development of digitisation and AI in agriculture . This group examines both administrative and technological aspects , with the aim of integrating digital and AI solutions into existing systems and processes. Key aims include: Evaluating the potential for expanding AMS applications into agricultural production Exploring integration with commercial digital and AI solutions Improving data-driven decision-making in agriculture and rural development Looking forward, the initiative seeks to broaden AMS’s scope beyond administrative monitoring to include practical tools for farmers and agricultural producers , enabling smarter, more sustainable farming practices. By combining public systems with commercial AI innovations, Slovenia aims to create a more digitally advanced agricultural sector .

The plan is intended to stimulate innovation, job creation, and economic growth while supporting environmental sustainability. Future outlook: Broader integration of AI and digital tools across bio-economy sectors Expansion of circular economy practices nationwide Strengthened linkages between research, industry, and policy to maintain long-term sustainability and competitiveness

title: Satellite Crop Monitoring System
description: The S2MUR project aims to enhance agricultural monitoring and forecasting to reduce crop losses. It provides farmers, policymakers, and stakeholders with comprehensive knowledge about crop conditions and predicts the impact of adverse weather events , such as droughts or storms. The project also generates maps and reports to estimate losses and calculate potential crop damage. Key features of the initiative include: Development of an information system that integrates satellite imagery, meteorological, soil, and statistical data Creation of a repository of machine learning (ML) models for analyzing crop conditions and forecasting risks Provision of a production environment to apply ML models and an environment for developing and training ML models Focus on estimating losses due to drought and other crop hazards The project’s future goals include expanding the range of ML models, improving prediction accuracy, and enhancing the system’s usability for farmers and agricultural authorities. By combining data-driven insights with machine learning , S2MUR supports more informed agricultural management and helps mitigate the economic impact of crop losses.

title: AI in Schools (various initiatives)
description: Ireland’s participation in the AI4T Erasmus+ project (AI FOR and BY teachers, 2021–2024) focused on exploring AI applications in education and producing policy recommendations. The project addressed key areas including: Professional learning pathways for educators Cross-national cooperation to strengthen EU AI capacity Ethical and legal considerations for AI use in schools Guidance requirements from education authorities Targeted training for inspectors and teacher trainers Evaluation of student outcomes and experiences Complementing this, Oide Technology in Education provides an AI Hub with practical resources on the safe, effective, and ethical use of AI in education. The platform includes: A video series and AI online course (AI for Schools, 1-hour) for teachers and school leaders Guidance on AI benefits, limitations, and challenges Opportunities for teachers to engage in Think-In events , sharing knowledge and discussing AI integration Several pilot activities were conducted in schools to develop practical use cases, gather insights, and inform policy development. Additionally, AI guidelines for schools are under development, with publication expected in early 2025.

title: High- and Highest-Performance-Computing for the Digital Age
description: This initiative by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) supports the development of next-generation high-performance computing (HPC) in Germany. It addresses two main challenges: the need for much more powerful computing systems and the high energy consumption of large-scale data centres. The SCALEXA programme focuses on exascale computing—systems that can perform extremely complex tasks at speeds far beyond current capabilities. These technologies are essential for fields like climate research, AI, and advanced simulations. The goal is to boost Germany’s role in cutting-edge HPC. In parallel, the GreenHPC initiative promotes energy-efficient computing solutions within the European EuroHPC framework. It supports innovations that reduce the environmental impact of supercomputing, such as better cooling systems and energy-saving software. Together, these programmes bring research institutions, industry, and government partners together to advance powerful yet sustainable HPC infrastructure in Germany and Europe.

title: Projects under Food Vision 2030
description: Ireland’s Food Vision 2030 strategy positions research and innovation as key drivers of a more sustainable agri-food system, with funding from the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM). Within this framework, AI has become an important tool for addressing sectoral challenges ranging from productivity to food safety and public health. Several recent projects highlight this trend: MUSHNOMICS applies AI to boost efficiency in mushroom production; SPECTROFOOD uses hyperspectral imaging for food quality control; RIBMINS explores AI-assisted methods in slaughterhouse inspections; APP4FARM develops smart farming solutions; AMBROSIA examines AI-supported nutrition for older adults; and food system mapping projects apply AI to track supply chains. Together, these initiatives are examples of how how AI research is being embedded across Ireland’s agri-food priorities under Food Vision 2030.

title: Methodological Guidelines for Cloud Services
description: The Methodological Guidelines for Cloud Services in the Slovak Republic provide practical recommendations for using cloud technologies within public administration. They address the challenge that adopting cloud services can be complex, with risks related to security, compatibility, and cost management. By offering clear guidance, the guidelines aim to help public institutions adopt cloud solutions safely and effectively. The main objectives are to ensure security of public data, promote interoperability between systems, and encourage cost-efficient use of cloud technologies. They also aim to standardize approaches across different government bodies, improving coordination and consistency in digital services. The guidelines were developed under the framework of NKIVS (National Concept of Informatization of the Slovak Republic), with input from government IT specialists and public sector stakeholders. They cover practical steps for selecting cloud providers, managing risks, ensuring legal compliance, and integrating cloud solutions with existing IT systems.

title: xPlain-AI
description: The aim of the project is a training application to make complex AI-based projects "explainable" to employees at the interface between medicine and technology. A major disadvantage of AI-based technologies in the medical field is that these systems are not explained to users. Together with Women in AI and the DIO, "Xplain-AI" will explain innovative projects with AI-based content in a user-oriented way – for example, data-driven, automated technologies, integration of machine learning, recognition of biases in the application of algorithms. The training application is barrier-free, web-based and includes human-centered design with an adaptive, human-in-the-loop learning algorithm. The reinforcement learning process learns the individual preferences of the user - everyone can help shape his/her training content by evaluating the content.

title: Interministerial framework for data administration
description: Governments today rely increasingly on data, algorithms, and software to provide public services and make decisions. However, managing these digital tools in a transparent and consistent way is a challenge. To address this, the government introduced a public policy focused on data, algorithms, and source codes. This policy sets out clear rules and a framework for government departments and agencies to register and document the data they use, the algorithms they develop, and the source codes behind their software. The aim is to improve transparency, coordination, and trust in how digital resources are managed across the public sector. The main objective of this initiative is to create a unified approach to handling important digital assets within the government. By registering data sets, algorithms, and source codes in an organized system, administrations can avoid duplication of efforts, ensure quality and security, and provide easier access to these resources when needed. This approach helps different government bodies share knowledge and collaborate more effectively while also making it easier for citizens to understand how public digital tools work. The framework involves multiple government ministries working together to establish common standards and practices. It defines how administrations should document their digital tools and outlines the services that support this registration process. title: Data – an underutilized resource for Sweden
description: Sweden's national data strategy, titled Data – an underutilized resource for Sweden , was introduced in 2021 as part of the government's innovation program. Developed in collaboration with industry stakeholders, the strategy aims to enhance access to data, particularly to support advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital innovation. Recognizing data as a critical asset, the strategy seeks to unlock its potential to drive economic growth, improve public services, and foster innovation across various sectors. To implement this strategy, the Swedish government issued seven specific commissions to various government agencies, coordinated by the National Innovation Council. These commissions focused on developing the necessary infrastructure and frameworks to facilitate secure and efficient data sharing and utilization. As of 2024, all assigned tasks have been completed, marking a significant milestone in Sweden's data-driven transformation. A key component of this initiative is the role of the Agency for Digital Government (DIGG), which has been tasked with coordinating data-driven innovation efforts across the public sector. DIGG's responsibilities include overseeing the implementation of shared data platforms, establishing data governance standards, and promoting the use of open data to stimulate innovation and improve public services. The agency's work ensures that data is utilized responsibly and effectively, aligning with Sweden's digitalization goals.

title: NeIC Heilsa
description: Heilsa Tryggvedottir is a Nordic project, funded through the Nordic e-Infrastructure Collaboration (NeIC) with participation by partner nodes, which builds on prior work under the NeIC Tryggve and Tryggve2 projects. Its purpose is to enable secure cross-border sharing and analysis of sensitive human data—such as combined genomic and phenotypic (phenomics) datasets—in order to drive discovery, strengthen public health, and improve healthcare outcomes. The project has several core objectives: To transform the prototype or experimental tools developed in earlier Tryggve phases into production-ready, interoperable services. To support federated data services across Nordic countries so that researchers with appropriate authorization can access or combine data hosted in different countries without moving sensitive raw data in insecure ways. To incorporate key infrastructure pieces such as sensitive data archives, synthetic data generation, and imputation services, along with federated authentication/authorization (e.g. using ELIXIR AAI) to ensure data is managed responsibly. Heilsa Tryggvedottir is carried out by ELIXIR node partners in Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, and Estonia, under the larger umbrella of NeIC. The project works closely with existing national sensitive data services and archives, and with European infrastructure efforts such as the Federated European Genome-phenome Archive (FEGA), combining legal, ethical, technical, and operational expertise.

title: Sunet Data Center DC Orion in Kalix + EOSC data storage
description: Sunet, Sweden’s national research and education network, is responsible for providing secure and reliable digital infrastructure to universities, research institutions, and public bodies. To strengthen the resilience of its services, Sunet is establishing a new data centre in northern Sweden under the project known as DC Orion . This development responds to the need for greater redundancy in national digital infrastructure, reducing the risk of disruption from regional outages or other incidents in the Stockholm area where many of Sunet’s existing systems are currently located. The main objective of the initiative is to ensure continuity of Sunet’s critical services—such as identity management (EduID), storage and archiving, virtual computing environments, media services, and DNS—by hosting them in a geographically distinct location with secure and scalable infrastructure. Locating the facility in the north offers additional benefits, including access to a stable power supply, robust fibre connectivity, and the natural advantages of a cooler climate for sustainable operations. The project is led by Sunet and has been developed through a detailed planning process, building on earlier feasibility studies. The facility is designed to meet high standards of security and reliability, including redundant power and network connections. Services are being progressively migrated to the new site, with Sunet’s Virtual Datacenter (VDC) now available from DC Orion. This supports both Sunet’s own redundancy needs and the growing demands of Sweden’s research and education communities for high-performance, secure, and flexible digital services.

title: IMPaCT
description: Spain’s IMPaCT initiative is a national programme, coordinated by the Carlos III Health Institute (Instituto de Salud Carlos III, ISCIII), designed to accelerate the deployment of Personalized Precision Medicine across the Spanish National Health System. It is intended to shift healthcare toward more preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic approaches that are tailored to each patient, making them safer and more effective. The structure of IMPaCT is arranged around three major axes or pillars: Predictive Medicine (the Cohort Axis): This involves building a large-scale, population-based cohort. The cohort is meant to include 200,000 people from 50 “nodes” spread across all 17 autonomous communities plus Ceuta and Melilla. Participants will provide data via clinical records, lifestyle/environmental inputs, biological sampling and periodic follow-ups. Data Science (the DATA Axis): This axis deals with integrating and analysing clinical, molecular and genetic data. It aims to ensure good practices around data collection, interoperability, secondary data use, and building models for research and healthcare decision making. Genomic Medicine (the GENOMICS Axis): This pillar supports the genomic-side of things: developing infrastructure to carry out high-complexity genomic analyses, sequencing, and making those resources available across the country. Two cross-cutting themes run through all of IMPaCT: ethics and scientific integrity, and internationalization.

title: Advanced digitalisation – future solutions in Swedish industry
description: Sweden's Advanced Digitalisation Programme, administered by Vinnova, the Swedish innovation agency, is a strategic initiative aimed at fostering industrial innovation through digital transformation. The programme supports approximately 100 innovation projects, including those focused on secure data flows for applied AI edge technologies. Funding Structure: The programme operates in three stages, with funding available for pre-studies and subsequent project phases, potentially up to SEK 50 million per year for six years. Collaboration: Projects are expected to be carried out in collaboration between at least two actors, including companies, universities, research institutes, and other relevant organizations. . Strategic Goals: Digital Sovereignty: Developing secure and sovereign digital solutions tailored for Swedish industry. Intersectoral Collaboration: Fostering cooperation between public and private sectors to drive innovation. title: AI Priority Research Program and Equipment (PEPR)
description: This program is a powerful tool supporting the national AI strategy, already encompassing nine ambitious projects. It aims to tackle key and fundamental challenges in machine learning across three complementary pillars: Trustworthy and Distributed AI Through a multifaceted approach to trust, this axis integrates: The development of robustness foundations using statistical approaches. The incorporation of formal methods for the specification, learning, and safety validation of AI models The development of decentralized learning mechanisms that ensure security. The integration of causal models with machine learning to provide explainable, evidence-based capabilities. Frugal and Embedded AI This involves deepening the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of machine learning to ensure data and computation frugality by design. It includes: Advanced model optimization and training guided by hardware constraints. The design of dedicated AI hardware architectures that are modular, flexible, and adaptive. The exploration of physics-informed computational models. New Mathematical Foundations of AI, particularly in the field of mathematical analysis, this pillar includes: The integration of tools and advances from partial differential equations, optimal control, and optimal transport. To develop novel architectures with stable optimization schemes, efficient solvers and approximations. The analytical treatment of generative and diffusion methods.

title: Important Project of Common European Interest – Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI-CIS)
description: The IPCEI-CIS (Important Project of Common European Interest – Cloud Infrastructure and Services) is a large European initiative designed to strengthen Europe’s digital independence. Today, many cloud services used in Europe are operated by non-European providers. This creates risks around data security, privacy, and long-term control. At the same time, emerging technologies—like autonomous vehicles or smart factories—need to process data quickly and close to where it is generated. Existing systems aren’t always fit for these needs. To address this, IPCEI-CIS aims to build a decentralised, secure, and efficient “cloud-edge continuum.” This means creating a system where different cloud and edge service providers across Europe can work together seamlessly. It will allow users to process and move data across different locations and providers, without being locked into one company’s platform. The goal is not just technical independence, but also the development of new, data-driven services and business models across industries. The project involves over 100 companies and research organisations from 12 EU countries, with Germany coordinating. Work is split into areas like building energy-efficient data centres, developing management software, and testing real-world applications. With around €2.6 billion in combined public and private funding, the project is now moving from research to deployment. Over time, IPCEI-CIS aims to create a lasting digital infrastructure for Europe—one that is secure, sustainable, and open to future innovation.

title: Irish Centre for High-End Computing (ICHEC)
description: The Irish Centre for High-End Computing (ICHEC) is Ireland’s national centre for high-performance computing and plays an active role in Europe’s quantum technology landscape. In 2021, it hosted the second European Quantum Technologies Conference, bringing together researchers, policymakers, and industry to explore advances in quantum computing and its applications. ICHEC is also a partner in major European projects, including NEASQC (Next Applications of Quantum Computing), which develops near-term quantum computing use cases, and HPCQS (High Performance Computer–Quantum Simulator), which connects supercomputers with quantum simulators to explore hybrid computing solutions. Through these initiatives, ICHEC seeks to strengthen Ireland’s contribution to cutting-edge computing research and innovation at the European level.

title: FARI Institute
description: FARI is a Brussels-based institute jointly founded by the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) to advance artificial intelligence (AI), data, and robotics for the public good. The initiative brings together around 300 researchers from diverse disciplines to develop solutions that address social challenges and promote responsible, human-centred innovation. The institute’s work responds to the growing need for trustworthy and transparent AI systems that can be applied to real-world issues, from sustainable urban development to public safety and digital inclusion. By fostering collaboration between academia, public authorities, and industry, FARI serves as a bridge between cutting-edge research and practical applications that deliver tangible societal impact. Projects undertaken within FARI span multiple domains, including AI-assisted public decision-making, ethical data governance, and the use of robotics in environmental and social contexts. Its interdisciplinary structure enables cross-sectoral innovation while maintaining a strong focus on ethics, fairness, and accountability in AI use.

title: C2.3. R3-I4 Consolidation of THE CEZIH health information infrastructure system (Central Health information system of the Republic of Croatia)
description: Croatia’s Central Health Information System (CEZIH) is essential for managing health data and services. However, its current setup lacks the reliability and security needed for a modern healthcare system. The system is vulnerable to outages and data loss, and it doesn’t meet high availability standards. To address this, the Croatian government launched a project to upgrade CEZIH’s infrastructure, ensuring stable, secure, and round-the-clock operations. The main goal is to move CEZIH into a state-managed cloud environment and build two data centres—primary and backup—that meet TIER 3 standards. This ensures high system availability and protection against failures. The project also includes disaster recovery planning, improved monitoring, and data backup to prevent service disruptions and data breaches. Led by the Central State Office for the Development of Digital Society and supported by Croatia’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan, the project runs from 2021 to 2025. Once completed, it will offer a stronger foundation for digital health services, with better reliability, data protection, and room to grow as technology and healthcare demands evolve.

title: Education and Employment Programme
description: Romania's Education and Employment Programme aims to align the country's vocational education and training (VET) system with the evolving needs of the labour market, particularly in the digital and green sectors. Key components of the programme include: Curriculum Development: Updating vocational training standards and curricula to reflect technological advancements in fields such as AI, 3D printing, and sustainable technologies. Teacher Training: Providing professional development opportunities for educators to equip them with the knowledge and skills necessary to teach the updated curricula effectively. Industry Collaboration: Engaging with industry partners to ensure that the training provided aligns with current and future labour market needs. Digital and Green Skills Focus: Emphasizing the development of digital and green competencies to prepare the workforce for the green and digital transition. The programme is supported by Romania's Recovery and Resilience Plan, which allocates significant funding for investments and reforms in education and employment. This includes investments in digital and green skills development, as well as initiatives to modernize vocational education and training institutions.

title: National Strategy for SMEs 2021-2027
description: The National Strategy for SMEs 2021–2027 serves as a key strategic document for Bulgaria, aligning with European Union policies to promote sustainable and digital growth of small and medium-sized enterprises. Key Objectives: Digital Transformation: Promote the adoption of digital technologies among SMEs to enhance efficiency and competitiveness. Innovation and Research: Encourage innovation and research activities within SMEs to foster growth and adaptation to market changes. Access to Finance: Improve access to financial resources for SMEs to support their development and expansion. Business Environment: Enhance the regulatory and institutional framework to facilitate the growth of SMEs. Implementation and Monitoring: The strategy is to be implemented through an Action Plan and annual programmes adopted by the Minister of Economy and Industry. An interim evaluation and analysis of the state of SMEs will be conducted to assess the effectiveness of the strategy and make necessary adjustments.

title: Pilots for the Impact Assessment Human Rights and Algorithms
description: In 2023, the Dutch Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations commissioned Rijks ICT Gilde (RIG) and Utrecht University (UU) to supervise a series of Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment (FRAIA) processes with government organizations. A total of 16 pilot projects were conducted, involving various public sector entities, to assess the human rights implications of algorithmic systems. These pilots aimed to build knowledge and expertise on issues regarding algorithms and human rights and to promote the use of the FRAIA tool among government organizations, particularly municipalities. The FRAIA is a discussion and decision-making tool designed to facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue among those responsible for the development and use of algorithmic systems. It comprises a series of questions that need to be addressed when considering the development, procurement, adjustment, or use of an algorithm, ensuring that fundamental rights are safeguarded throughout the process.

title: Cambodia Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021-2035
description: As pointed out in the Rectangular Strategy - Phase 4 and the Cambodia Vision 2050, as well as the readiness to respond to the Fourth Industrial Revolution and tap the potentials of the digital transformation, the "Cambodia Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021-2035" has been considered and prepared based on the actual needs, potentials, resources, and capabilities, both in the public and private sectors, for the development orientation and process of digital transformation in Cambodia. The digital transformation will bring about significant positive outcomes to the Cambodian economy and society, particularly the new growth driver that is highly resilient to future structural changes while being the driving force for the existing growth engines, which are now beginning to slow down and are severely affected by the Covid-19 crisis. Thus, the digital sector will bring about opportunities for new sources of growth, increase economic productivity, promote economic diversification, and create jobs, aimed at contributing to poverty alleviation and social inequality. 44 specific policy measures have been set out to build two foundations: (1)- developing digital infrastructure focusing on digital connectivity, financial technology infrastructure and digital payment systems, and logistics and last-mile delivery; and (2)- building trust and confidence in digital systems focusing on responsive and effective legal frameworks and strengthening digital security management. 82 policy measures have been put in place to strengthen the three pillars, including (1)- building digital citizens focusing on digital leadership, pools of talents, and digital citizens, (2)- building digital government focusing on digital government and public services, keys to boosting digital performance, and data-driven governance in the public sector, and (3)- enabling digital businesses focusing on enterprise transformation, entrepreneurial and startup ecosystems, and the digital value chains. The policy framework also considers 13 necessary measures to ensure inclusive participation in the digital sector, as well as to absorb, mitigate, and address the impacts of new trends stemmed from digital technology on the economy and society. These include changes in the structure of the workforce and labor; changes in tax revenue; increased state spending; impacts on culture, tradition, and communications; the loss of personal data; and cybercrime. This policy framework is designed as a "living document" that may eventually be revised to ensure consistency and appropriateness with the advancement of technology, the actual situation of the digital transformation, and the changing socio-economic circumstances in the country, the region, and the world; as well as to respond to risks.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), Section 26 (Transfer Limitation Obligation) and Personal Data Protection Regulations 2021
description: Under Section 26 of Singapore’s Personal Data Protection Act , private organisations may transfer personal data outside Singapore if the recipient is subject to legally enforceable obligations that ensure a level of data protection comparable to that required under Singapore law. These requirements are operationalised through the Personal Data Protection Regulations 2021 , which have been in force since 1 February 2021 . The framework does not impose data localisation requirements or restrict the use of foreign cloud service providers. Instead, it establishes conditions under which cross‑border data transfers — including those associated with cloud‑based AI training, processing, or analytics — may occur lawfully. Compliance mechanisms include contractual safeguards with overseas service providers, internal rules for intra‑group transfers, recognised certifications, or reliance on foreign legal regimes that provide comparable protection. Guidance issued by the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) clarifies how these statutory requirements apply in practice, including to cloud computing arrangements. While the guidance is non‑binding, it provides regulatory interpretation of the in‑force legal provisions. Overall, the PDPA cross‑border transfer regime addresses legal uncertainty related to international cloud use while maintaining enforceable data protection obligations for private organisations.

title: AI for Thai – Thai AI Service Platform
description: AI for Thai consolidates NECTEC's AI research outputs into an accessible API platform structured around three modules: Language (word segmentation, named entity recognition, machine translation, sentiment analysis), Vision (OCR, face recognition, object and activity recognition), and Conversation (speech-to-text, text-to-speech, chatbot). The platform's focus on "natural language processing of the Thai language, visual understanding in the context of Thainess, and Thai speech recognition and speech generation" addresses the specific challenge of adapting AI tools to a linguistic and cultural context underserved by international platforms. Sectoral use cases described include retail chatbots, logistics driver fatigue detection, medical image analysis, and tourism translation tools. By offering APIs with a free testing tier and targeting SMEs and start-ups alongside larger developers, the platform aims to lower barriers to AI adoption and enable rapid application development across Thai industry and public services.

title: National Programme on Artificial Intelligence
description: Slovenia’s National Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NpAI) addresses the opportunity to strengthen economic competitiveness, public service performance and societal well‑being through the development and use of trustworthy AI. It responds to challenges identified in the national context, including fragmented coordination, uneven uptake across sectors, skills gaps, limited data availability and concerns about public trust, legality and ethical use. The strategy adopts a horizontal approach across the full AI lifecycle rather than a sector‑specific model and is embedded within Slovenia’s wider digital and development policy framework. The strategy is structured around ten strategic axes: building a dynamic AI ecosystem; education and human resources; research and innovation; deployment of reference AI solutions; establishment of technical infrastructure; strengthening security through AI; increasing public confidence; ensuring an appropriate legal and ethical framework; international cooperation; and the creation of a national AI observatory. These axes translate into policy priorities focused on ethical and trustworthy AI, data and computing capacity, human‑centric deployment, and alignment with European initiatives. Identified weaknesses include insufficient coordination, shortages of skilled professionals, limited investment levels and uneven access to high‑quality data, which the strategy seeks to address through coordinated governance, investment and monitoring. Slovenia builds on recognised strengths, including more than four decades of AI research, established centres of excellence in universities and research institutes, and strong capabilities in language technologies, high‑performance computing and international cooperation. The strategy focuses on six priority areas with high expected impact: health, Industry 4.0, language technologies and cultural identity, public administration, sustainable food and agriculture, and the environment and spatial planning. Measures include support for research and innovation projects, development of data spaces and supercomputing infrastructure, and reference deployments to accelerate adoption by both the public and private sectors. Governance is ensured through an interministerial coordination structure led by the Ministry responsible for digital transformation, with participation from research institutions, industry, public authorities and civil society. The strategy places explicit emphasis on ethics, legality, human rights and safety, including requirements for privacy, transparency, accountability and human oversight. Expected outcomes include increased investment in AI, wider uptake across priority sectors, improved skills and education provision, strengthened public trust, and enhanced international visibility of Slovenian AI competences, with monitoring and renewal foreseen beyond the initial 2021–2026 period.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap (AI‑Rmap)
description: Malaysia’s National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap (AI‑Rmap) sets out a national approach for the development and application of artificial intelligence over the period 2021 to 2025. The strategy is intended to guide and coordinate national AI efforts by providing a shared direction for government, academia, industry and society. title: AI Centre Lipik
description: The AI Centre Lipik, founded by the Lipik Development and Touristic Agency (LIRA d.o.o.) in 2020, consists of an Education Centre and a Startup Incubator. The Education Centre runs a six-month AI programmer training programme involving both theory and hands-on practice, offering over 1,000 hours of teaching, with stipends and living support for participants. After completion, successful graduates are offered employment or support in starting their own business. The Startup Incubator is designed to help new and emerging companies working in AI and programming. It offers mentoring, business training, consulting, and access to infrastructure. As of the latest data, about 15 startups have been incubated in Lipik, employing several dozen people. The centre is also expanding its entrepreneurial modules, accelerator, and lab facilities. AI Centre Lipik is part of the AI & Gaming EDIH network (European Digital Innovation Hub) focused on helping SMEs, the public sector, and startups adopt digital technologies like AI, gamification, blockchain, and IoT. It offers services like “test-before-invest,” training, consulting, networking, and business support.

title: Datalabs
description: Since 2021, the German government has established Data Labs (Datenlabore) to enhance the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven decision-making within federal administration. The initiative addresses the need for specialised expertise in data science and AI to modernise administrative processes and improve the quality and efficiency of public services. The primary objective of the Data Labs is to recruit experts from academia, civil society, and the private sector who collaborate with government agencies to develop and implement AI-driven solutions. These experts support the federal administration in exploring innovative approaches to data analysis, predictive modelling, and AI application, ensuring that new technologies are effectively integrated into everyday public sector operations. The Data Labs provide a structured environment to test and prototype AI solutions, allowing ministries to assess feasibility, impact, and scalability before wider deployment. By fostering experimentation, knowledge exchange, and interdisciplinary collaboration, the labs help ensure that AI adoption is both responsible and results-oriented.

title: AI virtual assistant/chatbot network
description: The AI Virtual Assistant/Chatbot Network is a Latvian government initiative designed to centralise and streamline public access to information across multiple government websites. The platform addresses the challenge of fragmented digital services by providing a unified interface through which citizens and businesses can interact with public authorities, improving the efficiency and accessibility of online government services. A core objective of the initiative is to ensure compliance with accessibility requirements under Directive 2016/2102, enabling equal access to information for all users, including those with disabilities. By integrating AI-powered virtual assistants and chatbots, the platform can respond to queries efficiently, provide consistent information, and support user navigation across government websites. The initiative unites 55 public authorities into a single content management system, allowing for centralised administration and maintenance of web resources. This approach not only reduces operational costs and redundancies but also promotes standardisation of content and improves the overall quality and reliability of online public information.

title: InvestEU Guarantee Programme
description: The InvestEU Guarantee Programme is a major financial initiative designed to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Europe, including Bulgaria, in pursuing innovation and digital transformation. The programme addresses a critical challenge faced by many Bulgarian companies — limited access to financing for high-risk, technology-driven projects, including those involving artificial intelligence (AI). Under the InvestEU framework, Bulgarian businesses can access loans of up to EUR 2 million to develop and implement projects that integrate innovative and digital technologies. By providing a financial guarantee, the programme helps reduce investment risks for lenders, making it easier for companies to secure funding for activities that advance technological capacity and competitiveness. A key focus of the initiative is to promote the adoption of AI technologies in business operations, from process automation and data analytics to the creation of AI-based products and services. The InvestEU Guarantee Programme thus supports Bulgaria’s broader goals of digitalisation and innovation, contributing to the development of a resilient and future-ready business ecosystem.

title: RAIT - Radiological AI test center
description: The Radiological Artificial Intelligence Test center (RAIT) combines the experience of the Innovation unit at the radiology department at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital with the radiological Research group at Frederiksberg and Bispebjerg Hospital. With the unique combination of skills and data across the hospitals, RAIT aspires to establish a collective knowledge and competence center for developing, validating, and implementing AI applications in medical radiological imaging in the Capital Region of Denmark. With the joint forces, we seek to move barriers, standardize processes, and generate excellent best practices for validating and implementing AI in Radiology to generate equal health for all. RAIT consists of several AI-projects and a joint project office across Bispebjerg and Herlev Hospital. We ensure that good practice is shared and obstacles common to AI projects are identified and handled, fostering the future way for AI projects. Furthermore, we work in close collaboration with our partners, clinicians, national and international companies, universities, ministries etc. and support a non-competitive environment.

title: smart oversight (Subnational: Valle del Cauca)
description: The initiative was conducted by the Governor’s Office of Valle del Cauca through the analysis of a large administrative dataset obtained from DIAN, the Colombian Tax and Customs Authority, comprising 686,215 records. This work is based on the analysis of a large administrative dataset obtained from the DIAN (Colombian Tax and Customs Authority), comprising 686,215 records. The data originate from official tax reports, including: the Annual Simple Alternative Minimum Tax Return (IMAS) for self-employed individuals, the Annual Alternative Minimum Tax Return for employees (IMAS), the Declaration of Income and Complementary Taxes for resident natural and assimilated persons and resident liquid successions, as well as the Declaration of Income, Supplemental Income or Wealth for legal and assimilated persons, non-resident natural and assimilated persons, and non-resident liquid successions. The analytical procedures applied to the DIAN database and to the Chambers of Commerce datasets were conducted separately during 2018, ensuring methodological independence and robustness. The evidence obtained and the proposed methodological framework are highly relevant for the design and implementation of algorithm-based public policies, particularly those aimed at improving the targeting, prioritisation, and effectiveness of tax auditing and fiscal control processes. Results, outcomes and impacts As a result of this initiative, 1,000 companies that evaded or failed to pay departmental taxes were detected.

title: 060 WebChat. AI‑based Citizen Assistance Service
description: It seeks to address common issues in citizen services, such as long waiting times, the saturation of traditional channels (telephone or offices), and the difficulty of accessing clear and up‑to‑date information on public procedures and services. It offers a 24/7 conversational channel that allows citizens to access information autonomously, instantly, and from any device, reducing the volume of repetitive enquiries handled by human agents and improving the overall experience. Originally, it enabled access to the 060 citizen assistance service of the General State Administration (AGE) for citizens residing outside Spain, as they were unable to access it through the national short‑code number. The main objectives are to facilitate access to public information, improve the efficiency of citizen services, and optimise the Administration’s resources through the automation of frequent queries. It also aims to provide a coherent experience aligned with the 060 service, ensure compliance with data protection regulations, and allow complex enquiries to be escalated to human agents when necessary, combining automation with personalised assistance. It is based on a modular and scalable architecture, which facilitates its maintenance, expansion, and consolidation within the Administration’s digital services. It has the capability to extend the assistant to new channels, such as WhatsApp. In addition, the traceability of conversations enables continuous improvement of the model by refining intents, responses, and conversational flows. Results, outcomes and impacts To date, the initiative has served to alleviate pressure on traditional in-person and telephone channels. The figure of 150,000 annual conversations indicates substantial use, but the impacts extend well beyond mere volume. The assistant has enabled citizens to resolve enquiries outside of standard office hours (8:00 AM to 7:00 PM), reducing demand during peak telephone periods. At the end of each conversation, the user is asked for a rating (usually from 1 to 5 stars). This learning process will support the development of new services, such as the “060 Bot”, which will further enhance usability, accuracy rates, and the overall contribution to the digitalisation strategy for accessing public information.

title: Ethical Principles for Promoting National Artificial Intelligence Projects of NIA
description: As AI-based products and services rapidly proliferated across the public sector, the importance of ethical standards to be observed during the implementation of national AI projects was continuously raised. However, specific and systematic ethical principles that could be directly applied in the field were insufficient. Consequently, the National Information Society Agency (NIA) established the ‘Ethical Principles for National AI Project Implementation’ to strengthen the accountability and reliability of AI projects within the public sector. These principles were formulated based on common values derived from an analysis of 25 major domestic and international AI ethical standards and guidelines. They comprehensively reflect key elements such as fairness and non-discrimination, transparency and explainability, safety and security, personal data protection, accountability, and the promotion of human values. Notably, the national AI project implementation process is divided into three stages—Planning, Execution, and Expansion—with core values and detailed ethical principles systematically presented for each stage to provide a standard applicable throughout the entire project lifecycle. Furthermore, these ethical principles were implemented to ensure they were not merely declaratory but practically applicable to actual project implementation. Awareness among all employees was raised through declaration ceremonies and internal dissemination activities. External expansion was also pursued through various channels, such as publishing the principles on the official NIA website and reflecting them in standard Request for Proposal (RFP) templates. Through this initiative, a foundation has been established for the systematic adoption of ethical standards across public sector AI projects, contributing to the enhancement of accountability and public interest throughout the project implementation process. Results, outcomes and impacts Through this initiative, ethical standards for national AI projects were systematically established, creating a common framework for public sector AI. The principles were embedded in NIA’s internal processes and standard RFP templates, guiding project planning and operation. According to the submitting institution, awareness of ethical considerations across the project lifecycle has increased, strengthening accountability and transparency. Ongoing dissemination has expanded their application, laying a solid foundation for future policy development and AI project implementation.

title: Detecting tax evasion using artificial intelligence
description: The initiative focuses on the application of artificial intelligence and big data analytics to improve the detection of tax evasion and strengthen risk-based personal income tax compliance in Serbia. It addresses the challenge faced by tax administrations of limited human resources and growing volumes of complex data by shifting from predominantly random inspections to targeted, evidence-based audit selection. The project responds to the need for more efficient use of enforcement capacities by analysing large datasets available to the Serbian Tax Administration and identifying atypical taxpayer behaviour that may indicate increased risk of non-compliance. Through the development of algorithms and analytical models, the initiative supports the early detection of deviations from expected patterns, enabling inspectors to focus on cases with the highest risk and potential fiscal impact. The primary objectives of the initiative are to enhance the effectiveness of tax audits, increase voluntary compliance, and improve revenue collection outcomes while reducing the administrative burden on both the tax authority and compliant taxpayers. By strengthening analytical capabilities, the project aims to support more consistent, transparent, and data-driven decision-making in tax administration, contributing to greater public trust and integrity in the tax system. The initiative has already demonstrated strong and tangible results, substantially improving audit targeting and efficiency by generating higher newly identified revenues with fewer field inspections. In the longer term, the initiative supports the broader modernisation of the Serbian Tax Administration and aligns with strategic objectives to adopt innovative technologies in public financial management. It also provides a scalable and replicable approach that can be extended to other tax types and compliance areas, reinforcing evidence-based policymaking and the sustainable use of artificial intelligence in the public sector.

title: DX Investment Promotion Tax Incentive
description: The DX Investment Promotion Tax System (DX投資促進税制) was introduced in the FY2022 tax reform, effective from 2 August 2021, and has subsequently been revised and extended. It applies to companies that have obtained 'DX Certification' from METI and have a business plan certified under the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act (ICEA) that sets out investments in cloud services, AI systems, and digital infrastructure to achieve digital transformation across the enterprise. Eligible companies may choose between: a 5% tax credit on qualifying investment costs; or a 30% special depreciation allowance on qualifying assets. The tax credit is subject to a ceiling of 20% of annual corporate tax liability (bundled with the Carbon Neutrality investment credit). Eligible investments include: cloud computing migrations; enterprise AI system deployments; DX-related software and data infrastructure; and digital platform integration. The 2025 Tax Reform Act extended the regime by three years, to fiscal years beginning on or before 1 April 2028, while increasing the minimum qualifying investment size from JPY 20M to JPY 100M, and reducing the special depreciation rate for machinery and equipment from 40% to 35%. The programme is designed to incentivise large-scale, cross-departmental digital transformation rather than point-solution technology adoption.

title: NHR Alliance (National High Performance Computing)
description: The National High-Performance Computing Alliance (Nationales Hochleistungsrechnen, NHR) was established in 2020 as Germany's integrated national HPC infrastructure strategy, replacing the previous Gauss Centre for Supercomputing structure with a broader, application-oriented network. The NHR consists of 9 centres across German universities and research institutions (including ZIH Dresden, PC² Paderborn, NHR@KIT Karlsruhe, HLRS Stuttgart, LRZ Munich, Göttingen, Darmstadt, FAU Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Berlin), each specialising in particular application domains. Total federal funding is approximately EUR 62.5M per year (split equally between the Federal Government and the Länder). Centres provide CPU and GPU compute resources, storage, application support, training and education (including for AI/ML workloads), and consulting services for researchers and, to an increasing degree, for industry. The NHR supports AI training, inference, and simulation workloads and is increasingly aligned with BMFTR's AI compute infrastructure strategy. NHR centres also contribute to pan-European HPC initiatives through EuroHPC Joint Undertaking. Target audience: German academic researchers, public research institutions, and increasingly industrial R&D teams.

The National High-Performance Computing Alliance (Nationales Hochleistungsrechnen, NHR) was established in 2020 as Germany's integrated national HPC infrastructure strategy, replacing the previous Gauss Centre for Supercomputing structure with a broader, application-oriented network. The NHR consists of 9 centres across German universities and research institutions (including ZIH Dresden, PC² Paderborn, NHR@KIT Karlsruhe, HLRS Stuttgart, LRZ Munich, Göttingen, Darmstadt, FAU Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Berlin), each specialising in particular application domains. Total federal funding is approximately EUR 62.5M per year (split equally between the Federal Government and the Länder). Centres provide CPU and GPU compute resources, storage, application support, training and education (including for AI/ML workloads), and consulting services for researchers and, to an increasing degree, for industry. The NHR supports AI training, inference, and simulation workloads and is increasingly aligned with BMFTR's AI compute infrastructure strategy. NHR centres also contribute to pan-European HPC initiatives through EuroHPC Joint Undertaking. title: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence
description: From 19 February to 14 June 2020, citizens and stakeholders shared their opinions on the forthcoming policy and regulatory measures regarding artificial intelligence (AI). The European Commission aimed to encourage the adoption of AI while simultaneously addressing the associated risks by proposing a White Paper outlining policy and regulatory options for creating an "ecosystem for excellence and trust." This document was released on 19 February 2020, alongside an online survey that focused on three key areas:- Specific initiatives to support, develop, and promote AI across the EU economy and public administration.- Potential regulatory frameworks for AI in the future.- Safety and liability considerations related to AI.This report presents a "future regulatory framework" for the EU to navigate the evolving landscape of AI technology. It adopts a comprehensive approach, suggesting methods to make AI accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and addressing appropriate regulations for high-risk applications and liability in cases of physical or material harm.- The proposed "Ecosystem of Excellence" highlights the necessity of collaboration with member states to invest in AI research and development. Education should enhance AI-related skills and incorporate ethical training. Facilitating access to AI technology for SMEs will accelerate its development and adoption. The private sector should play a role in the research and innovation agenda, particularly through significant public-private partnerships. The White Paper identifies healthcare and transportation as sectors poised to benefit from AI-driven products. Investments should focus on ensuring access to data and computing infrastructure. Additionally, there should be international collaboration among global AI stakeholders to promote EU standards and create a "level playing field."- The "ecosystem of trust" encompasses: (1) human agency and oversight, (2) technical robustness and safety, (3) privacy and data governance, (4) transparency, (5) diversity, non-discrimination, and fairness, (6) societal and environmental well-being, and (7) accountability.- Legislative Updates- Current legislation must be revised to account for AI. The integration of AI technologies into products and services may introduce new safety risks for users. Issues in AI design may arise from the quality and availability of data or other challenges related to machine learning. While some risks are not exclusive to AI-dependent products and services, the use of AI may exacerbate these risks. A lack of clear safety regulations addressing these concerns could lead to legal uncertainty for businesses in the EU that market AI-related products.

description: The government of Colombia acknowledges that the implementation and deployment of AI cannot be achieved by the government alone. title: Data Sandbox Platform
description: Through the CONPES No. 3920 of 2018 (National Data Exploitation Policy - Big Data), action number seven, the Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications, along with the National Planning Department, will, in December of 2021, will provide a collaborative space (data sandbox) in which the data sets used and generated during the advanced projects, as well as the documentation of the processes and its result, are published in a work environment that allows its public use. The previously mentioned document, states that the Data Sandbox must allow the testing of standards and the collaboration of public and private actors, academia, and civil society. Additionally, this space will facilitate the coordination between entities to join efforts in the implementation of projects using Analytics, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for common issues in accordance with their capabilities and interests. This will allow to boost the implementation of analytics projects and institutional implementation.The initiative has the following objectives:Search within the Data Sandbox, among different users from the same entity, datasets in a collaborative and interactive manner.Store and process structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data through the use of Big Data technologies.Make available to the country's public entities, a collaborative space (Data Sandbox) for the implementation of pilot projects of Analytics and Big Data, prior to compliance with the terms and conditions of use of the Data Sandbox and the current capacity to maintain the pilot projects.Provide, for state entities, an experimental and iterative environment for solution testing and evaluation of Big Data technologies.Provide a collaborative space that allows public entities to share data, documentation, algorithms, and other results of pilot projects regarding Analytics and Big Data in the public sector.

title: Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Colombia
description: This framework was conceived and described in the Colombian AI Strategy (Conpes 3975, 2019). The Strategy highlighted the importance of developing a series or principles that shoud guide the design, implementation and development of AI in Colombia. Additionally, the ethical framework answers to a new direction in the regulatory process, especially in the regulation of emerging technologies. This strategy has been designed by the National Advisor for Digital Transformation, Victor Munoz. The purpose of the Colombian government is to develop a regulation that is evidence-based. The ethical framework allows the country to address ethical challenges while collecting evidence that allows Colombian authorities to consider a regulatory framework in the future and only in those specific cases in which the regulation seems to be required. To promote the discussion on the ethics of artificial intelligence and its implementation in Colombia, the Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Colombia was launched for discussion. There have been 6 discussion tables on the latter led by the Berkman Klein Center from Harvard University, the Development Bank of Latin America (CAF) and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). A total of more than 50 national and international contributors participated in these roundtables. Participants included Unicef, the World Economic Forum, Oxford University, the Council of Europe, the OECD and members of the European Parliament.https://inteligenciaartificial.gov.co/en/roundtables/The final document was launched on October 12, 2021.The initiative has the following objectives:To address ethical challenges posed by the design, implementation and deployment of AI systems.To provide principles that must guide the ethical use of data in the public sector.To create a culture of digital transformation in Colombia that values ethical principles and social good.To increase knowledge about this technology its benefits and risks among public servants.To motivate the private sector to increase its efforts in developing ethical codes of conduct and other strategies to reduce ethical risks in the design and implementation of this technology in Colombia.To implement the recommendations of the OECD on this subject.

title: Building a Regulatory Ecosystem for AI
description: The main purpose is to have an innovative approach towards the design of regulations applicable to AI systems. The Colombian government has designed a specific model to develop the first regulatory sandbox for AI in the region, that is expected to be implemented in 2021. Additionally, to address some of the risks posed by AI systems, the Colombian government has elaborated an AI ethical framework. This framework describes a series of principles applicable to AI systems such as accountability, transparency and explainability, amongst others. The initiative has the following objectives:To reduce information asymmetry within regulatory bodies, regarding AI systems features and main functionality.To provide a flexible regulatory framework for the deployment of the latest AI systems bening developed.To increase collaboration between Colombian regulators and private entitites, building trust amongst different stakeholders.To identify with precisions the risks generated by the implementation and deployment of AI systems in Colombia, consequently define the principles and ethical responses to such risks.To promote cost benefit analysis in the design of regulatory framework for AI systems.

title: AI 4.0
description: The programme and its networks have taken Finland towards the age of artificial intelligence through the following 11 key actions:Enhance business competitiveness through the use of AIEffectively utilise data in all sectorsEnsure that AI can be adopted more quickly and easilyEnsure top-level expertise and attract top expertsMake bold decisions and investmentsBuild the world's best public servicesEstablish new models for collaborationMake Finland a frontrunner in the age of AIPrepare for artificial intelligence to change the nature of workSteer AI development into a trust-based, human-centric directionPrepare for security challengesDuring Autumn 2021, the programme's thematic sub-groups have, together with stakeholders, specified the objectives and defined the key results as well as the measures and indicators required by them. This interim report compiles the results of the work of the sub-groups and four proposals for achieving the vision of Finland as a winner in the dual transition in 2030.The program is based on the results of the previous AI initiative and aims to promote the implementation of Artificial Intelligence as part of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, while also endorsing the new skills demanded during this digital transition. The aim is to respond to the specific challenges regarding digitalisation in Finland, such as the relatively low levels of investments in digital, the moderate re-generation of value creation in small or medium sized enterprises as well as the need for strategic leadership in the fourth industrial revolution. The program bases on the results of the AI Finland “program and aims to promote the implementation of Artificial Intelligence as part of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, while also endorsing the new skills demanded during this digital transition.In the Artificial Intelligence 4.0 program, AI technology is combined with a wide range of other digital technologies such as IoT (Internet of things), 3D-printing, robotics, quantum computing as well as the virtual and augmented reality. Together, these digital technologies enable change in the general functioning and practice of businesses, regenerate value creation, enable the detection of societal challenges and encourage sustainable growth.

title: Financing of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Technologies
description: The development of foundational technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain and the convergence with other key technologies like IoT is going to accelerate the digital transformation of industry and services. They will provide new opportunities to innovate, create new ventures and to invest in technologies and applications that will deeply change the existing business models. The support program will be critical for the successful implementation of this first EU-wide Deep Tech Investment Fund specifically focused on the development and acceleration of Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, Distributed Ledger technologies and the Convergence of these technologies.The initiative has the following objectives:As part of this Investment support program, the European Commission is aiming to: (i) to enhance the awareness and visibility of innovative AI and Blockchain companies and projects with financial intermediaries and the broader investment community; (ii) to carry out a series of market consultations with a broad range of stakeholders from the AI/blockchain ecosystem, Governments and private investors, (iii) to convene and to better link the investment community with innovative Blockchain/AI SME and startups (iv) support the portfolio development and originate a deal flow of technically and financially viable projects; and(v) to mobilise more investors and to facilitate cooperation schemes by contributing to the creation and optimal operation of an EU-wide Deep Tech Investment Program, with a focus on AI, Blockchain and the Convergence of technologies.

title: Juri Reports on "Making AI European"
description: In early October 2020, the Legal Affairs Committee of the European Parliament (JURI) approved three reports related to artificial intelligence (AI). These reports address (i) an ethical framework for AI, (ii) civil liability for AI-related damages, and (iii) the safeguarding of intellectual property rights concerning AI.1. The first report proposes an ethical framework for AI, aimed at establishing foundational ethical principles for the development, use, and deployment of AI within the EU. The guiding principles closely align with those outlined in the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, emphasizing safety, transparency, accountability, protection against bias and discrimination, the right to redress, social and environmental responsibility, and respect for fundamental rights. The report advocates for the European Commission to create a comprehensive and adaptable legal framework of ethical principles governing AI, robotics, and related technologies including software, algorithms, and data across the Union. It also suggests that the Commission incorporate various guiding principles for high-risk AI and related technologies into upcoming legislation, such as human oversight, transparency, accountability, non-bias, social responsibility, gender equality, environmental sustainability, and privacy considerations. Furthermore, EU law should impose specific requirements on high-risk technologies that could significantly harm individuals or violate EU fundamental rights and safety regulations. The Commission is encouraged to develop common guidance and compile a list of high-risk sectors (e.g., employment, healthcare) and high-risk applications (e.g., recruitment, automated driving, electoral processes) to identify AI technologies that require compliance assessments. The Parliament proposes that national authorities issue a European certificate of ethical compliance for technologies that meet these guiding principles, particularly regarding safety and the right to redress.2. The second report addresses liability for AI-induced damage, focusing on civil liability claims related to AI systems (led by MEP Axel Voss). This report recommends the establishment of a uniform and harmonized legal framework for civil liability claims, which would include a new regulation identifying high-risk AI systems and the critical sectors in which they operate. The Commission, with assistance from the standing Technical Committee for high-risk AI systems, should review and update this list every six months, potentially through a delegated act. The report suggests that operators of high-risk AI systems should be held strictly liable for any harm or damage resulting from activities, devices, or processes driven by those AI systems and should be required to maintain mandatory insurance coverage.

title: The Robustness and Explainability of Artificial Intelligence
description: This report puts forward several policy-related considerations for the attention of policy makers to establish a set of standardisation and certification tools for AI. First, the development of methodologies to evaluate the impacts of AI on society, built on the model of the Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA) introduced in the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), is discussed. Secondly, a focus is made on the establishment of methodologies to assess the robustness of systems that would be adapted to the context of use. This would come along with the identification of known vulnerabilities of AI systems, and the technical solutions that have been proposed in the scientific community to address them. Finally, the promotion of transparency systems in sensitive systems is discussed, through the implementation of explainability-by-design approaches in AI components that would provide guarantee of the respect of the fundamental rights.The initiative has the following objectives:To contribute to this movement for the establishment of a sound regulatory framework for AI, by making the connection between the principles embodied in current regulations regarding to the cybersecurity of digital systems and the protection of data, the policy activities concerning AI, and the technical discussions within the scientific community of AI, in particular in the field of machine learning, that is largely at the origin of the recent advancements of this technology.

title: AI Task Force
description: The Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic (DAPRE), in response to the technical assistance provided by the Multilateral Bank, has decided to work towards a greater dynamization of AI governance in the country. The Government of Colombia has positioned itself as a regional and global leader in the construction of a public policy on Artificial Intelligence. Thus, the need has arisen to achieve an adequate implementation of the initiatives that have been developed and that meet these expectations. To this end, and with the objective of reinforcing the commitment assumed in the framework of the technical assistance provided on the subject, the technical design of a Project exclusively dedicated to this purpose has been proposed. This is part of an effort to institutionalize the artificial intelligence policy and give it a long-term scope, within the framework of the functions of the Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic, aimed at providing guidelines for the evaluation, formulation and implementation of public policies, AI being one of the strategic sectors to be promoted by the government.The initiative has the following objectives:To define mechanisms and tools to accelerate the implementation of Colombia's AI strategy or policy and ethical framework.To monitor projects in public entities that are using AI systems to provide a more efficient and effective service to the public.To increase international cooperation and coordination with governments and international entities on AI-related topics to achieve the goals of Colombias AI strategy.To develop mechanisms to foster the access and use of data for the design and development of AI systems.To increase collaboration with the private sector and the entrepreneurship ecosystem in AI-related topics.

title: European Strategy for Data
description: The communication of this strategy outlines the place of data in society according to European values and laws in line with its vision for shaping Europe's digital future. Data is called lifeblood of economic development and seen as a key resource for social progress and green transformations (e.g. the European Green Deal). This paper also mentions the importance of data for economic development including for the advancement of AI which requires large data training sets. A current lack of data availability is identified as an impediment to AI development. The communication confirms that the Commission will invest in High Impact Projects to fund AI ecosystems related to the development of data spaces and cloud services.The initiative has the following objectives:To make sure the EU becomes a role model and a leader for a society empowered by data'.
