title: Enterprise Azerbaijan
description: Enterprise Azerbaijan is a national public initiative designed to support innovation-driven entrepreneurship and the development of technology-based solutions, including artificial intelligence applications. The initiative addresses challenges such as limited early-stage support, skills gaps, and weak co-ordination across the innovation ecosystem. It leverages the opportunity to strengthen economic diversification and productivity by helping new ideas move from concept to practical application. A core component of the initiative is the Startup School projects, which focus on supporting early-stage founders, students, and innovators at the beginning of their entrepreneurial journey. These projects respond to the need for accessible guidance and practical learning by offering structured training, mentoring, and hands-on support. Participants gain essential knowledge on problem-solving, product development, and responsible use of technology, including AI where relevant, helping them build confidence and basic market readiness. The objectives of Enterprise Azerbaijan include improving access to knowledge and collaboration, strengthening links between the public sector, academia, and business, and increasing the number of innovation-ready start-ups. Through Startup School and other programmes, the initiative supports capacity-building, investment readiness, and ecosystem development, while aligning with national priorities for innovation and digital development. Enterprise Azerbaijan is co-ordinated as a public platform and is designed to evolve through the expansion of its programmes, thematic areas, and partnerships. Startup School projects are expected to scale over time by reaching wider groups, introducing new focus areas, and strengthening international co-operation. In the long term, the initiative aims to become an institutionalised entry point into the national innovation ecosystem, supporting sustainable growth and responsible adoption of emerging technologies. Results, outcomes and impacts The Startup School initiative has delivered measurable results by supporting early-stage start-ups and strengthening cross-border collaboration. Since 2023, three editions have been implemented, attracting over 200 project applications from multiple countries, with more than 30 start-ups completing acceleration cycles. Results are measured through application data, participation rates, selection outcomes, mentoring completion, Demo Day performance, and awards received. Expected future impacts include scaling green and digital start-ups, expanding regional co-operation, increasing investment readiness, and integrating more start-ups into the national and international innovation ecosystem.

title: Integrated Innovation Strategy
description: Japan’s Integrated Innovation Strategy is an annual, Cabinet‑level plan published every year since 2018. It was created to replace the earlier Science and Technology Innovation Comprehensive Strategy (2013–2017) after the government determined that past approaches were insufficient for global competitiveness. The reform introduced a continuous, end‑to‑end innovation strategy—spanning basic research through social implementation—coordinated by the Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (CSTI) within the Cabinet Office. Eight editions have been issued to date (2018–2025), each approved by formal Cabinet decision. The 2018–2020 editions implemented the 5th Science and Technology Innovation (STI) Basic Plan, while the 2021–2025 editions function as annual implementation plans under the 6th Basic Plan. Each annual edition is structured around three consistent pillars that have evolved over time: the strategic promotion of advanced science and technologies; strengthening the knowledge base and human resource development; and the creation of innovation ecosystems. The first pillar covers priority technologies such as AI, quantum, biotechnology, materials science, fusion energy, and semiconductors. The second includes measures such as the 10‑trillion‑yen university endowment fund to enhance research capacity. The third focuses on expanding startup support and mobilising public–private R&D investment. Artificial intelligence has been a central theme across all editions, with emphasis intensifying in recent years. The 2024–2025 strategies incorporated the AI Promotion Act, economic security considerations, and international governance cooperation through the Hiroshima AI Process. title: Estishraf
description: Over recent years, SDAIA led national efforts to centralise government data through the National Data Bank (NDB), creating a unified platform for secure data sharing and integration across public-sector entities. This provides access to large volumes of administrative, economic and sectoral data from multiple systems. Estishraf was established to leverage this foundation, applying artificial intelligence and advanced analytics to transform integrated datasets into actionable insights that support evidence-based policymaking and strategic planning. Estishraf enables government entities to analyse integrated public-sector data and apply AI for complex policy analysis. Machine learning models and advanced methods detect patterns, forecast socio-economic trends, evaluate policy impacts and simulate alternative scenarios before implementation. Policymakers can examine cross-sector relationships spanning education, labour markets, transportation, housing and industry within a unified analytical environment. Workflows that previously required extensive manual effort are now executed rapidly on integrated national data, allowing faster responses to policy questions and significantly improving productivity and analytical depth. Since its establishment, Estishraf has supported more than 1.9k analytical projects across sectors. It also strengthens government analytical capacity by providing an advanced environment where data scientists, economists and policy analysts work with integrated datasets and modern infrastructure. Access to large-scale, cross-sectoral data and sophisticated tools supports attracting and retaining highly specialised talent in AI and data science. Illustrative AI applications include using machine learning on national traffic safety data to identify high-risk locations, contributing to a reduction in road fatalities of over 60% compared to 2016 levels, lowering mortality from 28.8 to below 10 per 100,000. Computer vision models analyse street-level imagery to detect and monitor visual pollution, enabling municipalities to identify violations and improve urban environments. In housing, machine learning clustering models applied to real estate, demographic and purchasing power data segment markets and estimate idle land supply, supporting policy simulation and calibration of the Idle Land Program. Additional analyses link education outcomes with employment and wage data to identify labour-market skill gaps. Estishraf demonstrates how governments can translate data and artificial intelligence into a practical national capability for policy analysis and strategic foresight.

title: farmpredict
description: farmpredict was created to support the Australian Government’s efforts to improve drought preparedness and response. Its objectives are to provide timely, forward-looking and geographically detailed information about the effects of drought and other events on the Australian farm sector. This includes the ability to model non-drought events and counterfactual scenarios that can explore impacts of possible future events or policy decisions. farmpredict predictions have been achieved by combining historical weather data, seasonal forecasts and climate data with agricultural models to generate ‘outcome-based’ indicators for specific agricultural impacts such as crop yields, pasture growth and farm business outcomes. This can be generated at a variety of spatial levels from national to individual farms. Currently DAFF is collaborating with the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) to implement farmpredict as the “engine” in the Australian Agricultural Drought Indicators (AADI), which will provide predictions across Australia at high resolution with an interface designed to support decision-makers. At present farmpredict only supports modelling for broadacre farming. Another expected evolution for the project is to improve model performance and accuracy and to expand the model to include other agricultural sectors (such as dairy farming).

title: Innovative Solutions Canada (ISC)
description: Launched in 2018 (merging the former Build in Canada Innovation Program and ISC predecessor programmes) and administered by ISED, Innovative Solutions Canada uses the federal government's buying power as a first purchaser of pre-commercial Canadian technology. The programme operates through two streams: (1) Challenge Stream — government departments and agencies post real operational challenges (including AI challenges for workflow automation, decision support, and process improvement); eligible Canadian SMEs with fewer than 500 FTE employees apply and can receive up to CAD 150,000 for a Phase 1 proof-of-feasibility (up to 6 months) and up to CAD 1M for Phase 2 prototype development (up to 2 years); and (2) Testing Stream — departments post solicitations for late-stage pre-commercial prototypes for operational testing; successful innovators receive contracts for testing in live government environments. Upon successful testing or prototype completion, eligible SMEs access the Pathway to Commercialization, enabling non-competitive government procurement contracts of up to CAD 8M per contract over three years. As of 2024, ISC had awarded over 960 contracts worth over CAD 446M across both streams. ISED's AI-specific challenge solicitation (EN578-25ISC2) targets AI and robotic process automation (RPA) solutions for government servic delivery. The programme is aligned with the Government of Canada's AI Strategy for the Federal Public Service and Treasury Board Secretariat (TBS) digital procurement policy.

title: Scale AI Supercluster (Supply Chains and Logistics Excellence AI)
description: Originally selected in February 2018 as one of five Innovation Superclusters under the Innovation Superclusters Initiative (ISI), Scale AI is an independent, industry-led not-for-profit funded by ISED. It operates under the Global Innovation Clusters (GIC) programme (renamed from ISI in 2022), which received an additional CAD 750M in Budget 2022 for the clusters collectively, plus CAD 125M from the second phase of the Pan-Canadian AI Strategy (2022) to accelerate AI commercialisation. Scale AI's total federal funding envelope is approximately CAD 284M over the programme period. Scale AI funds two categories of projects: (1) Industry-led collaborative projects for AI adoption in supply chains — companies can access up to 40% of eligible costs (up to 50% for projects in Québec), with no prescribed minimum or maximum per project; projects must have a minimum budget of CAD 1M and must involve at least one Canadian SME; and (2) Workforce training grants — refunding up to 85% of eligible costs for AI and digital intelligence training programmes designed by businesses. Eligible sectors include supply chain operators and AI solutions providers in retail, manufacturing, transportation, logistics, ICT, and critical infrastructure. Scale AI has funded hundreds of projects across Canada and has attracted over 8,000 members and 2,465+ project partners, with CAD 2.37B+ co-invested with industry across the five clusters since 2018.

title: NSF SBIR/STTR – AI Topic
description: Part of NSF's 'America's Seed Fund', the SBIR/STTR programme has funded AI-focused startups since the 1980s, with AI formalised as a dedicated topic area. Phase I awards (up to USD 305,000 for up to 12 months) support feasibility and proof-of-concept work; Phase II awards (up to USD 1,250,000 for up to 24 months) fund continued R&D and commercialisation. The AI topic covers eight subtopics including cognitive science-based technologies, computer vision, conversational and language-based AI, novel AI hardware (e.g. neuromorphic computing), sustainable AI, trustworthy AI (fair, transparent, explainable, privacy-preserving), and edge devices. Applicants must submit a Project Pitch before a full proposal; awards are non-dilutive and require all funded work to be performed in the US. A Fast-Track pilot combines Phase I and Phase II into a single application. Note: programme authorisation lapsed in late 2025, temporarily pausing new Project Pitch submissions.

title: Doctoral Graduates' Employment
description: Under the Decree 57/2016, amended by Law 57/2017, it funds a mechanism for public and private institutions integrated in the Portuguese Scientific and Technological System to hire doctoral researchers. This mechanism supports the hiring of doctoral researchers in all scientific areas through annual calls (Scientific Employment Stimulus - individual calls) as well as it supports the development of R&D institutional activities through calls directed at institutions to hire doctoral researchers (Scientific Employment Stimulus “ institutional calls).Since the Scientific Employment Stimulus entered into force, five individual calls (CEEC 2017, CEEC 2018, CEEC 2020, CEEC 2021 and CEEC 2022), and two institutional call (CEEC Institution 2018 and CEEC Institution 2021) have been issued.In these five individual calls, twenty-eight AI-oriented doctoral researchers were recommended to be granted a sixty-years contract. Doctoral researchers are funded for a period of three years according to three criteria, - i.e., the number of years holding a Ph.D., adequacy of the curriculum to the scientific area, and proof of scientific independence: junior researcher ( 2.128,34), assistant researcher ( 3.191,82), principal researcher ( 3.601,03), and coordinating researcher ( 4.664,97).The public investment in the AI-oriented doctoral researchers' employment is difficult to estimate in this exercise, due to different variables, namely the modalities of contract (directly or via institution), variable costs, and contractual changes (e.g. three contracts were terminated during the first year). However, it can be indicated the funding for 2019 ( 567 365,67) , for 2020 ( 1 163 876,43) and 2021 ( 1 229 025,46).The initiative has the following objectives:- Ensure the integration of highly qualified and international competitive scientists into research and academic centers.

title: Australia's National Enforcement Guidelines for Automated Vehicles
description: These National Enforcement Guidelines provide guidance about how the requirement of proper control in Australian Road Rule 297 should apply to vehicles with automated functions. The Guidelines also confirm that the human driver is responsible for compliance with road traffic laws when a vehicle has conditional automation engaged at a point in time.The initiative has the following objective(s):These National Enforcement Guidelines have been developed to: support road safety outcomes; be consistently adopted by all states and territories be technology-neutral; provide police with clear guidance about how Road Rule 297 and the requirement of proper control should apply to vehicles with automated functions; confirm that the human driver is responsible for complying with road traffic laws when a vehicle has conditional automation engaged at a point in time; be updated and kept relevant to ensure they reflect judicial interpretations of control, changes in legislation and developing technology; have regard to all levels of driving automation in the longer term; assist road transport agencies when considering the consequences of granting exemptions from traffic laws; and not affect current rules for drivers of non-automated vehicles.

title: Health Data Programme
description: Norway has several health registries and other sources to health data for secondary use - a unique source of knowledge about the populations health and the quality of health care services in Norway. Today, the access to our health data is time consuming and costly. A better utilisation of the health data for research, quality improvement, management, innovation and business development can bring great benefits to the society. Health analysis data platform:Access to health data for research and innovation is complicated and time consuming. (on average it takes 17 months to get access to data from more than one register). The program will establish the Health analysis data platform as a secure single entry point, aiming to coordinate register data (population based and clinical) with other relevant data sources (biobanks, cohorts, researcher data etc).The initiative has the following objectives:To increase the utilisation of health data for secondary use in research, quality improvement, management, innovation and business development by introducing a Health analysis data platform, and a national permit authority (Health data service).

The next transformation is turning electronics hardware and software intelligent, radically changing their relationships with human "wetware". While there is a strong consensus that Artificial Intelligence will be a game-changer and a key factor in economic development, there is a concurrent need to arrive at frameworks that will promote its deployment taking all social factors into account. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry has set up this Task force on Artificial Intelligence to kick-start the use of AI for India's economic transformation.

title: National Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical and Health Research Involving Human Participants
description: Research on human participants pertains to a broad range of scientific enquiry aimed at developing generalizable knowledge that improves health, increases understanding of disease and is ethically justified by its social value. Every research has some inherent risks and probabilities of harm or inconvenience to participants/communities. Therefore, protection of participants should be built into the design of the study. Do no harm (non-maleficence) has been the underlying universal principle guiding health care in all systems of medicine around the world. While conducting biomedical and health research, the four basic ethical principles namely; respect for persons (autonomy), beneficence, non-maleficence and justice have been enunciated for protecting the dignity, rights, safety and well-being of research participants. These four basic principles have been expanded into 12 general principles described in the guidance document, and those are to be applied to all biomedical, social and behavioural science research for health involving human participants, their biological material and data.The purpose of such research should be:i. directed towards enhancing knowledge about the human condition while maintaining sensitivity to the Indian cultural, social and natural environment;ii. conducted under conditions such that no person or persons become mere means for the betterment of others and that human beings who are participating in any biomedical and/or health research or scientific experimentation are dealt with in a manner conducive to and consistent with their dignity and well-being, under conditions of professional fair treatment and transparency; andiii. subjected to a regime of evaluation at all stages of the research, such as design, conduct and reporting of the results thereof.

title: Innovation Superclusters Initiative
description: The ISI was launched as part of the Innovation and Skills Plan to accelerate the development and growth of business-led innovation superclusters that will create new commercial and global opportunities for Canadian firms in fast-growing areas such as AI, advanced manufacturing, and clean technology. Through the ISI, the government will provide non-repayable contributions to industry-led, non-profit entities with ambitious proposals that build a competitive advantage for Canadian firms.The ISI will support five themes of activity:1. Creating technology leadership by supporting collaborative R&D or demonstration projects that enhance productivity, performance and competitiveness of member firms.2. Creating partnerships for scale by increasing demand for cluster products, linking SMEs with large firms, and supporting integration into global supply chains.3. Creating a diverse and skilled workforce by addressing industry needs for talent.4. Creating access to innovation by investing in and providing access to assets, services, or resources that benefit a range of cluster firms over a period of time.5. Creating global advantage by enabling firms to seize market opportunities and attract international investments and partnerships.The initiative has the following objectives:To build a shared competitive advantage for their cluster that attracts cutting-edge research, investment and talent by addressing gaps, aligning strengths, enhancing attributes, and positioning it as a world-leading innovation hotbed.To increase business expenditures on research and development (R&D) and advance a range of business-led innovation and technology leadership activities that will address important industrial challenges, boost productivity, performance and competiveness for Canadas sectors of economic strength.To generate new companies, and commercialize new products, processes and services that position firms to scale, connect to global supply chains, transition to high-value activities and become global market leaders; andTo foster a critical mass of growth-oriented firms, and strengthen collaborations between private, academic and public sector organizations pursuing private-sector led innovation and commercial opportunities to enhance the clusters pool of resources, capabilities and knowledge.

title: Joint R&D Project
description: In 2019 Innoviris launched a new Joint R&D project call focusing on predictive medicine. This call is coherent with our focus on health as one of our three major priorities in the Regional Innovation Plan. Thanks to the progress made on medical imagery and biotechnology, there is a possibility to move further on medicine. The long term goal is to move from therapeutic medicine to predictive medicine in order to put in place prevention strategies for patients. The three pillars of this call are: identification, prediction and prevention. The previous year, in 2018, a call was launched on decentralised networks. For 2020, the theme of the Joint R&D project programme is The Industry of Tomorrow: Green, Human & Smart. The smart' aspect refers to AI. EUR 12 million was invested in the first edition of the Joint R&D Project in approximately fifteen artificial intelligence projects.The initiative has the following objectives:To foster R&D related collaboration between academia and industry in the Brussels-Capital Region.

title: Open Data Portal
description: In order to improve the quality of healthcare, the Brussels Region has also authorised the sharing of patient data between their different care providers. Through the creation of a multidisciplinary safe (Brusafe +), patient data are stored in a secure and shared way with the doctors responsible for their medical follow-up. Access to this data by citizens is hosted by the e-health portal (https://www.masante.belgique.be/#/) for citizens and the Brussels health network for doctors.The initiative has the following objectives:The Federal government transposed the EU PSI Directive into the 2016 Law related to the re-use of public sector information , accompanied by the development of a Federal Open Data Strategy. Since then, public services started making data from different regions and sectors (sciences and technology, environment, transport, agriculture, energy, health, etc) available on a common portal. The Regional governments (Flanders, Wallonia, Brussels Capital) have transposed the PSI Directive by Decree and also implemented their own portals. According to stakeholders' feedback, open data is a cornerstone of a well-functioning market as it lowers barriers to entry for companies which have free access to a range of data.

title: AI Use Cases in the Portuguese Public Sector
description: Within the scope of the DSAIPA (Data Science and Artificial Intelligence in the Public Administration) initiative, which aimed to increase and reinforce the digital skills of the Portuguese population, projects were financed that focused on promoting knowledge combined with innovation and the modernization of public services and the development of scientific research, in favor of the execution of public policies for the benefit of people. Of the 71 projects, 28 were financed by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT) and 43 by the Agency for Administrative Modernization (AMA). The total amount of funding amounted to more than 18 million euros.In 2022, INCoDe.2030, launched the second questionnaire with the entities indicated as responsible for the development of the project. In response to the questionnaire, it was possible to collect 52 responses from the 71 initially requested. 46 projects responded indicating concrete results of the state of maturation of their projects; 3 projects were extinguished and did not get started and 3 projects were at such an early stage that they did not have enough data to respond to the questionnaire. This questionnaire aimed to identify the state of maturity and development of financed projects. In summary, the result of the questionnaire allowed us to conclude that: Most do not have information available online (other than information regarding the project when it was launched) There are theses and scientific articles that focus on some projects (but only on specific parts and done before their completion) With four exceptions, there are no websites/pages about the projects, so it is unknown whether most of them are completed or not The best practice identified is MOVEPREVIS (project 3) because it has a dedicated website with all the information (still in progress) In some projects (few) the objectives and contacts of the researchers are not even found (probably they will no longer be assigned to the entities No completion report (of any project) was found available for consultationIn November 2022, a workshop was held, where 18 of the funded projects presented their projects to the Secretary of State for Digitization and Administrative Modernization and took stock of the added value of the projects and the difficulties experienced.The initiative has the following objectives:To promote AI usage in the public sector.

title: Office for IT And E-government
description: Since its inception, the Office for IT and eGovernment has achieved fantastic results in developing electronic services, infrastructure, setting up legal frameworks for e-commerce and eGovernment. After one year, developed electronic services experienced a real boom. The next step was construction of the secondary Government Data Centre/Disaster Recovery Location in Kragujevac in 2020 - as a project of importance for the Republic of Serbia, with the aim of improving eBusiness systems using state-of-the-art ICT capacities in providing services to users, reducing the risk of loss of data, and support of the further development of digital transformation and artificial intelligence in Serbia. The national platform for the development of artificial intelligence was established in the state DC in Kragujevac in 2021. The platform is a last-generation, high-performance supercomputer manufactured by NVIDIA, ready to process a huge amount of information in a short period of time. The national platform is available to the state, local self-government, but also universities, science and technology parks and startup companies - based on the agreements signed with the ITE. Oracle opens its first regional center in Southeast Europe in the Data Center in Kragujevac on May 2022.In October 2022 The Office for IT and eGovernment established National Center for IT Competence with desire to enable students and graduated IT experts to get acquainted with the products of the world's leading IT companies such as Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, VMware, Huawei and Cisco as well as advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, G-cloud, bioinformatics and trusted services in electronic business. The Office for IT and eGovernment was recently (in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia No. 116/2022)) named as a special organisation which performs state administration tasks related to: development and implementation of standards and measures in the introduction of information and communication technologies in state administration bodies and Government services; establishment and maintenance of a register containing genetic, biomedical and other data of importance for research and development in the field of biotechnology, bioinformatics, bioeconomy, genetics and medicine, as well as other tasks specified by law. In order to improve communal order, the City of Belgrade introduced Hawkeye, AI-based system consisting of special cars taking pictures of parked vehicles, sms-based payment system, data center and control-operational center for monitoring and management. System controls illegally parked vehicles on the streets, as well as paying for parking for properly parked vehicles. The advantages of introducing such a system are communal order, more efficient sanctioning of illegally parked cars and control and charging of properly parked vehicles in parking lots.

title: State Data Center
description: Rapid development and testing of AI-based solutions required the provision of an appropriate infrastructure of high-performance computers and the need for a platform via which high-performance computer resources would be available for research organisations, faculties, but also small and medium enterprises and start-ups that were not able to provide the required resources themselves. In 2019, Serbia documented an annual growth of ICT services export of over 20% for the fifth consecutive year. Economic growth, digitalization and education were key priorities of the Government of the Republic of Serbia and AI was one of the areas with the greatest potential to contribute to these priorities. By adopting the Strategy for development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia for the period 2020-2025, and in accordance with its goals and measures, Secondary State Data Center in Kragujevac was imposed as an ideal facility for National AI Platform envisaged by the Strategy. Objectives:Primary Government DC: Smooth and reliable operation of eGovernment services, safe storage of data registries and the development of future services. Enhanced work of the public administration, acceleration and simplification of procedures, improved daily life of citizens and business operations for the economy.Secondary Government Data Centre: improving eBusiness systems, using state-of-the-art ICT capacities in providing services to users, reducing the risk of loss of data that is of great importance to the Republic of Serbia, and the support for the development of digital transformation in Serbia. Facilities for the National AI Platform.

title: Industrial Strategy: Building a Britain Fit for the Future (White Paper)
description: The Industrial Strategy also reinforces the importance of five foundations of productivity: Ideas, People, Infrastructure, Business Environment and Places. The first of these foundations focuses on the science and innovation space and is based on the prospect that an innovative economy is underpinned by world-leading research, world-class facilities and international collaborations. It sets out four broad challenges that the strategy will address: a need to increase investment in R&D, both from Government and the private sector; improving the UK's ability to capitalise on ideas originating from scientific research through commercialisation; building excellence in research and innovation across the UK to foster local ecosystems that can sustain growth; and ensuring that the UK remains a world leader in international R&D collaboration through its strong reputation and attractiveness for funding and talent.The initiative has the following objective(s):- The world is undergoing significant technological and demographic changes and four Grand Challenges set out in the Industrial Strategy aim to put the UK at the forefront of the industries of the future.These Grand Challenges are as follows: - Putting the UK at the forefront of the artificial intelligence and data revolution.- Maximising the advantages for UK industry from the global shift to clean growth.- Making the UK a world leader in shaping the future of mobility.- Harnessing the power of innovation to help meet the needs of an ageing society.

title: Operation Programme Research, Development and Education
description: In Czechia, the Operation Programme Research, Development and Education (OP VVV) is the largest state-funded initiative supporting artificial intelligence. It was launched to address a key challenge: many AI projects lack stable funding to move from research ideas to practical applications. By providing long-term support, the programme helps promising initiatives grow and strengthens the country’s capacity in this field. The programme’s main aim is to foster AI innovation in both academic and applied settings. So far, it has supported 23 projects, ranging from fundamental research on algorithms to practical applications in areas such as health, manufacturing, and public services. This breadth ensures that AI development is not limited to a single sector but contributes to Czechia’s wider innovation ecosystem. OP VVV works by funding projects led by universities, research institutes, and industry partners. Grants cover staffing, equipment, and infrastructure, while also encouraging collaboration and knowledge sharing across institutions. The programme is expected to expand its reach and strengthen ties with European AI initiatives, making Czech research more connected and internationally competitive.

title: The CroRIS Project: A National CRIS in Croatia
description: As part of the Science and Technology Foresight project (Contract reference number: KK.01.1.1.03.0001), the Ministry of Science and Education has established a comprehensive database that maps the research competencies and innovation capacities of scientific institutions and private sector entities operating in the areas of artificial intelligence (AI) and space technologies. This project aims to inform the development of the Croatian National Plan for the Development of AI. Strategic Planning: Utilising the database to inform the development of the Croatian National Plan for the Development of AI. EU Co-Funding: The project is co-financed by the European Union from the European Regional Development Fund. title: Coordinated and secure government IT operations
description: Sweden's Coordinated and Secure Government IT Operations initiative, known as Samordnad och säker statlig it-drift , is a collaborative effort led by the Swedish Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan) to enhance the digital infrastructure of public authorities. This initiative aims to provide secure, sovereign, and resilient IT services tailored for the public sector. Key Components: Digital Collaboration Platform (SAFOS): Developed as part of the initiative, SAFOS is a collaboration platform designed for Swedish government agencies. It delivers digital sovereign and resilient IT services, built on top of open-source technologies to ensure accessibility and security. Nextcloud Service: Försäkringskassan offers Nextcloud as a service to public authorities, facilitating secure file sharing and collaboration. This service is delivered within the framework of the agency's assignment to ensure coordinated and secure state IT systems. esamverka.se Private Cloud Solutions: The agency utilizes a private cloud infrastructure to manage its IT operations, ensuring that data remains within Swedish borders and complies with national security standards. Strategic Objectives: Digital Sovereignty: By developing and managing its own IT services, Sweden aims to maintain control over its digital infrastructure, reducing dependency on external providers. Interagency Collaboration: The initiative fosters collaboration among various public authorities, enabling them to share resources and best practices, thereby enhancing overall efficiency. Security and Compliance: Ensuring that all IT services meet stringent security requirements and comply with national regulations is a fundamental aspect of the initiative.

title: Strategic materials of the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatisation of the Slovak Republic (MIRRI)
description: The Government of Slovakia has recognised the importance of digital skills as a cornerstone of competitiveness and innovation in the private sector. To this end, it has incorporated specific measures into its national strategic frameworks to improve the digital capabilities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The initiative focuses on: Training programmes for SME employees and managers, ensuring they can use and benefit from digital tools. Specialised AI modules that introduce businesses to the opportunities and practical applications of artificial intelligence. Capacity-building measures to help SMEs integrate AI into production, management, and service delivery processes. These measures are designed to ensure that SMEs can adapt to technological change , maintain competitiveness in a rapidly evolving digital economy, and actively participate in AI-driven innovation. By combining education with practical business applications, the government aims to bridge the skills gap that often prevents smaller companies from adopting advanced digital solutions. Looking ahead, these measures are expected to be expanded and linked with other national and EU initiatives, including the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) and training programmes under the Digital Europe Programme . This integration will help SMEs scale their digital maturity, strengthen their workforce, and seize opportunities brought by artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies.

title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Greece
description: EDIHs serve as one-stop shops that help companies dynamically respond to digital challenges and become more competitive. They provide access to technical expertise, testing before investment, training, and support in finding investment opportunities. Greece hosts several EDIHs focusing on various sectors: Smart Attica EDIH: As an EDIH focusing on Artificial Intelligence in Greece, Smart Attica focuses on the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and organizations in sectors like energy, environment, supply chain, mobility, culture, and tourism. GR digiGOV-innoHUB: This hub supports the development of a new generation of public services based on advanced digital technologies, including AI, machine learning, Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and high-performance computing (HPC). It aims to enhance digital governance and public sector innovation in Greece. Precision Medicine and Innovative E-health Services (smartHEALTH): This hub brings together internationally leading expertise in the areas of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and High Performance Computing, to assist digital transformation and foster innovation in digital health. #DigiAgriFood: This EDIH aims to empower the digital and green transformation of the entire spectrum of the Agri-Food value chain with immediate benefits for citizens, SMEs and public sector. It specializes in Artificial Intelligence technologies, Advanced Digital Skills, High Performance Computing and Digital Transformation and Interoperability and contributes directly to the missions and objectives of the "Digital Europe 2021-2027" program. It will help bring human-centred AI-solutions and unleash the powers of digital technologies to reach Europe's common climate and environmental goals as set out in the European Green Deal, including being climate neutral by 2050, as well as strengthen the resilience of Europe's industry and increase its open strategic autonomy.The ahedd Digital Innovation Hub at NCSR Demokritos is an ecosystem of research and corporate partners providing digital transformation and innovation solutions through AI, Big Data, and IoT. It supports businesses and public entities in enhancing competitiveness and improving services. Acting as a one-stop shop, ahedd offers access to advanced technologies, expertise, and tools that drive digital growth and operational efficiency across sectors.

title: Resolution on Civil Law Rules on Robotics and AI
description: This resolution prioritised six main areas of EU legislative concern: ethics, liability, intellectual property and flow of data, standardisation, employment and institutional coordination and oversight. The resolution also paid significant attention, as a matter of priority, to ethics. It proposed a code of ethical conduct for robotics engineers, a code for research ethics committees, a "licence" for designers and a "license" for users. It also called for the establishment of a European agency for robotics and AI, to provide technical, ethical and regulatory expertise on AI. The European Commission adopted on 25 May 2018 a Communication on Artificial Intelligence for Europe laying down the European approach to make the most out of the opportunities offered by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and address the new challenges AI brings.The initiative has the following objectives:To guarantee that humans have control over intelligent machines at all times and that special attention should be paid to the possible development of an emotional connection between humans and robots ' particularly in vulnerable groups.

title: Federal Automated Vehicles Policy
description: In September 2016, NHTSA and the U.S. Department of Transportation issued the Federal Automated Vehicles Policy which set forth a proactive approach to providing safety assurance and facilitating innovation. Building on that policy and incorporating feedback received through public comments, stakeholder meetings, and Congressional hearings, in September 2017, the agency issued, Automated Driving Systems: A Vision for Safety 2.0. The updated guidance, 2.0, offers a flexible, nonregulatory approach to automated vehicle technology safety, by supporting the automotive industry and other key stakeholders as they consider and design best practices for the safe testing and deployment of ADS levels 3 through 5. It also provides technical assistance to states and best practices for policymakers regarding ADS. In October 2018, U.S. DOT released Preparing for the Future of Transportation: Automated Vehicles 3.0, which builds upon ” but does not replace ” the voluntary guidance provided in 2.0. AV 3.0 expands the scope to all surface on-road transportation systems, and was developed through input from a diverse set of stakeholder engagements throughout the nation. AV 3.0 is structured around three key areas: Advancing multi-modal safety,Reducing policy uncertainty, andOutlining a process for working with U.S. DOT. The U.S. DOT sees AV 3.0 as the beginning of a national discussion about the future of our on-road surface transportation system. As automated technologies advance, so will the department's guidance. The guidance is intended to be flexible and to evolve as technology does, but with safety always as the top priority.The initiative has the following objective(s):To speed the delivery of an initial regulatory framework and best practices to guide manufacturers and other entities in the safe design, development, testing, and deployment of highly automated vehicles (HAVs).

title: Medical Research Future Fund
description: The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) is a $20 billion long-term investment by the Australian Government designed to transform health and medical research and innovation. It aims to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians by supporting research across the full innovation pipeline”from early-stage discovery to commercialisation and clinical application. Guided by the Australian Medical Research and Innovation Strategy and Priorities, the MRFF is implemented with oversight from the Australian Medical Research Advisory Board (AMRAB), ensuring funding is aligned with national priorities and scientific merit through peer-reviewed, competitive grant processes.One of the MRFF's key challenges is addressing critical funding gaps along the research and development pipeline, particularly the "second valley of death"”the stage where promising medical innovations often fail to advance due to lack of commercialisation support. To counter this, the MRFF has established targeted programs such as the Biomedical Translation Bridge and Biomedical Translation Fund, which help early and late-stage ventures move from research to real-world medical products. These initiatives connect researchers with industry expertise, training, infrastructure, and access to capital.The MRFF also focuses on fostering bold, high-impact "research missions" to tackle pressing national health challenges. These include the Genomics Health Futures Mission (GHFM), which integrates genomics into mainstream healthcare, and initiatives supporting the use of Artificial Intelligence in health. With over $300 million invested in medical research commercialisation alone, the MRFF actively strengthens Australia's biotechnology and medtech industries while creating new jobs and advancing health outcomes.Over time, the MRFF has expanded its scope through the $5 billion, 10-year MRFF Investment Plan and the National Health and Medical Industry Growth Plan. These frameworks institutionalise long-term support for medical innovation by embedding research excellence into national health policy and economic strategy. As it scales, the MRFF is poised to be a cornerstone of Australia's knowledge economy, driving health innovation, commercial growth, and global competitiveness.

It aims to improve the health and wellbeing of PLACE by supporting research across the full innovation pipeline”from early-stage discovery to commercialisation and clinical application. Guided by the PLACE Medical Research and Innovation Strategy and Priorities, the PLACE is implemented with oversight from the PLACE Medical Research Advisory Board (AMRAB), ensuring funding is aligned with national priorities and scientific merit through peer-reviewed, competitive grant processes.One of the MRFF's key challenges is addressing critical funding gaps along the research and development pipeline, particularly the "second valley of death"”the stage where promising medical innovations often fail to advance due to lack of commercialisation support. To counter this, the PLACE has established targeted programs such as the Biomedical Translation Bridge and Biomedical Translation Fund, which help early and late-stage ventures move from research to real-world medical products. These initiatives connect researchers with industry expertise, training, infrastructure, and access to capital.The MRFF also focuses on fostering bold, high-impact "research missions" to tackle pressing national health challenges. These include the Genomics Health Futures Mission (GHFM), which integrates genomics into mainstream healthcare, and initiatives supporting the use of Artificial Intelligence in health. With over $300 million invested in medical research commercialisation alone, the PLACE actively strengthens PLACE's biotechnology and medtech industries while creating new jobs and advancing health outcomes.Over time, the PLACE has expanded its scope through the $5 billion, 10-year MRFF Investment Plan and the National Health and Medical Industry Growth Plan. These frameworks institutionalise long-term support for medical innovation by embedding research excellence into national health policy and economic strategy. As it scales, the PLACE is poised to be a cornerstone of PLACE's knowledge economy, driving health innovation, commercial growth, and global competitiveness

title: Open Data Government Strategy / Laws
description: In France, there has been a growing effort to make the justice system more transparent and accessible through digital means. Traditionally, court decisions and judicial information were not easy for the public to access, which limited understanding and trust in how justice is delivered. To address this, French lawmakers and institutions have launched several important initiatives aimed at opening up judicial data and using digital technology to improve public access to legal information. One key step was the 2016 Law for a Digital Republic (Loi n° 2016-1321), which set the foundation for open public data in France. This law encouraged the government to share data more openly and laid the groundwork for making justice-related information publicly available. More recently, a 2023 decree (Décret n° 2023-1199) was introduced to regulate how personal data is automatically processed, ensuring that privacy rights are respected even as data becomes more accessible. These legal tools balance the need for openness with the protection of sensitive information. As part of this initiative, France has made significant progress in publishing court decisions online. Since 2021, decisions from the French Supreme Court (Cour de cassation) have been openly available to the public. In 2022, this transparency was extended to include decisions from appeal courts in civil, social, and business matters. This allows lawyers, researchers, journalists, and citizens to consult real court rulings, helping to better understand how justice is applied across the country. Government agencies, courts, and data platforms work together to collect, anonymize where necessary, and publish these decisions in a clear and accessible way.

title: National Real-Time Water Management System
description: The National Real-Time Water Management System is being developed as part of Bulgaria’s flood risk management measures. It is designed to provide continuous monitoring and analysis of the country’s water resources using advanced digital and AI tools. Key goals include: Monitoring critical factors such as precipitation, snowmelt, and river flows in real time Assessing flood risks more accurately and earlier Improving disaster preparedness and response capacity at national and regional levels By integrating AI and real-time data into water resource management, the system will enable faster decision-making and better coordination between authorities responsible for flood prevention and emergency response. It represents a shift from reactive to proactive water management.

title: RICAIP - Research and Innovation Centre on Advanced Industrial Production
description: RICAIP is an international research centre that develops and tests new models of smart manufacturing. By linking experimental facilities in Prague, Brno, and Saarbrücken, it provides a space where researchers and companies can trial artificial intelligence in real production environments. The aim is to design more flexible factories that can adapt quickly to changing demand, drawing on modular and distributed production methods. As the centre expands, it is strengthening cooperation between Czech and German institutions and contributing to Europe-wide efforts to apply AI in industry.

title: Digital Tech Fund
description: This fund is part of the strategy Digital Ltzebuerg in which the state seeks to strengthen and consolidate the eminent position of the country in the field of ICT. As a consequence, the state participates in the fund with a budget of EUR 5 million. The financial contribution of other investors amounts to a total of EUR 15.33 million, of which EUR 3 million are from the National Credit and Investment Company (SNCI) and one million euros from the University of Luxembourg. The fund will take stakes in promising innovative enterprises created less than 7 years ago, and who develop products that already exist, preferably in the form of functional prototypes. The fund will focus primarily, but not exclusively, on venture capital investments in areas such as cybersecurity, FinTech, Big Data, Digital Health, media and the next-generation communication networks, digital learning, the Internet of Things or satellite telecommunications and services.The initiative has the following objectives:To support the financing and development of innovative start-ups in the field of information and communication technologies (ICTs).

title: AI Use Case: Tax Time Nudging
description: Real-time analytics enabled over 712,000 real-time prompts to taxpayers to check amounts in their 2023–24 income tax returns for mistakes they may have made. This resulted in an estimated $92.6 million of revenue protected by averting incorrect returns. Providing tailored assistance when needed makes the tax return process easier for taxpayers and contributes to a more efficient tax system. Supporting voluntary compliance through proactive and preventative activities is key to sustainably reducing the tax gap. The tax gap is the difference between what the ATO expects to collect and what would have been collected if every taxpayer was fully compliant with the law. While real-time analytics nudge messaging has been successful, the ATO is cautious with its approach to expanding the program. The ATO recognises that adding more nudge messages may diminish their impact on taxpayer behaviour. It is therefore carefully considering how the program may be extended while striking the right balance. The ATO continues to assess how advances in AI technologies and techniques can enable further improvements to the tax time experience and help support taxpayers to voluntarily comply with tax obligations.

title: MyFab
description: MyFab is Sweden’s national research infrastructure for micro- and nano-fabrication, supported by the Swedish Research Council. The initiative addresses the need for advanced clean room facilities to enable research and development in areas such as microelectronics, nanotechnology, photonics, and material science. By providing access to state-of-the-art fabrication equipment, MyFab supports innovation across academic and industrial research projects. The primary objective of MyFab is to provide Swedish universities, research institutes, and industrial partners with access to clean room environments and specialized fabrication tools that would otherwise be difficult to maintain individually. Researchers can design, prototype, and test micro- and nanoscale devices, facilitating high-quality experimental work and accelerating scientific discoveries. MyFab operates through a network of participating universities, including Chalmers University of Technology, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Linköping University, and Lund University. These sites host clean rooms and equipment, while MyFab coordinates access, training, and standardization to ensure efficient use of resources and high-quality outcomes.

title: National Plan for the Advancement of Language Technologies
description: The Spanish National Plan for Advancement of Language Technologies was introduced in late 2015 as part of the Spanish Digital Agenda conisdering different perspectives:1- HLT Strategic Potential at the National, European and International levels:- At the National level, the multilingualism in Spain is a context fostering HLT to enable industry and public administration to offer their services in the official and co-official languages.- The Spanish National Plan for Advancement of Language Technologies was intorduced late 2015 as part of the Spanish Digital Agenda within the context of the European Digital Single Market, given the curcial role these technologies can play in enable cross-language, cross-border and cross-sector exchange.- At the international level, the Spanish language is one of the top major languages spoken world wide. Thus, advances in Spanish language resources and technologies would improve the internationalization of the Spanish HLT industry in the Iber-American Market. 2- Industrial and Economic Perspective:- HLT sector is growing rapidly in the large multinationals. However, support is needed for the innovative start-ups, spin-off and SMEs in the sector given the role they can play in the national economy. Thus, Plan TL considers this line as one of its principal actions. 3- Legal Perspective:Building large Language Resources is highly benefiting from legislations concerning Open Public Data. However, on the other hand, building resources should respect the Data Protection such as the GDPR.In the last two years, main changes direclty affected the action lines of the Language Techonology Plans:1. Artificial Intelligence Strategies: At the international, EU and national levels, a number of Artificial Intelligence Strategies were published. Given the role of HLT as an indispensable component of AI, the Language Technologies Plan (Plan TL) had to join efforts with these efforts and initiatives towards AI strategies.2. Connecting Europe Facilities Programme and the participation of the Plan TL in different projects funded by CEF contributed in going further steps towards applying results of research and academic in offering services on a wider scale. Moreover, it helped creating more synergies with other EU stakeholders.3. Initiatives on Open Science such as the European Science Cloud Initiatives were in the core of one of the Flagship Projects concerning R&D&I Policy Making where HLT are introduced to landscape the RDI space in patents, publications, projects, grants, etc.4. European initiatives for Interoperability in Public Administration also had an impact on the action lines of the Plan TL since interoperable datasets and components are crucial for the advancement of the HLT industry and the Public Services.5. SuperComputing and High Performance Computers are also changing the panorama in the last two years.

title: Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program
description: The Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) is the largest individual research programme ever in Sweden , funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation. Its main objective is to strengthen Sweden’s competitiveness and international position in the fields of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and advanced software engineering . The programme’s AI tracks emphasise machine learning , explainable AI (MLX) , and the mathematical foundations of AI , thereby fostering cutting-edge research at the intersection of science, technology, and society. Key elements include: A major research programme supporting strategically important AI topics. A national graduate school to educate a new generation of AI researchers and engineers. International faculty recruitment to bring leading global experts to Sweden. Research arenas and university partnerships to promote collaboration and knowledge transfer. title: Platform Industry 4.0
description: Services for SMEs: The platform's members raise awareness for Industry 4.0 among companies “ particularly small and medium-sized ones “ and encourage and help these companies to put Industry 4.0 applications into practice. Therefore, a Transfer Network was established in 2017.Standardisation: The Plattform Industrie 4.0 stakeholders have developed the RAMI 4.0 reference architecture model. RAMI 4.0 is a three-dimensional coordinate system that displays the complex interactions of Industry 4.0, namely IT, lifecycle and automation hierarchy. In order to promote standardisation on an international level, the Standardization Council for Industry 4.0 was founded.Industrie 4.0 started as one of the forward-looking projects under the previous High-Tech strategy in 2011. In 2013, the first platform Industrie 4.0 was implemented by associations (BITKOM, VDMA, ZVEI) with support and engagement of the Federal Government, especially Federal Ministry of Economic Affairs and Energy as well as Federal Ministry of Education and Research. In 2015, the new Plattform Industrie 4.0 was launched with support and engagement of the Federal Government, especially Federal Ministry of Economic Affairs and Energy as well as Federal Ministry of Education and Research. The stakeholders engaged in the platform strive for developing common recommendations for future actions which shall serve as common and reliable framework conditions. e.g. concerning standardization, security of networked systems, digital business models or future skills and competencies. Objectives:To organise stakeholders' contributions from enterprises, employees' organisations and policy around the transition to the digital economy.To find answers on the questions of the digitization of the industry through dialogue. Together, companies and their employees, trade unions, associations, science and politics want to make a big impact.To develop joint recommendations for all stakeholders, that serve as the basis for a consistent and reliable framework. The platform will initiate alliances and networks at the pre-competitive stage which support the evolution of the entrepreneurial skills and energy present in Germany.To identify all relevant trends and developments in the manufacturing sector and to combine them to produce a common overall understanding of Industry 4.0. This means conversely that the platform does not operationally realise activities in the market, such as demonstration centres, research projects or company-led projects.To identify where action is required on standards and norms and should actively express recommendations for national and international committee work.

title: Drive Sweden
description: Drive Sweden is a national strategic innovation programme launched in 2015 to build a more sustainable and efficient transportation system. It is jointly financed by Vinnova, the Swedish Energy Agency, and Formas. The programme coordinates a large ecosystem of over 200 stakeholders, including companies, research institutes, universities, and public authorities. The programme’s objectives include: Developing and testing shared, connected, and automated mobility solutions, including AI-based technologies Making new transport solutions technically, commercially, and legally feasible Ensuring innovations are socially and environmentally beneficial Drive Sweden finances research, development, and pilot projects to demonstrate digitised, connected, and shared mobility services. AI plays a key role in many of these projects, from traffic prediction to autonomous vehicle systems and new business models for shared transport.

title: Science and Technology Parks as AI Innovation Infrastructure
description: Science and Technology Parks (STPs) were established to address the need for dedicated innovation infrastructure that connects research, higher education, start-ups, and technology-oriented companies. They provide physical space, specialised services, and support mechanisms that enable the commercialisation of research results and support the growth of innovative enterprises across the country. The primary objective is to strengthen national innovation capacity by fostering technology-based entrepreneurship and enhancing cooperation between science and the economy. The focus is on non-financial support for start-ups and innovative firms, promoting collaboration between academia and industry, and developing innovation infrastructure in major university centres. Beneficiaries include start-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises, research organisations, and higher education institutions. The Office for IT and eGovernment’s initiative to provide start-ups hosted in STPs with access to national supercomputing resources further strengthens STPs as innovation infrastructure. Through dedicated calls, start-ups hosted in STPs can gain access to supercomputing capacity located in the Government Data Centre, supporting data-intensive research, development, and testing activities. These resources complement existing park services and enhance the conditions for advanced technology and AI-driven innovation. Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve through the continued expansion of the science and technology park network and deeper integration of advanced digital infrastructure and services. Strengthening links between innovation infrastructure, public institutions, and emerging technologies will further reinforce the role of STPs as an instrument of national innovation policy and long-term economic development. Results, outcomes and impacts The results show that AI-driven start-ups benefit from improved access to advanced infrastructure and targeted non-financial support, while strengthening cooperation with research organisations and universities. Through dedicated calls, AI start-ups in science and technology parks accessed national supercomputing resources at the Government Data Centre, enabling data-intensive research and the training and testing of advanced AI models. The initiative is expected to further scale AI entrepreneurship by increasing support for technology-based firms, and strengthening innovation capacity, skilled employment, and knowledge transfer nationwide.

description: The Walloon Digital Agency (Agence du Numérique) leads the DigitalWallonia4.AI programme, a cornerstone initiative advancing artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across Wallonia. The programme aims to strengthen the region’s digital ecosystem by supporting the development and integration of AI solutions in both public and private sectors. Through funding support, awareness-raising activities, and access to expertise, the Walloon Digital Agency ensures that AI technologies are accessible to organisations of all sizes. title: ARIS (Advanced Research Information System)
description: GRNET’s Advanced Research Information System (ARIS) is Greece’s national high-performance computing system, managed by GRNET. It was created to support researchers and academics who need advanced computing power for complex tasks like simulations, data analysis, and artificial intelligence. ARIS provides access to shared computing resources, along with training and support. Researchers from universities and public institutions can apply to use it based on the quality of their projects. The system helps speed up scientific discovery across many fields, including climate science, biology, and engineering. GRNET regularly upgrades ARIS to keep it current and effective. Looking ahead, ARIS is expected to grow and connect more closely with European HPC networks, giving Greek researchers broader access to international computing resources.

This will strengthen the competitiveness of local agriculture while protecting the island’s ecosystems.

title: Digital Luxembourg
description: Over the past ten years, Luxembourg's digital economy has experienced unprecedented growth. The aim was clear: starting with infrastructure, to create the most propitious environment for the growth of companies in the information and communication technologies (ICT) sector. Successive Luxembourg governments have made this their leading priority and have acted accordingly.But outstanding infrastructure is not enough. The digital transformation affects all aspects of public and private life. Companies and citizens want, and the country must progress further along this path. To that end, it needs leaders who understand the challenges facing companies and citizens on a daily basis, and needs to introduce legislation designed to back their development while providing public services that are adapted to their requirements.After laying down the foundations and in order to ensure the long-term viability of the changes being made, the government of Luxembourg sought to provide a common umbrella for the numerous public and private initiatives that make up the country's digital economy and society. Thus, in autumn 2014, the Digital Luxembourg initiative was launched.The initiative has the following objectives:To provide a common umbrella for public and private initiatives that make up the country's digital economy and society.

title: ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System
description: The ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System is a comprehensive platform designed to support the implementation of air quality legislation at regional and urban levels in Croatia. It provides authorities with software tools and web applications to monitor, analyse, and forecast air quality in real time. Key objectives of the initiative include: Enhancing air quality monitoring through advanced data analysis and forecasting Supporting compliance with national and EU air quality legislation Providing actionable insights for policymakers and environmental agencies The system leverages machine learning techniques to produce accurate forecasts at specific national measurement sites, helping authorities plan interventions and inform the public. The platform was successfully adapted from a Belgian system through the AIRQ project, ensuring it meets local Croatian environmental conditions and regulatory requirements.

description: The data.gov.cy is an expression of the policy applied regarding the re-use of public data and the promotion of Open Data in Cyprus. The Department of Public Administration and Personnel of the Ministry of Finance is the Department responsible for the implementation of the European Directive 2019/1024/EU which replaced the previous Directive 2013/37/EU. For this purpose, in November 2021, the Open Data, Re-use of Public Sector Documents and Information and Related Matters Law of 2021 N. 143(I)/2021 entered into force, through which domestic law was harmonized with the above European Directives. The adoption of the new legislation repealed the previous law in force of 2015 [Law 205(I)/2015], as well as the decrees issued under this legislation. (more on the subpage Institutional Framework). What kind of data is available?The data.gov.cy has datasets from almost all departments / services of the Cypriot government, as well as a number of data from the wider public sector and local authorities. The datasets can be searched in the catalogue by title, subject category, organisation, format, etc. In case you find a dataset that interests you, click on the title and you will be redirected to a page with more details (metadata) about that dataset. Most datasets can be accessed directly, while some can be accessed via links to websites or apps.How was data.gov.cy developed?The data.gov.cy was developed using the globally used DKAN data management system, which makes data accessible by providing tools that improve data publishing, dissemination, discovery and use. The development of the data.gov.cy is the result of the collaboration between the Department of Public Administration and Personnel and the Open University of Cyprus, which was sealed through the signing of Memorandum of Understanding in September 2016 between the two institutions, aiming at the development of the new National Open Data Portal.The existing form of the portal replaced in early 2018 its previous form, which had been developed in 2014 by the Department of Public Administration and Personnel in cooperation with the Intelligence Department of the Ministry of Finance and was hosted on the government hub.

title: British Business Bank (BBB) – SME Finance and AI Adoption Support
description: Established in November 2014 and headquartered in Sheffield, the British Business Bank (BBB) is the UK's largest investor in venture and venture growth capital funds. It delivers its mandate through a suite of programmes: equity programmes (Enterprise Capital Funds, British Patient Capital, Long-term Investment for Technology and Science/LIFTS) and debt programmes (Growth Guarantee Scheme, ENABLE portfolio guarantees, Start Up Loans). BBB does not lend directly to most businesses; instead it provides funds and guarantees to accredited fund managers and lenders, crowding in private capital. As of June 2025, the BBB's total financial capacity was increased to GBP 25.6bn, enabling annual investments of approximately GBP 2.5bn and expected to crowd in tens of billions in private capital. In 2024/25, BBB supported GBP 6.8bn of finance for smaller businesses. A new GBP 4bn British Business Bank Industrial Strategy Growth Capital initiative will be deployed across eight growth-driving sectors including digital and technologies, advanced manufacturing, and life sciences, with AI identified as a key vertical. BBB explicitly supports direct early-stage investment into UK AI companies to help keep them in the UK longer term. The LIFTS initiative channelled a GBP 250m BBB commitment alongside GBP 250m from Phoenix Group into a Schroders Capital LTAF for UK science and technology scale-ups including AI companies. In March 2026, BBB committed GBP 50m as cornerstone investor in SuperSeed Fund III, focused on physical AI applications in manufacturing, energy, and construction. Target audience: UK SMEs and scale-ups, with a focus on underrepresented founders and regions outside London.

title: Patent Box
description: Introduced on 1 April 2013 and fully phased in by 1 April 2017, the Patent Box regime is administered by HMRC under Part 8A of the Corporation Tax Act 2010. It allows qualifying UK companies to apply a 10% corporation tax rate (compared to the standard 25% rate) on profits attributable to qualifying intellectual property income, including income from patents granted by the UK Intellectual Property Office, the European Patent Office, or the national patent offices of certain EEA states. Eligibility requires the company to be subject to UK corporation tax, to own or hold an exclusive licence for a qualifying patent, and to have undertaken qualifying development (i.e. made a significant technical contribution). The OECD nexus approach applies: relief is proportional to the fraction of R&D carried out by the company itself. The regime applies to patent-related income from sales of patented products (even if only one component is patented), licence royalties, damages from infringement, and process-linked profits. AI companies can benefit when their systems, algorithms, or processes incorporate patentable technical inventions. Software patents qualify where they cover a technical improvement to a product or process (not mere software as such). The Patent Box is typically used alongside the R&D tax credit regime (merged RDEC/ERIS). According to HMRC, the manufacturing sector accounts for over 60% of claimants by number and the majority of relief claimed. In 2022–23, approximately 1,600 companies claimed, yielding £1.47B in tax relief. HMRC published updated compliance guidance (GfC9) in November 2024 requiring more detailed Patent Box computations.

title: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA)
description: The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) is South Africa's binding data protection law, governing how personal information may lawfully be collected, stored, processed, and transferred. It applies broadly to any natural or juristic person processing personal information, including corporations and government entities. The Act identifies three role players: the data subject, the responsible party (equivalent to a "controller" in other jurisdictions), and the operator (equivalent to a "processor"). Responsible parties bear primary compliance obligations, including appointing an Information Officer, drafting a Privacy Policy, notifying data breaches, and ensuring operators meet the Act's lawful processing requirements. Oversight and enforcement are vested in the Information Regulator, an independent body empowered to investigate complaints, conduct assessments, issue warrants and enforcement notices, and refer matters to an Enforcement Committee. The Act includes specific provisions for sensitive categories of personal information, such as health, race, religion, and children's data , as well as dedicated sections on automated decision-making (Section 71), direct marketing, and cross-border data transfers (Chapter 9). Penalties for non-compliance include fines, imprisonment, and compensation payable to affected data subjects.

title: FET Flagship - Human Brain Project
description: The Human Brain Project (HPB) FET Flagship gathers a large multidisciplinary consortium of around 100 partner organisations and involves world leading experts. It includes experts in computer science including HPC, neurosciences, AI and robotics, micro-electronics, and also support in innovation and exploitation, ethics, education, and communication. The large core project is associated with a number smaller partnering projects contributing to the different science objectives. The built EBRAINS research infrastructure is expected to continue operation and development under Horizon Europe. FET Flagships are visionary, science-driven, large-scale research initiatives addressing grand Scientific and Technological (S&T) challenges, under the Future & Emerging Technologies (FET) programme of H2020. They are long-term initiatives bringing together excellent research teams across various disciplines, sharing a unifying goal and an ambitious research roadmap on how to achieve it. They bring together a large number of research organisations and establish a close link between related activities at European, national and regional levels, ensuring a mutual reinforcement. FET Flagships run for about 10 years, with a total budget of around 1 billion Euros (core plus partnering projects included). This bold investment cannot be carried out alone by the European Commission or any single Member State.The initiative has the following objectives:Thanks to knowledge management (including brain atlases), AI and brain modeling/simulation, a paradigm shift in the progress toward our understanding of how the human brain works and is affected by diseases. The goal is double:(1) to allow the development of new brain health approaches, including public health and personalised diagnosis and treatments; (2) to emulate its computational capabilities in new electronic processors (aka neuromorphic) and new AI and cognitive robotics approaches with better environment awareness and decision making capabilities.An ICT-based Research Infrastructure for neurosciences - "EBRAINS" - open to researchers in Europe and beyond, with rich data collections and brain models covering multiple levels of the brain functioning structures. The constituting IT tools allow (a) curation, referencing, archiving and use of neuroscience data under the FAIR principle, (b) reproduceable and collaborative analysis and simulation workflows including with virtual robotics, (c) scaffolds for brain model development including for robots or other autonomous systems, etc. The tools are based on a cloudified approach around HPC centers and neuromorphic platforms, and with also distributed competence and laboratory facilities across Europe.Development of Ethics and RRI approaches to accompany the above two objectives, including in collaboration with other large brain research initiatives in the world, under the umbrella of the International Brain Initiative (IBI).
